         needs to be acceded to. It is essential to reproduce
         the relevant paragraph for this purpose:-"48.The   question   is   with   regard   to   the   inherent 
                      power  of  the  High Court in quashing the criminal  
                      proceedings  against  an  offender  who  has settled 
                      his   dispute   with   the   victim   of   the   crime   but   the 
                      crime  in     which     he   is   allegedly  involved  is   not 
                      compoundable underSection 320of the Code.49.Section 482of the Code, as its very  language  
                      suggests,     saves   the   inherent   power   of   the   High  
                      Court   which   it   has   by   virtue   of     it     being     a 
                      superior  court  to  prevent  abuse  of  the  process  of 
                      any   court   or   otherwise     to   secure   the   ends   of 
                      justice. It begins  with  the  words,  'nothing  in 
                      this Code' which means that the provision   is   an  
                      overriding  provision.   These words leave no manner 
                      of doubt that none   of   the   provisions   of   the  
                      Code   limits   or   restricts   the   inherent   power.   The 
                      guideline for exercise   of   such power is provided 
                      inSection 482itself   i.e.,   to   prevent   abuse 
                      of  the process of any court or otherwise to secure 
                      the ends   of   justice.     As   has been repeatedly 
                      stated thatSection  482confers  no  new  powers  
                      on     High   Court;   it   merely   safeguards     existing 
                      inherent     powers     possessed     by     High   Court 
                      necessary   to   prevent   abuse   of   the   process   of   any  
                      Court  or  to  secure the ends of justice.   It is 
                      equally well settled that the power is  not  to
                      be resorted to if there is specific provision in the 
                      Code   for   the   redress of the grievance   of   an  
                      aggrieved  party.  It  should  be  exercised  very 
                      sparingly and it should not be exercised as against  
                      the   express   bar     of     law   engrafted   in   any   other 
                      provision of the Code.50. In different situations, the inherent power may 
                      be   exercised     in   different   ways   to   achieve   its 
                      ultimate objective. Formation   of   opinion   by the 
                      High   Court   before   it   exercises     inherent     powerPage 3 of 7HC-NIC                                  Page 3 of 7      Created On Tue Jul 12 01:22:32 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/15767/2016                                                ORDER


               underSection     482on   either   of   the   twin 
               objectives, (i) to prevent abuse of the  process of  
               any court or (ii) to secure the ends of justice, is 
               a sine qua non.51. In the very nature of   its   constitution,   it 
               is   the   judicial obligation of the High Court to 
               undo a wrong in course of administration  of justice 
               or to prevent continuation of unnecessary judicial 
               process. This  is founded on the legal maxim quando  
               lex aliquid  alicui  concedit, concedituret id sine  
               qua res ipsa esse non  potest. The  full  import  of  
               which     is   whenever   anything   is   authorised,   and 
               especially if, as  a  matter  of duty,required to be 
               done   by   law,   it   is   found   impossible   to   do   that 
               thing     unless   something   else   not   authorised   in 
               express terms be also    done,   may also   be done, 
               then   that   something   else   will   be   supplied     by 
               necessary       intendment.   Ex   debito   justitiae   is 
               inbuilt in such exercise; the whole idea  is  to  do  
               real, complete and substantial justice   for   which 
               it  exists.  The  power possessed by the High Court  
               underSection   482of the   Code   is   of   wide  
               amplitude but requires exercise with great caution 
               and circumspection.52.     It   needs   no   emphasis   that   exercise     of 
               inherent   power   by   the High Court would entirely 
               depend on the  facts  and  circumstances  of  each
               case.   It   is   neither   permissible   nor     proper     for 
               the     court     to     provide     a   straitjacket   formula 
               regulating     the     exercise     of     inherent     powers 
               underSection   482.   No   precise   and   inflexible 
               guidelines can also be provided.53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on 
               the  ground  of settlement between  an offender  and 
               victim  is  not  the  same  thing as compounding  of  
               offence.     They     are     different   and     not  
               interchangeable.   Strictly   speaking,   the   power   of 
               compounding of offences   given   to   a court underSection   320is   materially   different   from     the  
               quashing  of  criminal proceedings by the High Court 
               in   exercise   of   its   inherent   jurisdiction.     In  
               compounding of offences, power of a criminal court 
               is  circumscribed    by    the  provisions  contained  inSection 320and  the  court  is  guided  solely  and  
               squarely   thereby   while,   on   the   other   hand,   the 
               formation   of   opinion     by     the   High   Court   for  
               quashing     a       criminal     offence     or     criminal 
               proceeding   or criminal complaint is guided by the 
               material on record   as   to   whether   the ends of 
               justice   would   justify   such   exercise   of   power 
               although  the  ultimate consequence may be acquittalPage 4 of 7HC-NIC                           Page 4 of 7      Created On Tue Jul 12 01:22:32 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/15767/2016                                                ORDER


               or dismissal of indictment.54.  Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding  
               having regard  to the fact that dispute between the  
               offender  and   victim  has   been  settled although  
               offences are not compoundable,  it  does  so  as  in  
               its   opinion,continuation of   criminal proceedings 
               will  be an exercise in  futility  and
               justice in the case demands that the dispute between 
               the   parties   is     put     to   an   end   and   peace   is 
               restored;  securing  the  ends  of  justice  being 
               the ultimate guiding factor. No  doubt,  crimes  are 
               acts  which  have  harmful effect on the public and  
               consist in wrong  doing  that  seriously  endangers 
               and threatens  well­being  of  society  and  it  is not 
               safe to leave   the   crime­doer only because he and 
               the victim have settled  the  dispute  amicably  or  
               that   the   victim   has   been   paid   compensation,   yet  
               certain     crimes     have     been   made   compoundable   in 
               law, with or  without  permission  of  the  Court.  
               In respect of serious offences  like  murder,  rape, 
               dacoity,  etc;  or  other
               offences of mental depravity underIPCor offences 
               of moral turpitude   under special   statutes,   likePrevention  of  Corruption  Actor  the  offences
               committed by public servants while working in that 
               capacity,   the     settlement   between   offender   and 
               victim   can   have   no   legal   sanction     at     all. 
               However,certain   offences   which   overwhelmingly   and 
               predominantly bear  civil  flavour having arisen out 
               of   civil,   mercantile,   commercial,     financial, 
               partnership  or   such     like     transactions     or     the 
               offences  arising  out  of  matrimony, particularly  
               relating to dowry, etc.  or  the   family  dispute,  
               where     the   wrong   is   basically   to   victim   and   the 
               offender   and   victim     have     settled     all   disputes 
               between them amicably, irrespective of the fact that 
               such  offences have not been made compoundable, the  
               High Court may within the framework  of its inherent 
               power,   quash   the   criminal   proceeding   or   criminal 
               complaint   or F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the 
               face   of   such   settlement,   there   is hardly any 
               likelihood of offender being convicted and by   not 
               quashing  the criminal proceedings, justice shall be 
               casualty and   ends of justice   shall be defeated. 
               The above list is illustrative and not exhaustive. 
               Each  case will depend on  its  own  facts  and  no 
               hard  and  fast  category  can  be prescribed.57.   The   position   that   emerges   from   the   above 
               discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the  
               High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR  
               or   complaint   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
               jurisdiction   is   distinct   and   different   from   thePage 5 of 7HC-NIC                           Page 5 of 7      Created On Tue Jul 12 01:22:32 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/15767/2016                                               ORDER


               power given to a criminal court for compounding the  
               offences   under   Section   320   of   the   Code.   Inherent 
               power   is   of   wide   plenitude   with   no   statutory 
               limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with 
               the guideline  engrafted  in  such  power  viz;  (i)  to 
               secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse  
               of the process of any Court. In what cases power to 
               quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R 
               may be exercised where the offender and victim have  
               settled their dispute would depend on the facts and  
               circumstances  of  each  case  and  no category  can  be 
               prescribed. However, before exercise of such power, 
               the High Court must have due regard to the nature 
               and   gravity   of   the   crime.  Heinous   and   serious 
               offences   of   mental   depravity   or   offences   like 
               murder,   rape,   dacoity,   etc.   cannot   be   fittingly 
               quashed even though the victim or victims family and 
               the offender have settled the dispute. Such offences 
               are not private in nature and have serious impact on 
               society.   Similarly,   any   compromise   between   the 
               victim   and   offender   in   relation   to   the   offences 
               under special statutes likePrevention of Corruption 
               Actor   the   offences   committed   by   public   servants 
               while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide 
               for   any   basis   for   quashing   criminal   proceedings 
               involving   such   offences.   But   the   criminal   cases 
               having  overwhelmingly   and   predominatingly   civil 
               flavour stand on different footing for the purposes 
               of quashing, particularly the offences arising from 
               commercial,   financial,   mercantile,   civil, 
               partnership   or   such   like   transactions   or   the 
               offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, 
               etc.   or   the   family   disputes   where   the   wrong   is 
               basically   private   or   personal   in   nature   and   the  
               parties have resolved their entire dispute. In this 
               category   of   cases,   High   Court   may   quash   criminal 
               proceedings   if   in   its   view,   because   of   the 
               compromise   between   the   offender   and   victim,   the 
               possibility   of   conviction   is   remote   and   bleak   and 
               continuation of criminal case would put accused to 
               great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice 
               would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal  
               case   despite   full   and   complete   settlement   and 
               compromise with the victim. In other words, the High 
               Court  must  consider  whether  it  would  be unfair  or 
               contrary to the interest of justice to continue with 
               the   criminal   proceeding   or   continuation   of   the 
               criminal   proceeding   would   tantamount   to   abuse   of 
               process   of   law   despite   settlement   and   compromise 
               between   the   victim   and   wrongdoer   and   whether   to  
               secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that 
               criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to  
               the   above   question(s)   is   in   affirmative,   the   High 
               Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quashPage 6 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 6 of 7      Created On Tue Jul 12 01:22:32 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/15767/2016                                             ORDER


                      the criminal proceeding."Resultantly, this petition is allowed. The FIR

         acquittal              have     been         recorded.              He      ultimately

         principles governing and regulating the hearing

         very clearly explained by the Hon'ble Apex Court

         it has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court

         in Paragaph 36 and 37 as under:"36. The court of appeal would not
                  ordinarily interfere with the order of
                  acquittal unless the approach is vitiated by
                  manifest illegality. In an appeal against

                  learned courts below, while acquitting,
                  cannot be the views of a reasonable person
                  on the material on record.37.InChandrappa and Ors. v. State of

               power of appellate court dealing with an
               appeal against acquittal has been considered
               and this Court held as under:"42.....(4) An appellate court, however,
                     must bear in mind that in case of
                     acquittal, there is double presumption in
                     favour of the accused. Firstly, the
                     presumption of innocence is available to
                     him under the fundamental principle of
                     criminal jurisprudence that every person
                     shall be presumed to be innocent unless
                     he is proved guilty by a competent court
                     of law. Secondly, the accused having
                     secured his acquittal, the presumption of
                     his innocence is further reinforced,
                     reaffirmed and strengthened by the trial
                     court.(5) If two reasonable conclusions are
                     possible on the basis of the evidence on
                     record, the appellate court should not
                     disturb the finding of acquittal recorded
                     by the trial court."Unless there are substantial and compelling
               reasons, the order of acquittal is not
               required to be reversed in appeal. It has
               been so stated inState of Rajasthan vs.
               Shera Ram(2012) 1 SCC 602."6.2    In     the   case      ofState        of      Goa      V.      Sanjay

         16 as under:"16. From the aforesaid decisions, it is

                the approach of the lower Court is vitiated
                by   some   manifest    illegality and   the
                conclusion arrived at would not be arrived
                at by any reasonable person and, therefore,
                the decision is to be characterized as
                perverse. Merely because two views are
                possible, the Court of appeal would not take
                the view which would upset the judgment
                delivered by the Court below. However, the
                appellate court has a power to review the
                evidence if it is of the view that the
                conclusion arrived at by the Court below is
                perverse and the Court has committed a

                material evidence on record. A duty is cast

         Court in para 4 has held as under:"4. It is not in dispute that the trial
                Court,   on    appreciation    of    oral  and

                underSection 302read withSection 34of
                IPC and awarded RI for life. Since counsel
                for the appellant very much emphasized that
                the    High     Court    has    exceeded   its
                jurisdiction in upsetting the order of
                acquittal into conviction, let us analyze
                the scope and power of the High Court in an
                appeal    filed    against    the    order  of
                acquittal. This Court in a series of
                decisions has repeatedly laid down that as
                the first appellate court the High Court,
                even while dealing with an appeal against

                      proceedings  against  an  offender  who  has settled 
                      his   dispute   with   the   victim   of   the   crime   but   the

               compoundable underSection 320of the Code.49.Section 482of the Code, as its very  language  
               suggests,     saves   the   inherent   power   of   the   High  
               Court   which   it   has   by   virtue   of     it     being     a 
               superior  court  to  prevent  abuse  of  the  process  of 
               any   court   or   otherwise     to   secure   the   ends   of 
               justice. It begins  with  the  words,  'nothing  in 
               this Code' which means that the provision   is   an  
               overriding  provision.   These words leave no manner 
               of doubt that none   of   the   provisions   of   the  
               Code   limits   or   restricts   the   inherent   power.   The 
               guideline for exercise   of   such power is provided 
               inSection 482itself   i.e.,   to   prevent   abuse 
               of  the process of any court or otherwise to secure 
               the ends   of   justice.     As   has been repeatedly 
               stated thatSection  482confers  no  new  powers  
               on     High   Court;   it   merely   safeguards     existing 
               inherent     powers     possessed     by     High   Court 
               necessary   to   prevent   abuse   of   the   process   of   any  
               Court  or  to  secure the ends of justice.   It is 
               equally well settled that the power is  not  to
               be resorted to if there is specific provision in the 
               Code   for   the   redress of the grievance   of   an  
               aggrieved  party.  It  should  be  exercised  very 
               sparingly and it should not be exercised as against  
               the   express   bar     of     law   engrafted   in   any   other 
               provision of the Code.50. In different situations, the inherent power may 
               be   exercised     in   different   ways   to   achieve   its 
               ultimate objective. Formation   of   opinion   by the 
               High   Court   before   it   exercises     inherent     power  
               underSection     482on   either   of   the   twin 
               objectives, (i) to prevent abuse of the  process of  
               any court or (ii) to secure the ends of justice, is 
               a sine qua non.51. In the very nature of   its   constitution,   it 
               is   the   judicial obligation of the High Court to 
               undo a wrong in course of administration  of justice 
               or to prevent continuation of unnecessary judicial 
               process. This  is founded on the legal maxim quando  
               lex aliquid  alicui  concedit, concedituret id sine  
               qua res ipsa esse non  potest. The  full  import  of  
               which     is   whenever   anything   is   authorised,   and 
               especially if, as  a  matter  of duty,required to be 
               done   by   law,   it   is   found   impossible   to   do   that 
               thing     unless   something   else   not   authorised   in 
               express terms be also    done,   may also   be done, 
               then   that   something   else   will   be   supplied     by 
               necessary       intendment.   Ex   debito   justitiae   is 
               inbuilt in such exercise; the whole idea  is  to  do  
               real, complete and substantial justice   for   whichPage 3 of 7HC-NIC                           Page 3 of 7      Created On Sun Jun 19 04:13:12 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/14107/2016                                               ORDER


               it  exists.  The  power possessed by the High Court  
               underSection   482of the   Code   is   of   wide  
               amplitude but requires exercise with great caution 
               and circumspection.52.     It   needs   no   emphasis   that   exercise     of 
               inherent   power   by   the High Court would entirely 
               depend on the  facts  and  circumstances  of  each
               case.   It   is   neither   permissible   nor     proper     for 
               the     court     to     provide     a   straitjacket   formula 
               regulating     the     exercise     of     inherent     powers 
               underSection   482.   No   precise   and   inflexible 
               guidelines can also be provided.53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on 
               the  ground  of settlement between  an offender  and 
               victim  is  not  the  same  thing as compounding  of  
               offence.     They     are     different   and     not  
               interchangeable.   Strictly   speaking,   the   power   of 
               compounding of offences   given   to   a court underSection   320is   materially   different   from     the  
               quashing  of  criminal proceedings by the High Court 
               in   exercise   of   its   inherent   jurisdiction.     In  
               compounding of offences, power of a criminal court 
               is  circumscribed    by    the  provisions  contained  inSection 320and  the  court  is  guided  solely  and  
               squarely   thereby   while,   on   the   other   hand,   the 
               formation   of   opinion     by     the   High   Court   for  
               quashing     a       criminal     offence     or     criminal 
               proceeding   or criminal complaint is guided by the 
               material on record   as   to   whether   the ends of 
               justice   would   justify   such   exercise   of   power 
               although  the  ultimate consequence may be acquittal 
               or dismissal of indictment.54.  Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding  
               having regard  to the fact that dispute between the  
               offender  and   victim  has   been  settled although  
               offences are not compoundable,  it  does  so  as  in  
               its   opinion,continuation of   criminal proceedings 
               will  be an exercise in  futility  and
               justice in the case demands that the dispute between 
               the   parties   is     put     to   an   end   and   peace   is 
               restored;  securing  the  ends  of  justice  being 
               the ultimate guiding factor. No  doubt,  crimes  are 
               acts  which  have  harmful effect on the public and  
               consist in wrong  doing  that  seriously  endangers 
               and threatens  well­being  of  society  and  it  is not 
               safe to leave   the   crime­doer only because he and 
               the victim have settled  the  dispute  amicably  or  
               that   the   victim   has   been   paid   compensation,   yet  
               certain     crimes     have     been   made   compoundable   in 
               law, with or  without  permission  of  the  Court.  
               In respect of serious offences  like  murder,  rape,Page 4 of 7HC-NIC                           Page 4 of 7      Created On Sun Jun 19 04:13:12 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/14107/2016                                               ORDER


               dacoity,  etc;  or  other
               offences of mental depravity underIPCor offences 
               of moral turpitude   under special   statutes,   likePrevention  of  Corruption  Actor  the  offences
               committed by public servants while working in that 
               capacity,   the     settlement   between   offender   and 
               victim   can   have   no   legal   sanction     at     all. 
               However,certain   offences   which   overwhelmingly   and 
               predominantly bear  civil  flavour having arisen out 
               of   civil,   mercantile,   commercial,     financial, 
               partnership  or   such     like     transactions     or     the 
               offences  arising  out  of  matrimony, particularly  
               relating to dowry, etc.  or  the   family  dispute,  
               where     the   wrong   is   basically   to   victim   and   the 
               offender   and   victim     have     settled     all   disputes 
               between them amicably, irrespective of the fact that 
               such  offences have not been made compoundable, the  
               High Court may within the framework  of its inherent 
               power,   quash   the   criminal   proceeding   or   criminal 
               complaint   or F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the 
               face   of   such   settlement,   there   is hardly any 
               likelihood of offender being convicted and by   not 
               quashing  the criminal proceedings, justice shall be 
               casualty and   ends of justice   shall be defeated. 
               The above list is illustrative and not exhaustive. 
               Each  case will depend on  its  own  facts  and  no 
               hard  and  fast  category  can  be prescribed.57.   The   position   that   emerges   from   the   above 
               discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the  
               High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR  
               or   complaint   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
               jurisdiction   is   distinct   and   different   from   the 
               power given to a criminal court for compounding the  
               offences   under   Section   320   of   the   Code.   Inherent 
               power   is   of   wide   plenitude   with   no   statutory 
               limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with 
               the guideline  engrafted  in  such  power  viz;  (i)  to 
               secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse  
               of the process of any Court. In what cases power to 
               quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R 
               may be exercised where the offender and victim have  
               settled their dispute would depend on the facts and  
               circumstances  of  each  case  and  no category  can  be 
               prescribed. However, before exercise of such power, 
               the High Court must have due regard to the nature 
               and   gravity   of   the   crime.   Heinous   and   serious  
               offences   of   mental   depravity   or   offences   like 
               murder,   rape,   dacoity,   etc.   cannot   be   fittingly 
               quashed even though the victim or victims family and 
               the offender have settled the dispute. Such offences 
               are not private in nature and have serious impact on 
               society.   Similarly,   any   compromise   between   the 
               victim   and   offender   in   relation   to   the   offencesPage 5 of 7HC-NIC                           Page 5 of 7      Created On Sun Jun 19 04:13:12 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/14107/2016                                              ORDER


                     under special statutes likePrevention of Corruption 
                     Actor   the   offences   committed   by   public   servants 
                     while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide 
                     for   any   basis   for   quashing   criminal   proceedings 
                     involving   such   offences.   But   the   criminal   cases 
                     having   overwhelmingly   and   predominatingly   civil 
                     flavour stand on different footing for the purposes 
                     of quashing, particularly the offences arising from 
                     commercial,   financial,   mercantile,   civil, 
                     partnership   or   such   like   transactions   or   the 
                     offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, 
                     etc.   or   the   family   disputes   where   the   wrong   is 
                     basically   private   or   personal   in   nature   and   the  
                     parties have resolved their entire dispute. In this 
                     category   of   cases,   High   Court   may   quash   criminal 
                     proceedings   if   in   its   view,   because   of   the 
                     compromise   between   the   offender   and   victim,   the 
                     possibility   of   conviction   is   remote   and   bleak   and 
                     continuation of criminal case would put accused to 
                     great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice 
                     would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal  
                     case   despite   full   and   complete   settlement   and 
                     compromise with the victim. In other words, the High 
                     Court  must  consider  whether  it  would  be unfair  or 
                     contrary to the interest of justice to continue with 
                     the   criminal   proceeding   or   continuation   of   the 
                     criminal   proceeding   would   tantamount   to   abuse   of 
                     process   of   law   despite   settlement   and   compromise 
                     between   the   victim   and   wrongdoer   and   whether   to  
                     secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that 
                     criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to  
                     the   above   question(s)   is   in   affirmative,   the   High 
                     Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash 
                     the criminal proceeding."Resultantly, this petition is allowed. The FIR

                    compoundable underSection 320of the Code.49.Section 482of the Code, as its very  language  
                    suggests,     saves   the   inherent   power   of   the   High  
                    Court   which   it   has   by   virtue   of     it     being     a 
                    superior  court  to  prevent  abuse  of  the  process  of 
                    any   court   or   otherwise     to   secure   the   ends   of 
                    justice. It begins  with  the  words,  'nothing  in 
                    this Code' which means that the provision   is   an  
                    overriding  provision.   These words leave no manner 
                    of doubt that none   of   the   provisions   of   the  
                    Code   limits   or   restricts   the   inherent   power.   The 
                    guideline for exercise   of   such power is provided 
                    inSection 482itself   i.e.,   to   prevent   abuse 
                    of  the process of any court or otherwise to secure 
                    the ends   of   justice.     As   has been repeatedly 
                    stated thatSection  482confers  no  new  powers  
                    on     High   Court;   it   merely   safeguards     existing 
                    inherent     powers     possessed     by     High   Court 
                    necessary   to   prevent   abuse   of   the   process   of   any  
                    Court  or  to  secure the ends of justice.   It is 
                    equally well settled that the power is  not  to
                    be resorted to if there is specific provision in the 
                    Code   for   the   redress of the grievance   of   an  
                    aggrieved  party.  It  should  be  exercised  very 
                    sparingly and it should not be exercised as against  
                    the   express   bar     of     law   engrafted   in   any   other 
                    provision of the Code.50. In different situations, the inherent power may 
                    be   exercised     in   different   ways   to   achieve   its 
                    ultimate objective. Formation   of   opinion   by the 
                    High   Court   before   it   exercises     inherent     power  
                    underSection     482on   either   of   the   twin 
                    objectives, (i) to prevent abuse of the  process of  
                    any court or (ii) to secure the ends of justice, is 
                    a sine qua non.51. In the very nature of   its   constitution,   it 
                    is   the   judicial obligation of the High Court to 
                    undo a wrong in course of administration  of justice 
                    or to prevent continuation of unnecessary judicial 
                    process. This  is founded on the legal maxim quando  
                    lex aliquid  alicui  concedit, concedituret id sinePage 3 of 7HC-NIC                                Page 3 of 7      Created On Thu Apr 28 00:28:57 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/2488/2016                                               ORDER


              qua res ipsa esse non  potest. The  full  import  of  
              which     is   whenever   anything   is   authorised,   and 
              especially if, as  a  matter  of duty,required to be 
              done   by   law,   it   is   found   impossible   to   do   that 
              thing     unless   something   else   not   authorised   in 
              express terms be also    done,   may also   be done, 
              then   that   something   else   will   be   supplied     by 
              necessary       intendment.   Ex   debito   justitiae   is 
              inbuilt in such exercise; the whole idea  is  to  do  
              real, complete and substantial justice   for   which 
              it  exists.  The  power possessed by the High Court  
              underSection   482of the   Code   is   of   wide  
              amplitude but requires exercise with great caution 
              and circumspection.52.     It   needs   no   emphasis   that   exercise     of 
              inherent   power   by   the High Court would entirely 
              depend on the  facts  and  circumstances  of  each
              case.   It   is   neither   permissible   nor     proper     for 
              the     court     to     provide     a   straitjacket   formula 
              regulating     the     exercise     of     inherent     powers 
              underSection   482.   No   precise   and   inflexible 
              guidelines can also be provided.53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on 
              the  ground  of settlement between  an offender  and 
              victim  is  not  the  same  thing as compounding  of  
              offence.     They     are     different   and     not  
              interchangeable.   Strictly   speaking,   the   power   of 
              compounding of offences   given   to   a court underSection   320is   materially   different   from     the  
              quashing  of  criminal proceedings by the High Court 
              in   exercise   of   its   inherent   jurisdiction.     In  
              compounding of offences, power of a criminal court 
              is  circumscribed    by    the  provisions  contained  inSection 320and  the  court  is  guided  solely  and  
              squarely   thereby   while,   on   the   other   hand,   the 
              formation   of   opinion     by     the   High   Court   for  
              quashing     a       criminal     offence     or     criminal 
              proceeding   or criminal complaint is guided by the 
              material on record   as   to   whether   the ends of 
              justice   would   justify   such   exercise   of   power 
              although  the  ultimate consequence may be acquittal 
              or dismissal of indictment.54.  Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding  
              having regard  to the fact that dispute between the  
              offender  and   victim  has   been  settled although  
              offences are not compoundable,  it  does  so  as  in  
              its   opinion,continuation of   criminal proceedings 
              will  be an exercise in  futility  and
              justice in the case demands that the dispute between 
              the   parties   is     put     to   an   end   and   peace   is 
              restored;  securing  the  ends  of  justice  beingPage 4 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 4 of 7      Created On Thu Apr 28 00:28:57 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/2488/2016                                               ORDER


              the ultimate guiding factor. No  doubt,  crimes  are 
              acts  which  have  harmful effect on the public and  
              consist in wrong  doing  that  seriously  endangers 
              and threatens  well­being  of  society  and  it  is not 
              safe to leave   the   crime­doer only because he and 
              the victim have settled  the  dispute  amicably  or  
              that   the   victim   has   been   paid   compensation,   yet  
              certain     crimes     have     been   made   compoundable   in 
              law, with or  without  permission  of  the  Court.  
              In respect of serious offences  like  murder,  rape, 
              dacoity,  etc;  or  other
              offences of mental depravity underIPCor offences 
              of moral turpitude   under special   statutes,   likePrevention  of  Corruption  Actor  the  offences
              committed by public servants while working in that 
              capacity,   the     settlement   between   offender   and 
              victim   can   have   no   legal   sanction     at     all. 
              However,certain   offences   which   overwhelmingly   and 
              predominantly bear  civil  flavour having arisen out 
              of   civil,   mercantile,   commercial,     financial, 
              partnership  or   such     like     transactions     or     the 
              offences  arising  out  of  matrimony, particularly  
              relating to dowry, etc.  or  the   family  dispute,  
              where     the   wrong   is   basically   to   victim   and   the 
              offender   and   victim     have     settled     all   disputes 
              between them amicably, irrespective of the fact that 
              such  offences have not been made compoundable, the  
              High Court may within the framework  of its inherent 
              power,   quash   the   criminal   proceeding   or   criminal 
              complaint   or F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the 
              face   of   such   settlement,   there   is hardly any 
              likelihood of offender being convicted and by   not 
              quashing  the criminal proceedings, justice shall be 
              casualty and   ends of justice   shall be defeated. 
              The above list is illustrative and not exhaustive. 
              Each  case will depend on  its  own  facts  and  no 
              hard  and  fast  category  can  be prescribed.57.   The   position   that   emerges   from   the   above 
              discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the  
              High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR  
              or   complaint   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
              jurisdiction   is   distinct   and   different   from   the 
              power given to a criminal court for compounding the  
              offences   under   Section   320   of   the   Code.   Inherent 
              power   is   of   wide   plenitude   with   no   statutory 
              limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with 
              the guideline  engrafted  in  such  power  viz;  (i)  to 
              secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse  
              of the process of any Court. In what cases power to 
              quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R 
              may be exercised where the offender and victim have  
              settled their dispute would depend on the facts and  
              circumstances  of  each  case  and  no category  can  bePage 5 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 5 of 7      Created On Thu Apr 28 00:28:57 IST 2016
                R/SCR.A/2488/2016                                              ORDER


                    prescribed. However, before exercise of such power, 
                    the High Court must have due regard to the nature 
                    and   gravity   of   the   crime.   Heinous   and   serious  
                    offences   of   mental   depravity   or   offences   like 
                    murder,   rape,   dacoity,   etc.   cannot   be   fittingly 
                    quashed even though the victim or victims family and 
                    the offender have settled the dispute. Such offences 
                    are not private in nature and have serious impact on 
                    society.   Similarly,   any   compromise   between   the 
                    victim   and   offender   in   relation   to   the   offences 
                    under special statutes likePrevention of Corruption 
                    Actor   the   offences   committed   by   public   servants 
                    while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide 
                    for   any   basis   for   quashing   criminal   proceedings 
                    involving   such   offences.   But   the   criminal   cases 
                    having   overwhelmingly   and   predominatingly   civil 
                    flavour stand on different footing for the purposes 
                    of quashing, particularly the offences arising from 
                    commercial,   financial,   mercantile,   civil, 
                    partnership   or   such   like   transactions   or   the 
                    offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, 
                    etc.   or   the   family   disputes   where   the   wrong   is 
                    basically   private   or   personal   in   nature   and   the  
                    parties have resolved their entire dispute. In this 
                    category   of   cases,   High   Court   may   quash   criminal 
                    proceedings   if   in   its   view,   because   of   the 
                    compromise   between   the   offender   and   victim,   the 
                    possibility   of   conviction   is   remote   and   bleak   and 
                    continuation of criminal case would put accused to 
                    great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice 
                    would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal  
                    case   despite   full   and   complete   settlement   and 
                    compromise with the victim. In other words, the High 
                    Court  must  consider  whether  it  would  be unfair  or 
                    contrary to the interest of justice to continue with 
                    the   criminal   proceeding   or   continuation   of   the 
                    criminal   proceeding   would   tantamount   to   abuse   of 
                    process   of   law   despite   settlement   and   compromise 
                    between   the   victim   and   wrongdoer   and   whether   to  
                    secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that 
                    criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to  
                    the   above   question(s)   is   in   affirmative,   the   High 
                    Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash 
                    the criminal proceeding."Resultantly, this petition is allowed. The FIR

         MS BHAVINI C SHUKLA, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1

                                         ORAL ORDER1.      By present application, the applicant-informant seeks to quash

         and set aside the order dated 5.5.2016 passed by the learned Second

         Additional Sessions Judge Kheda at Nadiad in Criminal Miscellaneous

         Application No. 223 of 2016 granting bail to respondent No.2 -

         accused No.1 in connection with the FIR at annexure B registered

         with Mahudha Police Station Mahudha District Kheda for the offence

         undersection 143,147,148,149,302,323,324,504and506(2)of

         the Indian Penal Code read withsec. 135(1)of the Gujarat Police Act

         and to cancel the bail granted to respondent no.2 and to direct him toPage 1 of 12HC-NIC                                    Page 1 of 12     Created On Wed Jul 06 01:52:15 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13054/2016                                            ORDER



         surrender forthwith.2.    Learned advocate for the applicant submitted that after the

         case was committed to the Court of Session in connection with the

         FIR in question, trial of the sessions case no.115 of 2014 had

         commenced and four witnesses, i.e. complainant and three Doctors

         have been examined as Prosecution Witnesses and in the midst of

         trial, the respondent No.2 who is the main accused and responsible to

         cause murder of the deceased Mohammad@ Abdul Raheman Malek

         moved an application for bail under section 439 of the Code and his

         application for bail is allowed by the learned Judge on totally

         irrelevant consideration and ignoring the evidence collected against

         him by the investigating agency. Learned Advocate for the applicant

         submitted that as per the PM Report, it was on account of injury

         inflicted by the applicant with dagger on the chest of the deceased,

         the deceased lost his life and the respondent No.2                  having played

         vital role in causing death of the deceased, was not entitled to be

         released on bail especially when the co-accused who was alleged to

         have played lesser role was denied bail by this Court.3.    Respondent No.2 though served with the notice of rule has

         chosen not to appear before the Court.4.    Learned Public Prosecutor Mr. Amin appearing with the learned

         Addl. PP Ms. Bhatt for the respondent State submitted that there is

         ample evidence collected by the investigating agency to establish

         that the respondent no.2 inflicted injury on the chest of the deceasedPage 2 of 12HC-NIC                                Page 2 of 12     Created On Wed Jul 06 01:52:15 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13054/2016                                            ORDER



         with dagger. Mr. Amin took the Court to the column 17 of the PM

         Report to point out seriousness of the injury caused by dagger used

         by the respondent no.2 to the deceased. Mr. Amin submitted that

         when the presence of respondent no.2 was established and when it

         was found from the evidence collected by the Investigating Agency

         that the respondent no.2 had inflicted serious blow with dagger on

         the chest of the deceased which resulted into death of the deceased,

         there was no question of exercise of the discretion under section 439

         of the Code by the learned Judge to release the respondent no.2 on

         bail especially when the trial has commenced and the prosecution

         has started examining the witnesses.Mr.Amin submitted that the

         learned Judge has taken into consideration extraneous matters for

         releasing respondent no.2 on bail ignoring the fact that the co-

         accused who was alleged to have played lesser role was refused bail

         by this Court and when long time has not passed in trial. Learned P.P.

         thus supports the present application and submitted that in the facts

         of the case, order releasing respondent no.2 passed by the learned

         Judge is illegal and the same is required to be set aside by this Court

         and the bail granted to respondent no.2 is required to be cancelled by

         this court in exercise of the powers under sec.439(2) of the Code.5.    Having heard the learned advocate for the applicant and

         learned P.P., the Court finds that not only the complainant has

         alleged that the respondent no.2 inflicted blow on the chest of the

         deceased with dagger but the say of the complainant is also

         supported by the other witnesses whose statements were recordedPage 3 of 12HC-NIC                                Page 3 of 12     Created On Wed Jul 06 01:52:15 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13054/2016                                            ORDER



         by the investigating agency. They are Abdul Raheman Ahmadmiya,

         Sharifannisha, W/O. Abdulraheman Ahmadmiya Malek, Mohamadhanif

         Ahemadmiya Malek, Gulamnabi Jamalnabi Bin Hasammiya Malek,

         Jayedabibi w/o. Shanifmiya Yusufmiya Shaikh and others. It is

         required to note that a cross complaint being I CR No.43/14 in

         connection with incident allegedly happened at the same time came

         to be lodged by respondent no.2 himself for the offences undersection 323,324,504,506(2)of the Indian Penal Code andsection

         135of the Bombay Police Act against the deceased and the other

         persons alleging assault by the deceased with co-accused on him and

         his other family members with the weapons like iron pipe etc. and in

         this very complaint, respondent no.2 has clearly stated that since his

         father and other family members were being attacked and clothes of

         his mother were being torn, he went to his house and came back with

         weapon like dagger and to save his family members, he had raised

         dagger to create fear in the mind of the deceased but during the

         scuffle the deceased got injury with the said weapon and having

         received injury, he fell down and then other people gathered. By such

         FIR, presence of respondent no.2 could be said to have been

         established at the scene of offence. It needs to be recorded that as

         per the police investigation, respondent no.2 himself went to the

         hospital to take treatment as Out Door Patient and then went to the

         police station. In fact, as per the deposition of the Doctor Vikasbhai

         Vithalbhai Patel at Exh. 28, respondent no.2 was found with abrasion

         on the lips and there was swelling on his lips and he was dischargedPage 4 of 12HC-NIC                                Page 4 of 12     Created On Wed Jul 06 01:52:15 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13054/2016                                                  ORDER



         after giving primary treatment to him and his injuries were stated to

         be simple. So far as the deceased who succumbed to injury received

         by him on his chest, is concerned, his Post Motrum ("PM") report

         reveals following injuries:"A big vertical stab wound on left side of chest 5
                cm left of mid sterna line extending on 34d, 4th 5th
                Intercostal place

                (1) Length of 3 cm long
                (2) Breadth ½ cm broad
                (3) Deepth 4 ½ cm deep
                Elliptical shaped stab wound."6.    The cause of           death as stated in column no.23 of the PM

         Report is as under:"The final Cause of death is haemorrhage shock as a
               result of stab wound over left side of chest
               extending to Heart due to sharp cutting instrument."7.    From the PM Report, it thus appears that the death of the

         deceased was on account of the injuries allegedly inflicted by the

         respondent no.2 with dagger. It needs to be noted that the

         respondent no.2 had not filed any application for bail either before

         the charge sheet or after the charge sheet was submitted but

         preferred   application      for    bail     being         Criminal        Miscellaneous

         Application No. 223 of 2016 through his father on 25.4.2016 after the

         depositions (oral evidence) of four witnesses, 3                      Doctors and the

         complainant were over. It needs to be further recorded that before

         the evidence of the last witness - complainant was being taken, the

         co-accused Taufiqmiya @ Maharaj Vazir Mohammed Malek who was

         alleged to have used sword and caused injuries to injured witnessesPage 5 of 12HC-NIC                                      Page 5 of 12     Created On Wed Jul 06 01:52:15 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13054/2016                                            ORDER



         was refused bail by this Court by not entertaining his the successive

         bail application being Criminal Misc. Application No. 24262 of 2015

         vide order dated 15.1.2016 and in the said order, the Court directed

         to conclude the trial as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a

         period of six months from the date of receipt of the order. Thus, the

         co-accused who was alleged to have played lesser role than the role

         allegedly played by respondent no.2 for offences alleged was though

         denied bail by this Court, the learned Judge decided to grant the bail

         to respondent no.2 by the impugned order. On perusal of the order

         made by the learned Judge for granting bail to respondent no.2,it

         appears that      four main considerations weighed with the learned

         Judge for granting bail to respondent no.2, i.e.. (1) the respondent

         no.2 had never filed any application for bail at any earlier point of

         time. (2) the respondent No.2 has been in custody for the last two

         years and in the cross case in connection with the complaint filed by

         respondent no.2, out of 30 witnesses, eight witnesses were examined

         whereas in connection with the complaint against the respondent

         no.2, out of 59 witnesses, four witnesses have been examined and 54

         witnesses are still to be examined and there is likelihood of taking

         long time for completion of the trial. (3) there is no antecedents of

         respondent No.2. (4) the co-accused in both the cases have been

         released on bail.8.    Learned Judge has also taken into consideration the factum of

         release of respondent no.2 on interim bail three times for short span

         and that no untoward incident was noticed during interim bail. ThisPage 6 of 12HC-NIC                                Page 6 of 12     Created On Wed Jul 06 01:52:15 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13054/2016                                                 ORDER



         Court finds that the above all considerations by the learned Judge

         have no relevance and could be said to be extraneous matters for

         exercising the powers under sec. 439 of the Code in the facts of the

         case. Non-filing of the application for bail by respondent no.2 earlier

         could not be said to be a ground available in law for granting bail

         especially to the accused of serious offence. Passing of two years in

         custody by respondent no.2 is also irrelevant consideration in

         connection with the offence for which the sentence prescribed is of

         life imprisonment. Similarly, for such offence, on the assumption that

         the trial will take long time was also no good consideration for

         exercise of the powers under sec. 439 of the Code especially when no

         long time has passed in the trial and when after this Court issued

         direction in the co-accused's application for bail to conclude the trial

         as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of six months,

         the trial has progressed further by recording evidence of the

         complainant.     It is required to note that               learned Judge has not

         released the respondent no.2 on considering the evidence of any of

         the   prosecution       witnesses     examined          during        trial.     Similarly,

         consideration as regards the respondent No.2 having no antecedents

         was misplaced when he was found involved in the serious offence

         during investigation. Learned Judge                  has also gone wrong in

         observing that almost all co-accused have been released on bail.9.    In such view of the matter, the learned Judge could be said to

         have misdirected himself in releasing the respondent no.2                            on the

         above main considerations. What appears to have further weighedPage 7 of 12HC-NIC                                   Page 7 of 12       Created On Wed Jul 06 01:52:15 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13054/2016                                            ORDER



         with the learned Judge is that the respondent no.2 was released three

         times on interim bail for short span and during such interim release,

         no untoward incident has happened. In the facts of the case, such

         consideration ought not to have weighed with the learned Judge

         especially when the trial has commenced and the complainant's

         evidence was about to be completed and especially when this court

         in the case of co-accused, alleged to have played lesser role than the

         respondent no.2, refused to entertain his application for bail. Judicial

         propriety demanded that when the co-accused allegedly played

         lesser role was not granted bail by this Court even at his third

         successive bail application, learned Judge ought not to have

         entertained the application of respondent no.2.10.In the case ofKalyan Chandra Sarkar vs. Rajesh Ranjan

         Alias Pappu Yadav[(2004)7 SCC 528], the Hon'ble

         Supreme Court has held that mere fact that accused has

         undergone long period of incarceration by itself would not

                     IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

         CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR SUSPENSION OF SENTENCE) NO. 4900 of 2016
                                           In
                             CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 866 of 2014
         ===============================================
                   VIRALBHAI HASMUKHBHAI LOLARIYA & 1....Applicants
                                          Versus
                            STATE OF GUJARAT....Respondent
         ===============================================
         Appearance:
         MR AD SHAH, SENIOR ADVOCATE for the Applicants No. 1 - 2
         MS MAITHILI MEHTA APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ===============================================

              CORAM: HONOURABLE MS.JUSTICE HARSHA DEVANI
                     and
                     HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE G.R.UDHWANI

                                       Date : 08/03/2016

                                         ORAL ORDER(PER : HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE G.R.UDHWANI)

                       RULE. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor Ms. Maithili
         Mehta, waives service of notice of rule on behalf of the respondent.2.            This application prays for bail by suspending the
         sentence undersection 389of the Code of Criminal Procedure (for
         short theCr.PC) imposed in Sessions Case No.11 of 2012 by judgment
         and order dated 11.04.2014 passed by the learned 6th (Ad-hoc),
         Additional District and Sessions Judge, Junagadh inter alia sentencing
         the applicants and others for the various offences underIndian Penal
         Code, includingsections 302and323of the Indian Penal Code (for
         short theIPC).3.            By an order dated 12.10.2014, the appeal came to be
         admitted after condonation of delay in preferring the appeal.4.            Briefly stated, the prosecution case as emerging in the
         charge framed against the accused is that on 01.10.2011, the
         deceased-Ajay Laxmishanker Joshi had eloped with the minorPage 1 of 7HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 7      Created On Fri Mar 11 01:17:25 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/4900/2016                                            ORDER




         daughter of original accused No.1, for which the offence undersections 363and366of the IPC, being I-CR No.386 of 2011 came to
         be registered at Jamnagar City 'B' Division Police Station. The
         accused Nos.3 and 4 went to Junagadh from Jamnagar on 08.10.2011
         in search of the daughter of accused No.1. Deceased-Ajay and the
         daughter of accused No.1 were however found at Chitkhana Chowk at
         Junagadh by accused Nos.3, 4 and 7. The deceased was called by
         accused Nos.3, 4 and 7 and accused No.1 was informed by accused
         No.3 through a mobile phone and called him to Junagadh. All the
         aforesaid three accused, picked up the deceased-Ajay and the
         daughter of accused No.1 on the motorcycle to a secluded place in
         dark and there they were abused and the deceased was beaten.
         Thereafter, the deceased is said to have been taken to house
         belonging to Witness No.31 at Housing Board Block No.L-68/538 and
         therefrom he was taken to Dhoraji Chokdi at about 23:00 hours and in
         the street adjoining Ashwamegh Complex, the deceased was
         assaulted by means of wooden-log and plastic pipe and in the
         meanwhile, the accused Nos.1, 2, 5 and 6 came with the rented
         INDICA Vista Car belonging to accused No.1 alongwith witness No.26,
         between 01:30 and 2:00 a.m., and assaulted Ajay by wooden longs
         and fist and kick blows. Thereafter, the deceased was taken to
         Jamnagar and accused Nos.7 and 8 proceeded to Junagadh and
         deceased, daughter of accused No.1 and all other accused were then
         taken to Jamnagar City 'B' Division Police Station and owing to the
         injuries, the deceased was sent to the hospital for treatment, where
         deceased gave a complaint and ultimately, a case with Junagadh City
         'A' Division Police Station, being I-CR No.188 of 2011 came to be
         registered for the offence punishable underSection 307of the IPC on
         10.10.2011 against the present accused. It was, thus, alleged that
         between 21:00 hours of 08.10.2011 and 07:00 hours of 09.10.2011,
         accused formed unlawful assembly with an intention to abuse andPage 2 of 7HC-NIC                               Page 2 of 7      Created On Fri Mar 11 01:17:25 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/4900/2016                                             ORDER




         threat the deceased with life and to beat him and thus various
         injuries including fracture were caused to him and the deceased was
         abducted from Junagadh to Jamnagar by the accused persons with
         the aid of each other.5.          The learned Counsel for the applicants, Mr.A. D. Shah,
         invited the attention of the court to the complaint (exhibit-15)
         registered at the instance of deceased-Ajay on 09.10.2011 to point
         out that therein the deceased himself did not make any reference to
         the use of weapons for assaulting him, but only referred to the
         assault to him by fist and kick blows. The learned Counsel would
         contend that the deceased was taken to the police station around
         11:00 or 12:00 a.m., on 09.10.2011 and was at the Police Station
         around 03:00 p.m. It was only after the worsening of the physical
         condition of the deceased at the police station after three hours that
         he was taken to the hospital. It was argued that thus the possibility of
         police atrocity during the said period, cannot be ruled out.5.1         The learned Counsel also contended while relying upon
         the evidence on record, that the weapons attributed to the accused
         were admittedly not deadly weapons and looking to their weight and
         density, they were not as heavy as would cause serious injuries and
         one of the weapon was a hollow plastic pipe.                That such weapons
         were not capable of causing serious injuries like fracture. It was
         argued that most of the injuries were simple in nature and,
         admittedly were not on the vital part of the body and injuries
         individually were admittedly not sufficient to cause death of a person
         in the ordinary course of a nature.5.2         Relying upon the evidence of PW 30, Investigating
         Officer, who was also investigating the case lodged against thePage 3 of 7HC-NIC                                Page 3 of 7      Created On Fri Mar 11 01:17:25 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/4900/2016                                            ORDER




         deceased-Ajay, it was pointed out that on the basis of the complaint
         lodged by deceased -Ajay, a yadi was issued to the police station to
         register a case for the offences punishable undersections 323,504and114of the IPC and it being non-cognizable offence and having
         taken place at Junagadh, a yadi was sent to forward the case to
         Junagadh Police Station.6.           Countering the above submissions, the learned Additional
         Public Prosecutor for the respondent referred to the history given by
         the deceased to the doctors being Dr.Aruna (PW 14) and Dr.Kaushal
         (PW 15), wherein the deceased is said to have attributed the use of
         weapons like wooden log, stick, iron pipe and pointed electric wire to
         accused Yagnesh Shashtri, Viral, Nitin, Prince and other two persons
         and it was contended that the applicants and others were proved to
         have mercilessly assaulted the deceased-Ajay to death and that they
         had the motive to do so, since the deceased had eloped with the
         minor daughter of accused No.1.                Learned Additional Public
         Prosecutor would contend that the injuries, if cumulatively taken,
         were sufficient to cause death of a person in the ordinary course of a
         nature as deposed to by the doctors and, thus there was enough
         evidence, on which the trial court has based its findings and the
         accused having involved themselves in a heinous crime are not
         entitled to bail.7.           Having considered the rival submissions and the relevant
         record made available to this court by the learned Counsel for the
         applicants and being mindful of the fact that, at this stage, the court
         is not required to appreciate the evidence threadbare and record the
         conclusion as to the guilt or otherwise of the accused, it would be
         sufficient to state that for the purpose of suspension of the sentence
         and release of the applicants on bail, case is made out; inasmuch as,Page 4 of 7HC-NIC                                Page 4 of 7      Created On Fri Mar 11 01:17:25 IST 2016
                    R/CR.MA/4900/2016                                                        ORDER




         taking the case at the face value, it cannot be disputed that except
         one or two injuries, rest were simple injuries in the nature of
         contusions / abrasions on the non-vital part of the body of the
         deceased. The injury causing to the left ribs No.6, 7, 8 and 9 were,
         however, in the nature of fracture. It is a matter of consideration in
         appeal as to whether death was intended by such injuries or whether
         accused can be attributed with knowledge that by inflicting such
         injuries death was to occur.8.            The Supreme Court in the case ofRamesh Kumar v.
         State of Madhya PradeshwithGopal Prasad v. State of
         Madhya Pradesh, [2010 (6) SCC 685] was confronted with the
         similar situation and observed in paragraph No.12 thus:"12.    We        have      considered         the    rival       submissions         and the

              submissions made by Mr. Dubey commend us. We have extracted in

              the preceding paragraph of our judgment; injuries sustained by the

              deceased and from a perusal thereof it is difficult to hold that the

              appellants intended to cause such bodily injuries which they                               knew

              to      be       likely to      cause          the death. From that it is also not

              imperative that the appellants intended to cause bodily injury which

              is sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death. The

              injuries                                       found                                            on

              the person of the deceased also do not indicate that it is so

              imminently dangerous that it must in all probability cause death or

              such bodily injury is likely to cause death. It has to be borne in                          mind

              that       the      intention of       the           accused        is gathered from the

              nature of the weapon used, the part of the body chosen for assault

              and      other           attending circumstances. Here in the present case

              according                  to             the                  prosecution                      the

              weapon used for commission of the crime is "lathi" and "danda" and

              the part of the body chosen cannot be said to be a vital part of thePage 5 of 7HC-NIC                                         Page 5 of 7          Created On Fri Mar 11 01:17:25 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/4900/2016                                                    ORDER




               body. Further the injuries are contusions. It seems                          that         the

               deceased      was      not   taken         to   the    hospital immediately after

               the occurrence and he died. Perhaps, his life could have been saved

               had he given the medical aid immediately. In view of what we have

               observed above the ingredients for the offence of murder is not made

               out. However, the appellants have caused grievous                             hurt        by

               dangerous       weapon in    furtherance              of   their common intention

               and as such the facts proved make out the offence underSection

               326/34of the Indian Penal Code."9.           In the facts and circumstances discussed herein above,
         one of the questions that may fall for consideration in appeal, may be
         as to whether the accused can be liable to the punishment for the
         offence undersection 302of the IPC. Prima facie, having regard to
         the discussion made above, a doubt does arise as to whether the
         case against the accused undersection 302of the IPC is sustainable.
         Therefore, this court is inclined to exercise its discretion by
         suspending the sentence and admitting the applicants to bail.10.          The application, therefore, succeeds and is allowed
         accordingly. The sentence imposed in Sessions Case No.11 of 2012
         by judgment and order dated 11.04.2014 passed by the learned 6th
         (Ad-hoc), Additional District and Sessions Judge, Junagadh qua the
         applicants herein is hereby ordered to be suspended till the pendency
         of the appeal and the applicants are ordered to be enlarged on
         regular on their executing a personal bond of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees
         twenty thousand only) each subject to the following terms and
         conditions that they shall:(a)    not take undue advantage of their liberty or abuse their
                      liberty;(b)    maintain law and order;Page 6 of 7HC-NIC                                      Page 6 of 7        Created On Fri Mar 11 01:17:25 IST 2016
                      R/CR.MA/4900/2016                                              ORDER




               (c)       surrender their passport, if any, to the lower court, withina week and if they do not possess any passport, then
                         they shall make a declaration to that effect before the
                         trial court;(d)      If during the pendency of the criminal appeal any change
                         in their residential address, permanent or temporary,
                         takes place, then the applicants shall intimate the same
                         to the trial court as well as the concerned Police Station.11.             Bail before the trial court having jurisdiction.12.             However, it is made clear that any observations made
         while deciding these bail application will not affect merits of the case
         at the time of final arguments.13.             Rule is made absolute accordingly.Direct Service is permitted.(HARSHA DEVANI, J.)

         Appearance:
