                                        ORAL ORDERRule returnable today. Learned APP Mr.Ronak
         Rawal waives service of notice of rule for and on
         behalf of the respondent No.1-State.This Criminal Misc. Application is preferred
         underSection 482of Cr.P.C for quashment of
         complaint being FIR No. II-CR No.242 of 2016 is
         registered with Palitana Town Police Station for the
         offences punishable underSections 504,506(2),507and114of the IPC r/w.Section 33and34of the
         Bombay Money Lenders Act, 1946.The petitioner and the                       original complainant-respondent No.2 are present before this Court.Page 1 of 7HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 7      Created On Tue Jun 14 03:00:20 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/12191/2016                                            ORDERAffidavit of the respondent No.2 is brought on
         record.Parties have chosen to settle their disputes on
         the ground that the petitioner does not have any
         criminal antecedents and there is no involvement
         of the        public money or tempering with the
         documents.Upon instructions, Mr. Apurva Kapadia, learned
         advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that
         there are            no criminal antecedents qua the
         petitioner anywhere, not even in                               the District
         Palitana. It was to oblige the complainant and on
         his personal request, money has been given to him
         for cultivation of the crops. He also submits that the
         petitioner does not deal with the money lending
         activity. He further submits that for accused No.2
         and 3, the        complaint was quashed vide its order
         dated 18th March, 2016 passed in Criminal Misc.
         Application No. 6140 of 2016.Learned          advocate       B.N.Limbachiya,                     learned
         advocate appearing for the original complainant-respondent No.2 submits that the complainant has
         no coercion           and has chosen to enter into the
         compromise. The parties have amicably arrived at
         a settle.Page 2 of 7HC-NIC                              Page 2 of 7      Created On Tue Jun 14 03:00:20 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/12191/2016                                                 ORDERBoth the sides have been heard. This Court has
         taken a note of contents of the affidavit and                                         the
         same have been verified by learned APP from the
         complainant.               It appears that out of their own
         volition, they have settled their disputes . In case
         of two other accused also having found that                                           the
         parties had chosen to enter into full and complete
         settlement        out of their own volition and there is
         absence of criminal antecedents of the petitioner.
         No useful purpose is likely to be served                                                   in
         continuing with the proceedings in                                  light of the
         compromise. The court may not continue the luxury
         of litigation, bearing in mind the decision ofGian
         Singh Vs. State of Punjab and Anotherreported
         in 2012 (10)SCC 303. Request of the applicant to
         quash the FIR needs to be acceded to. It is essential
         to reproduce the relevant paragraph for this
         purpose:-"48.The   question   is   with   regard   to   the   inherent 
                     power  of  the  High Court in quashing the criminal  
                     proceedings  against  an  offender  who  has settled 
                     his   dispute   with   the   victim   of   the   crime   but   the 
                     crime  in     which     he   is   allegedly  involved  is   not 
                     compoundable under Section 320 of the Code.49.  Section 482 of the Code, as its very  language  
                     suggests,     saves   the   inherent   power   of   the   High  
                     Court   which   it   has   by   virtue   of     it     being     a 
                     superior  court  to  prevent  abuse  of  the  process  of 
                     any   court   or   otherwise     to   secure   the   ends   of 
                     justice. It begins  with  the  words,  'nothing  in 
                     this Code' which means that the provision   is   anPage 3 of 7HC-NIC                                   Page 3 of 7      Created On Tue Jun 14 03:00:20 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/12191/2016                                               ORDER


               overriding  provision.   These words leave no manner 
               of doubt that none   of   the   provisions   of   the  
               Code   limits   or   restricts   the   inherent   power.   The 
               guideline for exercise   of   such power is provided 
               in Section 482   itself   i.e.,   to   prevent   abuse 
               of  the process of any court or otherwise to secure 
               the ends   of   justice.     As   has been repeatedly 
               stated that Section  482  confers  no  new  powers  
               on     High   Court;   it   merely   safeguards     existing 
               inherent     powers     possessed     by     High   Court 
               necessary   to   prevent   abuse   of   the   process   of   any  
               Court  or  to  secure the ends of justice.   It is 
               equally well settled that the power is  not  to
               be resorted to if there is specific provision in the 
               Code   for   the   redress of the grievance   of   an  
               aggrieved  party.  It  should  be  exercised  very 
               sparingly and it should not be exercised as against  
               the   express   bar     of     law   engrafted   in   any   other 
               provision of the Code.50. In different situations, the inherent power may 
               be   exercised     in   different   ways   to   achieve   its 
               ultimate objective. Formation   of   opinion   by the 
               High   Court   before   it   exercises     inherent     power  
               under     Section     482     on   either   of   the   twin 
               objectives, (i) to prevent abuse of the  process of  
               any court or (ii) to secure the ends of justice, is 
               a sine qua non.51. In the very nature of   its   constitution,   it 
               is   the   judicial obligation of the High Court to 
               undo a wrong in course of administration  of justice 
               or to prevent continuation of unnecessary judicial 
               process. This  is founded on the legal maxim quando  
               lex aliquid  alicui  concedit, concedituret id sine  
               qua res ipsa esse non  potest. The  full  import  of  
               which     is   whenever   anything   is   authorised,   and 
               especially if, as  a  matter  of duty,required to be 
               done   by   law,   it   is   found   impossible   to   do   that 
               thing     unless   something   else   not   authorised   in 
               express terms be also    done,   may also   be done, 
               then   that   something   else   will   be   supplied     by 
               necessary       intendment.   Ex   debito   justitiae   is 
               inbuilt in such exercise; the whole idea  is  to  do  
               real, complete and substantial justice   for   which

              justice. It begins  with  the  words,  'nothing  in 
              this Code' which means that the provision   is   an  
              overriding  provision.   These words leave no manner 
              of doubt that none   of   the   provisions   of   the  
              Code   limits   or   restricts   the   inherent   power.   The 
              guideline for exercise   of   such power is provided 
              inSection 482itself   i.e.,   to   prevent   abuse 
              of  the process of any court or otherwise to secure 
              the ends   of   justice.     As   has been repeatedly 
              stated thatSection  482confers  no  new  powers  
              on     High   Court;   it   merely   safeguards     existing 
              inherent     powers     possessed     by     High   Court 
              necessary   to   prevent   abuse   of   the   process   of   any  
              Court  or  to  secure the ends of justice.   It is 
              equally well settled that the power is  not  to
              be resorted to if there is specific provision in the 
              Code   for   the   redress of the grievance   of   an  
              aggrieved  party.  It  should  be  exercised  very 
              sparingly and it should not be exercised as against  
              the   express   bar     of     law   engrafted   in   any   other 
              provision of the Code.50. In different situations, the inherent power may 
              be   exercised     in   different   ways   to   achieve   its 
              ultimate objective. Formation   of   opinion   by the 
              High   Court   before   it   exercises     inherent     power  
              underSection     482on   either   of   the   twin 
              objectives, (i) to prevent abuse of the  process of  
              any court or (ii) to secure the ends of justice, is 
              a sine qua non.51. In the very nature of   its   constitution,   it 
              is   the   judicial obligation of the High Court to 
              undo a wrong in course of administration  of justice 
              or to prevent continuation of unnecessary judicial 
              process. This  is founded on the legal maxim quando  
              lex aliquid  alicui  concedit, concedituret id sine  
              qua res ipsa esse non  potest. The  full  import  of  
              which     is   whenever   anything   is   authorised,   and 
              especially if, as  a  matter  of duty,required to be 
              done   by   law,   it   is   found   impossible   to   do   that 
              thing     unless   something   else   not   authorised   in 
              express terms be also    done,   may also   be done, 
              then   that   something   else   will   be   supplied     by 
              necessary       intendment.   Ex   debito   justitiae   is 
              inbuilt in such exercise; the whole idea  is  to  do  
              real, complete and substantial justice   for   which 
              it  exists.  The  power possessed by the High Court  
              underSection   482of the   Code   is   of   wide  
              amplitude but requires exercise with great caution 
              and circumspection.52.     It   needs   no   emphasis   that   exercise     of 
              inherent   power   by   the High Court would entirelyPage 3 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 3 of 7      Created On Wed Apr 27 00:27:08 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/9104/2016                                              ORDER


              depend on the  facts  and  circumstances  of  each
              case.   It   is   neither   permissible   nor     proper     for 
              the     court     to     provide     a   straitjacket   formula 
              regulating     the     exercise     of     inherent     powers 
              underSection   482.   No   precise   and   inflexible 
              guidelines can also be provided.53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on 
              the  ground  of settlement between  an offender  and 
              victim  is  not  the  same  thing as compounding  of  
              offence.     They     are     different   and     not  
              interchangeable.   Strictly   speaking,   the   power   of 
              compounding of offences   given   to   a court underSection   320is   materially   different   from     the  
              quashing  of  criminal proceedings by the High Court 
              in   exercise   of   its   inherent   jurisdiction.     In  
              compounding of offences, power of a criminal court 
              is  circumscribed    by    the  provisions  contained  inSection 320and  the  court  is  guided  solely  and  
              squarely   thereby   while,   on   the   other   hand,   the 
              formation   of   opinion     by     the   High   Court   for  
              quashing     a       criminal     offence     or     criminal 
              proceeding   or criminal complaint is guided by the 
              material on record   as   to   whether   the ends of 
              justice   would   justify   such   exercise   of   power 
              although  the  ultimate consequence may be acquittal 
              or dismissal of indictment.54.  Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding  
              having regard  to the fact that dispute between the  
              offender  and   victim  has   been  settled although  
              offences are not compoundable,  it  does  so  as  in  
              its   opinion,continuation of   criminal proceedings 
              will  be an exercise in  futility  and
              justice in the case demands that the dispute between 
              the   parties   is     put     to   an   end   and   peace   is 
              restored;  securing  the  ends  of  justice  being 
              the ultimate guiding factor. No  doubt,  crimes  are 
              acts  which  have  harmful effect on the public and  
              consist in wrong  doing  that  seriously  endangers 
              and threatens  well­being  of  society  and  it  is not 
              safe to leave   the   crime­doer only because he and 
              the victim have settled  the  dispute  amicably  or  
              that   the   victim   has   been   paid   compensation,   yet  
              certain     crimes     have     been   made   compoundable   in 
              law, with or  without  permission  of  the  Court.  
              In respect of serious offences  like  murder,  rape, 
              dacoity,  etc;  or  other
              offences of mental depravity underIPCor offences 
              of moral turpitude   under special   statutes,   likePrevention  of  Corruption  Actor  the  offences
              committed by public servants while working in that 
              capacity,   the     settlement   between   offender   and 
              victim   can   have   no   legal   sanction     at     all.Page 4 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 4 of 7      Created On Wed Apr 27 00:27:08 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/9104/2016                                              ORDERHowever,certain   offences   which   overwhelmingly   and 
              predominantly bear  civil  flavour having arisen out 
              of   civil,   mercantile,   commercial,     financial, 
              partnership  or   such     like     transactions     or     the 
              offences  arising  out  of  matrimony, particularly  
              relating to dowry, etc.  or  the   family  dispute,  
              where     the   wrong   is   basically   to   victim   and   the 
              offender   and   victim     have     settled     all   disputes 
              between them amicably, irrespective of the fact that 
              such  offences have not been made compoundable, the  
              High Court may within the framework  of its inherent 
              power,   quash   the   criminal   proceeding   or   criminal 
              complaint   or F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the 
              face   of   such   settlement,   there   is hardly any 
              likelihood of offender being convicted and by   not 
              quashing  the criminal proceedings, justice shall be 
              casualty and   ends of justice   shall be defeated. 
              The above list is illustrative and not exhaustive. 
              Each  case will depend on  its  own  facts  and  no 
              hard  and  fast  category  can  be prescribed.57.   The   position   that   emerges   from   the   above 
              discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the  
              High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR  
              or   complaint   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
              jurisdiction   is   distinct   and   different   from   the 
              power given to a criminal court for compounding the  
              offences   under   Section   320   of   the   Code.   Inherent 
              power   is   of   wide   plenitude   with   no   statutory 
              limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with 
              the guideline  engrafted  in  such  power  viz;  (i)  to 
              secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse  
              of the process of any Court. In what cases power to 
              quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R 
              may be exercised where the offender and victim have  
              settled their dispute would depend on the facts and  
              circumstances  of  each  case  and  no category  can  be 
              prescribed. However, before exercise of such power, 
              the High Court must have due regard to the nature 
              and   gravity   of   the   crime.   Heinous   and   serious  
              offences   of   mental   depravity   or   offences   like 
              murder,   rape,   dacoity,   etc.   cannot   be   fittingly 
              quashed even though the victim or victims family and 
              the offender have settled the dispute. Such offences

              society.   Similarly,   any   compromise   between   the 
              victim   and   offender   in   relation   to   the   offences 
              under special statutes likePrevention of Corruption 
              Actor   the   offences   committed   by   public   servants 
              while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide 
              for   any   basis   for   quashing   criminal   proceedings 
              involving   such   offences.   But   the   criminal   cases 
              having   overwhelmingly   and   predominatingly   civil 
              flavour stand on different footing for the purposesPage 5 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 5 of 7      Created On Wed Apr 27 00:27:08 IST 2016

                                     ORAL JUDGMENT(PER : HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE KS JHAVERI)1.    The appellant - original accused was inter alia sentenced
         to undergo life imprisonment and was directed to pay fine of

         Panchmahal at Godhra.2.    The brief matrix of the prosecution case as disclosed
         during the trial is that there existed a property dispute
         between the deceased and the accused.                      On 08.08.2009, the
         deceased had gone to the forest as he worked as a watchman
         in the Bakor Forest range. While the deceased was sleeping
         on the ground in the forest, he felt someone pour kerosene on

         him ablaze. The accused and one Reva Reshma who was also
         present along with the accused at the scene of offence ran

         entered his house and his family members poured water on
         him and thereafter took him to hospital.2.1   A complaint         in respect          of the      said      incident        was
         registered with Khanpur Police Station being C.R. I-No. 65 ofPage 2 of 11HC-NIC                                  Page 2 of 11     Created On Wed May 04 00:12:05 IST 2016

         was carried out and chargesheet was submitted against the

         Punjab and Another reported in 2012 (10)SCC303.    Request of the applicant to quash the FIR
         needs to be acceded to. It is essential to reproduce
         the relevant paragraph for this purpose:-"48.The   question   is   with   regard   to   the   inherent 
                     power  of  the  High Court in quashing the criminal  
                     proceedings  against  an  offender  who  has settled 
                     his   dispute   with   the   victim   of   the   crime   but   the

                     compoundable underSection 320of the Code.49.Section 482of the Code, as its very  language  
                     suggests,     saves   the   inherent   power   of   the   High  
                     Court   which   it   has   by   virtue   of     it     being     a 
                     superior  court  to  prevent  abuse  of  the  process  of 
                     any   court   or   otherwise     to   secure   the   ends   of 
                     justice. It begins  with  the  words,  'nothing  in 
                     this Code' which means that the provision   is   an  
                     overriding  provision.   These words leave no manner 
                     of doubt that none   of   the   provisions   of   the  
                     Code   limits   or   restricts   the   inherent   power.   The 
                     guideline for exercise   of   such power is provided 
                     inSection 482itself   i.e.,   to   prevent   abuse 
                     of  the process of any court or otherwise to secure 
                     the ends   of   justice.     As   has been repeatedly 
                     stated thatSection  482confers  no  new  powers  
                     on     High   Court;   it   merely   safeguards     existing 
                     inherent     powers     possessed     by     High   Court 
                     necessary   to   prevent   abuse   of   the   process   of   any  
                     Court  or  to  secure the ends of justice.   It is 
                     equally well settled that the power is  not  to
                     be resorted to if there is specific provision in the 
                     Code   for   the   redress of the grievance   of   an  
                     aggrieved  party.  It  should  be  exercised  very 
                     sparingly and it should not be exercised as against  
                     the   express   bar     of     law   engrafted   in   any   other 
                     provision of the Code.50. In different situations, the inherent power may 
                     be   exercised     in   different   ways   to   achieve   its 
                     ultimate objective. Formation   of   opinion   by the 
                     High   Court   before   it   exercises     inherent     power  
                     underSection     482on   either   of   the   twin 
                     objectives, (i) to prevent abuse of the  process of  
                     any court or (ii) to secure the ends of justice, is 
                     a sine qua non.51.     In the very nature of   its   constitution,   itPage 3 of 7HC-NIC                                 Page 3 of 7      Created On Wed Apr 27 01:58:59 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/9609/2016                                              ORDER


              is   the   judicial obligation of the High Court to 
              undo a wrong in course of administration  of justice 
              or to prevent continuation of unnecessary judicial 
              process. This  is founded on the legal maxim quando  
              lex aliquid  alicui  concedit, concedituret id sine  
              qua res ipsa esse non  potest. The  full  import  of  
              which     is   whenever   anything   is   authorised,   and 
              especially if, as  a  matter  of duty,required to be 
              done   by   law,   it   is   found   impossible   to   do   that 
              thing     unless   something   else   not   authorised   in 
              express terms be also    done,   may also   be done, 
              then   that   something   else   will   be   supplied     by 
              necessary       intendment.   Ex   debito   justitiae   is 
              inbuilt in such exercise; the whole idea  is  to  do  
              real, complete and substantial justice   for   which 
              it  exists.  The  power possessed by the High Court  
              underSection   482of the   Code   is   of   wide  
              amplitude but requires exercise with great caution 
              and circumspection.52.     It   needs   no   emphasis   that   exercise     of 
              inherent   power   by   the High Court would entirely 
              depend on the  facts  and  circumstances  of  each
              case.   It   is   neither   permissible   nor     proper     for 
              the     court     to     provide     a   straitjacket   formula 
              regulating     the     exercise     of     inherent     powers 
              underSection   482.   No   precise   and   inflexible 
              guidelines can also be provided.53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on 
              the  ground  of settlement between  an offender  and 
              victim  is  not  the  same  thing as compounding  of  
              offence.     They     are     different   and     not  
              interchangeable.   Strictly   speaking,   the   power   of 
              compounding of offences   given   to   a court underSection   320is   materially   different   from     the  
              quashing  of  criminal proceedings by the High Court 
              in   exercise   of   its   inherent   jurisdiction.     In  
              compounding of offences, power of a criminal court 
              is  circumscribed    by    the  provisions  contained  inSection 320and  the  court  is  guided  solely  and  
              squarely   thereby   while,   on   the   other   hand,   the 
              formation   of   opinion     by     the   High   Court   for  
              quashing     a       criminal     offence     or     criminal 
              proceeding   or criminal complaint is guided by the 
              material on record   as   to   whether   the ends of 
              justice   would   justify   such   exercise   of   power 
              although  the  ultimate consequence may be acquittal 
              or dismissal of indictment.54.  Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding  
              having regard  to the fact that dispute between the  
              offender  and   victim  has   been  settled although  
              offences are not compoundable,  it  does  so  as  inPage 4 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 4 of 7      Created On Wed Apr 27 01:58:59 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/9609/2016                                              ORDER


              its   opinion,continuation of   criminal proceedings 
              will  be an exercise in  futility  and
              justice in the case demands that the dispute between 
              the   parties   is     put     to   an   end   and   peace   is 
              restored;  securing  the  ends  of  justice  being 
              the ultimate guiding factor. No  doubt,  crimes  are

              consist in wrong  doing  that  seriously  endangers 
              and threatens  well­being  of  society  and  it  is not

              that   the   victim   has   been   paid   compensation,   yet  
              certain     crimes     have     been   made   compoundable   in 
              law, with or  without  permission  of  the  Court.  
              In respect of serious offences  like  murder,  rape, 
              dacoity,  etc;  or  other
              offences of mental depravity underIPCor offences 
              of moral turpitude   under special   statutes,   likePrevention  of  Corruption  Actor  the  offences
              committed by public servants while working in that

              predominantly bear  civil  flavour having arisen out

              offender   and   victim     have     settled     all   disputes

              such  offences have not been made compoundable, the

              quashing  the criminal proceedings, justice shall be 
              casualty and   ends of justice   shall be defeated. 
              The above list is illustrative and not exhaustive. 
              Each  case will depend on  its  own  facts  and  no 
              hard  and  fast  category  can  be prescribed.57.   The   position   that   emerges   from   the   above 
              discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the  
              High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR  
              or   complaint   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
              jurisdiction   is   distinct   and   different   from   the 
              power given to a criminal court for compounding the  
              offences   under   Section   320   of   the   Code.   Inherent 
              power   is   of   wide   plenitude   with   no   statutory 
              limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with 
              the guideline  engrafted  in  such  power  viz;  (i)  to 
              secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abusePage 5 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 5 of 7      Created On Wed Apr 27 01:58:59 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/9609/2016                                             ORDER


              of the process of any Court. In what cases power to 
              quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R 
              may be exercised where the offender and victim have  
              settled their dispute would depend on the facts and  
              circumstances  of  each  case  and  no category  can  be 
              prescribed. However, before exercise of such power, 
              the High Court must have due regard to the nature 
              and   gravity   of   the   crime.   Heinous   and   serious  
              offences   of   mental   depravity   or   offences   like

              discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the

              while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide 
              for   any   basis   for   quashing   criminal   proceedings 
              involving   such   offences.   But   the   criminal   cases 
              having   overwhelmingly   and   predominatingly   civil 
              flavour stand on different footing for the purposes 
              of quashing, particularly the offences arising from 
              commercial,   financial,   mercantile,   civil, 
              partnership   or   such   like   transactions   or   the 
              offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, 
              etc.   or   the   family   disputes   where   the   wrong   is 
              basically   private   or   personal   in   nature   and   the  
              parties have resolved their entire dispute. In this 
              category   of   cases,   High   Court   may   quash   criminal 
              proceedings   if   in   its   view,   because   of   the 
              compromise   between   the   offender   and   victim,   the 
              possibility   of   conviction   is   remote   and   bleak   and 
              continuation of criminal case would put accused to 
              great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice 
              would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal  
              case   despite   full   and   complete   settlement   and 
              compromise with the victim. In other words, the High 
              Court  must  consider  whether  it  would  be unfair  or 
              contrary to the interest of justice to continue with 
              the   criminal   proceeding   or   continuation   of   the 
              criminal   proceeding   would   tantamount   to   abuse   of 
              process   of   law   despite   settlement   and   compromise 
              between   the   victim   and   wrongdoer   and   whether   toPage 9 of 10HC-NIC                         Page 9 of 10     Created On Tue Apr 05 02:20:18 IST 2016

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

         ==========================================================
                 DEVABHAI LADHUBHAI JAMOD (KOLI) & 4....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus

         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR EE SAIYED, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 5
         MS.NISHA THAKORE, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                       Date : 22/08/2016


                                        ORAL ORDER1.    The Petitioners are before this Court seeking the 
         quashment   of   the   complaint   being   I­C.R.   No.   89/2011 
         registered   at   Sayla   Police   Station,   District:Surendranagar   for   the   offence   punishable   underSections 363,366,506(2),504and114of the Indian 
         Penal   Code.   The   said   FIR   has   culminated   into   New 
         Sessions   Case   No.97/2012   where   according   to   the 
         learned advocate Mr. E.E. Saiyed for the petitioners, 
         ten   eye­witnesses   have   already   been   examined. 
         According to the learned advocate for the petitioners, 
         almost   all   of   them   have   turned   hostile.   The 
         prosecutrix was aged 17 years and 11 months when she 
         chose  to  elope  with   the  petitioner   no.5   herein.  The 
         other petitioners are the relatives of the petitonerPage 1 of 8HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 8      Created On Thu Aug 25 04:05:00 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/20082/2016                                            ORDER




         no.5   Shri   Jagabhai   Devabhai   Jamod,   who   has   already 
         married   to   the  daughter  of  the   complainant   and   they 
         have a child born out of the said wedlock. The parties 
         are   before   this   Court   seeking  quashment   of   the   said 
         complaint as the petitioner no.5 and prosecutrix have 
         married   and   registration   of   their   marriage   was 
         effected on 13.09.2011. Earlier petition preferred by 
         the petitioner was dismissed for want of prosecution 
         being   Criminal   Misc.   Application   No.   1856   of   2012 
         dated 26.02.2013.2.   This   Court   has   heard   learned   advocates   on   both 
         the   sides   and   also   has   taken   into   consideration  the 
         chronology of the events. The Sessions Case is going 
         on and ten eye­witnesses have been examined. None of 
         the   eye­witnesses   has   spoken   against   the   petitioner 
         No.5   where   the  charges   against   the   petitioner   no.   5 
         are   underSections   363,366,506(2)and114of   the 
         Indian   Penal   Code.   Both  the   petitioner  no.5   and  the 
         prosecutrix   are   happily   leading   their   lives.   The 
         complainant   is   also   not   desirous   to   prosecute   the 
         petitioners any further.3.   At   this   stage   the   decision   of   the   Apex   Court 
         rendered in the case ofJitendra Raghuvanshi and Ors 
         v. Babita  Raghuvanshi  and  Anr.,  reported  in (2013)4 
         SCC 58,  deserves consideration.  In the instant case, 
         it has been noticed that:"11.The   inherent   powers   of   the   High   Court  
                      underSection 482of the Code are wide and 
                      unfettered.   In   B.S.   Joshi   (AIR   2003   SCPage 2 of 8HC-NIC                                Page 2 of 8      Created On Thu Aug 25 04:05:00 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/20082/2016                                            ORDER




              1386   :   2003   AIR   SCW   1824)   (supra),   this 
              Court   has   upheld   the   powers   of   the   High 
              Court   underSection   482to   quash   criminal 
              proceedings   where   dispute   is   of   a   private 
              nature   and   a   compromise   is   entered   into 
              between   the   parties   who   are   willing   to 
              settle   their   differences   amicably.   We   are 
              satisfied that the said decision is directly  
              applicable to the case on hand and the High 
              Court   ought   to   have   quashed   the   criminal 
              proceedings   by   accepting   the   settlement 
              arrived at.12.   In   our   view,   it   is   the   duty   of   the 
              courts   to   encourage   genuine   settlements   of 
              matrimonial disputes, particularly, when the 
              same   are   on   considerable   increase.   Even   if  
              the   offences   are   non­compoundable,   if   they 
              relate to matrimonial disputes and the court  
              is   satisfied   that   the   parties   have   settled  
              the same amicably and without any pressure, 
              we   hold   that   for   the   purpose   of   securing 
              ends   of   justice,Section   320of   the   Code 
              would not be a bar to the exercise of power  
              of   quashing   of   FIR,   complaint   or   the 
              subsequent criminal proceedings.13.   There   has   been   an   outburst   of 
              matrimonial   disputes   in   recent   times.   The 
              institution   of   marriage   occupies   an 
              important place and it has an important role  
              to   play   in   the   society.   Therefore,   every 
              effort should be made in the interest of thePage 3 of 8HC-NIC                        Page 3 of 8      Created On Thu Aug 25 04:05:00 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/20082/2016                                            ORDER




              individuals   in   order   to   enable   them   to 
              settle down in life and live peacefully. If 
              the   parties   ponder   over   their   defaults   and  
              terminate their disputes amicably by mutual 
              agreement   instead   of   fighting   it   out   in   a 
              court   of   law,   in   order   to   do   complete  
              justice   in   the   matrimonial   matters,   the 
              courts should be less hesitant in exercising  
              its extraordinary jurisdiction. It is trite 
              to   state   that   the   power   underSection   482should   be   exercised   sparingly   and   with 
              circumspection   only   when   the   court   is 
              convinced,   on   the   basis   of   material   on 
              record,   that   allowing   the   proceedings   to 
              continue would be an abuse of the process of  
              the   court   or   that   the   ends   of   justice  
              require   that   the   proceedings   ought   to   be 
              quashed. We also make it clear that exercise  
              of   such   power   would   depend   upon   the   facts 
              and circumstances of each case and it has to  
              be   exercised   in   appropriate   cases   in   order  
              to do real and substantial justice  for the 
              administration   of   which   alone   the   courts 
              exist.   It   is   the   duty   of   the   courts   to  
              encourage genuine settlements of matrimonial 
              disputes andSection 482of the Code enables  
              the   High   Court   andArticle   142of   the  
              Constitution enables this Court to pass such  
              orders.14. In   the   light   of   the   above   discussion, 
              we hold that the High Court in exercise ofPage 4 of 8HC-NIC                        Page 4 of 8      Created On Thu Aug 25 04:05:00 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/20082/2016                                            ORDER




                     its   inherent   powers   can   quash   the   criminal  
                     proceedings   or   FIR   or   complaint   in 
                     appropriate cases in order to meet the ends 
                     of justice andSection 320of the Code does 
                     not limit or affect the powers of the High 
                     Court underSection 482of the Code. Under 
                     these   circumstances,   we   set   aside   the  
                     impugned   judgment   of   the   High   Court   dated04.07.2012   passed   in   M.Cr.C.   No.   2877   of 
                     2012   D/­   4­7­2012   (MP)   Reversed   and   quash 
                     the proceedings in Criminal Case No. 4166 of  
                     2011   pending   on   the   file   of   Judicial 
                     Magistrate Class­I, Indore."4.   Apt would be to refer to the decision rendered in 
         the case ofGian Singh v. State of Punjabreported in  
         (2012) 10 SCC 303, whereby it is held that it is the 
         duty   of   the   Courts   to   encourage   genuine   settlements 
         andsection   482of   the   Code   of   Criminal   Procedure, 
         1973, enables the High Court to pass such orders.It 
         would   be   beneficial   to   reproduce   the   relevant 
         observations   and   findings   of   the   Apex   Court   in   the 
         case ofGian Singh(supra), which read as under :"53.   Quashing   of   offence   or   criminal 
                     proceedings   on   the   ground   of   settlement 
                     between   an   offender   and   victim   is   not   the 
                     same   thing   as   compounding   of   offence.   They  
                     are   different   and   not   interchangeable. 
                     Strictly speaking, the power of compounding 
                     of offences given to a court  underSection 
                     320is   materially   different   from   thePage 5 of 8HC-NIC                               Page 5 of 8      Created On Thu Aug 25 04:05:00 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/20082/2016                                            ORDER



              quashing of criminal proceedings by the High 
              Court   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
              jurisdiction.   In   compounding   of   offences, 
              power   of   a   criminal   court   is   circumscribed  
              by   the   provisions   contained   inSection   320and the court is guided solely and squarely 
              thereby   while,   on   the   other   hand,   the 
              formation of opinion by the High Court for 
              quashing   a   criminal   offence   or   criminal 
              proceeding   or   criminal   complaint   is   guided 
              by the material on record as to whether the 
              ends of justice would justify such exercise 
              of   power   although   the   ultimate   consequence 
              may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.54.  Where   High   Court   quashes   a   criminal 
              proceeding   having   regard   to   the   fact   that 
              dispute between the offender and victim has 
              been   settled   although   offences   are   not 
              compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, 
              continuation of criminal proceedings will be 
              an exercise in futility and justice in the 
              case   demands   that   the   dispute   between   the 
              parties   is   put   to   an   end   and   peace   is 
              restored; securing the ends of justice being  
              the   ultimate   guiding   factor.   No   doubt, 
              crimes are acts which have harmful effect on  
              the public  and consist  in wrong  doing that 
              seriously   endangers   and   threatens   wellbeing 
              of society and it is not safe to leave the  
              crime   doer   only   because   he   and   the   victim 
              have   settled   the  dispute   amicably   or   thatPage 6 of 8HC-NIC                        Page 6 of 8      Created On Thu Aug 25 04:05:00 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/20082/2016                                            ORDER




              the   victim   has   been   paid   compensation,   yet  
              certain   crimes   have   been   made   compoundable 
              in   law,   with   or   without   permission   of   the 
              Court.   In   respect   of   serious   offences   like  
              murder,   rape,         dacoity,   etc;   or   other 
              offences   of   mental   depravity   underIPCor 
              offences   of   moral   turpitude   under   special 
              statutes, likePrevention of Corruption Actor the offences committed by public servants  
              while   working   in   that   capacity,   the 
              settlement   between   offender   and   victim   can 
              have   no   legal   sanction   at   all.   However, 
              certain   offences   which   overwhelmingly   and 
              predominantly   bear   civil   flavour   having 
              arisen out of civil, mercantile, commercial, 
              financial,   partnership   or   such   like 
              transactions or the offences arising out of 
              matrimony,   particularly   relating   to   dowry, 
              etc. or the family dispute, where the wrong 
              is basically to victim and the offender and 
              victim   have   settled   all   disputes   between 
              them amicably, irrespective of the fact that  
              such   offences   have   not   been   made 
              compoundable, the High Court may within the 
              framework   of   its   inherent   power,   quash   the  
              criminal proceeding or criminal complaint or 
              F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the face of 
              such   settlement,there   is   hardly   any 
              likelihood   of   offender   being   convicted   and 
              by   not  quashing   the   criminal   proceedings, 
              justice   shall   be   casualty   and   ends   ofPage 7 of 8HC-NIC                        Page 7 of 8      Created On Thu Aug 25 04:05:00 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/20082/2016                                            ORDER




                      justice shall be defeated. The above list is  
                      illustrative   and   not   exhaustive.   Each   case 
                      will depend on its own facts and no hard and 
                      fast category can be prescribed."5.    In   the   light   of   the   development   of   which   the 
         Court has been apprised of, no purpose is likely to be 
         served   to   continue   the   prosecution.   Prosecutrix   was 
         short by one month when she eloped with the petitioner 
         no.5   and   now   with   the   change   of   circumstance   as 
         prosecutrix and the petitioner no.5 are the spouses, 
         all proceedings deserve quashment. The complaint being 
         I­C.R. No. 89/2011 registered at Sayla Police Station, 
         District:   Surendranagar,   therefore,   deserves   to   be 
         quashed with all consequential proceedings.Direct Service permitted.6.    The petition stands disposed of accordingly.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

         needs to be acceded to. It is essential to reproduce

                      suggests,     saves   the   inherent   power   of   the   High

                      this Code' which means that the provision   is   an  
                      overriding  provision.   These words leave no manner 
                      of doubt that none   of   the   provisions   of   the  
                      Code   limits   or   restricts   the   inherent   power.   The 
                      guideline for exercise   of   such power is provided 
                      inSection 482itself   i.e.,   to   prevent   abuse 
                      of  the process of any court or otherwise to secure 
                      the ends   of   justice.     As   has been repeatedly 
                      stated thatSection  482confers  no  new  powers  
                      on     High   Court;   it   merely   safeguards     existing 
                      inherent     powers     possessed     by     High   Court 
                      necessary   to   prevent   abuse   of   the   process   of   any  
                      Court  or  to  secure the ends of justice.   It is

                      be resorted to if there is specific provision in the 
                      Code   for   the   redress of the grievance   of   an  
                      aggrieved  party.  It  should  be  exercised  very 
                      sparingly and it should not be exercised as against  
                      the   express   bar     of     law   engrafted   in   any   other 
                      provision of the Code.50. In different situations, the inherent power may 
                      be   exercised     in   different   ways   to   achieve   its

                      High   Court   before   it   exercises     inherent     power  
                      underSection     482on   either   of   the   twin 
                      objectives, (i) to prevent abuse of the  process of  
                      any court or (ii) to secure the ends of justice, is 
                      a sine qua non.51. In the very nature of   its   constitution,   it 
                      is   the   judicial obligation of the High Court to 
                      undo a wrong in course of administration  of justice 
                      or to prevent continuation of unnecessary judicialPage 4 of 8HC-NIC                                  Page 4 of 8      Created On Sat Aug 06 00:50:21 IST 2016

               process. This  is founded on the legal maxim quando  
               lex aliquid  alicui  concedit, concedituret id sine

               which     is   whenever   anything   is   authorised,   and

               the   parties   is     put     to   an   end   and   peace   is

              Code   limits   or   restricts   the   inherent   power.   The 
              guideline for exercise   of   such power is provided

              substance.     The   learned  Additional   Public   Prosecutor  also

         reproduce the relevant paragraph for this purpose:-"48.The   question   is   with   regard   to   the   inherent 
                    power  of  the  High Court in quashing the criminal  
                    proceedings  against  an  offender  who  has settled 
                    his   dispute   with   the   victim   of   the   crime   but   the 
                    crime  in     which     he   is   allegedly  involved  is   not 
                    compoundable underSection 320of the Code.49.Section 482of the Code, as its very  language  
                    suggests,     saves   the   inherent   power   of   the   High  
                    Court   which   it   has   by   virtue   of     it     being     a 
                    superior  court  to  prevent  abuse  of  the  process  of 
                    any   court   or   otherwise     to   secure   the   ends   of 
                    justice. It begins  with  the  words,  'nothing  in 
                    this Code' which means that the provision   is   an  
                    overriding  provision.   These words leave no manner 
                    of doubt that none   of   the   provisions   of   the  
                    Code   limits   or   restricts   the   inherent   power.   The 
                    guideline for exercise   of   such power is provided 
                    inSection 482itself   i.e.,   to   prevent   abuse 
                    of  the process of any court or otherwise to secure 
                    the ends   of   justice.     As   has been repeatedly 
                    stated thatSection  482confers  no  new  powers  
                    on     High   Court;   it   merely   safeguards     existingPage 3 of 7HC-NIC                                Page 3 of 7      Created On Thu Mar 24 02:39:39 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/6936/2016                                              ORDER


              inherent     powers     possessed     by     High   Court 
              necessary   to   prevent   abuse   of   the   process   of   any  
              Court  or  to  secure the ends of justice.   It is 
              equally well settled that the power is  not  to
              be resorted to if there is specific provision in the 
              Code   for   the   redress of the grievance   of   an  
              aggrieved  party.  It  should  be  exercised  very 
              sparingly and it should not be exercised as against  
              the   express   bar     of     law   engrafted   in   any   other 
              provision of the Code.50. In different situations, the inherent power may 
              be   exercised     in   different   ways   to   achieve   its 
              ultimate objective. Formation   of   opinion   by the 
              High   Court   before   it   exercises     inherent     power  
              underSection     482on   either   of   the   twin 
              objectives, (i) to prevent abuse of the  process of  
              any court or (ii) to secure the ends of justice, is 
              a sine qua non.51. In the very nature of   its   constitution,   it 
              is   the   judicial obligation of the High Court to 
              undo a wrong in course of administration  of justice 
              or to prevent continuation of unnecessary judicial 
              process. This  is founded on the legal maxim quando  
              lex aliquid  alicui  concedit, concedituret id sine  
              qua res ipsa esse non  potest. The  full  import  of  
              which     is   whenever   anything   is   authorised,   and 
              especially if, as  a  matter  of duty,required to be 
              done   by   law,   it   is   found   impossible   to   do   that 
              thing     unless   something   else   not   authorised   in 
              express terms be also    done,   may also   be done, 
              then   that   something   else   will   be   supplied     by 
              necessary       intendment.   Ex   debito   justitiae   is 
              inbuilt in such exercise; the whole idea  is  to  do  
              real, complete and substantial justice   for   which 
              it  exists.  The  power possessed by the High Court  
              underSection   482of the   Code   is   of   wide  
              amplitude but requires exercise with great caution 
              and circumspection.52.     It   needs   no   emphasis   that   exercise     of 
              inherent   power   by   the High Court would entirely 
              depend on the  facts  and  circumstances  of  each
              case.   It   is   neither   permissible   nor     proper     for 
              the     court     to     provide     a   straitjacket   formula 
              regulating     the     exercise     of     inherent     powers 
              underSection   482.   No   precise   and   inflexible 
              guidelines can also be provided.53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on 
              the  ground  of settlement between  an offender  and 
              victim  is  not  the  same  thing as compounding  of  
              offence.     They     are     different   and     notPage 4 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 4 of 7      Created On Thu Mar 24 02:39:39 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/6936/2016                                              ORDER


              interchangeable.   Strictly   speaking,   the   power   of 
              compounding of offences   given   to   a court underSection   320is   materially   different   from     the  
              quashing  of  criminal proceedings by the High Court 
              in   exercise   of   its   inherent   jurisdiction.     In  
              compounding of offences, power of a criminal court 
              is  circumscribed    by    the  provisions  contained  inSection 320and  the  court  is  guided  solely  and  
              squarely   thereby   while,   on   the   other   hand,   the 
              formation   of   opinion     by     the   High   Court   for  
              quashing     a       criminal     offence     or     criminal 
              proceeding   or criminal complaint is guided by the 
              material on record   as   to   whether   the ends of 
              justice   would   justify   such   exercise   of   power 
              although  the  ultimate consequence may be acquittal 
              or dismissal of indictment.54.  Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding  
              having regard  to the fact that dispute between the  
              offender  and   victim  has   been  settled although  
              offences are not compoundable,  it  does  so  as  in  
              its   opinion,continuation of   criminal proceedings 
              will  be an exercise in  futility  and
              justice in the case demands that the dispute between 
              the   parties   is     put     to   an   end   and   peace   is 
              restored;  securing  the  ends  of  justice  being 
              the ultimate guiding factor. No  doubt,  crimes  are 
              acts  which  have  harmful effect on the public and  
              consist in wrong  doing  that  seriously  endangers 
              and threatens  well­being  of  society  and  it  is not 
              safe to leave   the   crime­doer only because he and 
              the victim have settled  the  dispute  amicably  or  
              that   the   victim   has   been   paid   compensation,   yet  
              certain     crimes     have     been   made   compoundable   in 
              law, with or  without  permission  of  the  Court.  
              In respect of serious offences  like  murder,  rape, 
              dacoity,  etc;  or  other
              offences of mental depravity underIPCor offences 
              of moral turpitude   under special   statutes,   likePrevention  of  Corruption  Actor  the  offences
              committed by public servants while working in that 
              capacity,   the     settlement   between   offender   and 
              victim   can   have   no   legal   sanction     at     all. 
              However,certain   offences   which   overwhelmingly   and 
              predominantly bear  civil  flavour having arisen out 
              of   civil,   mercantile,   commercial,     financial, 
              partnership  or   such     like     transactions     or     the 
              offences  arising  out  of  matrimony, particularly  
              relating to dowry, etc.  or  the   family  dispute,  
              where     the   wrong   is   basically   to   victim   and   the 
              offender   and   victim     have     settled     all   disputes 
              between them amicably, irrespective of the fact that 
              such  offences have not been made compoundable, the  
              High Court may within the framework  of its inherentPage 5 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 5 of 7      Created On Thu Mar 24 02:39:39 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/6936/2016                                             ORDER


              power,   quash   the   criminal   proceeding   or   criminal 
              complaint   or F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the 
              face   of   such   settlement,   there   is hardly any 
              likelihood of offender being convicted and by   not 
              quashing  the criminal proceedings, justice shall be 
              casualty and   ends of justice   shall be defeated. 
              The above list is illustrative and not exhaustive. 
              Each  case will depend on  its  own  facts  and  no 
              hard  and  fast  category  can  be prescribed.57.   The   position   that   emerges   from   the   above 
              discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the  
              High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR  
              or   complaint   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
              jurisdiction   is   distinct   and   different   from   the 
              power given to a criminal court for compounding the  
              offences   under   Section   320   of   the   Code.   Inherent 
              power   is   of   wide   plenitude   with   no   statutory 
              limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with 
              the guideline  engrafted  in  such  power  viz;  (i)  to 
              secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse 
              of the process of any Court. In what cases power to 
              quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R 
              may be exercised where the offender and victim have  
              settled their dispute would depend on the facts and  
              circumstances  of  each  case  and  no category  can  be 
              prescribed. However, before exercise of such power, 
              the High Court must have due regard to the nature 
              and   gravity   of   the   crime.   Heinous   and   serious  
              offences   of   mental   depravity   or   offences   like 
              murder,   rape,   dacoity,   etc.   cannot   be   fittingly 
              quashed even though the victim or victims family and 
              the offender have settled the dispute. Such offences 
              are not private in nature and have serious impact on 
              society.   Similarly,   any   compromise   between   the 
              victim   and   offender   in   relation   to   the   offences 
              under special statutes likePrevention of Corruption 
              Actor   the   offences   committed   by   public   servants 
              while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide 
              for   any   basis   for   quashing   criminal   proceedings 
              involving   such   offences.   But   the   criminal   cases 
              having   overwhelmingly   and   predominatingly   civil 
              flavour stand on different footing for the purposes 
              of quashing, particularly the offences arising from 
              commercial,   financial,   mercantile,   civil, 
              partnership   or   such   like   transactions   or   the 
              offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, 
              etc.   or   the   family   disputes   where   the   wrong   is 
              basically   private   or   personal   in   nature   and   the  
              parties have resolved their entire dispute. In this 
              category   of   cases,   High   Court   may   quash   criminal 
              proceedings   if   in   its   view,   because   of   the 
              compromise   between   the   offender   and   victim,   the 
              possibility   of   conviction   is   remote   and   bleak   andPage 6 of 7HC-NIC                         Page 6 of 7      Created On Thu Mar 24 02:39:39 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/6936/2016                                               ORDER


                     continuation of criminal case would put accused to 
                     great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice 
                     would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal  
                     case   despite   full   and   complete   settlement   and 
                     compromise with the victim. In other words, the High 
                     Court  must  consider  whether  it  would  be unfair  or 
                     contrary to the interest of justice to continue with 
                     the   criminal   proceeding   or   continuation   of   the 
                     criminal   proceeding   would   tantamount   to   abuse   of 
                     process   of   law   despite   settlement   and   compromise 
                     between   the   victim   and   wrongdoer   and   whether   to  
                     secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that 
                     criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to  
                     the   above   question(s)   is   in   affirmative,   the   High 
                     Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash 
                     the criminal proceeding."Resultantly, this petition is allowed. The FIR

                     and   gravity   of   the   crime.   Heinous   and   serious

                     commercial,   financial,   mercantile,   civil, 
                     partnership   or   such   like   transactions   or   the 
                     offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry,

                     parties have resolved their entire dispute. In this

                     compromise   between   the   offender   and   victim,   the 
                     possibility   of   conviction   is   remote   and   bleak   and

                     Court  must  consider  whether  it  would  be unfair  or 
                     contrary to the interest of justice to continue with 
                     the   criminal   proceeding   or   continuation   of   the 
                     criminal   proceeding   would   tantamount   to   abuse   of 
                     process   of   law   despite   settlement   and   compromise 
                     between   the   victim   and   wrongdoer   and   whether   to  
                     secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that 
                     criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to  
                     the   above   question(s)   is   in   affirmative,   the   High 
                     Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash

              underSection   482.   No   precise   and   inflexible 
              guidelines can also be provided.53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on 
              the  ground  of settlement between  an offender  and 
              victim  is  not  the  same  thing as compounding  of  
              offence.     They     are     different   and     not  
              interchangeable.   Strictly   speaking,   the   power   of 
              compounding of offences   given   to   a court underSection   320is   materially   different   from     the  
              quashing  of  criminal proceedings by the High Court 
              in   exercise   of   its   inherent   jurisdiction.     In  
              compounding of offences, power of a criminal court 
              is  circumscribed    by    the  provisions  contained  inSection 320and  the  court  is  guided  solely  and  
              squarely   thereby   while,   on   the   other   hand,   the 
              formation   of   opinion     by     the   High   Court   for  
              quashing     a       criminal     offence     or     criminal 
              proceeding   or criminal complaint is guided by the 
              material on record   as   to   whether   the ends of 
              justice   would   justify   such   exercise   of   power 
              although  the  ultimate consequence may be acquittal 
              or dismissal of indictment.54.  Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding  
              having regard  to the fact that dispute between the  
              offender  and   victim  has   been  settled although  
              offences are not compoundable,  it  does  so  as  in  
              its   opinion,continuation of   criminal proceedings 
              will  be an exercise in  futility  and
              justice in the case demands that the dispute between 
              the   parties   is     put     to   an   end   and   peace   is 
              restored;  securing  the  ends  of  justice  being 
              the ultimate guiding factor. No  doubt,  crimes  are 
              acts  which  have  harmful effect on the public and  
              consist in wrong  doing  that  seriously  endangers 
              and threatens  well­being  of  society  and  it  is not 
              safe to leave   the   crime­doer only because he and 
              the victim have settled  the  dispute  amicably  or  
              that   the   victim   has   been   paid   compensation,   yet  
              certain     crimes     have     been   made   compoundable   in 
              law, with or  without  permission  of  the  Court.  
              In respect of serious offences  like  murder,  rape, 
              dacoity,  etc;  or  other
              offences of mental depravity underIPCor offences 
              of moral turpitude   under special   statutes,   likePrevention  of  Corruption  Actor  the  offencesPage 4 of 6HC-NIC                          Page 4 of 6      Created On Fri Apr 22 01:20:40 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/7781/2016                                               ORDER


              committed by public servants while working in that 
              capacity,   the     settlement   between   offender   and 
              victim   can   have   no   legal   sanction     at     all. 
              However,certain   offences   which   overwhelmingly   and 
              predominantly bear  civil  flavour having arisen out 
              of   civil,   mercantile,   commercial,     financial, 
              partnership  or   such     like     transactions     or     the 
              offences  arising  out  of  matrimony, particularly  
              relating to dowry, etc.  or  the   family  dispute,  
              where     the   wrong   is   basically   to   victim   and   the 
              offender   and   victim     have     settled     all   disputes 
              between them amicably, irrespective of the fact that 
              such  offences have not been made compoundable, the  
              High Court may within the framework  of its inherent 
              power,   quash   the   criminal   proceeding   or   criminal 
              complaint   or F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the 
              face   of   such   settlement,   there   is hardly any 
              likelihood of offender being convicted and by   not 
              quashing  the criminal proceedings, justice shall be 
              casualty and   ends of justice   shall be defeated. 
              The above list is illustrative and not exhaustive. 
              Each  case will depend on  its  own  facts  and  no 
              hard  and  fast  category  can  be prescribed.57.   The   position   that   emerges   from   the   above 
              discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the  
              High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR  
              or   complaint   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
              jurisdiction   is   distinct   and   different   from   the 
              power given to a criminal court for compounding the  
              offences   under   Section   320   of   the   Code.   Inherent 
              power   is   of   wide   plenitude   with   no   statutory 
              limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with 
              the guideline  engrafted  in  such  power  viz;  (i)  to 
              secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse  
              of the process of any Court. In what cases power to 
              quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R 
              may be exercised where the offender and victim have  
              settled their dispute would depend on the facts and  
              circumstances  of  each  case  and  no category  can  be 
              prescribed. However, before exercise of such power, 
              the High Court must have due regard to the nature 
              and   gravity   of   the   crime.   Heinous   and   serious  
              offences   of   mental   depravity   or   offences   like 
              murder,   rape,   dacoity,   etc.   cannot   be   fittingly 
              quashed even though the victim or victims family and 
              the offender have settled the dispute. Such offences 
              are not private in nature and have serious impact on 
              society.   Similarly,   any   compromise   between   the 
              victim   and   offender   in   relation   to   the   offences 
              under special statutes likePrevention of Corruption 
              Actor   the   offences   committed   by   public   servants 
              while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide 
              for   any   basis   for   quashing   criminal   proceedingsPage 5 of 6HC-NIC                          Page 5 of 6      Created On Fri Apr 22 01:20:40 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/7781/2016                                               ORDER


                     involving   such   offences.   But   the   criminal   cases 
                     having   overwhelmingly   and   predominatingly   civil 
                     flavour stand on different footing for the purposes 
                     of quashing, particularly the offences arising from 
                     commercial,   financial,   mercantile,   civil, 
                     partnership   or   such   like   transactions   or   the 
                     offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, 
                     etc.   or   the   family   disputes   where   the   wrong   is 
                     basically   private   or   personal   in   nature   and   the  
                     parties have resolved their entire dispute. In this 
                     category   of   cases,   High   Court   may   quash   criminal 
                     proceedings   if   in   its   view,   because   of   the 
                     compromise   between   the   offender   and   victim,   the 
                     possibility   of   conviction   is   remote   and   bleak   and 
                     continuation of criminal case would put accused to 
                     great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice 
                     would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal  
                     case   despite   full   and   complete   settlement   and 
                     compromise with the victim. In other words, the High 
                     Court  must  consider  whether  it  would  be unfair  or 
                     contrary to the interest of justice to continue with 
                     the   criminal   proceeding   or   continuation   of   the 
                     criminal   proceeding   would   tantamount   to   abuse   of 
                     process   of   law   despite   settlement   and   compromise 
                     between   the   victim   and   wrongdoer   and   whether   to  
                     secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that 
                     criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to  
                     the   above   question(s)   is   in   affirmative,   the   High 
                     Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash 
                     the criminal proceeding."Resultantly, this petition is allowed. The FIR
         being CR No. I-69           of      2014 registered with Harij
         Police Station, District Patan stands quahsed.All the consequential proceedings pursuant
         thereto shall stand terminated.Rule is made absolute. Direct service is
         permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                    following order:-" The prosecutrix and the applicant
                              herein were fond of each other.Page 1 of 9HC-NIC                                       Page 1 of 9      Created On Thu Jun 09 00:36:48 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/3121/2016                                            ORDERTheir initial liking resulted into
                     their marrying with each other,

                     24th January 2016. They are now
                     residing together as husband and
                     wife.Rule returnable on 18th February
                     2016. Learned APP Shri JK Shah

                     applicant till the next adjourned

           was fixed and the following order was
           passed:-"1. Shri Keyur Vyas, learned counsel,
                     appears for the respondent No.2-

                     applicant Shri Hardik Barot, the
                     applicant   and   the   victim   have

                     victim as the same are lying with the

                     the applicant and, therefore, in the
                     wake of further adjournment, the same

                     appearing for the respondent No.2,

                     counsel appearing for the applicant,
                     submits that the applicant and the
                     victim have married. However, the
                     registration of their marriage was
                     not possible for want of documents ofPage 3 of 9HC-NIC                       Page 3 of 9      Created On Thu Jun 09 00:36:48 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/3121/2016                                            ORDER



                     the victim girl, which shall be done

           petitioner has pointed out that the
           registration of marriage is not feasible

         order, the birth certificate of the prosecutrix

         Court.4.            Heard both the sides and considered the
         fact    that        the      petitioner              has       married            to       the

         majority and the certificate of marriage was not
         feasible for want to testimonials. However, now,

         petitioner and they have been living together as
         husband and wife since 02.02.2016, i.e. the day
         on which the marriage was solemnized, this Court

         complaint and the same deserves to be quashed in
         view of the observations made by the                                              Hon'ble
         Apex Court in the case of "GIAN SINGH VS. STATE
         OF PUNJAB AND ANR.", (2012) 10 SCC 303, wherein,
