          R/CR.MA/3121/2016                                            ORDER"61. The position that emerges from the
           above discussion can be summarised thus:the power of the High Court in quashing a
           criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint
           in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction
           is distinct and different from the power
           given to a criminal court for compounding
           the offences under Section 320 of the
           Code. Inherent power is of wide plenitude
           with no statutory limitation but it has
           to be exercised in accord with the
           guideline engrafted in such power viz;
           (I) to secure the ends of justice or (ii)
           to prevent abuse of the process of any
           Court. In what cases power to quash the
           criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R
           may be exercised where the offender and
           victim have settled their dispute would
           depend on the facts and circumstances of
           each   case    and   no   category    can   be
           prescribed. However, before exercise of
           such power, the High Court must have due
           regard to the nature and gravity of the
           crime. Heinous and serious offences of
           mental depravity or offences like murder,
           rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly
           quashed    even    though   the   victim    or
           victim's family and the offender have
           settled the dispute. Such offences are
           not private in nature and have serious
           impact    on    society.    Similarly,     any
           compromise    between     the    victim    and
           offender in relation to the offences
           under special statutes likePrevention of
           Corruption Actor the offences committed
           by public servants while working in that
           capacity etc; cannot provide for any
           basis for quashing criminal proceedings
           involving such offences. But the criminal
           cases having      overwhelmingly and      pre-dominatingly    civil    flavour   stand    on
           different footing for the purposes ofPage 7 of 9HC-NIC                       Page 7 of 9      Created On Thu Jun 09 00:36:48 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/3121/2016                                            ORDER



                 quashing,    particularly     the    offences
                 arising    from    commercial,     financial,
                 mercantile, civil, partnership or such
                 like transactions or the offences arising
                 out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc.
                 or the family disputes where the wrong is
                 basically private or personal in nature
                 and the parties have resolved their
                 entire dispute. In this category of
                 cases, High Court may quash criminal
                 proceedings if in its view, because of
                 the compromise between the offender and
                 victim, the possibility of conviction is
                 remote and bleak and continuation of
                 criminal case would put accused to great
                 oppression and     prejudice and      extreme
                 injustice would be caused to him by not
                 quashing the criminal case despite full
                 and complete settlement and compromise
                 with the victim. In other words, the High
                 Court must consider whether it would be
                 unfair or contrary to the interest of
                 justice to continue with the criminal
                 proceeding    or    continuation     of   the
                 criminal proceeding would tantamount to
                 abuse   of    process     of   law    despite
                 settlement and compromise between the
                 victim and wrongdoer and whether to
                 secure the     ends of     justice, it     is
                 appropriate that criminal case is put to
                 an end and if the answer to the above
                 question(s) is in affirmative, the High
                 Court   shall     be    well    within    its
                 jurisdiction    to    quash   the    criminal
                 proceeding."5.        Further, this Court cannot be oblivious

         Prosecutor has submitted that so far no affidavit
         is filed.6.            In      the      result,            while          QUASHING               the
         impugned complaint being I-C.R. No. 7 of 2016
         lodged with the Mansa Police Station along with
         all     consequential           proceedings,                let        the        matter
         appear on 13TH JUNE, 2016, for the limited purpose
         of      filing       of      affidavit            so      as       to       pass            an
         appropriate order qua the complainant-Respondent.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

               CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                                 FIR/ORDER) NO. 24128 of 2016
         ==========================================================
                      ALTAFBHAI HAJIBHAI MAKWA....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                       STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR VAIBHAV B SHUKLA, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         MR RONAK RAVAL, PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================
         CORAM:             HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
                                  Date : 20/09/2016
                                            ORAL ORDER1.           This       is     a    petition            by      the       petitioner
         underArticle 226of the Constitution of India
         andSection          482of        the       Code          of        Criminal
         Procedure,         seeking         quashment              of      the       complaint
         being II-C.R. No. 161/2013 registered with Sanand
         Police     Station           underSections            294(B),323and506(2)of the Indian Penal Code.2.           It       is       the        case          of        the          original
         complainant-Respondent                    No.2        that        while          he      was
         discharging duties as a Doctor, the petitioner,
         herein, misbehaved with him and abused him and
         also beaten him.               This led to the filing of the
         impugned complaint.3.           The Court notices that a cross-complaint
         being II-C.R. No. 47/2013 is filed by the presentPage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                      Page 1 of 5      Created On Thu Sep 22 01:13:53 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/24128/2016                                                   ORDER



         petitioner against Respondent No.2, herein, with
         Sanand Police Station underSections 294(B),323and506(2)of the Indian Penal Code andSection
         3(1)(x)of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled
         Tribes Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1988. For
         quashment         of         the     same,           Respondent              No.2         has
         already preferred a petition before this Court
         being     Criminal            Misc.        Application               No.        7616           of
         2013.4.           Learned Advocates for the parties stated
         that    both        the       parties             have      joined           different
         institutions and they no longer work together.
         The    parties         have         settled          their         disputes,              and
         therefore, the petitioner is before this Court
         seeking quashment of the complaint.5.           The complainant-Respondent No.2 is also
         present       before          this        Court,          who        confirms             the
         contents of his affidavit. He, further, submits
         that no grievance survives now. He has further
         urged that the present petitioner is also going
         to make the similar request for quashment of the
         complaint lodged against him.6.           On verification from the Respondent No.2
         the    genuineness             of    the          compromise            and       as      the
         parties have arrived at a compromise without any
         threat or coercion, bearing in mind the decisionPage 2 of 5HC-NIC                                       Page 2 of 5      Created On Thu Sep 22 01:13:53 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/24128/2016                                                  ORDER



         of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case ofGIAN
         SINGH VS. STATE OF PUNJAB AND ANR., (2012) 10 SCC
         303,   wherein,             at   Paragraph-61,                the       Apex        Court
         observed as under;""61. The position that emerges from
                            the    above     discussion    can    be
                            summarised thus: the power of the
                            High Court in quashing a criminal
                            proceeding or FIR or complaint in
                            exercise of its inherent jurisdiction
                            is distinct and different from the
                            power given to a criminal court for
                            compounding     the    offences    under
                            Section 320 of the Code. Inherent
                            power is of wide plenitude with no
                            statutory limitation but it has to be
                            exercised    in     accord   with    the
                            guideline engrafted in such power
                            viz.,(i)to secure the ends of justice
                            or (ii) to prevent abuse of the
                            process of any Court. In what cases
                            power    to    quash     the    criminal
                            proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may
                            be exercised where the offender and
                            victim have settled their dispute
                            would   depend    on   the   facts   and
                            circumstances of each case and no
                            category can be prescribed. However,
                            before exercise of such power, the
                            High Court must have due regard to
                            the nature and gravity of the crime.
                            Heinous   and    serious   offences   of
                            mental depravity or offences like
                            murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be
                            fittingly quashed even though the
                            victim or victim's family and the
                            offender have settled the dispute.
                            Such offences are not private in
                            nature and have serious impact on
                            society. Similarly, any compromisePage 3 of 5HC-NIC                                     Page 3 of 5      Created On Thu Sep 22 01:13:53 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/24128/2016                                            ORDER



                     between the victim and offender in
                     relation   to    the    offences    under
                     special statutes likePrevention of
                     Corruption    Actor   the    offences
                     committed by public servants while
                     working in that capacity etc; cannot
                     provide for any basis for quashing
                     criminal proceedings involving such
                     offences. But the criminal cases
                     having    overwhelmingly      and    pre-
                     dominatingly civil flavour stand on
                     different footing for the purposes of
                     quashing, particularly the offences
                     arising from commercial, financial,
                     mercantile, civil, partnership or
                     such   like    transactions      or   the
                     offences arising out of matrimony
                     relating to dowry, etc. or the family
                     disputes where the wrong is basically
                     private or personal in nature and the
                     parties have resolved their entire
                     dispute. In this category of cases,
                     High   Court    may     quash    criminal
                     proceedings if in its view, because
                     of   the    compromise     between    the
                     offender and victim, the possibility
                     of conviction is remote and bleak and
                     continuation of criminal case would
                     put accused to great oppression and
                     prejudice and extreme injustice would
                     be caused to him by not quashing the
                     criminal   case    despite     full   and
                     complete settlement and compromise
                     with the victim. In other words, the
                     High Court must consider whether it
                     would be unfair or contrary to the
                     interest of justice to continue with
                     the     criminal       proceeding      or
                     continuation      of     the     criminal
                     proceeding would tantamount to abuse
                     of process of law despite settlement
                     and compromise between the victim and
                     wrongdoer and whether to secure the
                     ends of justice, it is appropriatePage 4 of 5HC-NIC                        Page 4 of 5      Created On Thu Sep 22 01:13:53 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/24128/2016                                                     ORDER



                             that criminal case is put to an end
                             and if the answer to the above
                             question(s) is in affirmative, the
                             High Court shall be well within its
                             jurisdiction to quash the criminal
                             proceeding."7.           In     wake       of     the         settlement              between           the
         parties and in view of the fact that the disputes
         between the parties are of personal in nature and
         it does not involve misappropriation of any public
         money    or       forgery        of       any        public           document,             the
         request for quashment needs to be acceded to.8.           Resultantly, this petition is ALLOWED and
         the     impugned             complaint            is       QUASHED             with          all
         consequential                proceedings.               Direct            service                is
         permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                   IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD


         CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR REGULAR BAIL) NO. 1801 of 2016

                           In CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 450 of 2014

         ==========================================================
                    NAVGHAN BHIMA KARAVADARA & 3....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                         STATE OF GUJARAT....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR AD SHAH, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1-4
         MS NISHA THAKORE ADDITIONAL PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the
         RESPONDENT(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

                CORAM: HONOURABLE MS.JUSTICE HARSHA DEVANI
                       and
                       HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE G.R.UDHWANI

                                    Date : 19/02/2016


                                     ORAL ORDER(PER : HONOURABLE MS.JUSTICE HARSHA DEVANI)1.   By this application undersection 389of the Code of
         Criminal Procedure, 1973, the applicants-convicts seek to be
         enlarged on bail during the pendency of Criminal Appeal
         No.450 of 2014 on suitable terms and conditions.2.   By a judgment and order dated 7.2.2014, the applicants
         have been convicted of the offence undersection 302read
         withsection 114of the Indian Penal Code and have been
         sentenced to life imprisonment as well as fine of Rs.2000/- and
         in default of payment of fine, to undergo further simplePage 1 of 6HC-NIC                                Page 1 of 6     Created On Sun Feb 28 04:13:37 IST 2016
               R/CR.MA/1801/2016                                               ORDER



         imprisonment for a further period of two months. The
         applicants have also been convicted of the offence under
         section 504 read withsection 114and 506(2) read withsection
         114of the Indian Penal Code and have been sentenced to
         imprisonment of one year and two years respectively.3.   Mr. A. D. Shah, learned counsel for the appellants invited
         the attention of the court to the testimony of the medical
         witness, namely, Dr. Niraliben Odedara to point out the nature
         of the injuries sustained by the deceased. It was submitted
         that all the injuries inflicted on the deceased are on the hands
         and legs and no injuries have been inflicted on any vital part of
         the body. It was, accordingly, submitted that it is, therefore,
         evident that there was no intention on the part of the accused
         persons to cause the death of the deceased. It was submitted
         that moreover, the weapons which are alleged to have been
         used for the commission of the offence are in the nature of iron
         pipes and crowbar and that having regard to the injuries which
         are reflected in the injury certificate and the post-mortem
         report, the same could not have been caused by the use of
         such weapons. It was further submitted that before the doctor,
         the deceased had named four persons only by first names and
         an unknown person and that before the police officer at the
         first instance no one was named. Subsequently, in the first
         information report, full names of the applicants have been
         given. It was submitted that having regard to the injury
         sustained by the deceased, and the time when the deceased
         was admitted at the hospital and the time when first
         information report is stated to have been recorded, the
         deceased could not have been in a fit state of mind so as to
         give such details as have been recorded in the first informationPage 2 of 6HC-NIC                             Page 2 of 6     Created On Sun Feb 28 04:13:37 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/1801/2016                                                   ORDER



         report. It was submitted that the case is based upon the
         testimony of witnesses before whom the deceased is stated to
         have made oral dying declarations; however, most of the
         witnesses have not supported the prosecution case and have
         been declared hostile. That even if the testimony of the
         witnesses is accepted, at best, the offence would fall undersection 304, Part-II of theIndian Penal Codeand, therefore, the
         sentence imposed upon the applicants, ultimately, would be
         required to be reduced. It was submitted that the applicants
         have already undergone more than five years imprisonment
         and hence, during the pendency of the appeal, the applicants
         are entitled to the grant of regular bail inasmuch as in case the
         order of sentence is not suspended, the applicants would
         continue to remain in jail and if, ultimately, they succeed in the
         appeal even to the extent of conversion of the sentence to
         304, Part-II,IPCgrave prejudice would be caused to the
         applicants.      It   was,   accordingly,         urged        that       in     these
         circumstances the court may exercise discretion in favour of
         the applicants.3.1   In support of his submissions, the learned counsel placed
         reliance upon the decision of the Supreme Court in the case ofRanjha and another v. State of Punjab, AIR 1996 SC 2741,
         wherein except one abraded contusion on the back of the
         lower part of the chest, beneath which three ribs were found
         fractured, all other injuries were simple and most of them were
         inflicted on non-vital parts of the body, the court held that the
         offence would fall undersection 304, Part-II,IPC.3.2   Reliance was also placed upon the decisions of the
         Supreme Court in the case of Bhoopat Singh v. J. B.Page 3 of 6HC-NIC                                  Page 3 of 6     Created On Sun Feb 28 04:13:37 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/1801/2016                                               ORDER



         Katariya, (2009) 17 SCC 484, in the case of Kariya v. State
         of Karnataka, JT 2002 (6) SC 582 and in the case ofState of
         Punjab v. Balkar Singh and others, 1998 Supreme Court
         Cases (Cri) 399 for a similar proposition of law.3.3   Reliance was also placed upon the decision of the
         Supreme Court in the case ofPara Seenaiah and another
         v. State of Andhra Pradesh and another, (2012) 6 SCC
         800, wherein the trial court recorded a finding that since the
         accused had caused injury only on the non-vital part of the
         body of the deceased, there was no intention to do away with
         his life and, accordingly, acquitted them of the charge of
         murder but convicted for the offence undersection 326, IPC,
         the Supreme Court upheld the said order.4.    Opposing the application, Ms. Nisha Thakore, learned
         Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that the deceased had
         sustained as many as fourteen injuries, many of which are in
         the nature of contused lacerated wounds and are also
         accompanied by fractures. It was submitted that having regard
         to the nature of the injuries inflicted upon the deceased, it is
         evident that the accused persons intended to cause his death.
         It was submitted that on the basis of the evidence of the
         medical witness as well as the oral dying declaration made by
         the deceased before other witnesses, the prosecution has duly
         established the charge against the accused and that at this
         stage the court may not exercise discretion in favour of the
         applicants.5.    This court has considered the submissions advanced by
         the learned counsel for the respective parties and has perused
         the evidence as referred to by the learned counsel for thePage 4 of 6HC-NIC                              Page 4 of 6     Created On Sun Feb 28 04:13:37 IST 2016
               R/CR.MA/1801/2016                                                  ORDER



         respective parties.6.   This being an application for suspension of sentence and
         grant of bail, it is not necessary to enter into any elaborate
         discussion on the merits of the case.7.   In the opinion of this court, having regard to the nature of
         the injuries sustained by the deceased which are on non-vital
         parts of the body, the contention raised on behalf of the
         applicants that the present case would fall undersection 304,
         Part-II of theIndian Penal Codeand not undersection 302thereof, cannot be ruled out. Under the circumstances, if at the
         time of final disposal of the appeal, the court comes to the
         conclusion that a lesser offence is made out and imposes
         sentence accordingly, undue prejudice would be caused to the
         applicant. In these circumstances, the court is of the view that
         a prima facie case has been made out for grant of bail pending
         the appeal.8.   The application, therefore, succeeds and is, accordingly,
         allowed. The sentence imposed by the learned Additional
         Sessions Judge, Porbandar, vide judgment and order dated
         7.2.2014 rendered in Sessions Case No.16 of 2011 is hereby
         suspended and the applicants are ordered to be released on
         bail till the final disposal of the appeal on their executing a
         personal bond of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only)
         each with one solvent surety of the like amount to the
         satisfaction of the lower Court with following conditions;(a)     They shall not take undue advantage of their liberty
              or abuse their liberty;Page 5 of 6HC-NIC                               Page 5 of 6      Created On Sun Feb 28 04:13:37 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/1801/2016                                                 ORDER




               (b)     They shall maintain law and order;


               (c)      They shall surrender their passports, if any, to thelower court, within a week and if any of the applicants
                does not possess any passport, then he shall make a
                declaration to that effect before the trial court;(d)      If during the pendency of the criminal appeal any
                 change in the residential addresses, permanent or
                 temporary, of any of the applicants takes place, then he
                 shall intimate the same to the trial court as well as the
                 concerned Police Station.9.     Bail before the trial court having jurisdiction.10.   It is, however, made clear that any observations made
         while deciding this bail application will not affect merits of the
         case at the time of final arguments.11.   Rule is made absolute. Direct service is permitted.(HARSHA DEVANI, J.)




                                                                      (G.R.UDHWANI, J.)

Try out ourPremium Member Services--Sign up todayand get free trial for one month.Gujarat High CourtAnkit Gaurangbhai Raval vs State Of Gujarat & on 10 February, 2016Author:Sonia GokaniBench:Sonia GokaniR/CR.MA/2043/2015                                               ORDER



         `
                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

              CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                                 FIR/ORDER) NO. 2043 of 2015


                                             With
                   SPECIAL CRIMINAL APPLICATION NO. 380 of 2015
         ==========================================================
                         ANKIT GAURANGBHAI RAVAL....Applicant(s)
                                        Versus
                          STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR PAWAN A BAROT, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         MR VAIBHAV B SHUKLA, ADVOCATE for the Respondent(s) No. 2
         PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

                 CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                      Date : 10/02/2016


                                        ORAL ORDER1. Both   the   matters   i.e.   Criminal   Miscellaneous 

               Application   as   well   as   Special   Criminal 

               Application,   are   arising   out   of   a   first 

               information   report   being   I­C.R.   No.6   of   2015 

               registered   with   Karelibaug   Police   Station, 

               Vadodara,   for   the   offences   punishable   undersections   406,408,409and114of   the   Indian 

               Penal   Code,   1860.   The   first   information   report 

               came to be lodged against both the applicants byPage 1 of 6HC-NIC                                  Page 1 of 6      Created On Sat Feb 27 23:28:57 IST 2016
              R/CR.MA/2043/2015                                            ORDER



           the respondent No.2­Imtiyas Rahemanbhai Vora, who 

           is   the   Senior   Officer   (Store)   at   The   Sandesh 

           Limited.2. During   the   course   of   investigation,   the 

           applicants   were   protected   by   way   of   interim 

           relief   granted   by   the   Court.   The   parties   have 

           chosen to settle the dispute as an unconditional 

           apology   has   been   tendered   by   the   applicants   in 

           the   name   of   Managing   Director,   The   Sandesh 

           Limited   and   because   of   cordial   relationship   of 

           the   past   years,   the   management   of   such   company 

           has   accepted   the   gesture   on   the   part   of   the 

           applicants. The consent terms in both the matters 

           are  brought  on  record  and  a  request  is  made  to 

           quash   and   set   aside   the   said   first   information 

           report and all consequential proceedings thereof.3. Shri Hardik Dave,  learned counsel appearing with 

           learned   counsel   Shri   Pawan   Barot   for   the 

           applicants   as   well   as   Shri   Vaibhav   Shukla, 

           learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent 

           No.2­original complainant, have urged that therePage 2 of 6HC-NIC                           Page 2 of 6      Created On Sat Feb 27 23:28:57 IST 2016
              R/CR.MA/2043/2015                                            ORDER



           is   no   element   of   any   public   officer  or   public 

           property   involved   in   the   present   case   and   the 

           first   information   report  is   being   strictly 

           between private parties, the same may be quashed 

           and set aside.4. Bearing in mind, the decision of the Apex Court 

           in the case ofGian Singh v. State of Punjab and  

           others, reported in AIR 2012 SC (SUPP.) 838, it 

           would   be   apt   to   reproduce   the   findings   and 

           observations ofthe said decisionfor the purpose 

           of allowing the request of quashment of the first 

           information   report   qua   the   present   applicants, 

           which read as under :"53. Quashing   of   offence   or   criminal 
                 proceedings   on   the   ground   of   settlement 
                 between   an   offender   and   victim   is   not   the  
                 same   thing   as   compounding   of   offence.   They 
                 are   different   and   not   interchangeable. 
                 Strictly speaking, the power of compounding 
                 of offences given to a court  underSection  
                 320is   materially   different   from   the 
                 quashing of criminal proceedings by the High 
                 Court   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
                 jurisdiction.   In   compounding   of   offences,Page 3 of 6HC-NIC                           Page 3 of 6      Created On Sat Feb 27 23:28:57 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/2043/2015                                            ORDER



             power   of   a   criminal   court   is   circumscribed  
             by   the   provisions   contained   inSection   320and the court is guided solely and squarely 
             thereby   while,   on   the   other   hand,   the 
             formation of opinion by the High Court for  
             quashing   a   criminal   offence   or   criminal 
             proceeding   or   criminal   complaint   is   guided 
             by the material on record as to whether the 
             ends of justice would justify such exercise 
             of   power   although   the   ultimate   consequence 
             may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.54.   Where   High   Court   quashes   a   criminal 
             proceeding   having   regard   to   the   fact   that 
             dispute between the offender and victim has 
             been   settled   although   offences   are   not 
             compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, 
             continuation of criminal proceedings will be 
             an exercise in futility and justice in the  
             case   demands   that   the   dispute   between   the 
             parties   is   put   to   an   end   and   peace   is  
             restored; securing the ends of justice being 
             the   ultimate   guiding   factor.   No   doubt, 
             crimes are acts which have harmful effect on 
             the public  and consist  in wrong  doing that  
             seriously endangers and threatens well­being 
             of society and it is not safe to leave the 
             crimedoer   only   because   he   and   the   victim  
             have   settled   the   dispute   amicably   or   that 
             the   victim   has   been   paid   compensation,   yet  
             certain   crimes  have   been   made   compoundablePage 4 of 6HC-NIC                       Page 4 of 6      Created On Sat Feb 27 23:28:57 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/2043/2015                                            ORDER



             in   law,   with   or   without   permission   of   the  
             Court.   In   respect   of   serious   offences   like  
             murder,   rape,   dacoity,   etc;   or   other 
             offences   of   mental   depravity   underIPCor 
             offences   of   moral   turpitude   under   special 
             statutes, likePrevention of Corruption Actor the offences committed by public servants 
             while   working   in   that   capacity,   the 
             settlement   between   offender   and   victim   can 
             have   no   legal   sanction   at   all.   However, 
             certain   offences   which   overwhelmingly   and 
             predominantly   bear   civil   flavour   having 
             arisen out of civil, mercantile, commercial, 
             financial,   partnership   or   such   like 
             transactions or the offences arising out of 
             matrimony,   particularly   relating   to   dowry, 
             etc. or the family dispute, where the wrong 
             is basically to victim and the offender and 
             victim   have   settled   all   disputes   between 
             them amicably, irrespective of the fact that 
             such   offences   have   not   been   made  
             compoundable, the High Court may within the 
             framework   of   its   inherent   power,   quash   the  
             criminal proceeding or criminal complaint or 
             F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the face of  
             such   settlement,there   is   hardly   any 
             likelihood   of   offender   being   convicted   and 
             by   not   quashing   the   criminal   proceedings, 
             justice   shall   be   casualty   and   ends   of 
             justice shall be defeated. The above list is 
             illustrative   and   not   exhaustive.   Each   casePage 5 of 6HC-NIC                       Page 5 of 6      Created On Sat Feb 27 23:28:57 IST 2016
                      R/CR.MA/2043/2015                                             ORDER



                         will depend on its own facts and no hard and  
                         fast category can be prescribed."5. In view of aforesaid and the above cited decision 

                 of the Apex Court, the request of the applicants 

                 is acceded to. Both the matters succeed and the 

                 same   are,   accordingly,   allowed   in   terms   of   the 

                 compromise   arrived   at   between   the   parties.   The 

                 first   information   report   and   the   consequential 

                 proceedings   emanating   therefrom   are   quashed   and 

                 set aside qua the present applicants only. 

                                   Direct Service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

              CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                                 FIR/ORDER) NO. 14531 of 2015
                                                 With
                    CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION NO. 20442 of 2016
         ==========================================================
                    ASIABANU IQBALBHAI SHAIKH & 2....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
              ALIABANU W/O MOHAMMAD NAHIN SHAIKH & D/O FIROZKHAN
                      AHMEDKHAN PATHAN & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR RJ GOSWAMI, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 3
         MR SR YADAV, ADVOCATE for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         MS CM SHAH, PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 2
         ==========================================================
         CORAM:             HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
                                  Date : 23/08/2016
                                      COMMON ORAL ORDER1.           The petitioner Nos.1 to 3 in Criminal
         Misc.    Application              No.     14531        of       2015,         are        the
         maternal-aunt, maternal uncle and brother-in-law
         of   the       original           complainant-Respondent                            No.1,
         therein, who has lodged the complaint being I-
         C.R. No. 47 of 2015 registered with Mahila Police
         Station       underSections           498(A),323,294(B),506(1)and114of    the          Indian       Penal          Code         andSections 3and7of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
         which culminated into Criminal Case No.188/2016,
         which is pending before the learned Metropolitan
         Magistrate, Court No.11, Ahmedabad .2.           Further, the petitioner Nos.1 to 3 inPage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                     Page 1 of 5      Created On Sat Aug 27 04:58:21 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/14531/2015                                                ORDER



         Criminal Misc. Application No. 20442 of 2016, are
         the husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law of
         the      original             complainant-Respondent                               No.1,
         therein.3.           The charge-sheet in connection with the
         impugned         complaint           came          to         be         filed              on
         25.05.2016.4.           The      parties      are        before           this        Court            as
         they     have        settled       all           their         disputes.                The
         original complainant is present in person before
         this Court along with her father.                               She has stated
         that she has received an amount of Rs.1.75/- lacs
         and all the articles towards 'Stridhan' etc. and
         that nothing is left with the petitioners, now.5.           Having heard the learned Counsel for the
         petitioners          and     the   learned            APP       in       respective
         petition and having found that the parties have
         settled their disputes amicably, no purpose would
         be served in continuing the prosecution against
         the    petitioners           and   the        request           for        quashment
         needs to be acceded to.6.In above view of the matter, here, it
         would be profitable to refer to the observations
         made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case ofGIAN SINGH VS. STATE OF PUNJAB AND ANR., (2012) 10Page 2 of 5HC-NIC                                   Page 2 of 5       Created On Sat Aug 27 04:58:21 IST 2016
               R/CR.MA/14531/2015                                            ORDER



         SCC 303, wherein, at Paragraph-61, the Apex Court
         observed as under;""61. The position that emerges from
                          the    above      discussion     can    be
                          summarised thus: the power of the
                          High Court in quashing a criminal
                          proceeding or FIR or complaint in
                          exercise of its inherent jurisdiction
                          is distinct and different from the
                          power given to a criminal court for
                          compounding      the    offences     under
                          Section 320 of the Code. Inherent
                          power is of wide plenitude with no
                          statutory limitation but it has to be
                          exercised     in     accord    with    the
                          guideline engrafted in such power
                          viz.,(i)to secure the ends of justice
                          or (ii) to prevent abuse of the
                          process of any Court. In what cases
                          power    to     quash     the     criminal
                          proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may
                          be exercised where the offender and
                          victim have settled their dispute
                          would   depend      on  the   facts    and
                          circumstances of each case and no
                          category can be prescribed. However,
                          before exercise of such power, the
                          High Court must have due regard to
                          the nature and gravity of the crime.
                          Heinous   and     serious   offences    of
                          mental depravity or offences like
                          murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be
                          fittingly quashed even though the
                          victim or victim's family and the
                          offender have settled the dispute.
                          Such offences are not private in
                          nature and have serious impact on
                          society. Similarly, any compromise
                          between the victim and offender in
                          relation    to     the   offences    under
                          special statutes like Prevention ofPage 3 of 5HC-NIC                             Page 3 of 5      Created On Sat Aug 27 04:58:21 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/14531/2015ORDER



                     Corruption    Actor   the    offences
                     committed by public servants while
                     working in that capacity etc; cannot
                     provide for any basis for quashing
                     criminal proceedings involving such
                     offences. But the criminal cases
                     having    overwhelmingly      and    pre-
                     dominatingly civil flavour stand on
                     different footing for the purposes of
                     quashing, particularly the offences
                     arising from commercial, financial,
                     mercantile, civil, partnership or
                     such   like    transactions      or   the
                     offences arising out of matrimony
                     relating to dowry, etc. or the family
                     disputes where the wrong is basically
                     private or personal in nature and the
                     parties have resolved their entire
                     dispute. In this category of cases,
                     High   Court    may     quash    criminal
                     proceedings if in its view, because
                     of   the    compromise     between    the
                     offender and victim, the possibility
                     of conviction is remote and bleak and
                     continuation of criminal case would
                     put accused to great oppression and
                     prejudice and extreme injustice would
                     be caused to him by not quashing the
                     criminal   case    despite     full   and
                     complete settlement and compromise
                     with the victim. In other words, the
                     High Court must consider whether it
                     would be unfair or contrary to the
                     interest of justice to continue with
                     the     criminal       proceeding      or
                     continuation      of     the     criminal
                     proceeding would tantamount to abuse
                     of process of law despite settlement
                     and compromise between the victim and
                     wrongdoer and whether to secure the
                     ends of justice, it is appropriate
                     that criminal case is put to an end
                     and if the answer to the above
                     question(s) is in affirmative, thePage 4 of 5HC-NIC                        Page 4 of 5      Created On Sat Aug 27 04:58:21 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/14531/2015                                                      ORDER



                             High Court shall be well within its
                             jurisdiction to quash the criminal
                             proceeding."7.           Further, bearing in mind the decision in
         the case ofJITENDRA RAGHUVANSHI & ORS. VS. BABITA
         RAGHUVANSHI & ANR., (2013) 4 SCC 58, and in view
         of the nature of disputes being matrimonial in
         nature      and      when         the         parties           have        voluntarily
         chosen     to      end       all        their           grievances             by      mutual
         understanding,               it    is        desirable             that        the       Court
         show     indulgence               and        invoke          the        powers           underSection 482of the Code of Criminal Procedure for
         bringing lasting peace between the parties.8.           Resultantly,                   both         the         petitions                are
         ALLOWED and the request for quashment is acceded
         to. The impugned complaint is QUASHED with all
         consequential proceedings.9.           Learned              Advocate,                Mr.          S.R.           Yadav,
         appears         for          Respondent                   No.2-the                 original
         complainant          and          he     is          permitted          to       file         his
         appearance.Direct service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                                      COMMON ORAL ORDER1.           Both        these      petitions              arise          from         the
         complaint        lodged       with       Zinjuvada            Police          Station
         being II-C.R. No. 3028 of 2012 for the offence
         punishable underSection 323,504,506(2)and114of the Indian Penal Code. It is in connection
         with a private complaint lodged in the year 2001,
         which    was      numbered        as      Criminal           Case        No.       6        of
         2001. Later on, it was given a new number being
         Criminal Case No. 221 of 2013. The complaint was
         initially         lodged       at      learned           JMFC,          Limbdi              on
         16.05.2001 and was transferred to JMFC, Chuda.
         It is, at present, pending before the learned
         JMFC, Chuda.2.           Now, the parties have chosen to amicably
         settle all their disputes, as they happen to bePage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                    Page 1 of 5      Created On Wed Jun 08 00:56:05 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/10608/2016                                                   ORDER



         close relatives. The complainant is also present
         before this Court. An affidavit is filed by the
         complainant          stating,            therein,             that        there          was
         dispute     with       his        wife      and      in-laws           and       out          of
         emotional       turmoil,           the        complaint            was       filed            by
         him.    Now, once again he has reunited with his
         wife and they are living happily together and no
         grievance survives.3.          Learned APP has also inquired from the
         complainant         and      this        Court          has     also        confirmed
         that   this      compromise              is       not    borne         out       of      any
         compulsion or coercion.4.          Thus, in view of the amicable settlement
         between the private parties and in view of the
         decision of the Apex Court in Hon'ble Apex Court
         in the case of "GIAN SINGH VS. STATE OF PUNJAB
         AND ANR.", (2012) 10 SCC 303, the request for
         quashment        of         the     complaint               requires              to          be
         accepted.In "GIAN SINGH VS. STATE OF PUNJAB AND
         ANR."(Supra),           the       Apex           Court     at       Paragraph-61,
         observed as under;"61.    The position that emerges from
                       the above discussion can be summarised
                       thus: the power of the High Court in
                       quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR
                       or   complaint   in  exercise  of  its
                       inherent jurisdiction is distinct and
                       different from the power given to a
                       criminal court for compounding thePage 2 of 5HC-NIC                                      Page 2 of 5      Created On Wed Jun 08 00:56:05 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/10608/2016                                            ORDER



                offences underSection 320of the Code.
                Inherent power is of wide plenitude
                with no statutory limitation but it has
                to be exercised in accord with the
                guideline engrafted in such power viz;
                (I) to secure the ends of justice or(ii) to prevent abuse of the process of
                any Court. In what cases power to quash
                the criminal proceeding or complaint or
                F.I.R   may    be   exercised     where   the
                offender and victim have settled their
                dispute would depend on the facts and
                circumstances of each case and no
                category can be prescribed. However,
                before exercise of such power, the High
                Court must have due regard to the
                nature   and    gravity   of    the    crime.Heinous and serious offences of mental
                depravity or offences like murder,
                rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly
                quashed even though the victim or
                victim's family and the offender have
                settled the dispute. Such offences are
                not private in nature and have serious
                impact   on    society.    Similarly,     any
                compromise    between    the    victim    and
                offender in relation to the offences
                under special statutes likePrevention
                of Corruption Actor the offences
                committed by public servants while
                working in that capacity etc; cannot
                provide for any basis for quashing
                criminal    proceedings    involving     such
                offences. But the criminal cases having
                overwhelmingly     and    pre-dominatingly
                civil   flavour     stand    on    different
                footing for the purposes of quashing,
                particularly the offences arising from
                commercial,      financial,      mercantile,
                civil,    partnership     or     such    like
                transactions or the offences arising
                out of matrimony relating to dowry,
                etc. or the family disputes where the
                wrong is basically private or personalPage 3 of 5HC-NIC                        Page 3 of 5      Created On Wed Jun 08 00:56:05 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/10608/2016                                             ORDER



                       in nature and the parties have resolved
                       their entire dispute. In this category
                       of cases, High Court may quash criminal
                       proceedings if in its view, because of
                       the compromise between the offender and
                       victim, the possibility of conviction
                       is remote and bleak and continuation of
                       criminal case would put accused to
                       great oppression and prejudice and
                       extreme injustice would be caused to
                       him by not quashing the criminal case
                       despite full and complete settlement
                       and compromise with the victim. In
                       other   words,   the   High    Court   must
                       consider whether it would be unfair or
                       contrary to the interest of justice to
                       continue with the criminal proceeding
                       or    continuation    of    the    criminal
                       proceeding would tantamount to abuse of
                       process of law despite settlement and
                       compromise    between   the   victim    and
                       wrongdoer and whether to secure the
                       ends of justice, it is appropriate that
                       criminal case is put to an end and if
                       the answer to the above question(s) is
                       in affirmative, the High Court shall be
                       well within its jurisdiction to quash
                       the criminal proceeding."5.          Resultantly,           both          the          matters              are
         ALLOWED and the request for quashment is acceded

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

              CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                                 FIR/ORDER) NO. 13523 of 2016

         ==========================================================
                      ALPESH GOPALBHAI DONGA & 3....Applicant(s)
                                      Versus
                        STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR SANDEEP R LIMBANI, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 4
         MR MI MERCHANT, ADVOCATE for the Respondent(s) No. 2
         PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                         Date : 16/06/2016


                                          ORAL ORDER1.    Applicants         have     approached             this       Court         seeking

         quashment of the First Information Report being C.R.No.I-222

         of 2016 registered with Malaviya Nagar police station, Rajkot

         for the offences punishable undersections 406,420and114of

         the Indian Penal Code andsections 5,38,40and42of the

         Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.2.    Considering the details from the investigating officer and

         his report, which is placed on record, indicating the possible

         market value on the strength of the information provided by

         Sarpanch of Khijadia village, the price quoted is about Rs.44Page 1 of 4HC-NIC                                     Page 1 of 4      Created On Sun Jun 19 03:16:21 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/13523/2016                                            ORDER



         lakhs for the land in the village. According to learned advocate

         for the complainant, the complaint has no cause or grievance

         to survive. He has already received a substantial amount and

         his dues are also squared of. Applicants have no antecedents.3.   The learned counsel appearing for the complainant

         confirms the aspect of settlement by and between the parties.4.   Having considered the submissions made on behalf of

         both the sides and the fact that it is a private dispute and the

         parties have arrived at an amicable settlement, especially

         when the complainant has chosen to put an end to the matter,

         no cause survives and, therefore, it would be desirable to

         quash the first information report in view of the decision of the

         Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh v. State of Punjab

         and another, reported in AIR 2012 SC (Supp.) 838,

         whereby it is held that it is the duty of the Courts to encourage

         genuine settlements andsection 482of the Code of Criminal

         Procedure, 1973, enables the High Court to pass such orders.It

         would be beneficial to reproduce the relevant observations and

         findings of the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra),

         which read as under :"53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on                       the
              ground of settlement between an offender and victim is                    not
              the same thing as compounding of offence. They                            are
              different and not interchangeable. Strictly speaking,                     thePage 2 of 4HC-NIC                               Page 2 of 4      Created On Sun Jun 19 03:16:21 IST 2016
              R/CR.MA/13523/2016                                             ORDER



           power of compounding of offences given to a court under
           Section 320 is materially different from the quashing of
           criminal proceedings by the High Court in exercise of its
           inherent jurisdiction. In compounding of offences, power of a
           criminal court is circumscribed by the provisions contained
           in Section 320 and the court is guided solely and squarely
           thereby while, on the other hand, the formation of opinion
           by the High Court for quashing a criminal offence or criminal
           proceeding or criminal complaint is guided by the material
           on record as to whether the ends of justice would justify
           such exercise of power although the ultimate consequence
           may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.54.Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding having
           regard to the fact that dispute between the offender and
           victim has been settled although offences are not
           compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, continuation of
           criminal proceedings will be an exercise in futility and justice
           in the case demands that the dispute between the parties is
           put to an end and peace is restored; securing the ends of
           justice being the ultimate guiding factor. No doubt, crimes
           are acts which have harmful effect on the public and consist
           in wrong doing that seriously endangers and threatens well-
           being of society and it is not safe to leave the crimedoer
           only because he and the victim have settled the dispute
           amicably or that the victim has been paid compensation, yet
           certain crimes have been made compoundable in law, with
           or without permission of the Court. In respect of serious
           offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc; or other offences of
           mental depravity underIPCor offences of moral turpitude
           under special statutes, likePrevention of Corruption Actor
           the offences committed by public servants while working in
           that capacity, the settlement between offender and victim
           can have no legal sanction at all. However, certain offences
           which overwhelmingly and predominantly bear civil flavour
           having arisen out of civil, mercantile, commercial, financial,
           partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising
           out of matrimony, particularly relating to dowry, etc. or the
           family dispute, where the wrong is basically to victim and
           the offender and victim have settled all disputes between
           them amicably, irrespective of the fact that such offences
           have not been made compoundable, the High Court may
           within the framework of its inherent power, quash the
           criminal proceeding or criminal complaint or F.I.R if it is
           satisfied that on the face of such settlement,there is hardly
           any likelihood of offender being convicted and by not
           quashing the criminal proceedings, justice shall be casualty
           and ends of justice shall be defeated. The above list is
           illustrative and not exhaustive. Each case will depend on itsPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                             Page 3 of 4      Created On Sun Jun 19 03:16:21 IST 2016
                     R/CR.MA/13523/2016                                            ORDER



                  own facts and no hard and fast category can be prescribed."5.       For the foregoing reasons and in view of the decisions of

         the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra), the present

         application succeeds and the same is, accordingly, allowed in

         view of an amicable settlement arrived at by and between the

         parties. The first information report being C.R.No.I-222 of 2016

         registered with Malaviya Nagar police station, Rajkot and all

         the proceedings emanating therefrom, are quashed and set

         aside. Rule is made absolute accordingly.Direct Service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

         Surendranagar,   for   commission   of   offences

           settlement by and between the parties. The same

           especially when the respondent No.2 has chosen to

           first information report in question any further, 

           no   cause   survives   and,   therefore,   it   would   be

         the   case   ofGian   Singh(supra),   which   read   as

         IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

                      FIR/ORDER) No. 3234 of 2016

           PRAVINBHAI SHANKARBHAI PATEL & 1....Applicant(s)

                CORAM: HONOURABLE Ms. JUSTICE SONIA
                       GOKANI

         ORAL ORDERThe petitioners herein are the original accused and

         the respondent no. 2 is the original complainant. An FIR

         came to be lodged by the complainant, being I-C.R No.

         280 of 2007 before Fateganj Police Station, Vadodara for

         the offence punishable underSections 406,420,465,468,471,120-B,506&114IPC. Chargesheet came to be filed,

         after due investigation, before the concerned learned

         JMFC, Vadodara, which is pending. It is the say of the

         applicants that by mutual understanding, the parties have

         amicably settled their disputes, as it being essentially civilPage 1 of 4HC-NIC                               Page 1 of 4      Created On Sun Feb 28 03:44:48 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/3234/2016                                             ORDER



         in nature and pertaining to a parcel of land, being Survey

         No. 651 paiki of village Sama.Learned advocate Mr. Pravin Gondaliya appearing for

         the applicants and learned advocate Ms. Sanjana Dave

         appearing for the respondent no. 2 have jointly submitted

         that complaint be quashed as it does not involve any

         tempering with public document. According to them, it is

         purely a personal dispute, which the parties have chosen

         to settle amicably.Bearing in mind the ratio laid down by the Apex Court

         in case ofGian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr.,

         reported in 2012 (10)SCC 303, parties to the proceeding

         are permitted to compromise the complaint, as the

         complaint concerned is between the two private parties

         with no bearing on the public property or public money.

         Apt it would be, to reproduce the observations made by

         the Court in this regard, which reads thus -"61. The position that emerges from the above discussion
              can be summarised thus: the power of the High Court in
              quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in
              exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different
              from the power given to a criminal court for compounding
              the offences underSection 320of the Code. InherentPage 2 of 4HC-NIC                                Page 2 of 4      Created On Sun Feb 28 03:44:48 IST 2016
            R/CR.MA/3234/2016                                              ORDER



         power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but
         it has to be exercised in accord with the guideline
         engrafted in such power viz; (i) to secure the ends of
         justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.
         In what cases power to quash the criminal proceeding or
         complaint or F.I.R may be exercised where the offender
         and victim have settled their dispute would depend on the
         facts and circumstances of each case and no category can
         be prescribed. However, before exercise of such power,
         the High Court must have due regard to the nature and
         gravity of the crime. Heinous and serious offences of
         mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity,
         etc. cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or
         victims family and the offender have settled the dispute.
         Such offences are not private in nature and have serious
         impact on society. Similarly, any compromise between the
         victim and offender in relation to the offences under
         special statutes likePrevention of Corruption Actor the
         offences committed by public servants while working in
         that capacity etc; cannot provide for any basis for
         quashing criminal proceedings involving such offences.
         But   the    criminal   cases     having      overwhelmingly             and
         predominatingly civil flavour stand on different footing for
         the purposes of quashing, particularly the offences arising
         from commercial, financial, mercantile, civil, partnership
         or such like transactions or the offences arising out of
         matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or the family disputes
         where the wrong is basically private or personal in nature
         and the parties have resolved their entire dispute. In this
         category of cases, High Court may quash criminal
         proceedings if in its view, because of the compromise
         between the offender and victim, the possibility of
         conviction is remote and bleak and continuation ofPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                            Page 3 of 4      Created On Sun Feb 28 03:44:48 IST 2016
                     R/CR.MA/3234/2016                                            ORDER



               criminal case would put accused to great oppression and
               prejudice and extreme injustice would be caused to him by
               not quashing the criminal case despite full and complete
               settlement and compromise with the victim. In other
               words, the High Court must consider whether it would be
               unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with
               the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal
               proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law
               despite settlement and compromise between the victim
               and wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice,
               it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if
               the answer to the above question(s) is in affirmative, the
               High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the
               criminal proceeding."In the result, this Misc. Criminal Application is allowed. The F.I.R.

         consequential proceedings pursuant thereto shall stand terminated.Rule is made absolute. Direct service is permitted.{Ms. Sonia Gokani, J.}

                                                 ORAL ORDER1.    Present application is filed underSection 438of the Code of
         Criminal     Procedure          ('the    Code')       seeking       anticipatory           bail    in
         connection with the FIR, being C.R. No.I-60 of 2016, registered with
         Valsad Police Station for the offences punishable underSections 302,392,324,143,144,147,148,149,504,506(2)of the Indian Penal
         Code andSection 135of the Gujarat Police Act.2.    As per the allegations in the FIR, the applicant with other
         accused had formed unlawful assembly and had assaulted the injured
         witnesses with weapons like sticks, etc., as a result of which, one
         injured Hiteshbhai succumbed to his injuries.3.    It is pointed out by learned advocate Mr. Dave as also
         Additional Public Prosecutor Ms. Thakore thatSections 395and120-Bof the Indian Penal Code are also added in the FIR.4.    Learned advocate Mr. Dave for the applicant submitted that thePage 1 of 4HC-NIC                                           Page 1 of 4      Created On Fri Jul 01 00:35:01 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/13660/2016                                             ORDER




         applicant is serving as an officer in Income Tax Department and
         except showing his presence at the scene of incident, he is not
         alleged to have used any weapon or caused any injury to any injured
         witness. Mr. Dave submitted that on the side of the applicant, there is
         a cross complaint filed and the complainant in the present complaint
         has seen to it that maximum persons could be involved in the
         offences alleged and though the applicant was not responsible to
         cause any injury to any person, he is involved in the offences alleged.
         Mr. Dave has also referred to some photographs to point out that
         deceased Hiteshbhai, who succumbed to his injuries, was aggressor
         and had come with weapon like axe in his hand and persons from
         both the sides had gathered together and it is not possible to believe
         that    the applicant who is serving as officer in Income Tax
         Department at nearby place, i.e. at Vapi, would take part in the
         serious offence, like committing murder, and other offences as
         alleged in the FIR and it is wrongly alleged that the applicant was part
         of the unlawful assembly. He therefore, requests to exercise
         discretion under Section 438 of the Code in favour of the applicant.5.     Learned Additional Public Prosecutor Ms. Thakore on the other
         hand submitted that the applicant is residing at 3 kilometer away
         from the place of incident. Ms. Thakore submitted that presence of
         the applicant is established at the scene of offence by statements of
         three eye witnesses. She has referred statements of Ramanbhai
         Chhanabhai Patel dated 8.5.2016- the day of incident, Divyeshbhai
         Patel dated 10.5.2016 and Nileshbhai Jaganbhai Kodi Patel dated
         10.5.2015, wherefrom she pointed out that these witnesses have
         clearly stated that the applicant had come with stick with other
         persons and he had assaulted deceased Hiteshbhai with other
         persons. Ms. Thakore also submitted that as per the postmortem
         note, deceased Hiteshbhai received multiple injuries on different
         parts of the body and submitted that the applicant was one of thePage 2 of 4HC-NIC                                 Page 2 of 4      Created On Fri Jul 01 00:35:01 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13660/2016                                              ORDER




         persons responsible to cause injury to deceased Hiteshbhai as stated
         by three witnesses. She submitted that since the investigation is in
         progress, this Court may not exercise discretion under Section 438 of
         the Code in favour of the applicant.6.    Learned advocate Ms. Kruti Shah appearing for the complainant
         submitted that there is an ample evidence collected by the
         investigating officer establishing the presence of the applicant at the
         scene of offence. Ms. Shah submitted that considering the nature of
         allegations and the role attributed to the applicant of giving blow with
         stick to deceased Hiteshbhai and since investigation is in progress,
         this Court may not exercise discretion in favour of the applicant under
         Section 438 of the Code. Ms. Shah has also placed reliance on some
         photographs annexed with the affidavit filed by the complainant to
         show that the applicant was part of the unlawful assembly and to
         achieve common object and intention, the applicant also played vital
         role and considering his presence and use of stick by him for the
         purpose of achieving the common object, this Court may not consider
         the application of the applicant for anticipatory bail.7.    Having heard learned advocates for both the sides and having
         considered the nature of allegations made in the FIR, pointing to
         commission of serious offences under Sections 302, 392, 395 etc. by
         forming unlawful assembly, it appears that with the statements of
         witnesses shown to the Court from police papers, the presence of the
         applicant could be said to be established at the scene of offence and
         the applicant appears to be part of the unlawful assembly. It is
         required to note that learned advocate Mr. Dave when was referring
         to the photographs placed by the complainant with affidavit-in-reply,
         had shown the presence of the applicant with other persons at the
         scene of the offence. Therefore, when the applicant was stated to be
         present at the scene of offence with other accused and when SectionPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                                 Page 3 of 4      Created On Fri Jul 01 00:35:01 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13660/2016                                              ORDER




         149 is applied with serious offences underSections 302,392and395of the Indian Penal Code, showing the applicant to be part of the
         unlawful assembly, if the statements of the witnesses are considered,
         the applicant appears to have taken part in commission of offences.
         As could be seen from the statement of Shri Ramanbhai Chhanabhai
         Patel dated 8.5.2016- the day of incident, the applicant is stated to be
         present with other accused with stick and formed unlawful assembly
         and gave blow with stick with other persons on the body of deceased
         Hiteshbhai. As per the statements of two other witnesses dated
         10.5.2016, i.e. of Divyeshbhai Patel and Nileshbhai Jaganbhai Kodi
         Patel, the applicant with other co-accused had assaulted deceased
         Hiteshbhai. Thus, the Court finds that there is clear involvement of
         the applicant in the serious offence, like murder, with other offences
         alleged in the FIR and when in respect of such serious offence,
         investigation is in progress, this Court does not find it proper to
         exercise its discretion under Section 438 of the Code in favour of the
         applicant. The application is therefore, rejected. Rule is discharged.Sd/-(C.L. SONI, J.)
