                                             ORAL ORDER1.           The       petitioners                are    before           this        Court

         seeking quashment of the complaint being II-C.R.

         No.     3040      of         2016    registered              with         Vav        Police

         Station underSections 323,294(B),506(2)and114of the Indian Penal Code.2.           This Court has heard both the sides and

         also     inquired             from       the         complainant,                 who          is

         present        before          this        Court.           The        complainant-Respondent           No.2,          herein,          has        vindicated                 the

         contents of his affidavit. The parties have now

         arrived at an amicable settlement, without any

         threat or coercion, out of their own volition.Page 1 of 4HC-NIC                                       Page 1 of 4      Created On Sat Aug 06 02:23:06 IST 2016
                R/SCR.A/5509/2016                                             ORDERThus, no purpose would be served in permitting to

         continue the prosecution.3.In above view of the matter, here, it

         would be profitable to refer to the                           observations

         made by the           Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of

         "GIAN SINGH VS. STATE OF PUNJAB AND ANR.", (2012)

         10 SCC 303, wherein, at Paragraph-61, the Apex

         Court observed as under;"61.    The position that emerges from
                      the above discussion can be summarised
                      thus: the power of the High Court in
                      quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR
                      or   complaint   in    exercise   of   its
                      inherent jurisdiction is distinct and
                      different from the power given to a
                      criminal court for compounding the
                      offences underSection 320of the Code.
                      Inherent power is of wide plenitude
                      with no statutory limitation but it has
                      to be exercised in accord with the
                      guideline engrafted in such power viz;
                      (I) to secure the ends of justice or(ii) to prevent abuse of the process of
                      any Court. In what cases power to quash
                      the criminal proceeding or complaint or
                      F.I.R   may  be    exercised   where   the
                      offender and victim have settled their
                      dispute would depend on the facts and
                      circumstances of each case and no
                      category can be prescribed. However,
                      before exercise of such power, the High
                      Court must have due regard to the
                      nature   and   gravity   of   the   crime.Page 2 of 4HC-NIC                              Page 2 of 4      Created On Sat Aug 06 02:23:06 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/5509/2016                                            ORDER



                Heinous and serious offences of mental
                depravity or offences like murder,
                rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly
                quashed even though the victim or
                victim's family and the offender have
                settled the dispute. Such offences are
                not private in nature and have serious
                impact   on    society.    Similarly,    any
                compromise    between    the    victim   and
                offender in relation to the offences
                under special statutes likePrevention
                of Corruption Actor the offences
                committed by public servants while
                working in that capacity etc; cannot
                provide for any basis for quashing
                criminal   proceedings     involving    such
                offences. But the criminal cases having
                overwhelmingly     and    pre-dominatingly
                civil   flavour     stand    on    different
                footing for the purposes of quashing,
                particularly the offences arising from
                commercial,     financial,       mercantile,
                civil,    partnership     or     such   like
                transactions or the offences arising
                out of matrimony relating to dowry,
                etc. or the family disputes where the
                wrong is basically private or personal
                in nature and the parties have resolved
                their entire dispute. In this category
                of cases, High Court may quash criminal
                proceedings if in its view, because of
                the compromise between the offender and
                victim, the possibility of conviction
                is remote and bleak and continuation of
                criminal case would put accused to
                great oppression and prejudice and
                extreme injustice would be caused to
                him by not quashing the criminal case
                despite full and complete settlement
                and compromise with the victim. In
                other   words,    the   High    Court   must
                consider whether it would be unfair or
                contrary to the interest of justice to
                continue with the criminal proceedingPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                       Page 3 of 4      Created On Sat Aug 06 02:23:06 IST 2016
                  R/SCR.A/5509/2016                                                   ORDER



                        or   continuation    of    the   criminal
                        proceeding would tantamount to abuse of
                        process of law despite settlement and
                        compromise   between   the   victim   and
                        wrongdoer and whether to secure the
                        ends of justice, it is appropriate that
                        criminal case is put to an end and if
                        the answer to the above question(s) is
                        in affirmative, the High Court shall be
                        well within its jurisdiction to quash
                        the criminal proceeding."4.          Resultantly,             this         petition             is      allowed.The     impugned            complaint          is       QUASHED             with          all

         PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                         Date : 16/06/2016


                                             ORAL ORDER1.    Applicants are before this Court seeking quashment of

         the First Information Report being C.R.No.I-278 of 2015

         registered before Anand Town police station for the offences

         punishable undersections 384,504,506(2),511and114of the

         Indian Penal Code.2.    The    parties         have     chosen         to    settle        the      disputes.

         Complainant is before this Court. She has also filed an affidavit

         to the effect that without any coercion and duress, she has

         chosen to settle the dispute with the applicants. She also

         submitted that her husband is serving at Dubai. No difficulty orPage 1 of 4HC-NIC                                       Page 1 of 4      Created On Sun Jun 19 03:16:36 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/13970/2016                                            ORDER



         coercion is experienced by her.3.     The learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2

         confirms the aspect of settlement by and between the parties.

         He urges that he may be permitted to file his Vakalatnama on

         behalf of the respondent No.2 during the course of the day.

         Permission as prayed for is granted.4.     Having considered the submissions made on behalf of

         both the sides and the fact that it is a private dispute and the

         parties have arrived at an amicable settlement, especially

         when     respondent No.2 has chosen to put an end to the

         matter, no cause survives and, therefore, it would be desirable

         to quash the first information report in view of the decision of

         the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh v. State of Punjab

         and another, reported in AIR 2012 SC (Supp.) 838,

         whereby it is held that it is the duty of the Courts to encourage

         genuine settlements andsection 482of the Code of Criminal

         Procedure, 1973, enables the High Court to pass such orders.It

         would be beneficial to reproduce the relevant observations and

         findings of the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra),

         which read as under :53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on the
                ground of settlement between an offender and victim is
                not the same thing as compounding of offence. They are
                different and not interchangeable. Strictly speaking, thePage 2 of 4HC-NIC                                 Page 2 of 4      Created On Sun Jun 19 03:16:36 IST 2016
            R/CR.MA/13970/2016                                             ORDER



         power of compounding of offences given to a court underSection 320is materially different from the quashing of
         criminal proceedings by the High Court in exercise of its
         inherent jurisdiction. In compounding of offences, power of
         a criminal court is circumscribed by the provisions
         contained inSection 320and the court is guided solely and
         squarely thereby while, on the other hand, the formation of
         opinion by the High Court for quashing a criminal offence
         or criminal proceeding or criminal complaint is guided by
         the material on record as to whether the ends of justice
         would justify such exercise of power although the ultimate
         consequence may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.54. Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding
         having regard to the fact that dispute between the
         offender and victim has been settled although offences are
         not compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, continuation
         of criminal proceedings will be an exercise in futility and
         justice in the case demands that the dispute between the
         parties is put to an end and peace is restored; securing the
         ends of justice being the ultimate guiding factor. No doubt,
         crimes are acts which have harmful effect on the public
         and consist in wrong doing that seriously endangers and
         threatens well-being of society and it is not safe to leave
         the crimedoer only because he and the victim have settled
         the dispute amicably or that the victim has been paid
         compensation, yet certain crimes have been made
         compoundable in law, with or without permission of the
         Court. In respect of serious offences like murder, rape,
         dacoity, etc; or other offences of mental depravity underIPCor offences of moral turpitude under special statutes,
         likePrevention of Corruption Actor the offences committed
         by public servants while working in that capacity, the
         settlement between offender and victim can have no legal
         sanction at all. However, certain offences which
         overwhelmingly and predominantly bear civil flavour
         having arisen out of civil, mercantile, commercial,
         financial, partnership or such like transactions or the
         offences arising out of matrimony, particularly relating to
         dowry, etc. or the family dispute, where the wrong is
         basically to victim and the offender and victim have settled
         all disputes between them amicably, irrespective of the
         fact that such offences have not been made
         compoundable, the High Court may within the framework
         of its inherent power, quash the criminal proceeding or
         criminal complaint or F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the face
         of such settlement,there is hardly any likelihood of
         offender being convicted and by not quashing the criminal
         proceedings, justice shall be casualty and ends of justicePage 3 of 4HC-NIC                           Page 3 of 4      Created On Sun Jun 19 03:16:36 IST 2016
                     R/CR.MA/13970/2016                                            ORDER



                  shall be defeated. The above list is illustrative and not
                  exhaustive. Each case will depend on its own facts and no
                  hard and fast category can be prescribed."5.       For the foregoing reasons and in view of the decisions of

         the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra), the present

         application succeeds and the same is, accordingly, allowed in

         view of an amicable settlement arrived at by and between the

         parties. The first information report being C.R.No.I-278 of 2015

         registered before Anand Town police station and all the

         proceedings emanating therefrom, are quashed and set aside.

         Rule is made absolute accordingly.Direct Service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                                     ORAL ORDER1.          The       petitioner              is    before            this         Court,
         seeking quashment of the complaint underArticle
         226of the Constitution read withSection 482of
         the Code of Criminal Procedure being II-C.R. No.
         3048/2016         registered           with          Meganinagar                   Police
         Station      for       the     offence             underSections              323,294(b)and427of the Indian Penal Code.2.          The parties appear to have settled their
         disputes. In support of such a compromise, an
         affidavit of the Respondent-complainant is also
         brought on record, wherein, it has been stated,
         inter alia, that without any undue influence or
         coercion,        the        compromise         has        taken          place,              and
         therefore, the criminal proceedings deserve to be
         quashed.3.          Heard           learned       Advocates                on       both             thePage 1 of 4HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 4        Created On Fri Jun 17 02:16:11 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13618/2016                                                        ORDER



         sides and also ascertained the truthfulness of
         the     contents              of      the            affidavit                 from               the
         Respondent-complainant,                      wherein,                the       aspect              of
         compromise            is       stated.               The          disputes                 being
         predominantly                personal         in        nature            and         as          the
         parties have entered into a compromise out of
         their     own      volition          and          without            any        duress             or
         coercion,          the        request             for       quashment                of           the
         complaint deserves consideration, as no purpose
         is    likely          to       be      served              by        directing                    the
         petitioner to undergo the ordeal of trial.4.           Here it would be profitable to refer to
         the     observations made by the                             Hon'ble Apex Court
         in the case of "GIAN SINGH VS. STATE OF PUNJAB
         AND     ANR.",         (2012)         10          SCC       303,          wherein,                 at
         Paragraph-61, the Apex Court observed as under;"61.    The position that emerges from
                         the above discussion can be summarised
                         thus: the power of the High Court in
                         quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR
                         or   complaint   in  exercise  of   its
                         inherent jurisdiction is distinct and
                         different from the power given to a
                         criminal court for compounding the
                         offences underSection 320of the Code.
                         Inherent power is of wide plenitude
                         with no statutory limitation but it has
                         to be exercised in accord with the
                         guideline engrafted in such power viz;
                         (I) to secure the ends of justice or(ii) to prevent abuse of the process of
                         any Court. In what cases power to quash
                         the criminal proceeding or complaint orPage 2 of 4HC-NIC                                       Page 2 of 4         Created On Fri Jun 17 02:16:11 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/13618/2016                                              ORDER



                 F.I.R   may    be   exercised     where   the
                 offender and victim have settled their
                 dispute would depend on the facts and
                 circumstances of each case and no
                 category can be prescribed. However,
                 before exercise of such power, the High
                 Court must have due regard to the
                 nature   and    gravity   of    the    crime.Heinous and serious offences of mental
                 depravity or offences like murder,
                 rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly
                 quashed even though the victim or
                 victim's family and the offender have
                 settled the dispute. Such offences are
                 not private in nature and have serious
                 impact   on    society.    Similarly,     any
                 compromise    between    the    victim    and
                 offender in relation to the offences
                 under special statutes likePrevention
                 of Corruption Actor the offences
                 committed by public servants while
                 working in that capacity etc; cannot
                 provide for any basis for quashing
                 criminal    proceedings    involving     such
                 offences. But the criminal cases having
                 overwhelmingly     and    pre-dominatingly
                 civil   flavour     stand    on    different
                 footing for the purposes of quashing,
                 particularly the offences arising from
                 commercial,      financial,      mercantile,
                 civil,    partnership     or     such    like
                 transactions or the offences arising
                 out of matrimony relating to dowry,
                 etc. or the family disputes where the
                 wrong is basically private or personal
                 in nature and the parties have resolved
                 their entire dispute. In this category
                 of cases, High Court may quash criminal
                 proceedings if in its view, because of
                 the compromise between the offender and
                 victim, the possibility of conviction
                 is remote and bleak and continuation of
                 criminal case would put accused to
                 great oppression and prejudice andPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                        Page 3 of 4      Created On Fri Jun 17 02:16:11 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13618/2016                                                       ORDER



                         extreme injustice would be caused to
                         him by not quashing the criminal case
                         despite full and complete settlement
                         and compromise with the victim. In
                         other   words,   the   High    Court   must
                         consider whether it would be unfair or
                         contrary to the interest of justice to
                         continue with the criminal proceeding
                         or    continuation    of    the    criminal
                         proceeding would tantamount to abuse of
                         process of law despite settlement and
                         compromise    between   the   victim    and
                         wrongdoer and whether to secure the
                         ends of justice, it is appropriate that
                         criminal case is put to an end and if
                         the answer to the above question(s) is
                         in affirmative, the High Court shall be
                         well within its jurisdiction to quash
                         the criminal proceeding."5.           Resultantly,               this         petition              is      ALLOWED.
         The     impugned             complaint            is       quashed              with             all
         consequential proceedings.6.           Learned          Advocate,              Mr.        V.M.        Pathan,               is
         permitted          to        file       his          V.P.          on        behalf              of
         Respondent No.2-the complainant. Direct service
         is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

         ==========================================================
                    YUNUSBHAI HAJIBHAI JUNEJA & 1....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                       STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR IMRAN H PATHAN, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 2
         MR RONAK RAVAL, ADDL. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s)
         No. 1
         MR MT SAIYED, ADVOCATE for Respondent No.2
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                      Date : 10/08/2016


                                       ORAL ORDER1. Applicants   have   approached   this   Court   seeking 

              quashment   of   the   First   Information   Report   ("the 

              FIR"   for   short)   sbeing   C.R.No.I­85   of   2016 

              registered   with   Pradhyumannagar   police   station, 

              Rajkot for the offenses punishable undersections 

              341,323,504,506(2)and114of the Indian Penal 

              Code.2. During the pendency of investigation, the partiesPage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                 Page 1 of 5        Created On Fri Aug 12 02:50:03 IST 2016
              R/CR.MA/19655/2016                                                ORDER



           have   settled   their   disputes   amicably   due   to 

           intervention of the  family and friends and  have 

           sought quashment of the FIR. The applicants have 

           got   no   criminal   antecedents,   as   submitted   by 

           learned   advocate   for   the   applicants.   The 

           complainant is present and ratifies the contents 

           of his affidavit.Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab  

           and anotherreported in (2012) 10 SCC 303.3. Mr.M.T.Saiyed, learned advocate appearing for the 

           respondent No.2 confirms the aspect of settlement 

           by and between the parties. He urges that he may 

           be permitted to file his Vakalatnama on behalf of 

           the respondent No.2 during the course of the day. 

           Permission as prayed for is granted.4. Having considered the submissions made on behalf 

           of   both   the   sides   and   the   fact   that   it   is   a 

           private dispute and the parties have arrived at 

           an   amicable   settlement,   especially   when 

           respondent No.2 has chosen to put an end to the 

           matter,   no   cause   survives   and,   therefore,   it 

           would be desirable to quash the first informationPage 2 of 5HC-NIC                            Page 2 of 5        Created On Fri Aug 12 02:50:04 IST 2016
            R/CR.MA/19655/2016                                                ORDER



         report in view of the decision of the Apex Court 

         in the case ofGian Singh(supra),  whereby it is 

         held   that   it   is   the   duty   of   the   Courts   to 

         encourage genuine settlements andsection 482of 

         the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, enables the 

         High   Court   to   pass   such   orders.It   would   be 

         beneficial to reproduce the relevant observations 

         and   findings   of   the   Apex   Court   in   the   case   ofGian Singh(supra), which read as under :"53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings 
         on the ground of settlement between an offender 
         and victim is not the same thing as compounding  
         of   offence.   They   are   different   and   not 
         interchangeable. Strictly speaking, the power of 
         compounding   of   offences   given   to   a   court   underSection   320is   materially   different   from   the  
         quashing   of   criminal   proceedings   by   the   High  
         Court   in   exercise   of   its   inherent   jurisdiction. 
         In compounding of offences, power of a criminal 
         court   is   circumscribed   by   the   provisions 
         contained inSection 320and the court is guided  
         solely and squarely thereby while, on the other 
         hand, the formation of opinion by the High Court  
         for   quashing   a   criminal   offence   or   criminal 
         proceeding or criminal complaint is guided by the 
         material   on   record   as   to   whether   the   ends   of 
         justice   would   justify   such   exercise   of   power  
         although   the   ultimate   consequence   may   be 
         acquittal or dismissal of indictment.54. Where   High   Court   quashes   a   criminal 
         proceeding having regard to the fact that dispute 
         between the offender and victim has been settled 
         although   offences   are   not   compoundable,   it   doesPage 3 of 5HC-NIC                          Page 3 of 5        Created On Fri Aug 12 02:50:04 IST 2016
            R/CR.MA/19655/2016                                                ORDER



         so   as   in   its   opinion,   continuation   of   criminal 
         proceedings will be an exercise in  futility and 
         justice   in   the   case   demands   that   the   dispute 
         between the parties is put to an end and peace is  
         restored; securing the ends of justice being the 
         ultimate   guiding   factor.   No   doubt,   crimes   are 
         acts which have harmful effect on the public and  
         consist   in   wrong   doing   that   seriously   endangers 
         and threatens well­being of society and it is not 
         safe to leave the crimedoer only because he and  
         the victim have settled the dispute amicably or 
         that the victim has been paid compensation, yet 
         certain   crimes   have   been   made   compoundable   in 
         law, with or without permission of the Court. In  
         respect   of   serious   offences   like   murder,   rape,  
         dacoity,   etc;   or   other   offences   of   mental 
         depravity   underIPCor   offences   of   moral 
         turpitude under special statutes, likePrevention 
         of   Corruption   Actor   the   offences   committed   by 
         public   servants   while   working   in   that   capacity, 
         the   settlement   between   offender   and   victim   can  
         have no legal sanction at all. However, certain 
         offences   which   overwhelmingly   and   predominantly 
         bear   civil   flavour   having   arisen   out   of   civil, 
         mercantile, commercial, financial, partnership or 
         such   like   transactions   or   the   offences   arising  
         out of matrimony, particularly relating to dowry, 
         etc.   or   the   family   dispute,   where   the   wrong   is  
         basically to victim and the offender and victim 
         have settled all disputes between them amicably, 
         irrespective of the fact that such offences have 
         not   been   made   compoundable,   the   High   Court   may 
         within the framework of its inherent power, quash 
         the criminal proceeding or criminal complaint or 
         F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the face of such  
         settlement,there   is   hardly   any   likelihood   of 
         offender being convicted and by not quashing the 
         criminal   proceedings,   justice   shall   be   casualty 
         and ends of justice shall be defeated. The above  
         list   is   illustrative   and   not   exhaustive.   Each 
         case will depend on its own facts and no hard and  
         fast category can be prescribed."Page 4 of 5HC-NIC                          Page 4 of 5        Created On Fri Aug 12 02:50:04 IST 2016
                     R/CR.MA/19655/2016                                                     ORDER5.  For the foregoing reasons and in view of the 

                  decisions of the Apex Court in the case ofGian  

                  Singh(supra),   the   present   application   succeeds 

                  and the same is, accordingly, allowed in view of 

                  an amicable settlement arrived at by and between 

                  the   parties.   The  first   information   report   being 

                  C.R.No.I­85                of         2016              registered                       with 

                  Pradhyumannagar   police   station,   Rajkot    and   all 

                  the proceedings emanating therefrom, are quashed 

                  and set aside.Direct Service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

         Report   being   C.R.No.I­65   of   2016   registered   with   Kalol 

         Taluka   police   station,   District:   Gandhinagar   for   the 

         offences   punishable   undersections   465,467,468,471,120Band114of the Indian Penal Code.2.   Complainant is before this Court.  It is urged that 

         the   parties   have   arrived   at   an   amicable   settlement. 

         The   respondent   No.3   has   filed   her   affidavit   dated 

         28.6.2016,   in   support   of   the   plea   of   quashment   by 

         stating   therein   that   she   has   amicably   settled   thePage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 5      Created On Sun Jul 03 03:27:04 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/14335/2016                                             ORDER



         matter with the applicants and wants to withdraw the 

         first information report in question. It is submitted 

         that because of the intervention of the elderly people 

         and relative the settlement could be arrived at and, 

         therefore, the grievances between the parties do not 

         survive any more.3.   The learned advocate Mr. Karia appearing for the 

         respondent No.3 confirms the aspect of settlement by 

         and between the parties.4.   He   urges   that   he   may   be   permitted   to   file   his 

         Vakalatnama   on   behalf   of   the   respondent   No.3   during 

         the   course   of   the   day.   Permission   as   prayed   for   is 

         granted.5.   Having considered the submissions made on behalf 

         of both the sides and the fact that it is a private 

         dispute   and  the   parties  have   arrived   at   an   amicable 

         settlement,   especially   when   the   respondent   No.3   has 

         chosen to put an end to the matter, no cause survives 

         and,   therefore,   it   would   be   desirable   to   quash   the 

         first  information  report   in   view  of  the   decision   of 

         the Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh v. State ofPage 2 of 5HC-NIC                                Page 2 of 5      Created On Sun Jul 03 03:27:04 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/14335/2016                                             ORDER



         Punjab and another, reported in AIR 2012 SC (Supp.)  

         838,  whereby  it is  held that it is the duty of the 

         Courts   to   encourage   genuine   settlements   andsection 

         482of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, enables 

         the   High   Court   to   pass   such   orders.   It   would   be 

         beneficial to reproduce the relevant observations and 

         findings of the Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh  

         (supra), which read as under :"53.   Quashing   of   offence   or   criminal 
              proceedings on the ground of settlement between  
              an offender and victim is not the same thing as  
              compounding of offence. They are different and 
              not   interchangeable.   Strictly   speaking,   the 
              power   of   compounding   of   offences   given   to   a 
              court underSection 320is materially different  
              from   the   quashing   of   criminal   proceedings   by 
              the   High   Court   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
              jurisdiction. In compounding of offences, power 
              of   a   criminal   court   is   circumscribed   by   the  
              provisions   contained   inSection   320and   the 
              court   is   guided   solely   and   squarely   thereby 
              while,   on   the   other   hand,   the   formation   of 
              opinion   by   the   High   Court   for   quashing   a 
              criminal   offence   or   criminal   proceeding   or  
              criminal complaint is guided by the material on 
              record as to whether the ends of justice would 
              justify   such   exercise   of   power   although   the 
              ultimate   consequence   may   be   acquittal   or 
              dismissal of indictment.54.    Where   High   Court   quashes   a   criminal 
              proceeding   having   regard   to   the   fact   that 
              dispute   between   the   offender   and   victim   has 
              been   settled   although   offences   are   not 
              compoundable,   it   does   so   as   in   its   opinion,  
              continuation of criminal proceedings will be an  
              exercise   in   futility   and   justice   in   the   case  
              demands that the dispute between the parties is 
              put to an end and peace is restored; securingPage 3 of 5HC-NIC                               Page 3 of 5      Created On Sun Jul 03 03:27:04 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/14335/2016                                             ORDER



              the ends of justice being the ultimate guiding 
              factor.   No   doubt,   crimes   are   acts   which   have  
              harmful   effect   on   the   public   and   consist   in 
              wrong   doing   that   seriously   endangers   and 
              threatens well­being  of society and it is not 
              safe to leave the crimedoer only because he and  
              the victim have settled the dispute amicably or 
              that the victim has been paid compensation, yet 
              certain crimes have been made compoundable in  
              law, with or without permission of the Court. 
              In   respect   of   serious   offences   like   murder, 
              rape, dacoity, etc; or other offences of mental 
              depravity   underIPCor   offences   of   moral  
              turpitude   under   special   statutes,   likePrevention   of   Corruption   Actor   the   offences 
              committed by public servants while working in  
              that capacity, the settlement between offender 
              and victim can have no legal sanction at all. 
              However, certain offences which overwhelmingly 
              and   predominantly   bear   civil   flavour   having 
              arisen   out   of   civil,   mercantile,   commercial, 
              financial,   partnership   or   such   like 
              transactions   or   the   offences   arising   out   of 
              matrimony, particularly relating to dowry, etc. 
              or   the   family   dispute,   where   the   wrong   is 
              basically to victim and the offender and victim 
              have   settled   all   disputes   between   them 
              amicably,   irrespective   of   the   fact   that   such 
              offences have not been made compoundable, the  
              High   Court   may   within   the   framework   of   its 
              inherent   power,   quash   the   criminal   proceeding  
              or   criminal   complaint   or   F.I.R   if   it   is 
              satisfied   that   on   the   face   of   such 
              settlement,there   is   hardly   any   likelihood   of 
              offender   being   convicted   and   by   not   quashing 
              the   criminal   proceedings,   justice   shall   be  
              casualty and ends of justice shall be defeated. 
              The   above   list   is   illustrative   and   not  
              exhaustive.   Each   case   will   depend   on   its   own  
              facts   and   no   hard   and   fast   category   can   be 
              prescribed."6.   For   the   foregoing   reasons   and   in   view   of   the 

         decisions of the Apex Court in the case of Gian SinghPage 4 of 5HC-NIC                               Page 4 of 5      Created On Sun Jul 03 03:27:04 IST 2016
                    R/CR.MA/14335/2016                                             ORDER



         (supra), the present application succeeds and the same 

         is,   accordingly,   allowed   in   view   of   an   amicable 

         settlement arrived at by and between the parties. The 

         first   information   report  being  C.R.No.I­65   of   2016 

         registered with Kalol Taluka police station, District:Gandhinagar            and   all   the   proceedings   emanating 

         therefrom, are quashed and set aside.Direct Service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

              CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                                 FIR/ORDER) NO. 3302 of 2016
         ==========================================================
                     JANAK RAMANLAL JOSHI & 1....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                      STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR VIRAT G POPAT, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 2
         Mr.J.K.Shah, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================
                 CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                      Date : 10/02/2016


                                        ORAL ORDER1.    Rule returnable today. Learned APP Mr.J.K.Shah
         waives service of notice of rule for and on behalf of
         the respondent No.1-State.2.    This       application has been preferred                                by the
         applicants for quashment of the complaint being I-
         CR No. 27 of 2012                registered with Bopal Police
         Station for the offences punishable underSections
         406,409,417,420,294-B,506(2),34,35,114and120-Bof the Indian Penal Code, which culminated
         eventually into criminal case No. 5641 of 2012. It is
         urged that the parties have amicably settled the
         disputes. There are no other                         victims who could
         have been affected, since this being case which isPage 1 of 4HC-NIC                                  Page 1 of 4      Created On Sat Feb 27 23:29:54 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/3302/2016                                                  ORDER



         exclusively       between            the         private          parties.            The
         impugned FIR              and    criminal case deserves to be
         quashed and set aside .3.   Mr.Virat Popat, learned advocate appearing for
         the applicant has sought to rely upon decision of
         the Apex Court rendered in case ofGian Singh Vs.
         State of Punjab and Anotherreported in 2012
         (10)SCC 303 to harp                      upon the requirement to
         quash on the ground that                            this is a                 dispute
         between the private parties which has nothing to
         do with any public offices or properties. He further
         urged that the affidavit of the parties having settled
         the disputes has already been places on record.4.   Mr.J.K.Shah, learned APP has ascertained from
         the concerned Investigating Officer that there are
         no other victims of the complaints in question.5.   Ms.Panna Bhalla, learned advocate appears for
         the complainant and confirms the contents of the
         affidavit, which is before this Court.6.   The dispute is essentially between the two
         private parties. Bearing in mind the decision ofGian
         Singh(Supra), his request to quash the FIR needs
         to be acceded to. It is essential to reproduce the
         relevant paragraph for this purpose:-61.   The   position   that   emerges   from   the   abovePage 2 of 4HC-NIC                                   Page 2 of 4      Created On Sat Feb 27 23:29:54 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/3302/2016                                              ORDER


              discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the  
              High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR  
              or   complaint   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
              jurisdiction   is   distinct   and   different   from   the 
              power given to a criminal court for compounding the  
              offences   underSection   320of   the   Code.   Inherent 
              power   is   of   wide   plenitude   with   no   statutory 
              limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with 
              the guideline  engrafted  in  such  power  viz;  (i)  to 
              secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse  
              of the process of any Court. In what cases power to 
              quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R 
              may be exercised where the offender and victim have  
              settled their dispute would depend on the facts and  
              circumstances  of  each  case  and  no category  can  be 
              prescribed. However, before exercise of such power, 
              the High Court must have due regard to the nature 
              and   gravity   of   the   crime.   Heinous   and   serious  
              offences   of   mental   depravity   or   offences   like 
              murder,   rape,   dacoity,   etc.   cannot   be   fittingly 
              quashed even though the victim or victims family and 
              the offender have settled the dispute. Such offences 
              are not private in nature and have serious impact on 
              society.   Similarly,   any   compromise   between   the 
              victim   and   offender   in   relation   to   the   offences 
              under special statutes likePrevention of Corruption 
              Actor   the   offences   committed   by   public   servants 
              while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide 
              for   any   basis   for   quashing   criminal   proceedings 
              involving   such   offences.   But   the   criminal   cases 
              having   overwhelmingly   and   predominatingly   civil 
              flavour stand on different footing for the purposes 
              of quashing, particularly the offences arising from 
              commercial,   financial,   mercantile,   civil, 
              partnership   or   such   like   transactions   or   the 
              offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, 
              etc.   or   the   family   disputes   where   the   wrong   is 
              basically   private   or   personal   in   nature   and   the  
              parties have resolved their entire dispute. In this 
              category   of   cases,   High   Court   may   quash   criminal 
              proceedings   if   in   its   view,   because   of   the 
              compromise   between   the   offender   and   victim,   the 
              possibility   of   conviction   is   remote   and   bleak   and 
              continuation of criminal case would put accused to 
              great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice 
              would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal  
              case   despite   full   and   complete   settlement   and 
              compromise with the victim. In other words, the High 
              Court  must  consider  whether  it  would  be unfair  or 
              contrary to the interest of justice to continue with 
              the   criminal   proceeding   or   continuation   of   the 
              criminal   proceeding   would   tantamount   to   abuse   of 
              process   of   law   despite   settlement   and   compromise 
              between   the   victim   and   wrongdoer   and   whether   toPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                         Page 3 of 4      Created On Sat Feb 27 23:29:54 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/3302/2016                                               ORDER


                       secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that 
                       criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to  
                       the   above   question(s)   is   in   affirmative,   the   High 
                       Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash 
                       the criminal proceeding.7.     This being a complaint resulting into monetary
         loss to the complainant which has been made good
         by the applicant and both the sides have confirmed
         the     truthfulness         of     contents             of       compromise.
         Resultantly, petition is allowed. The FIR being CR
         No. I-27 of 2012 registered with Bopal Police Station
         stands quashed.7.     All the consequential proceedings also stand
         quashed and set-aside.8.     Rule     is     made absolute.                 Direct          service             is
         permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

         CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR REGULAR BAIL) NO. 24193 of 2015

         MR KP RAVAL, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1

                 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE Z.K.SAIYED

                                      Date : 05/02/2016


                                       ORAL ORDER1.    This   Application   has   been   preferred   underSection   439of   the   Code   of   Criminal   Procedure, 
         1973   in   connection   with   the   offence   being   CR 
         No.I­70   of   2015   registered   with   Surendranagar 
         City   Police   Station,   Surendranagar   for   the 
         offencesu/s.302,394,365,323,120(B)and34of 
         the IPC andu/s.135of the Gujarat Police Act.2.    Heard Mr.E.E.Saiyed, learned counsel for the 
         applicant.   He   has   contended   that   present 
         applicant   has   not   committed   any   offence   as 
         alleged  against  him.  He has  contended  that  only 
         allegation   against   the   present   applicant   is   he 
         was present in the muddamal car which was used by 
         the   co­accused   in   the   murder.   He   has   contendedPage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                  Page 1 of 5      Created On Sat Feb 06 02:35:36 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/24193/2015                                            ORDER



         that   no   direct   evidence   against   the   present 
         applicant   is   produced   by   the   Investigating 
         Agency.   He   has   read   panchnama   of   physical 
         condition of the present applicant and contended 
         that   no   injury   is   shown   on   the   body   of   the 
         present applicant. He has contended that from the 
         clothes   of   the   present   applicant   blood   of   "B" 
         group was found and deceased blood group is also 
         of   "B"   group.   He   has   contended   that   applicant 
         blood   group   is   also   of   "B"   group.   He   has 
         contended   that   no   overact   is   attributed   in   the 
         charge­sheet   to   the   present   applicant.   He   has 
         contended   that   simple   presence   in   the   muddamal 
         car is not the ground to keep present applicant 
         behind   the   bar.   He   has   contended   that   the 
         applicant will be available for interrogation and 
         will  remain  present  during  the  trial  before  the 
         trial  Court.   The applicant  will  not tamper   with 
         the   evidence.   He   has   prayed   to   grant   bail   to 
         present applicant.3.   Heard   Mr.K.P.Raval,   learned   APP   for   the 
         respondent   -   State.   He   has   vehemently   opposed 
         bail application. He has read charge­sheet papers 
         as   well   as   circumstantial   evidence   produced   on 
         record   in   the   form   of   serological   report   and 
         contended   that   blood   group   "B"   of   deceased   is 
         found  from  the  clothes  of present  applicant.  He 
         has   contended   that   as   per   say   of   thePage 2 of 5HC-NIC                               Page 2 of 5      Created On Sat Feb 06 02:35:36 IST 2016

                     present with the details qua the criminal 
                     antecedents of the applicants herein along

              the   Investigating   Officer   submits   that   none   of

              Ganatra   named   in   the   FIR   being   I­C.R.

              1973, the applicants have sought for quashment of

              09.07.2016, in  support of the plea of quashmentPage 2 of 7HC-NIC                               Page 2 of 7      Created On Wed Jul 20 01:06:20 IST 2016

              by stating  therein that he has amicably settled 

              the   matter   with   the   applicants   and   wants   to 

              withdraw   the   first   information   report   in 

              question.   It   is  submitted   that   because   of   the 

              intervention of the  family members and relatives

         in the case ofGian Singh v. State of Punjab and

         observations   and   findings   of   the   Apex   Court   in 

         the   case   ofGian   Singh(supra),   which   read   as 

         under :"53.   Quashing   of   offence   or   criminal 
                proceedings   on   the   ground   of   settlement 
                between an offender and victim is not the  
                same thing as compounding of offence. They 
                are   different   and   not   interchangeable. 
                Strictly   speaking,   the   power   of 
                compounding  of offences given to a court  
                underSection  320is materially different 
                from the quashing of criminal proceedings 
                by   the   High  Court   in   exercise   of   its 
                inherent  jurisdiction.   In   compounding   of 
                offences,     power   of   a   criminal   court   is 
                circumscribed by the provisions contained 
                inSection   320and   the   court   is   guided 
                solely and squarely thereby while, on the 
                other   hand,   the   formation   of   opinion   by 
                the   High   Court   for   quashing   a   criminal  
                offence or criminal proceeding or criminal 
                complaint   is   guided   by   the   material   on  
                record as to whether the ends of justice 
                would   justify   such   exercise     of   power 
                although   the   ultimate   consequence  may   be 
                acquittal or dismissal of indictment.54.   Where   High   Court   quashes   a   criminalPage 4 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 4 of 7      Created On Wed Jul 20 01:06:20 IST 2016

              proceeding having regard to the fact that 
              dispute   between   the   offender   and   victim 
              has been settled although offences are not 
              compoundable,   it   does   so   as   in   its 
              opinion,   continuation   of   criminal 
              proceedings   will   be   an   exercise   in 
              futility and justice in the case demands  
              that   the   dispute   between   the  parties   is 
              put   to   an   end   and   peace   is  restored;

              ultimate guiding factor. No doubt, crimes 
              are acts which have harmful effect on the 
              public   and   consist   in   wrong   doing   that  
              seriously   endangers   and   threatens 
              wellbeing of society and it is not safe to 
              leave   the  crimedoer   only   because   he   and 
              the   victim   have   settled   the   dispute 
              amicably or that the victim has been paid  
              compensation, yet certain crimes have been 
              made compoundable  in law, with or without 
              permission   of   the   Court.   In   respect   of  
              serious   offences   like   murder,   rape,

              certain offences which overwhelmingly and 
              predominantly   bear   civil   flavour   having 
              arisen   out   of   civil,   mercantile, 
              commercial, financial, partnership or such 
              like transactions or the offences arising 
              out of matrimony, particularly relating to 
              dowry, etc. or the family dispute, where 
              the wrong is basically to victim and the 
              offender   and   victim   have   settled   all 
              disputes   between   them   amicably, 
              irrespective   of   the   fact   that   such 
              offences have not been made compoundable, 
              the High Court may within the framework of 
              its   inherent   power,   quash   the  criminal 
              proceeding or criminal complaint or  F.I.R 
              if   it   is   satisfied   that   on   the   face   ofPage 5 of 7HC-NIC                        Page 5 of 7      Created On Wed Jul 20 01:06:20 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/16827/2016                                            ORDER



                     such   settlement,there   is   hardly   any 
                     likelihood of offender being convicted and 
                     by not quashing the criminal proceedings, 
                     justice   shall   be   casualty   and   ends   of 
                     justice shall be defeated. The above list 
                     is   illustrative   and   not   exhaustive.   Each 
                     case will depend on its own facts and no 
                     hard and fast category can be prescribed."7.In   light   of   the   above   observations   of   the   Apex

              heinous   offences   showing   extreme   depravity   nor

              decisions of the Apex Court in the case ofGian

                    R/CR.MA/16827/2016                                            ORDER



                 set   aside   qua   the   present   applicants.  Rule   is

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

              CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                                FIR/ORDER) NO. 14942 of 2016

         ==========================================================
                  GORDHANBHAI RUDABHAI PATEL & 2....Applicant(s)
                                   Versus
                     STATE OF GUJARAT & 2....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR NIRAL R MEHTA, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 3
         MR. JAYNEEL S PARIKH, ADVOCATE for the Respondent(s) No. 3
         MR RONAK RAVAL, ADDL.PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No.
         1
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                      Date : 29/06/2016


                                       ORAL ORDER1.   Applicants   have   filed   this   application   for 

         quashment   of   the   First   Information   Report   being 

         C.R.No.I­16 of 2016 registered with Vivekanand Nagar 

         police station, Ahmedabad for the offences punishable 

         undersections   465,467,468,181and114of   the 

         Indian Penal Code.2.   Investigating   Officer   is   present.   There   are   no 

         criminal antecedents against the applicants. There is 

         no tempering with the Government documents. What wasPage 1 of 4HC-NIC                                  Page 1 of 4      Created On Wed Jul 06 00:24:07 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/14942/2016                                            ORDER



         produced was an affidavit which was correct and this 

         being essentially a dispute between the private party 

         in relation to the share in the property, they have 

         chosen to end it by way of a compromise.3.   Learned   advocate   Mr.   Parikh   for   respondent   No.3 

         has   confirmed   the  contents  of  the   affidavit   so   also 

         the aspect of settlement by and between the parties.4.   Having considered the submissions made on behalf 
         of both the sides and the fact that it is a private 
         dispute   and  the   parties  have   arrived   at   an   amicable 
         settlement,   especially   when   the   respondent   No.3   has 
         chosen to put an end to the matter, no cause survives 
         and,   therefore,   it   would   be   desirable   to   quash   the 
         first  information  report   in   view  of  the   decision   of 
         the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh v. State of  
         Punjab and another, reported in AIR 2012 SC (Supp.)  
         838,  whereby  it is  held that it is the duty of the 
         Courts   to   encourage   genuine   settlements   andsection 
         482of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, enables 
         the   High   Court   to   pass   such   orders.It   would   be 
         beneficial to reproduce the relevant observations and 
         findings of the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra), which read as under :"53.   Quashing   of   offence   or   criminal 
              proceedings   on   the   ground   of   settlement  
              between an offender and victim is not the same  
              thing   as   compounding   of   offence.   They   are 
              different   and   not   interchangeable.   Strictly 
              speaking, the power of compounding of offencesPage 2 of 4HC-NIC                               Page 2 of 4      Created On Wed Jul 06 00:24:07 IST 2016
            R/CR.MA/14942/2016                                            ORDER



         given   to   a   court   underSection   320is 
         materially   different   from   the   quashing   of  
         criminal   proceedings   by   the   High   Court   in 
         exercise   of   its   inherent   jurisdiction.   In  
         compounding   of   offences,   power   of   a   criminal 
         court   is   circumscribed   by   the   provisions 
         contained   inSection   320and   the   court   is 
         guided   solely   and   squarely   thereby   while,   on 
         the   other   hand,   the   formation   of   opinion   by 
         the High Court for quashing a criminal offence 
         or   criminal   proceeding   or   criminal   complaint 
         is   guided   by   the   material   on   record   as   to 
         whether the ends of justice would justify such 
         exercise   of   power   although   the   ultimate  
         consequence   may   be   acquittal   or   dismissal   of 
         indictment.54. Where   High   Court   quashes   a   criminal  
         proceeding   having   regard   to   the   fact   that 
         dispute   between   the   offender   and   victim   has 
         been   settled   although   offences   are   not  
         compoundable,   it   does   so   as   in   its   opinion, 
         continuation   of   criminal   proceedings   will   be 
         an   exercise   in   futility   and   justice   in   the 
         case   demands   that   the   dispute   between   the 
         parties   is   put   to   an   end   and   peace   is 
         restored;   securing   the   ends   of   justice   being 
         the ultimate guiding factor. No doubt, crimes 
         are   acts   which   have   harmful   effect   on   the 
         public   and   consist   in   wrong   doing   that 
         seriously   endangers   and   threatens   well­being 
         of   society   and   it   is   not   safe   to   leave   the  
         crimedoer only because he and the victim have 
         settled   the   dispute   amicably   or   that   the 
         victim has been paid compensation, yet certain 
         crimes   have   been   made   compoundable   in   law, 
         with   or   without   permission   of   the   Court.   In 
         respect of serious offences like murder, rape, 
         dacoity,   etc;   or   other   offences   of   mental 
         depravity   underIPCor   offences   of   moral 
         turpitude   under   special   statutes,   likePrevention   of   Corruption   Actor   the   offences 
         committed by public servants while working in 
         that capacity, the settlement between offender 
         and victim can have no legal sanction at all. 
         However, certain offences which overwhelmingly 
         and   predominantly   bear   civil   flavour   havingPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                          Page 3 of 4      Created On Wed Jul 06 00:24:07 IST 2016
                     R/CR.MA/14942/2016                                            ORDER



                  arisen   out   of   civil,   mercantile,   commercial, 
                  financial,   partnership   or   such   like 
                  transactions   or   the   offences   arising   out   of 
                  matrimony,   particularly   relating   to   dowry, 
                  etc. or the family dispute, where the wrong is  
                  basically   to   victim   and   the   offender   and 
                  victim have settled all disputes between them 
                  amicably,   irrespective   of   the   fact   that   such 
                  offences have not been made compoundable, the 
                  High   Court   may   within   the   framework   of   its 
                  inherent  power,   quash   the   criminal   proceeding  
                  or   criminal   complaint   or   F.I.R   if   it   is  
                  satisfied   that   on   the   face   of   such 
                  settlement,there   is   hardly   any   likelihood   of 
                  offender   being   convicted   and   by   not   quashing 
                  the   criminal   proceedings,   justice   shall   be  
                  casualty   and   ends   of   justice   shall   be 
                  defeated.   The   above   list   is   illustrative   and 
                  not   exhaustive.   Each   case   will   depend   on   its 
                  own facts and no hard and fast category can be  
                  prescribed.5.       For   the   foregoing   reasons   and   in   view   of   the 
         decisions of the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra), the present application succeeds and the same 
         is,   accordingly,   allowed   in   view   of   an   amicable 
         settlement arrived at by and between the parties. The 
         first   information   report  being  C.R.No.I­16   of   2016 
         registered   with   Vivekanand   Nagar   police   station, 
         Ahmedabad and all the proceedings emanating therefrom, 
         are   quashed   and   set   aside.   Rule   is   made   absolute 
         accordingly.Direct Service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

         altercation   and   other   sundry   matters   are   resolved

         grievance survives.5.   In   such   circumstances,   the   question   that   arises 
         as to whether the Court needs to quash the complaint 
         and permit the matter to be resolved and prosecution 
         to withdraw.Page 2 of 6HC-NIC                               Page 2 of 6      Created On Tue Aug 23 01:57:00 IST 2016

              of   power   although   the   ultimate   consequence

              proceeding   having   regard   to   the   fact   that 
              dispute between the offender and victim has 
              been   settled   although   offences   are   not 
              compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, 
              continuation of criminal proceedings will be

         ==========================================================
         Appearance:

         ==========================================================
         CORAM:             HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
                                  Date : 20/10/2016
                                            ORAL ORDER1.           This is a petition by the petitioner underArticle 226of the Constitution of Indian and underSection      482of     the    Code         of      Criminal            Procedure,
         seeking     quashment          of      the       complaint              being         I-C.R.
         No.17/2016, registered with Liliya Police Station
         underSections 363and366of the Indian Penal
         Code.2.           The       petitioner,               who         is       the        original
         accused, is following 'Islam' and that appears to
         be the main cause of resistance on the part of
         Respondent No.2 and his community.                                     The          parties
         have, however, chosen to amicably settle all their
         disputes now, and therefore, they have approached
         this    Court       seeking         termination                of      the       criminal
         prosecution pending between the parties.3.           Respondent No.2-the original complainant,
         namely Anandbhai Vibhabhai Shiroliya), who happensPage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                      Page 1 of 5        Created On Sat Dec 03 00:26:24 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/28017/2016                                                       ORDER




         to be the father of the prosecutrix, is present
         before this Court. Respondent No.2                                    stated that the
         prosecutrix was firstly engaged, when she was four
         years     of      age.              Thereafter,                 once          again,           her
         engagement took place. The prosecutrix has studied
         upto Standard-7.4.           The       prosecutrix                 is     also        brought            before
         this Court.            She apprehends any personal harm to
         her or a forcible marriage.5.           This        Court,            made            inquires              from          the
         prosecutrix and also made a request to the learned
         Advocate, Ms. Kruti Shah, who is present                                                in the
         Court, to assist the Court. As the prosecutrix is
         scared of her life and or of forcible marriage,
         Respondent No.2 shall FILE a pursis in the form of
         an    undertaking            before        this          Court         that        till        the
         prosecutrix          attains            the         age         of       majority,                 no
         marriage shall take place. She shall also not be
         forcibly married elsewhere.6.           Here,           it     may      also          be       noted         that         the
         prosecutrix had also shown her desire to talk to
         the     learned          Advocate,                 Ms.       Kruti           Shah,           over
         telephone         on         a    regular               basis          so        that          the
         prosecutrix can confide in her and can ventilate
         her grievances, if there arise any.7.           Since,           the     prosecutrix                   apprehends               that
         either she shall be done away or shall be forciblyPage 2 of 5HC-NIC                                        Page 2 of 5         Created On Sat Dec 03 00:26:24 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/28017/2016                                               ORDER




         married elsewhere, to ensure that no harm is caused
         to the prosecutrix either physically or otherwise,
         the IO concerned is directed to ENSURE her safety.
         Further,      a     lady     protection          officer           of      the       area
         concerned shall also visit the prosecutrix EVERY
         WEEK and shall ensure her protection.8.            The aforesaid arrangement shall continue
         for a period of SIX MONTHS from today.9.            Under the circumstances, here, it would be
         profitable to refer to the observations made by the
         Hon'ble Apex Court in the case ofGIAN SINGH VS.
         STATE    OF       PUNJAB     AND    ANR.,         (2012)          10      SCC        303,
         wherein, at Paragraph-61, the Apex Court observed
         as under;"61. The position that emerges from
                             the above discussion can be summarised
                             thus: the power of the High Court in
                             quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR
                             or   complaint   in   exercise  of  its
                             inherent jurisdiction is distinct and
                             different from the power given to a
                             criminal court for compounding the
                             offences underSection 320of the
                             Code.   Inherent   power   is  of  wide
                             plenitude with no statutory limitation
                             but it has to be exercised in accord
                             with the guideline engrafted in such
                             power viz.,(i)to secure the ends of
                             justice or (ii)     to prevent abuse of
                             the process of any Court. In what
                             cases power to quash the criminal
                             proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may
                             be exercised where the offender andPage 3 of 5HC-NIC                                  Page 3 of 5       Created On Sat Dec 03 00:26:24 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/28017/2016                                            ORDER



                     victim have settled their dispute
                     would   depend     on    the     facts   and
                     circumstances of each case and no
                     category can be prescribed. However,
                     before exercise of such power, the
                     High Court must have due regard to the
                     nature and gravity of the crime.
                     Heinous and serious offences of mental
                     depravity or offences like murder,
                     rape,    dacoity,      etc.     cannot    be
                     fittingly quashed even though the
                     victim or victim's family and the
                     offender have settled the dispute.
                     Such offences are not private in
                     nature and have serious impact on
                     society.    Similarly,    any     compromise
                     between the victim and offender in
                     relation to the offences under special
                     statutes likePrevention of Corruption
                     Actor the offences committed by
                     public servants while working in that
                     capacity etc; cannot provide for any
                     basis      for      quashing        criminal
                     proceedings involving such offences.But    the    criminal      cases     having
                     overwhelmingly     and    pre-dominatingly
                     civil   flavour     stand    on    differentfooting for the purposes of quashing,
                     particularly the offences arising from
                     commercial,     financial,       mercantile,
                     civil,    partnership     or     such   like
                     transactions or the offences arising
                     out of matrimony relating to dowry,
                     etc. or the family disputes where the
                     wrong is basically private or personal
                     in   nature    and    the    parties    have
                     resolved their entire dispute. In this
                     category of cases, High Court may
                     quash criminal proceedings if in its
                     view,   because     of    the     compromise
                     between the offender and victim, the
                     possibility of conviction is remote
                     and bleak and continuation of criminal
                     case   would    put   accused     to   great
                     oppression and prejudice and extremePage 4 of 5HC-NIC                        Page 4 of 5      Created On Sat Dec 03 00:26:24 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/28017/2016                                            ORDER



                             injustice would be caused to him by
                             not quashing the criminal case despite
                             full   and   complete  settlement   and
                             compromise with the victim. In other
                             words, the High Court must consider
                             whether it would be unfair or contrary
                             to the interest of justice to continue
                             with   the   criminal   proceeding   or
                             continuation     of    the     criminal
                             proceeding would tantamount to abuse
                             of process of law despite settlement
                             and compromise between the victim and
                             wrongdoer and whether to secure the
                             ends of justice, it is appropriate
                             that criminal case is put to an end
                             and if the answer to the above
                             question(s) is in affirmative, the
                             High Court shall be well within its
                             jurisdiction to quash the criminal
                             proceeding."10.          In the result, while QUASHING the impugned
         complaint with all consequential proceedings, the
         matter is kept ALIVE to ensure the safety of the
         prosecutrix.11.          At this stage, this Court places on record
         the services rendered by the learned Advocate, Ms.
         Kruti Shah.12.          S.O. to 22ND NOVEMBER, 2016. Direct service
         is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)
