         ==========================================================

         CORAM        HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
             :

                                      Date : 02/05/2016


                                        ORAL ORDER1. A  first information report  came to be lodged by 

              the respondent No.3 against the applicants being 

              I­C.R.No.43   of   2016   registered   with   Deesa   Rural 

              Police Station, Deesa, for commission of offences 

              punishable   undersections   323,504,506(2),366and114of   the   Indian   Penal   Code,   1860   andsection   3(1)(x)of   the   Scheduled   Castes   and 

              Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 

              1989. The applicants have prayed for quashment of 

              the said  first information report  on the groundPage 1 of 6HC-NIC                                  Page 1 of 6      Created On Thu May 05 01:45:26 IST 2016
               R/CR.MA/9738/2016                                           ORDER



           of an amicable settlement arrived by and between 

           the parties.2. RULE.   The   formal   service   of   notice   of   Rule   is 

           waived by the learned counsel appearing for the 

           respective   respondents.   The   Rule   is   fixed 

           forthwith on consent.3. By   way   of   present   application   preferred   undersection   482of   the   Code   of   Criminal   Procedure, 

           1973, the applicant has sought for quashment of 

           the   said  first   information   report  by   entering 

           into a compromise with the respondent No.3. The 

           respondent   No.3   has   filed   his   affidavit   dated 

           April   19,   2016,   in   support   of   the   plea   of 

           quashment   by   stating   therein   that   due   to 

           intervention of respected members of the society 

           and family members of both the sides, the parties 

           have amicably arrived at an amicable settlement. 

           Therefore,   their   grievances   do   not   survive   any 

           more.4. The learned counsel appearing for the respondent 

           No.3­original complainant confirms the aspect of 

           settlement by and between the parties.Page 2 of 6HC-NIC                            Page 2 of 6      Created On Thu May 05 01:45:26 IST 2016
               R/CR.MA/9738/2016                                              ORDERHe   urges   that   he   may   be   permitted   to 

          file his Vakalatnama on behalf of the respondent 

          No.3 during the course of the day. Permission as 

          prayed for is granted.5.Having considered the submissions made on behalf 

          of   both   the   sides   and   the   fact   that   it   is   a 

          private dispute and the parties have arrived at 

          an   amicable   settlement,   especially   when   the 

          respondent No.3 has chosen to put an end to the 

          entire dispute, no cause survives and, therefore, 

          it   would   be   desirable   to   quash   the  first 

          information   report   in   view   of   the   decisions   of 

          the   Apex   Court   in   the   case   ofGian   Singh   v.  

          State   of   Punjab   and   another,   reported   in   AIR  

          2012 SC (Supp.) 838,  whereby it is held that it 

          is   the   duty   of   the   Courts   to   encourage   genuine 

          settlements   andsection   482of   the   Code   of 

          Criminal Procedure, 1973, enables the High Court 

          to   pass   such   orders.It   would   be   beneficial   to 

          reproduce the relevant observations and findings 

          of   the   Apex   Court   in   the   case   ofGian   Singh(supra), which read as under :53.   Quashing   of   offence   or   criminalPage 3 of 6HC-NIC                               Page 3 of 6      Created On Thu May 05 01:45:26 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/9738/2016                                             ORDER



             proceedings   on   the   ground   of   settlement 
             between   an   offender   and   victim   is   not   the 
             same   thing   as   compounding   of   offence.   They 
             are   different   and   not   interchangeable.Strictly speaking, the power of compounding 
             of   offences   given   to   a  court   under   Section 
             320   is   materially   different   from   the 
             quashing of criminal proceedings by the High 
             Court   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
             jurisdiction.   In   compounding   of   offences, 
             power   of   a   criminal   court   is   circumscribed 
             by   the   provisions   contained   in   Section   320 
             and the court is guided solely and squarely 
             thereby   while,   on   the   other   hand,   the 
             formation   of   opinion   by   the   High   Court   for 
             quashing   a   criminal   offence   or   criminal 
             proceeding   or   criminal   complaint   is   guided 
             by the material on record as to whether the  
             ends of justice would justify such exercise 
             of   power   although   the   ultimate   consequence 
             may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.54.      Where   High   Court   quashes   a   criminal 
             proceeding   having   regard   to   the   fact   that 
             dispute between the offender and victim has 
             been   settled   although   offences   are   not  
             compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, 
             continuation of criminal proceedings will be  
             an   exercise   in   futility   and   justice   in   the 
             case   demands   that   the   dispute   between   the 
             parties   is   put   to   an   end   and   peace   isPage 4 of 6HC-NIC                         Page 4 of 6      Created On Thu May 05 01:45:26 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/9738/2016                                           ORDER



             restored; securing the ends of justice being 
             the   ultimate   guiding   factor.   No   doubt,  
             crimes are acts which have harmful effect on  
             the   public   and   consist   in  wrong   doing   that 
             seriously endangers and threatens well­being  
             of society and it is not safe to leave the  
             crimedoer   only  because   he   and   the   victim 
             have   settled   the   dispute   amicably   or   that 
             the   victim   has   been   paid   compensation,   yet 
             certain   crimes   have   been   made   compoundable 
             in   law,   with   or   without   permission   of   the 
             Court.   In   respect   of   serious   offences   like 
             murder,   rape,   dacoity,   etc;   or   other 
             offences   of   mental   depravity   underIPCor 
             offences   of   moral   turpitude   under   special  
             statutes, likePrevention of Corruption Actor the offences committed by public servants 
             while   working   in   that   capacity,   the 
             settlement   between   offender   and   victim   can 
             have   no   legal   sanction   at   all.   However, 
             certain   offences   which   overwhelmingly   and 
             predominantly   bear   civil   flavour   having 
             arisen out of civil, mercantile, commercial,  
             financial,   partnership   or   such   like 
             transactions or the offences arising out of 
             matrimony,   particularly   relating   to   dowry, 
             etc. or the family dispute, where the wrong 
             is basically to victim and the offender and 
             victim   have   settled   all   disputes   between 
             them amicably, irrespective of the fact that 
             such   offences            have   not   been   madePage 5 of 6HC-NIC                       Page 5 of 6      Created On Thu May 05 01:45:26 IST 2016
                      R/CR.MA/9738/2016                                           ORDER



                         compoundable, the High Court may within the 
                         framework   of   its   inherent   power,   quash   the 
                         criminal proceeding or criminal complaint or  
                         F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the face of  
                         such   settlement,there   is   hardly   any 
                         likelihood  of   offender   being   convicted   and 
                         by   not   quashing   the   criminal   proceedings,  
                         justice   shall   be   casualty   and   ends   of 
                         justice shall be defeated. The above list is 
                         illustrative   and   not   exhaustive.   Each   case 
                         will depend on its own facts and no hard and  
                         fast category can be prescribed."4.For   the   foregoing   reasons   and   in   view   of   the 

                 decisions of the Apex Court in the case ofGian  

                 Singh(supra),   the   present   application   succeeds

                 I­C.R.No.43   of   2016   registered   with   Deesa   Rural 

                 Police   Station,   Deesa   and   all   the   proceedings 

                 emanating   therefrom,   are   quashed   and   set   aside.

                          MAHESH WALABHAI JALLU....Applicant(s)

         Appearance:
         MR A.D. SHAH, ADVOCATE WITH MR. NAYAN D PAREKH, ADVOCATE for

                                       ORAL ORDER(PER : HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE G.R.UDHWANI)1.           Rule. Ms. Maithili Mehta, learned Additional Public
         Prosecutor, waives service of notice of rule on behalf of the
         respondent.2.           By this application undersection 389of the Code of
         Criminal    Procedure,      1973,      the      applicant        seeks        bail        by
         suspension of the sentence dated 29.1.2013 passed by the
         learned 5th (Ad hoc) Additional Sessions Judge, Junagadh, in
         Sessions Case No. 57 of 2009 whereby the applicant originalPage 1 of 6HC-NIC                                  Page 1 of 6      Created On Wed Mar 16 01:15:38 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/24425/2015                                            ORDER




         accused No. 8 amongst others was sentenced to rigorous
         imprisonment, fine and default sentence for various offences
         punishable undersections 302read withsection 149,143,149,148of the Indian Penal Code and undersection 135of the
         Bombay Police Act.3.          At the outset, Mr. A.D. Shah, learned counsel for the
         applicant, pointed out that this is a successful bail application
         and that the earlier application came to be withdrawn on
         29.4.2013 and by now the applicant has already suffered a
         sentence of more than 6 years and 9 months. The learned
         counsel for the applicant referred to the medical evidence and
         submitted that, though, the members of the unlawful assembly
         were attributed with sharp cutting weapons, they were not
         used to inflict any injury and on the contrary, only blunt part of
         the weapons were used and thus, the applicant cannot be said
         to have intended to cause death of the deceased. Referring to
         the testimony of PW-26 Bharat Jinabhai, the complainant, it
         was contended that the names of the other assailants were
         disclosed by the witness but no name of the applicant was
         disclosed and it was not stated in the evidence that the two
         unknown     persons referred to by the complainant were known
         to him by name. It was argued that it was only by way of
         improvement in the statement of the complainant recorded on
         the next day that the witness came out with an improved
         version that he knew the said two unknown persons by names
         and thus, naming the applicant during the evidence and that
         too in response to a leading question put to him by the learned
         Additional Public Prosecutor to an affect as to what the witness
         had stated in his further statement, the applicant was sought
         to implicated, falsely. It was argued that in his testimony thePage 2 of 6HC-NIC                               Page 2 of 6      Created On Wed Mar 16 01:15:38 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/24425/2015                                                   ORDER




         witness did not assign any specific role or weapon to the
         applicant. Referring to the testimonies of PW-27 Jagmal Pooja -
         the son of the deceased and PW-28 Bhupatbhai Jinabhai, it was
         argued that the statements of both these witnesses were
         recorded    subsequent          to    the      improved            version          of    the
         complainant recorded by the police after lodgement of the
         complaint and thus, prima facie, it was established that the
         witnesses had intention to frame the applicant. It was also
         contended that the applicant pleaded and proved his alibi by
         showing his presence at a marriage party arranged by his
         distant relatives but the trial court unjustifiably rejected the
         alibi merely on the ground that the applicant had failed to
         prove that he was not present at the place other than the
         marriage party. It was argued that shifting of such a burden on
         the applicant was unwarranted and legally not sustainable.Referring to the medical evidence, the learned counsel for the
         applicant contended that except a solitary head injury, the
         other injuries were not on the vital part of the body of the
         deceased suggesting that the accused did not intend to kill
         him. The learned counsel for the applicant further argued that
         in any case even if the case of the prosecution is taken at its
         face value, the offence cannot be said to have been made out
         undersection 302of the Indian Penal Code. It was contended
         that under the aforesaid circumstances, the accused having
         suffered more than 6 years and 9 months in prison by now, he
         is entitled to bail. The learned counsel for the applicant has
         relied on the decision of the Apex Court in the case ofBalbir
         Singh v. State of Punjab and Haryana2005(9) SCC 299.4.          Ms.      Maithili    Mehta,            learned       Additional          Public
         Prosecutor, for the respondents invited the attention of thisPage 3 of 6HC-NIC                                    Page 3 of 6        Created On Wed Mar 16 01:15:38 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/24425/2015                                               ORDER




         court to the testimonies of the above two witnesses i.e. PW-26
         Bharat Jinabhai and PW-22 Doctor Tina Ukabhai and other
         corroborative evidence and contended that as against the plea
         of alibi advanced by the applicant, the version of the eye
         witness involved him in the serious offence and in absence of
         rebuttal by cogent evidence as held by the court below, the
         case beyond reasonable doubt was established against the
         applicant. It was argued that a cumulative effect of the injuries
         caused to the deceased resulted into his death.5.          Having considered the rival contentions and the
         evidence on record and being mindful of the fact that at this
         stage of the proceedings, the court is not required to
         reappreciate the evidence on record,. suffice it to say that,
         taking the prosecution case at its face value, the applicant was
         attributed with the use of stick and no specific role came to be
         assigned to him except an omnibus statement that all the
         accused were assaulting the deceased at random. The
         testimonies of the witnesses, particularly that of PW-26, the
         complainant,      in    not   naming         the   applicant         in     the      first
         information report though in the evidence and in his statement
         recorded undersection 161of the Code of Criminal Procedure
         he contended that he knew the applicant by name, prima
         facie, appears to be surrounded by clouds of doubt to an effect
         as to whether the witnesses are attempting to implicate the
         accused-applicant falsely. The plea of the applicant for alibi
         was not rejected on merits by the trial court i.e. the evidence
         of the defence witness establishing the said plea was not
         rejected but the only reason assigned by the trial court for
         rejecting the said plea was that the applicant has not proved
         that he was not present at a place other than the marriagePage 4 of 6HC-NIC                                  Page 4 of 6      Created On Wed Mar 16 01:15:38 IST 2016
                    R/CR.MA/24425/2015                                            ORDER




         party. Prima facie, the question arises as to whether rejection
         of the plea of alibi was warranted under the above reasoning
         by the trial court.6.             It is also noticed that the applicant has not been
         attributed with the injury on the deceased on his vital part of
         the body and except one injury on the head attributed to the
         members of the unlawful assembly, all other injuries were on
         the non-vital part of the body of the deceased. Therefore, the
         question that may arise in the appeal is as to whether such a
         case would amount to culpable homicide amounting to murder,
         in appeal. Prima facie, having regard to the facts discussed
         above as also almost the similar facts dealt with by the Apex
         Court inBalbir Singh's v. State of Punjab and Haryana(supra), it appears that the applicant has made out a prima
         facie case for suspension of the sentence and his release on
         bail.7.             The application, therefore, succeeds and is allowed
         accordingly. The sentence imposed by learned 5th (Ad hoc)
         Additional Sessions Judge, Junagadh, in Sessions Case No. 57
         of 2009 vide judgement and order dated 29.1.2013 is hereby
         ordered to be suspended from the date of enlargement of the
         applicant on bail till the final disposal of the appeal and
         accordingly the applicant is ordered to be enlarged on bail on
         his executing a personal bond of Rs. 20,000/- (Rupees twenty
         thousand only) and a surety of equal amount subject to the
         following terms and conditions:(a)     he shall not take undue advantage of his liberty or abuse
         his liberty;Page 5 of 6HC-NIC                                  Page 5 of 6      Created On Wed Mar 16 01:15:38 IST 2016
                    R/CR.MA/24425/2015                                            ORDER(b)     he shall maintain law and order;(c)     he shall surrender his passport, if any, to the lower court,
         within a week and if he does not possess a passport, he shall
         make a declaration to that effect before the trial court;(d)     If during the pendency of the criminal appeal any change
         in the residential address, permanent or temporary of the
         applicant takes place, then the concerned applicant shall
         intimate the same to the         trial       court    as     well      as      to     the
         concerned Police Station.8.             Bail before the trial court having jurisdiction.9.             It is, however, made clear that the observations in
         this order are only prima facie observations made for the
         purpose of deciding the bail application and the same shall
         have no bearing on the merits of the case at the time of final
         hearing of the appeal.10.             Rule is made absolute accordingly. Direct service is
         permitted.(HARSHA DEVANI, J.)

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

              CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                                FIR/ORDER) NO. 13678 of 2016

         ==========================================================
                  KANAKSINH PRABHATSINH JHALA & 1....Applicant(s)
                                    Versus
                      STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR IH SYED with MR.CHIRAG B UPADHYAY, ADVOCATES for the
         Applicant(s) No. 1 - 2
         MS CHETNA SHAH, ADDL. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s)
         No. 1
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                      Date : 17/06/2016


                                         ORAL ORDER1.   Applicants        herein     seek        quashment             of      the       First

         Information Report being C.R.No.I-38 of 2016 registered with

         Joravarnagar police station, Surendranagar for the offences

         punishable undersections 279and392of the Indian Penal

         Code andsection 177and184of the Motor Vehicles Act.2.   The parties have chosen to settle their disputes out of

         their own volition. The complainant has given his affidavit

         stating therein that due to intervention of leaders and

         respected members of the society, they have chosen to settlePage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 5      Created On Sun Jun 19 04:13:01 IST 2016
                     R/CR.MA/13678/2016                                              ORDER



         the disputes.3.     Learned advocate Mr.I.H.Syed appearing with learned

         advocate Mr.Chirag Upadhyay submits that the applicants

         have no criminal antecedents. The contents and reasons given

         in   the     affidavit-in-reply     have        been       verified        by     learned

         Additional Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1-State. It is

         confirmed by this Court that no coercion or duress is used for

         the complainant to arrive at such a settlement.4.     Having considered the submissions made on behalf of

         both the sides and the fact that it is a private dispute and the

         parties have arrived at an amicable settlement, especially

         when       respondent No.2 has chosen to put an end to the

         matter, no cause survives and, therefore, it would be desirable

         to quash the first information report in view of the decision of

         the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh v. State of Punjab

         and another, reported in AIR 2012 SC (Supp.) 838,

         whereby it is held that it is the duty of the Courts to encourage

         genuine settlements andsection 482of the Code of Criminal

         Procedure, 1973, enables the High Court to pass such orders.It

         would be beneficial to reproduce the relevant observations and

         findings of the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra),

         which read as under :Page 2 of 5HC-NIC                                     Page 2 of 5      Created On Sun Jun 19 04:13:01 IST 2016
            R/CR.MA/13678/2016                                                  ORDER



         "53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on the
         ground of settlement between an offender and victim is not
         the same thing as compounding of offence. They are
         different and not interchangeable. Strictly speaking, the
         power of compounding of offences given to a court under
         Section 320 is materially different from the quashing of
         criminal proceedings by the High Court in exercise of its
         inherent jurisdiction. In compounding of offences, power of
         a criminal court is circumscribed by the provisions
         contained in Section 320 and the court is guided solely and
         squarely thereby while, on the other hand, the formation of
         opinion by the High Court for quashing a criminal offence
         or criminal proceeding or criminal complaint is guided by
         the material on record as to whether the ends of justice
         would justify such exercise of power although the ultimate
         consequence may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.54.    Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding
         having regard to the fact that dispute between the offender
         and victim has been settled although offences are not
         compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, continuation of
         criminal proceedings will be an exercise in futility and
         justice in the case demands that the dispute between the
         parties is put to an end and peace is restored; securing the
         ends of justice being the ultimate guiding factor. No doubt,
         crimes are acts which have harmful effect on the public
         and consist in wrong doing that seriously endangers and
         threatens well-being of society and it is not safe to leave
         the crimedoer only because he and the victim have settled
         the dispute amicably or that the victim has been paid
         compensation,          yet   certain       crimes    have       been       made
         compoundable in law, with or without permission of the
         Court. In respect of serious offences like murder, rape,Page 3 of 5HC-NIC                                Page 3 of 5      Created On Sun Jun 19 04:13:01 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/13678/2016                                                       ORDER



              dacoity, etc; or other offences of mental depravity underIPCor offences of moral turpitude under special statutes,
              likePrevention of Corruption Actor the offences committed
              by public servants while working in that capacity, the
              settlement between offender and victim can have no legal
              sanction      at       all.   However,          certain      offences         which
              overwhelmingly           and    predominantly            bear      civil    flavour
              having arisen out of civil, mercantile, commercial, financial,
              partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising
              out of matrimony, particularly relating to dowry, etc. or the
              family dispute, where the wrong is basically to victim and
              the offender and victim have settled all disputes between
              them amicably, irrespective of the fact that such offences
              have not been made compoundable, the High Court may
              within the framework of its inherent power, quash the
              criminal proceeding or criminal complaint or F.I.R if it is
              satisfied that on the face of such settlement,there is hardly
              any likelihood of offender being convicted and by not
              quashing the criminal proceedings, justice shall be casualty
              and ends of justice shall be defeated. The above list is
              illustrative and not exhaustive. Each case will depend on its
              own facts and no hard and fast category can be
              prescribed."5.   For the foregoing reasons and in view of the decisions of

          CORAM:               HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
                                       Date : 09/08/2016
                                        ORAL ORDER1.           The        petitioner            has        approached                  this
         Court, seeking quashment of the complaint being
         I-C.R.     No.       14/2015      registered               with         Ambaliyara
         Police Station, Arvalli, underSections 363,366and376of the Indian Penal Code and Sections A-
         4, 6(H), 12 and 17 of theProtection of Children
         from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, which culminated
         into Sessions / Special Case (POCSO) No. 69 of
         2015, pending before the learned Special Sessions
         Judge, Himmatnagar, Sabarkantha.2.           The learned Advocate for the Petitioner,
         Mr.    Barot,        urged    that        the      petitioner                and       the
         prosecutrix, on her attaining the majority, have
         married with each other. Both the petitioner and
         the prosecutrix are present before this Court in
         person. The date of birth of the prosecutrix                                               is
         10.05.1998 and as such she is aged about 18 yearsPage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 5      Created On Fri Aug 12 02:07:26 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/12520/2016                                                   ORDER



         and 3 months, at present. Necessary documents in
         relation to the marriage of the prosecutrix with
         the petitioner have also been brought on record.
         The   prosecutrix            has      also        filed         an       affidavit,
         wherein,      she          has   supported             this         petition                by
         stating,      therein,           that          she      has         married             the
         petitioner out of her own free will and there is
         no threat or coercion to her.3.         This Court also made inquires from the
         prosecutrix         through         the        learned            APP        and        she
         vindicated the contents of her affidavit.4.In above view of the matter, here, it
         would be profitable to refer to the                                  observations
         made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of
         "GIAN SINGH VS. STATE OF PUNJAB AND ANR.", (2012)
         10 SCC 303, wherein, at Paragraph-61, the Apex
         Court observed as under;"61.    The position that emerges from
                      the above discussion can be summarised
                      thus: the power of the High Court in
                      quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR
                      or   complaint   in  exercise  of   its
                      inherent jurisdiction is distinct and
                      different from the power given to a
                      criminal court for compounding the
                      offences under Section 320 of the Code.
                      Inherent power is of wide plenitude
                      with no statutory limitation but it has
                      to be exercised in accord with the
                      guideline engrafted in such power viz;
                      (I) to secure the ends of justice orPage 2 of 5HC-NIC                                    Page 2 of 5      Created On Fri Aug 12 02:07:26 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/12520/2016                                             ORDER(ii) to prevent abuse of the process of
                any Court. In what cases power to quash
                the criminal proceeding or complaint or
                F.I.R   may    be   exercised     where   the
                offender and victim have settled their
                dispute would depend on the facts and
                circumstances of each case and no
                category can be prescribed. However,
                before exercise of such power, the High
                Court must have due regard to the
                nature   and    gravity   of    the    crime.Heinous and serious offences of mental
                depravity or offences like murder,
                rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly
                quashed even though the victim or
                victim's family and the offender have
                settled the dispute. Such offences are
                not private in nature and have serious
                impact   on    society.    Similarly,     any
                compromise    between    the    victim    and
                offender in relation to the offences
                under special statutes likePrevention
                of Corruption Actor the offences
                committed by public servants while
                working in that capacity etc; cannot
                provide for any basis for quashing
                criminal    proceedings    involving     such
                offences. But the criminal cases having
                overwhelmingly     and    pre-dominatingly
                civil   flavour     stand    on    different
                footing for the purposes of quashing,
                particularly the offences arising from
                commercial,      financial,      mercantile,
                civil,    partnership     or     such    like
                transactions or the offences arising
                out of matrimony relating to dowry,
                etc. or the family disputes where the
                wrong is basically private or personal
                in nature and the parties have resolved
                their entire dispute. In this category
                of cases, High Court may quash criminal
                proceedings if in its view, because of
                the compromise between the offender and
                victim, the possibility of convictionPage 3 of 5HC-NIC                        Page 3 of 5      Created On Fri Aug 12 02:07:26 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/12520/2016                                                    ORDER



                       is remote and bleak and continuation of
                       criminal case would put accused to
                       great oppression and prejudice and
                       extreme injustice would be caused to
                       him by not quashing the criminal case
                       despite full and complete settlement
                       and compromise with the victim. In
                       other   words,   the   High    Court   must
                       consider whether it would be unfair or
                       contrary to the interest of justice to
                       continue with the criminal proceeding
                       or    continuation    of    the    criminal
                       proceeding would tantamount to abuse of
                       process of law despite settlement and
                       compromise    between   the   victim    and
                       wrongdoer and whether to secure the
                       ends of justice, it is appropriate that
                       criminal case is put to an end and if
                       the answer to the above question(s) is
                       in affirmative, the High Court shall be
                       well within its jurisdiction to quash
                       the criminal proceeding."5.           Bearing in mind the ratiolaid down bythe Apex Court in the aforesaid decision and in
         wake of the fact that the prosecutrix is major
         and    she     has          married         Petitioner                of       her        own
         volition, it is desirable that the Court show
         indulgence and invoke the powers underSection
         482of the Code of Criminal Procedure.6.           Resultantly,              the       request           for       quashment
         is    acceded       to       and     the         impugned           complaint                 is
         QUASHED       with          all       consequential                    proceedings.

                                        ORAL ORDER1.   This is an application underSection 482of the 
         Criminal Procedure Code seeking the quashment of the 
         complaint initiated by the respondent in the form of

         punishable underSections 381read withSection 114of 
         the IPC.2.   It   is   the   case   of   the   applicant   that   he   has 
         served in the telecom sector for about 9 years and as 
         a   Technician   with   Parmeshwarkrupa   Electricals,   which 
         has   entered   into   a   management   service   contract   with 
         Airtel   Mobile   since   last   seven   years.   The   complaint 
         came to be filed on assumption and presumption as hePage 1 of 6HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 6      Created On Sat Aug 27 07:28:25 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/21182/2016                                            ORDER



         had not visited the site on the day or at the time of 
         incident as all technical faults are examined online 
         by   way   of   Remote   Log­in   and   he   has   not   visited   the 
         site actually. It is also his say that in the event of 
         theft/   deficiency   or   technical   fault   an   alarm   is 
         generated   in   the   Global   Delivery   Centre   situated   at 
         Noida   Office   automatically.   Therefore,   he   is   before 
         this   Court   seeking   the   quashment   of   the   complaint 
         being   I­CR.   No134/2016   registered   with   Gotri   Police 
         Station at Vadodara for the offences punishable underSection 381read withSection 114of the Indian Penal 
         Code.3.    The   parties   have   settled   the   dispute   and   the 
         original complainant has filed his affidavit stating 
         therein   that   the   applicant   is   not   involved   in 
         commissioning   of   the  alleged   incident   as   he   was  not 
         required to visit the site on or before the date of 
         the said incident.4.    This   Court   has   heard   the   learned   advocate   Ms. 
         Shivani Purohit for the applicant and learned advocate 
         Mr. Vikas Nair for the respondent complainant. Learned 
         APP Ms. Nisha Thakore has represented the State.5.    Considering   the   fact   that   the   parties   have 
         entered into compromise and in view of the affidavit 
         filed by the complainant in which it is categorically 
         mentioned   that   a   report   has   been   received   by   the 
         applicant   from   Global   Delivery   Centre,   Noida   on   the 
         basis   of   which   the   applicant   made   a   Remote   Log­in 
         while  sitting   in   the  Cluster   Office  at  Vadodara.   HePage 2 of 6HC-NIC                                 Page 2 of 6      Created On Sat Aug 27 07:28:25 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/21182/2016                                            ORDER



         does   not   intend   to   pursue   the   complaint   and   has   no 
         objection and consent for quashing and setting aside 
         the said complaint.6.   Apt would be to refer to the decision rendered in 
         the case ofGian Singh v. State of Punjabreported in  
         (2012) 10 SCC 303, whereby it is held that it is the 
         duty   of   the   Courts   to   encourage   genuine   settlements 
         andsection   482of   the   Code   of   Criminal   Procedure, 
         1973, enables the High Court to pass such orders.It 
         would   be   beneficial   to   reproduce   the   relevant 
         observations   and   findings   of   the   Apex   Court   in   the 
         case ofGian Singh(supra), which read as under :"53.   Quashing   of   offence   or   criminal 
                      proceedings   on   the   ground   of   settlement 
                      between   an   offender   and   victim   is   not   the 
                      same   thing   as   compounding   of   offence.   They  
                      are   different   and   not   interchangeable. 
                      Strictly speaking, the power of compounding 
                      of offences given to a court  underSection 
                      320is   materially   different   from   the 
                      quashing of criminal proceedings by the High  
                      Court   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
                      jurisdiction.   In   compounding   of   offences, 
                      power   of   a   criminal   court   is   circumscribed  
                      by   the   provisions   contained   inSection   320and the court is guided solely and squarely 
                      thereby   while,   on   the   other   hand,   the 
                      formation of opinion by the High Court for 
                      quashing   a   criminal   offence   or   criminal 
                      proceeding   or   criminal   complaint   is   guidedPage 3 of 6HC-NIC                                Page 3 of 6      Created On Sat Aug 27 07:28:25 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/21182/2016                                            ORDER



              by the material on record as to whether the 
              ends of justice would justify such exercise 
              of   power   although   the   ultimate   consequence 
              may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.54. Where   High   Court   quashes   a   criminal 
              proceeding   having   regard   to   the   fact   that 
              dispute between the offender and victim has 
              been   settled   although   offences   are   not 
              compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, 
              continuation of criminal proceedings will be 
              an exercise in futility and justice in the 
              case   demands   that   the   dispute   between   the 
              parties   is   put   to   an   end   and   peace   is 
              restored; securing the ends of justice being  
              the   ultimate   guiding   factor.   No   doubt, 
              crimes are acts which have harmful effect on  
              the public  and consist  in wrong  doing that 
              seriously   endangers   and   threatens   wellbeing 
              of society and it is not safe to leave the  
              crime   doer   only   because   he   and   the   victim 
              have   settled   the   dispute   amicably   or   that 
              the   victim   has   been   paid   compensation,   yet  
              certain   crimes   have   been   made   compoundable 
              in   law,   with   or   without   permission   of   the 
              Court.   In   respect   of   serious   offences   like  
              murder,   rape,   dacoity,   etc;   or   other 
              offences   of   mental   depravity   underIPCor 
              offences   of   moral   turpitude   under   special 
              statutes, likePrevention of Corruption Actor the offences committed by public servants  
              while   working   in   that   capacity,   thePage 4 of 6HC-NIC                        Page 4 of 6      Created On Sat Aug 27 07:28:25 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/21182/2016                                            ORDER




                      settlement   between   offender   and   victim   can 
                      have   no   legal   sanction   at   all.   However, 
                      certain   offences   which   overwhelmingly   and 
                      predominantly   bear   civil   flavour   having 
                      arisen out of civil, mercantile, commercial, 
                      financial,   partnership   or   such   like 
                      transactions or the offences arising out of 
                      matrimony,   particularly   relating   to   dowry, 
                      etc. or the family dispute, where the wrong 
                      is basically to victim and the offender and 
                      victim   have   settled   all   disputes   between 
                      them amicably, irrespective of the fact that  
                      such   offences   have   not   been   made 
                      compoundable, the High Court may within the 
                      framework   of   its   inherent   power,   quash   the  
                      criminal proceeding or criminal complaint or 
                      F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the face of 
                      such   settlement,there   is   hardly   any 
                      likelihood   of   offender   being   convicted   and 
                      by   not   quashing   the   criminal   proceedings, 
                      justice   shall   be   casualty   and   ends   of 
                      justice shall be defeated. The above list is  
                      illustrative   and   not   exhaustive.   Each   case 
                      will depend on its own facts and no hard and 
                      fast category can be prescribed."7.   From   the   ratio   laid   down   as   referred   to 
         hereinabove, it can be held that no purpose is likely 
         to   be   served   in   wake   of   the   parties   having   settled 
         their dispute to continue the prosecution. It appears 
         to be a case more of misunderstanding on the part ofPage 5 of 6HC-NIC                                Page 5 of 6      Created On Sat Aug 27 07:28:25 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/21182/2016                                            ORDER



         the complainant rather than the actual theft which has 
         been   alleged   in   the   complaint.   Resultantly,   the 
         quashment of the complaint is allowed.8.    The petition is disposed of accordingly.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

              CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                                 FIR/ORDER) NO. 5360 of 2016
         ==========================================================
                     NIKUNJ RAJENDRABHAI PATEL....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                      STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR ASHISH M DAGLI, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         Mr.H.K.Patel, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================
          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                      Date : 04/03/2016


                                        ORAL ORDER1.    Rule         returnable            today.             Learned                 APP
         Mr.H.K.Patel waives service of notice of rule for and
         on behalf of the respondent No.1-State.2.    This      application has been preferred                                by the
         applicant for quashment of the complaint being I-CR
         No.13 of 2016 registered with Fatehganj Police
         Station for the offences punishable underSections
         143,147,427,506of IPC.3.    It is the say of the applicant that the applicant
         has also given a complaint to the Fatehganj Police
         Station on 16th January, 2016 which of course has
         not been registered by the police. In the meantime,Page 1 of 5HC-NIC                                  Page 1 of 5      Created On Sun Mar 06 03:06:33 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/5360/2016                                                 ORDER



         the parties have amicably settled the disputes.4.    Mr.Mahesh Pujara, learned advocate appearing
         for the respondent No.2-original complainant brings
         on record the affidavit which is permitted to be
         taken on record.5.    The complainant in his affidavit also has stated
         that the settlement is arrived at by and between the
         parties.            It      is     also           stated            that          minor
         misunderstanding and misconception resulted into
         filing of the FIR. However, due to intervention of the
         friends     and          relatives,            they     have           chosen               to
         compromise and settled the issue once and for all.
         The complainant has also confirmed that he has
         been given back the possession of Final Plot No. 21
         for    which          the        complainant's                   brother               has
         relinquished rights in favour of one Shri Arvindbhai
         uncle of the applicant herein.6.    Mr.H.K.Patel, learned APP has verified the
         contents of the affidavit from the complainant and
         confirmed that the settlement is genuine and
         entered without any coercion.7.    Bearing in mind the decision of the Apex Court
         rendered in case ofGian Singh Vs. State of
         Punjab and Anotherreported in 2012 (10)SCC
         303 as the dispute concerned is strictly betweenPage 2 of 5HC-NIC                                    Page 2 of 5      Created On Sun Mar 06 03:06:33 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/5360/2016                                             ORDER



         the   private        parties.     There         is      no       element                of
         involvement in the public property or public money.
         They have chosen to amicably settled the disputes.
         No purpose is likely to be served in allowing this
         criminal proceedings.The applicant, if is made to
         undergo the trial           it would be                   a mere ordeal
         therefore, this Court is of the opinion that the
         request of the quashment of the FIR is required to
         be acceded to.8.    Bearing in mind the decision ofGian Singh(Supra), his request to quash the FIR needs to be
         acceded to. It is essential to reproduce the relevant
         paragraph for this purpose:-61.   The   position   that   emerges   from   the   above 
                     discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the  
                     High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR  
                     or   complaint   in   exercise   of   its   inherent 
                     jurisdiction   is   distinct   and   different   from   the 
                     power given to a criminal court for compounding the  
                     offences   underSection   320of   the   Code.   Inherent 
                     power   is   of   wide   plenitude   with   no   statutory 
                     limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with 
                     the guideline  engrafted  in  such  power  viz;  (i)  to 
                     secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse  
                     of the process of any Court. In what cases power to 
                     quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R 
                     may be exercised where the offender and victim have  
                     settled their dispute would depend on the facts and  
                     circumstances  of  each  case  and  no category  can  be 
                     prescribed. However, before exercise of such power, 
                     the High Court must have due regard to the nature 
                     and   gravity   of   the   crime.   Heinous   and   serious  
                     offences   of   mental   depravity   or   offences   like 
                     murder,   rape,   dacoity,   etc.   cannot   be   fittingly 
                     quashed even though the victim or victims family and 
                     the offender have settled the dispute. Such offences 
                     are not private in nature and have serious impact on 
                     society.   Similarly,   any   compromise   between   thePage 3 of 5HC-NIC                                Page 3 of 5      Created On Sun Mar 06 03:06:33 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/5360/2016                                              ORDER


                    victim   and   offender   in   relation   to   the   offences 
                    under special statutes likePrevention of Corruption 
                    Actor   the   offences   committed   by   public   servants 
                    while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide 
                    for   any   basis   for   quashing   criminal   proceedings 
                    involving   such   offences.   But   the   criminal   cases 
                    having   overwhelmingly   and   predominatingly   civil 
                    flavour stand on different footing for the purposes 
                    of quashing, particularly the offences arising from 
                    commercial,   financial,   mercantile,   civil, 
                    partnership   or   such   like   transactions   or   the 
                    offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, 
                    etc.   or   the   family   disputes   where   the   wrong   is 
                    basically   private   or   personal   in   nature   and   the  
                    parties have resolved their entire dispute. In this 
                    category   of   cases,   High   Court   may   quash   criminal 
                    proceedings   if   in   its   view,   because   of   the 
                    compromise   between   the   offender   and   victim,   the 
                    possibility   of   conviction   is   remote   and   bleak   and 
                    continuation of criminal case would put accused to 
                    great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice 
                    would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal  
                    case   despite   full   and   complete  settlement   and 
                    compromise with the victim. In other words, the High 
                    Court  must  consider  whether  it  would  be unfair  or 
                    contrary to the interest of justice to continue with 
                    the   criminal   proceeding   or   continuation   of   the 
                    criminal   proceeding   would   tantamount   to   abuse   of 
                    process   of   law   despite   settlement   and   compromise 
                    between   the   victim   and   wrongdoer   and   whether   to  
                    secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that 
                    criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to  
                    the   above   question(s)   is   in   affirmative,   the   High 
                    Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash 
                    the criminal proceeding.9.   Both the sides have confirmed the truthfulness
         of contents of compromise. Resultantly, the petition
         is allowed.        The FIR being CR No. I-13 of 2016
         registered with Fatehganj Police Station stands
         quashed.10. All the consequential proceedings also stand
         quashed and set-aside.11. Registry         shall   accept           the       Vakalatpatra                    ofPage 4 of 5HC-NIC                                Page 4 of 5      Created On Sun Mar 06 03:06:33 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/5360/2016                                           ORDER



         Mr.Mahesh Pujara, learned advocate appearing for
         the complainant.12. Rule       is     made absolute.              Direct          service             is
         permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

              CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                                 FIR/ORDER) NO. 15241 of 2016

         ==========================================================
                   SADHABHASI BHALUBHAI NATDA & 8....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                       STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         HARSHESH R KAKKAD, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 9
         MR RC KAKKAD, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 9
         PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                       Date : 29/06/2016


                                        ORAL ORDER1.   Applicants   have   approached   this   Court   seeking 

         quashment   of   the   First   Information   Report   being 

         C.R.No.I­14   of   2016   registered   with   Jodiya   police 

         station,   Surat   for   the   offences   punishable   undersections 143,504,506(2)and427of the Indian Penal 

         Code.2.   In   all   there   are   nine   applicants.   Parties   have 

         amicably settled their disputes due to intervention of 

         some   eminent   persons.   Deed   of   compromise   dated 

         22.6.2016   has   already   been   entered   into   which   hasPage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 5      Created On Tue Jul 05 01:14:51 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/15241/2016                                             ORDER



         formed   part   of   Annexure­B.   There   are   no   criminal 

         antecedents of any of the applicants. Complainant is 

         present before this Court. He has confirmed that out 

         of   his   own   volition,   he   has   chosen   to   end   this 

         dispute. No grievance survives.3.   Having considered the submissions made on behalf 

         of both the sides and the fact that it is a private 

         dispute   and  the   parties  have   arrived   at   an   amicable 

         settlement,   especially   when   the   respondent   No.2   has 

         chosen to put an end to the matter, no cause survives 

         and,   therefore,   it   would   be   desirable   to   quash   the 

         first  information  report   in   view  of  the   decision   of 

         the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh v. State of  

         Punjab and another, reported in AIR 2012 SC (Supp.)  

         838,  whereby  it is  held that it is the duty of the 

         Courts   to   encourage   genuine   settlements   andsection 

         482of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, enables 

         the   High   Court   to   pass   such   orders.It   would   be 

         beneficial to reproduce the relevant observations and 

         findings of the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra), which read as under :"53.   Quashing   of   offence   or   criminal 
              proceedings   on   the   ground   of   settlement  
              between an offender and victim is not the samePage 2 of 5HC-NIC                               Page 2 of 5      Created On Tue Jul 05 01:14:51 IST 2016
            R/CR.MA/15241/2016                                             ORDER



         thing   as   compounding   of   offence.   They   are 
         different   and   not   interchangeable.   Strictly  
         speaking, the power of compounding of offences 
         given   to   a   court   underSection  320is 
         materially   different   from   the   quashing   of 
         criminal   proceedings   by   the   High   Court   in 
         exercise   of   its   inherent   jurisdiction.   In 
         compounding  of  offences,  power  of  a  criminal 
         court   is   circumscribed   by   the   provisions 
         contained   inSection   320and   the   court   is  
         guided  solely   and  squarely  thereby  while,  on 
         the   other   hand,   the   formation   of   opinion   by 
         the High Court for quashing a criminal offence 
         or   criminal   proceeding   or   criminal   complaint 
         is   guided   by   the   material   on   record   as   to 
         whether the ends of justice would justify such 
         exercise   of   power   although   the   ultimate  
         consequence  may  be  acquittal   or  dismissal  of 
         indictment.54. Where   High   Court   quashes   a   criminal 
         proceeding   having   regard   to   the   fact   that 
         dispute   between   the   offender   and   victim   has 
         been   settled   although   offences   are   not 
         compoundable,   it   does   so   as   in   its   opinion, 
         continuation   of   criminal   proceedings   will   be 
         an   exercise   in   futility   and   justice   in   the  
         case   demands   that   the   dispute   between   the 
         parties   is   put   to   an   end   and   peace   is  
         restored;  securing  the  ends  of  justice  being 
         the ultimate guiding factor. No doubt, crimes 
         are   acts   which   have   harmful   effect   on   the  
         public   and   consist   in   wrong   doing   that 
         seriously   endangers   and   threatens   well­being 
         of   society   and   it   is   not   safe   to   leave   the  
         crimedoer only because he and the victim have 
         settled   the   dispute   amicably   or   that   the 
         victim has been paid compensation, yet certain 
         crimes   have   been   made   compoundable   in   law, 
         with   or   without   permission   of   the   Court.   In 
         respect of serious offences like murder, rape, 
         dacoity,   etc;   or   other   offences   of   mental 
         depravity   underIPCor   offences   of   moral 
         turpitude   under   special   statutes,   likePrevention  of  Corruption  Actor  the  offences 
         committed by public servants while working inPage 3 of 5HC-NIC                          Page 3 of 5      Created On Tue Jul 05 01:14:51 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/15241/2016                                             ORDER



              that capacity, the settlement between offender 
              and victim can have no legal sanction at all.  
              However, certain offences which overwhelmingly  
              and   predominantly   bear  civil   flavour   having 
              arisen   out   of   civil,   mercantile,   commercial, 
              financial,   partnership   or   such   like 
              transactions   or   the   offences   arising   out   of 
              matrimony,   particularly   relating   to   dowry, 
              etc. or the family dispute, where the wrong is 
              basically   to   victim   and   the   offender   and 
              victim have settled all disputes between them 
              amicably,  irrespective   of  the  fact  that  such 
              offences have not been made compoundable, the 
              High   Court   may   within   the   framework   of   its  
              inherent power, quash the criminal proceeding  
              or   criminal   complaint   or   F.I.R   if   it   is 
              satisfied   that   on   the   face   of   such 
              settlement,there   is   hardly   any   likelihood   of 
              offender  being  convicted  and   by  not  quashing 
              the   criminal   proceedings,   justice   shall   be  
              casualty   and   ends   of   justice   shall   be  
              defeated.  The   above  list  is  illustrative   and 
              not exhaustive. Each case will depend on its 
              own facts and no hard and fast category can be 
              prescribed."4.   For   the   foregoing   reasons   and   in   view   of   the 
         decisions of the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra), the present application succeeds and the same 
         is,   accordingly,   allowed   in   view   of   an   amicable 
         settlement arrived at by and between the parties. The 
         first   information   report  being  C.R.No.I­14   of   2016 
         registered with Jodiya police station, Surat  and all 
         the proceedings emanating therefrom, are quashed and 
         set aside. Rule is made absolute accordingly.Direct service permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)Page 4 of 5HC-NIC                               Page 4 of 5      Created On Tue Jul 05 01:14:51 IST 2016

                   IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

               CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                            FIR/ORDER) NO. 13342 of 2016
                                       With
                     CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION NO. 9867 of 2016
         ==========================================================
                MANOJBHAI KAMLESHKUMAR SUKHLAL & 2....Applicant(s)
                                    Versus
                      STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR HARDIK A DAVE, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 3
         MS CM SHAH, PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         MR PRASHANT KHANDERIA, for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================
         CORAM:                HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
                                     Date : 14/06/2016
                                  COMMON ORAL ORDER1.           Respondent            No.2,           herein,               i.e.               the
         original        complainant,             has       lodged           a      complaint
         being I-C.R. No. 64 of 2016 with Morbi Taluka
         Police Station. The petitioner, herein, is the
         son     of       the         petitioner           in        Criminal                Misc.
         Application No. 9867 of 2016.2.           The petitioners in respective petition,
         i.e. original accused, seek quashment of the said
         complaint underArticle 226of the Constitution
         read withSection 482of the Code of Criminal
         Procedure on various grounds raised in respective
         petition.3.           This Court had, earlier, protected the
         petitioner of Criminal Misc. Application No. 9867
         of     2016.          During        the           pendancy               of         thesePage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                    Page 1 of 5      Created On Fri Jun 17 02:15:44 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13342/2016                                                    ORDER



         proceedings, the parties have chosen to settle
         their      disputes          amicably.              The       complainant                     has
         filed his affidavit in both the matters stating,
         therein,         that        due        to       intervention                    of           the
         community leaders and elders of the family, the
         matter is settled without there being any threat,
         duress        or       coercion            on       the          part           of            the
         petitioners.4.           On          being            satisfied                   about                   the
         truthfulness of the contents of the affidavit,
         after due verification from the complainant, this
         Court is of the opinion that, though, some of the
         provisions are non-compoundable, bearing in mind
         the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in the case
         of "GIAN SINGH VS. STATE OF PUNJAB AND ANR.",
         (2012)      10      SCC      303,        wherein,             the        Apex         Court
         permitted the quashment of the complaint, as the
         disputes were predominantly personal in nature,
         the request for quashment deserves consideration.
         Here,       it       would       be         apt        to        reproduce                    the
         observations made by the Apex Court in Paragraph-
         61 ofthe said judgment;"61.    The position that emerges from
                          the above discussion can be summarised
                          thus: the power of the High Court in
                          quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR
                          or   complaint   in  exercise  of  its
                          inherent jurisdiction is distinct and
                          different from the power given to a
                          criminal court for compounding thePage 2 of 5HC-NIC                                      Page 2 of 5      Created On Fri Jun 17 02:15:44 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/13342/2016                                              ORDER



                 offences underSection 320of the Code.
                 Inherent power is of wide plenitude
                 with no statutory limitation but it has
                 to be exercised in accord with the
                 guideline engrafted in such power viz;
                 (I) to secure the ends of justice or(ii) to prevent abuse of the process of
                 any Court. In what cases power to quash
                 the criminal proceeding or complaint or
                 F.I.R   may    be   exercised     where   the
                 offender and victim have settled their
                 dispute would depend on the facts and
                 circumstances of each case and no
                 category can be prescribed. However,
                 before exercise of such power, the High
                 Court must have due regard to the
                 nature   and    gravity   of    the    crime.Heinous and serious offences of mental
                 depravity or offences like murder,
                 rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly
                 quashed even though the victim or
                 victim's family and the offender have
                 settled the dispute. Such offences are
                 not private in nature and have serious
                 impact   on    society.    Similarly,     any
                 compromise    between    the    victim    and
                 offender in relation to the offences
                 under special statutes likePrevention
                 of Corruption Actor the offences
                 committed by public servants while
                 working in that capacity etc; cannot
                 provide for any basis for quashing
                 criminal    proceedings    involving     such
                 offences. But the criminal cases having
                 overwhelmingly     and    pre-dominatingly
                 civil   flavour     stand    on    different
                 footing for the purposes of quashing,
                 particularly the offences arising from
                 commercial,      financial,      mercantile,
                 civil,    partnership     or     such    like
                 transactions or the offences arising
                 out of matrimony relating to dowry,
                 etc. or the family disputes where the
                 wrong is basically private or personalPage 3 of 5HC-NIC                        Page 3 of 5      Created On Fri Jun 17 02:15:44 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/13342/2016                                                     ORDER



                       in nature and the parties have resolved
                       their entire dispute. In this category
                       of cases, High Court may quash criminal
                       proceedings if in its view, because of
                       the compromise between the offender and
                       victim, the possibility of conviction
                       is remote and bleak and continuation of
                       criminal case would put accused to
                       great oppression and prejudice and
                       extreme injustice would be caused to
                       him by not quashing the criminal case
                       despite full and complete settlement
                       and compromise with the victim. In
                       other   words,   the   High    Court   must
                       consider whether it would be unfair or
                       contrary to the interest of justice to
                       continue with the criminal proceeding
                       or    continuation    of    the    criminal
                       proceeding would tantamount to abuse of
                       process of law despite settlement and
                       compromise    between   the   victim    and
                       wrongdoer and whether to secure the
                       ends of justice, it is appropriate that
                       criminal case is put to an end and if
                       the answer to the above question(s) is
                       in affirmative, the High Court shall be
                       well within its jurisdiction to quash
                       the criminal proceeding."5.         In the case on hand also, the dispute is
         predominantly of personal in nature. Therefore,
         by   permitting            the   prosecution                to      continue,                no
         fruitful result shall be obtained, as the parties
         have entered into a compromise and the chances of
         conviction           are         very             bleak.             Hence,                  the
         intervention is necessary.6.         Resultantly,               both          the          petitions                   are
         ALLOWED. The impugned complaint is QUASHED withPage 4 of 5HC-NIC                                    Page 4 of 5       Created On Fri Jun 17 02:15:44 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13342/2016                                                 ORDER



         all consequential proceedings.7.           Learned            Advocate,                   Mr.              Prashant
         Khanderiya,           is     permitted        to      file        his        V.P.          on
         behalf of Respondent No.2-the complainant. Direct
         service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)
