                    IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

                SPECIAL CRIMINAL APPLICATION (DIRECTION) NO. 6 of 2015
         ==========================================================
                  ASHRAFHUSSAIN ALIMOHAMAD SHEKHANI....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                       STATE OF GUJARAT & 9....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MS JAYSHREE C BHATT, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         MR VIVEK N MAPARA, ADVOCATE for the Respondent(s) No. 7
         NOTICE SERVED for the Respondent(s) No. 2 - 6 , 8 - 10
         MS NISHA THAKORE, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

             CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE J.B.PARDIWALA

                                            Date : 20/12/2016
                                              ORAL ORDER1      By this application underArticle 226of the Constitution of India, 
         the writ applicant, father of the original first informant, has prayed for 
         the following reliefs:"14(A)Be pleased to admit and allow this application.(B)     Be   pleased   to   direct   the   respondent   no.1   to   hand   over   police  
                investigation to CBI, CID Crime or any independent agency looking to the  
                seriousness of the incident and also looking to the deposition of the victim-   Ajima   before   the   Ld.   JMFC,   Gondal   and   her   photographs   and   more  
                particularly   an   application   at   Ex.   16   in   Criminal   Case   No.1882/08  
                regarding addition ofSec. 307of IPC by the Additional Public Prosecutor  
                and  order  passed  by the Ld. JMFC,  Gondal at Ex.  16 at Annexure  - B 
                Colly. in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, in the interest of  
                justice.(C)      Your Lordships may be pleased to direct the res. no.2 - PI of Gondal  
                Police   Station   to   add   the   names   of   res.   No.4   Mithiumiyabapu   Nagani  
                Saiyad and res. no.5 Ajrudin Ashrafbhai Bakali as an accused persons as  
                they are  connected  with the  incident  though  they are  co­accused  of the  
                incident they have left from the very beginning in the incident.Page 1 of 4HC-NIC                                         Page 1 of 4       Created On Wed Dec 21 00:11:31 IST 2016
                      R/SCR.A/6/2015                                                 ORDER



                (D)     Be pleased to grant such other and further relief/s which may deem  
                fit and proper in the interest of justice."2      It   is   the   case   of   the   writ   applicant   that   his   daughter,   namely, 
         Ajimabanu got married to one Firoz Ashraf Bakali, original accused No.1. 
         The marriage of the daughter of the writ applicant was solemnized with 
         Firoz  in   the   year   2002.   In   the   wedlock,   two   children   were   born,   a 
         daughter   named  Kubrabanu  and   a   son   named  Mohammad   Hussain.  It 
         appears that the daughter of the writ applicant was not happy at her 
         matrimonial   home   as   disputes   cropped   up   between   the   husband   and 
         wife. On 26th July 2008, the daughter of the writ applicant lodged a First 
         Information Report being II­C.R. No.3127 of 2008 at the Gondal Police 
         Station, Rajkot for the offence punishable underSections 323,498Aread 
         with 114 of theIndian Penal Code. In the First Information Report, she 
         has alleged that on account of incessant harassment and torture at the 
         hands of the accused persons, she made an attempt to commit suicide by 
         pouring   kerosene   on   her   body   and   setting   herself   on   fire.   The   First 
         Information Report was investigated, and ultimately, chargesheet came 
         to be filed in the Court of the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, 
         Gondal. It also appears that  a  dying  declaration  was  recorded by the 
         Executive Magistrate on 11th  June 2008. In the dying declaration, her 
         version was altogether  different than the  one she has narrated in the 
         F.I.R.   In   the   dying   declaration,   she   has   come   out   with   a   case   of 
         accidental fire. According to her, she was preparing herself to cook food 
         and in the meantime, something went wrong with the stove containing 
         kerosene on account of which she sustained burn injuries.3      Soon thereafter, the trial commenced. The daughter of the writ 
         applicant  entered  the  box  as   the  P.W.­1.  For   the   first  time   while   her 
         evidence was being recorded, she came out with the case that kerosene 
         was poured on her body by the accused persons and she was set on fire.Page 2 of 4HC-NIC                                        Page 2 of 4      Created On Wed Dec 21 00:11:31 IST 2016
                      R/SCR.A/6/2015                                                 ORDERThus, according to her, there was an attempt on the part of the accused 
         persons   to   commit   her   murder.   Having   regard   to   the   nature   of   the 
         deposition, the Public Prosecutor preferred an application to addSection 
         307of the Indian Penal Code and amend the charge. The application 
         Exhibit: 16 filed by the Public Prosecutor in this regard was looked into 
         by the Additional Judicial Magistrate First Class, Gondal, and vide order 
         dated 13th February 2013 directed the Investigating Agency to carry out 
         investigation in this regard. Pursuant to such direction issued by the trial 
         Court, some investigation was carried out and a report came to be filed 
         by the Police Sub­Inspector of the Gondal Police Station in the Court of 
         the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Gondal stating that there was 
         not an iota of evidence to even remotely suggest that the case is one of 
         attempt to commit murder. In the meantime, this writ application came 
         to be filed seeking transfer of the investigation to the C.B.I. or C.I.D. 
         (Crime).4      Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and 
         having considered the materials on record, I am of the view that no case 
         worth the name is made out by the writ applicant herein being the father 
         of the victim for transfer of the investigation to any other agency, like 
         the C.B.I. or C.I.D. (Crime). As on date, there are three different versions 
         put­forward by  Ajimabanu.  There are no eyewitnesses to the incident. I

                                     ORAL ORDER1.          Leave to amend prayer clause.2.          The      petitioners          are      before          this         Court,
         seeking following reliefs;"[A]       This application may be allowed.[B] The Criminal Complaint bearing No. I-
                   18 of 2016 filed on 25-03-2016 before the
                   Kalupur Police Station, Ahmedabad, against
                   the applicant herein under section 406, 420
                   and 120(b) of TheIndian Penal Code, be

                   of this application, further proceedings in
                   connection with the Criminal Complaint
                   bearing No. I-18 of 2016 filed on 25-03-

                   Ahmedabad, against the applicant herein
                   undersection 406,420and120(b)of the
                   Indian Penal Code, be stayed;[D] Any other and/or further relief/s that
                   this Hon'ble Court may deem fit looking toPage 1 of 4HC-NIC                               Page 1 of 4         Created On Thu Jun 16 02:40:51 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13508/2016                                                    ORDER



                     the facts and circumstances of the case may
                     be awarded to the present applicant."3.           The complainant is before this Court and
         he has filed his affidavit, indicating clearly that
         he    has      settled         the        disputes            by       settling             and
         accepting the accounts with the applicants and no
         grievance survives, now.4.           This            Court        also         inquired               from          the
         complainant,           who      has          in       terms         confirmed               the
         truthfulness          of      the       contents           of      the       affidavit.
         Some of the offences are, though, not compoundable,
         the Court needs to intervene in the wake of the
         fact that the disputes are purely of private in
         nature and as the parties have amicably settled the
         same,     no     purpose         is         likely          to      be       served             in
         continuing the prosecution. Hence, the request for
         quashment deserves consideration.5.           Here it would be profitable to refer to
         the     observations made by the                           Hon'ble Apex Court
         in the case of "GIAN SINGH VS. STATE OF PUNJAB AND
         ANR." (Supra), wherein, at Paragraph-61, the Apex
         Court observed as under;"61.   The position that emerges from
                        the above discussion can be summarised
                        thus: the power of the High Court in
                        quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or
                        complaint in exercise of its inherent
                        jurisdiction is distinct and different
                        from the power given to a criminal courtPage 2 of 4HC-NIC                                        Page 2 of 4      Created On Thu Jun 16 02:40:51 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/13508/2016                                            ORDER



                for   compounding   the    offences     underSection 320of the Code. Inherent power
                is of wide plenitude with no statutory
                limitation but it has to be exercised in
                accord with the guideline engrafted in
                such power viz; (I) to secure the ends
                of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of
                the process of any Court. In what cases
                power to quash the criminal proceeding
                or complaint or F.I.R may be exercised
                where the offender and victim have
                settled their dispute would depend on
                the facts and circumstances of each case
                and no category can be prescribed.
                However, before exercise of such power,
                the High Court must have due regard to
                the nature and gravity of the crime.
                Heinous and serious offences of mental
                depravity or offences like murder, rape,
                dacoity,   etc.    cannot    be     fittingly
                quashed   even   though   the     victim   or
                victim's family and the offender have
                settled the dispute. Such offences are
                not private in nature and have serious
                impact   on    society.    Similarly,     any
                compromise   between    the     victim    and
                offender in relation to the offences
                under special statutes likePrevention
                of   Corruption   Actor   the     offences
                committed   by   public    servants     while
                working in that capacity etc; cannot
                provide for any basis for quashing
                criminal   proceedings     involving     such
                offences. But the criminal cases having
                overwhelmingly     and     pre-dominatingly
                civil flavour stand on different footing
                for    the     purposes     of      quashing,
                particularly the offences arising from
                commercial,     financial,       mercantile,
                civil,    partnership    or      such    like
                transactions or the offences arising out
                of matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or
                the family disputes where the wrong is
                basically private or personal in nature
                and the parties have resolved theirPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                        Page 3 of 4      Created On Thu Jun 16 02:40:51 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/13508/2016                                                     ORDER



                        entire dispute. In this category of
                        cases, High Court may quash criminal
                        proceedings if in its view, because of
                        the compromise between the offender and
                        victim, the possibility of conviction is
                        remote and bleak and continuation of
                        criminal case would put accused to great
                        oppression and prejudice and extreme
                        injustice would be caused to him by not
                        quashing the criminal case despite full
                        and complete settlement and compromise
                        with the victim. In other words, the
                        High Court must consider whether it
                        would be unfair or contrary to the
                        interest of justice to continue with the
                        criminal proceeding or continuation of
                        the criminal proceeding would tantamount
                        to abuse of process of law despite
                        settlement and compromise between the
                        victim and wrongdoer and whether to
                        secure the ends of justice, it is
                        appropriate that criminal case is put to
                        an end and if the answer to the above
                        question(s) is in affirmative, the High
                        Court   shall    be   well   within   its
                        jurisdiction   to   quash  the   criminal
                        proceeding."6.           Resultantly this application is ALLOWED.
         The     impugned             complaint            is        QUASHED            with          all
         consequential proceedings.7.           Registry          to      accept            the        VP      of       learned

              "Conclusion/Directions120.   In   view   of   the   aforesaid   discussion,   we  
              hold :120.1   The   registration   of   FIR   is   mandatory 
              underSection   154of   the   Code,   if   the

         120.3. If the inquiry discloses the commission

         further.120.4. The police officer cannot avoid his duty  
         of registering offence if cognizable offence is

         officers   who   do   not   register   the   FIR   if 
         information   received   by   him   discloses   a 
         cognizable offence.120.5. The scope of preliminary inquiry is not  
         to   verify   the   veracity   or   otherwise   of   the 
         information   received   but   only   to   ascertain 
         whether the information reveals any cognizable 
         offence.120.6.   As   to   what   type   and   in   which   cases 
         preliminary   inquiry   is   to   be   conducted   will 
         depend on the facts and circumstances of each 
         case.   The   category   of   cases   in   which 
         preliminary inquiry may be made are as under :(a) Matrimonial disputes/ family disputes;(b) Commercial offences;(c) Medical negligence cases;(d) Corruption cases;(e) Cases where there is abnormal delay/laches 
         in   initiating   criminal   prosecution,   for  
         example, over 3 months delay in reporting the  
         matter   without   satisfactorily   explaining   the 
         reasons for delay.The   aforesaid   are   only   illustrations   and   not 
         exhaustive of all conditions which may warrant 
         preliminary inquiry.120.7. While ensuring and protecting the rights  
         of   the   accused   and   the   complainant,   a 
         preliminary   inquiry   should   be   made   time   bound 
         and   in   any   case   it   should   not  exceed   7  days. 
         The   fact   of   such   delay   and   the   causes   of   itPage 3 of 5HC-NIC                         Page 3 of 5      Created On Tue Jul 05 00:32:06 IST 2016

              must be reflected in the General Diary entry.120.8.   Since   the   General   Diary/Station

         ==========================================================
         Appearance:

         ==========================================================

         CORAM        HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
             :

                                      Date : 13/07/2016


                                       ORAL ORDER1. By   way   of   present   petition   preferred   underArticle   226of   the   Constitution   of   India,   the 

              petitioners   have   prayed   for   the   following 

              substantial reliefs :"7(A)           Your Lordships be pleased to issue 
                     appropriate   writ,   order   or   directions,  
                     directing   the   respondent   nos.2   and   3   to 
                     forthwith   grant   police   protection   to   the 
                     petitioners,   in   view   of   peculiar   facts   and 
                     circumstances   stated   in   this   petition,   for 
                     some   reasonable   period,  in   the   interest   ofPage 1 of 6HC-NIC                                  Page 1 of 6      Created On Fri Jul 15 02:45:39 IST 2016
              R/SCR.A/2287/2016                                             ORDER



                 justice;(B)  Your Lordships be pleased to direct the  
                 respondent   nos.2   and   3   to   grant   police  
                 protection   to   the   petitioners,   pending   the 
                 admission,   hearing   and   final   disposal   of 
                 this petition, in the interest of justice;"2.It is the case of the petitioners that they are 

           legally   wedded   couple,   whose   marriage   was 

           solemnised   and   registered   with   the   Registrar   of 

           Marriages   on   March   16,   2016.   They   are   seeking 

           police   protection.   Their   marriage   is   an   inter­

           religion.   A   marriage   certificate   to   that   effect 

           is also brought on record of the matter.3.It   is   the   say   of   the  learned   counsel   appearing 

           for the petitioners  Shri Manan Shah that despite 

           the best of the efforts made by the petitioners 

           to convince the parents of the petitioner No.1, 

           they   have   chosen   to   pressurise   the   petitioner 

           No.1   to   marry   elsewhere   with   a   boy   of   their 

           choice   and,   therefore,   they   are   apprehensive   of 

           their   life   and   afraid   of   honour   killing.In 

           support   of   his   submissions,   the  learned   counselPage 2 of 6HC-NIC                           Page 2 of 6      Created On Fri Jul 15 02:45:39 IST 2016
              R/SCR.A/2287/2016                                                ORDER



           appearing for the petitioners has relied upon the 

           decision of the Apex Court in the case ofLata  

           Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh, reported in AIR  

           2006 SC 2522.4.Heard Shri Manan Shah,  learned counsel appearing 

           for the petitioners and Shri Ronak Raval, learned 

           Additional   Public   Prosecutor   for   the   respondent 

           No.1­State.5. Having   considered   the   contents   of   the   petition 

           and   the   material   on   record,   as   also   the 

           submissions made by both the sides as well as the 

           decision of the Apex Court in the case ofLata  

           Singh(supra), this Court is of the opinion that 

           the   petitioners   deserve   to   be   granted   police 

           protection. At this stage, it would be profitable 

           to   regurgitate   the   relevant   observations   and 

           findings   ofthe   said   decision,   which   read   as 

           under :"17.            The caste system is a curse on the  
                 nation   and   the   sooner   it   is   destroyed   the 
                 better. In  fact, it  is dividing  the nationPage 3 of 6HC-NIC                              Page 3 of 6      Created On Fri Jul 15 02:45:39 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/2287/2016                                             ORDER



             at a time when we have to be united to face  
             the   challenges   before   the   nation   unitedly. 
             Hence, inter­caste marriages are in fact in 
             the national interest as they will result in  
             destroying   the   caste   system.   However, 
             disturbing   news   are   coming   from   several 
             parts   of   the   country   that   young   men   and 
             women who undergo inter­caste marriage, are 
             threatened   with   violence,   or   violence   is 
             actually committed on them. In our opinion, 
             such   acts   of   violence   or   threats   or 
             harassment are wholly illegal and those who 
             commit them must be severely punished. This 
             is a free and democratic country, and once a  
             person becomes a major he or she can marry 
             whosoever he/she likes.If the parents of the  
             boy   or   girl   do   not   approve   of   such   inter­
             caste   or   inter­religious   marriage   the 
             maximum they can do is that they can cut off 
             social   relations   with   the   son   or   the 
             daughter,   but   they   cannot   give   threats   or 
             commit   or   instigate   acts   of   violence   and 
             cannot harass the person who undergoes such 
             inter­caste or inter­religious marriage. We, 
             therefore,   direct   that   the   administration/ 
             police   authorities   throughout   the   country 
             will see to it that if any boy or girl who 
             is   a   major   undergoes   inter­caste   or   inter­
             religious marriage with a  woman or  man who 
             is a major, the couple are not harassed by 
             any one nor subjected to threats or acts ofPage 4 of 6HC-NIC                       Page 4 of 6      Created On Fri Jul 15 02:45:39 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/2287/2016                                             ORDER



             violence, and any one who gives such threats  
             or   harasses   or   commits   acts   of   violence 
             either   himself   or   at   his   instigation,   is 
             taken   to   task   by   instituting   criminal  
             proceedings   by   the   police   against   such 
             persons   and   further   stern   action   is   taken 
             against such persons as provided by law.18.   We   sometimes   hear   of   'honour'   killings  
             of   such   persons   who   undergo   inter­caste   or  
             inter­religious   marriage   of   their   own   free 
             will.   There   is   nothing   honourable   in   such 
             killings, and  in fact they are nothing but 
             barbaric   and   shameful   acts   of   murder 
             committed   by   brutal,   feudal   minded   persons 
             who   deserve   harsh   punishment.   Only   in   this  
             way can we stamp out such acts of barbarism.19.In   the   circumstances,   the   writ   petition 
             is   allowed.   The   proceedings   in   Sessions 
             Trial No. 1201/2001 titledState of U.P. v. 
             Sangita   Gupta   and   Ors.arising   out   of   FIR 
             No.   336/2000   registered   at   Police   Station 
             Sarojini   Nagar,   Lucknow   and   pending   in   the  
             Fast Track Court V, Lucknow are quashed. The 
             warrants   against   the   accused   are   also  
             quashed.   The   police   at   all   the   concerned 
             places   should   ensure   that   neither   the  
             petitioner nor her husband nor any relatives  
             of the petitioner's husband are harassed or 
             threatened   nor   any   acts   of  violence   are 
             committed against them. If anybody is foundPage 5 of 6HC-NIC                       Page 5 of 6      Created On Fri Jul 15 02:45:39 IST 2016
                    R/SCR.A/2287/2016                                              ORDER



                       doing   so,   he   should   be   proceeded   against 
                       sternly   in   accordance   with   law,   by   the 
                       authorities concerned."6.In view of aforesaid facts and circumstances of

                                             ORAL ORDER1.           By      way      of      the         present           petition,              the
         petitioner           challenges              illegality                of       the        FIR
         registered as I-C.R. No. 141 of 2015 registered
         with Sayajiganj Police Station underSections 363and366of the Indian Penal Code.2.           During          the     pendency             of      the       complaint,
         the parties have entered into a compromise and
         have     chosen          to     end        all        their          disputes.                  An
         affidavit          of        both      the           complainant                and        her
         daughter        are      also       brought           on      record,            who       are
         present before this Court.                           According to them, no
         grievance survives, now. It is also the say of
         the prosecutrix that she had, on her own, gone to
         Delhi and nobody is to be blamed for the same.
         Likewise, the complainant has also stated that
         due to some misunderstanding he had alleged ofPage 1 of 4HC-NIC                                       Page 1 of 4       Created On Thu Aug 25 06:51:15 IST 2016
                 R/SCR.A/6045/2016                                                ORDER



         kidnapping.3.          The learned Advocate appearing for the
         complainant-Respondent No.2, Mr. Dave, has urged
         that   in     all          probabilities          this         may        help        the
         prosecutrix in bringing lasting peace between the
         parties.        At present, they have chosen to bury
         all their disputes.4.In above view of the matter, here, it
         would be profitable to refer to the observations
         made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case ofGIAN SINGH VS. STATE OF PUNJAB AND ANR., (2012) 10
         SCC 303, wherein, at Paragraph-61, the Apex Court
         observed as under;"61. The position that emerges from
                            the    above     discussion    can    be
                            summarised thus: the power of the
                            High Court in quashing a criminal
                            proceeding or FIR or complaint in
                            exercise of its inherent jurisdiction
                            is distinct and different from the
                            power given to a criminal court for
                            compounding     the    offences    underSection 320of the Code. Inherent
                            power is of wide plenitude with no
                            statutory limitation but it has to be
                            exercised    in     accord   with    the
                            guideline engrafted in such power
                            viz.,(i) to    secure    the   ends   of
                            justice or (ii)     to prevent abuse of
                            the process of any Court. In what
                            cases power to quash the criminal
                            proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may
                            be exercised where the offender andPage 2 of 4HC-NIC                                   Page 2 of 4      Created On Thu Aug 25 06:51:15 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/6045/2016                                            ORDER



                     victim have settled their dispute
                     would    depend    on    the    facts   and
                     circumstances of each case and no
                     category can be prescribed. However,
                     before exercise of such power, the
                     High Court must have due regard to
                     the nature and gravity of the crime.
                     Heinous    and   serious      offences   of
                     mental depravity or offences like
                     murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be
                     fittingly quashed even though the
                     victim or victim's family and the
                     offender have settled the dispute.
                     Such offences are not private in
                     nature and have serious impact on
                     society. Similarly, any compromise
                     between the victim and offender in
                     relation    to    the    offences     under
                     special statutes likePrevention of
                     Corruption     Actor   the     offences
                     committed by public servants while
                     working in that capacity etc; cannot
                     provide for any basis for quashing
                     criminal proceedings involving such
                     offences. But the criminal cases
                     having     overwhelmingly       and    pre-
                     dominatingly civil flavour stand on
                     different footing for the purposes of
                     quashing, particularly the offences
                     arising from commercial, financial,
                     mercantile, civil, partnership or
                     such    like    transactions       or   the
                     offences arising out of matrimony
                     relating to dowry, etc. or the family
                     disputes where the wrong is basically
                     private or personal in nature and the
                     parties have resolved their entire
                     dispute. In this category of cases,
                     High    Court    may     quash     criminal
                     proceedings if in its view, because
                     of    the    compromise      between    the
                     offender and victim, the possibility
                     of conviction is remote and bleak and
                     continuation of criminal case wouldPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                        Page 3 of 4      Created On Thu Aug 25 06:51:15 IST 2016
                    R/SCR.A/6045/2016                                                 ORDER



                               put accused to great oppression and
                               prejudice and extreme injustice would
                               be caused to him by not quashing the
                               criminal   case   despite   full   and
                               complete settlement and compromise
                               with the victim. In other words, the
                               High Court must consider whether it
                               would be unfair or contrary to the
                               interest of justice to continue with
                               the     criminal     proceeding     or
                               continuation     of    the    criminal
                               proceeding would tantamount to abuse
                               of process of law despite settlement
                               and compromise between the victim and
                               wrongdoer and whether to secure the
                               ends of justice, it is appropriate
                               that criminal case is put to an end
                               and if the answer to the above
                               question(s) is in affirmative, the
                               High Court shall be well within its
                               jurisdiction to quash the criminal
                               proceeding."5.            Resultantly,              the       request          for       quashment
         is      acceded        to     and     the         impugned           complaint                 is
         QUASHED         with          all      consequential                   proceedings.

         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         HARSH V GAJJAR, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 2
         MS CHETNA SHAH, ADDL. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s)

         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                          Date : 15/06/2016


                                           ORAL ORDER1.     Applicants         have       approached             this       Court         seeking

         quashment of the First Information Report being C.R.No.I-53 of

         2016         registered       with       Deesa          Rural         police         station,

         District:Banaskantha with the following reliefs:-"7.     The petitioners, therefore, prays that:-(A)   YOUR LORDSHIPS may be pleased to admit and allow
                the present petition.(B)   YOUR LORDSHIPS be pleased to issue appropriate
                order and or direction directing for quashing and setting
                aside of the FIR registered as C.R.No.I-53/2016 with Deesa
                Rural Police Station (District: Banaskantha) dated 3/5/2016
                and all other consequential proceedings thereto;(C)     YOUR LORDSHIPS be pleased to order that pendingPage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                        Page 1 of 5      Created On Tue Jun 21 01:15:06 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/11538/2016                                                  ORDERadmission and hearing of the present petition, the further
               proceedings of the FIR being C.R.No.I-53/2016 registered
               with Deesa Rural Police Station (Dist. Banaskantha) be
               stayed in the interest of justice;(D) YOUR LORDSHIPS be pleased to order that pending
               admission and hearing of the present petition, no coercive
               steps may be taken against the petitioners by the
               investigating authority.(E)   YOUR LORDSHIPS may be pleased to grant such
               other and further relief as may be deemed fit in the
               interest of justice."2.    Parties have chosen to settle the disputes. Affidavit-in-

         reply filed by the complainant suggests that they are cousins

         and dispute being personal in nature, they do not intend to

         continue the prosecution. It was a pure commercial transaction

         and   an    amicable         end    is    brought        to     the      dispute.         The

         complainant when asked, he says that no grievance survives.3.    The learned advocate Mr. B.S.Khatanu appearing for the

         respondent No.2 confirms the aspect of settlement by and

         between the parties.4.    He    urges      that    he      may       be     permitted           to     file       his

         Vakalatnama on behalf of respondent No.2 during the course

         of the day. Permission as prayed for is granted.5.    Having considered the submissions made on behalf of

         both the sides and the fact that it is a private dispute and the

         parties have arrived at an amicable settlement, especiallyPage 2 of 5HC-NIC                                      Page 2 of 5      Created On Tue Jun 21 01:15:06 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/11538/2016                                             ORDER



         when the respondent No.2 has chosen to put an end to the

         matter, no cause survives and, therefore, it would be desirable

         to quash the first information report in view of the decision of

         the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh v. State of Punjab

         and another, reported in AIR 2012 SC (Supp.) 838,

         whereby it is held that it is the duty of the Courts to encourage

         genuine settlements andsection 482of the Code of Criminal

         Procedure, 1973, enables the High Court to pass such orders.It

         would be beneficial to reproduce the relevant observations and

         findings of the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra),

         which read as under :"53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on the
              ground of settlement between an offender and victim is not
              the same thing as compounding of offence. They are
              different and not interchangeable. Strictly speaking, the
              power of compounding of offences given to a court underSection 320is materially different from the quashing of
              criminal proceedings by the High Court in exercise of its
              inherent jurisdiction. In compounding of offences, power of a
              criminal court is circumscribed by the provisions contained
              inSection 320and the court is guided solely and squarely
              thereby while, on the other hand, the formation of opinion
              by the High Court for quashing a criminal offence or criminal
              proceeding or criminal complaint is guided by the material
              on record as to whether the ends of justice would justify
              such exercise of power although the ultimate consequence
              may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.54. Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding
              having regard to the fact that dispute between the offender
              and victim has been settled although offences are not
              compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, continuation of
              criminal proceedings will be an exercise in futility and justice
              in the case demands that the dispute between the parties is
              put to an end and peace is restored; securing the ends of
              justice being the ultimate guiding factor. No doubt, crimes
              are acts which have harmful effect on the public and consistPage 3 of 5HC-NIC                                Page 3 of 5      Created On Tue Jun 21 01:15:06 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/11538/2016                                                 ORDER



              in wrong doing that seriously endangers and threatens well-
              being of society and it is not safe to leave the crimedoer
              only because he and the victim have settled the dispute
              amicably or that the victim has been paid compensation, yet
              certain crimes have been made compoundable in law, with
              or without permission of the Court. In respect of serious
              offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc; or other offences of
              mental depravity underIPCor offences of moral turpitude
              under special statutes, likePrevention of Corruption Actor
              the offences committed by public servants while working in
              that capacity, the settlement between offender and victim
              can have no legal sanction at all. However, certain offences
              which overwhelmingly and predominantly bear civil flavour
              having arisen out of civil, mercantile, commercial, financial,
              partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising
              out of matrimony, particularly relating to dowry, etc. or the
              family dispute, where the wrong is basically to victim and
              the offender and victim have settled all disputes between
              them amicably, irrespective of the fact that such offences
              have not been made compoundable, the High Court may
              within the framework of its inherent power, quash the
              criminal proceeding or criminal complaint or F.I.R if it is
              satisfied that on the face of such settlement,there is hardly
              any likelihood of offender being convicted and by not
              quashing the criminal proceedings, justice shall be casualty
              and ends of justice shall be defeated. The above list is
              illustrative and not exhaustive. Each case will depend on its
              own facts and no hard and fast category can be prescribed."6.   For the foregoing reasons and in view of the decisions of

         the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra), the present

         application succeeds and the same is, accordingly, allowed in

         view of an amicable settlement arrived at by and between the

         parties. The first information report being C.R.No.I-53 of 2016

         registered        with      Deesa               Rural          police             station,

         District:Banaskantha        and   all       the     proceedings             emanating

         therefrom, are quashed and set aside. Application is disposed

         of accordingly.Page 4 of 5HC-NIC                                 Page 4 of 5         Created On Tue Jun 21 01:15:06 IST 2016
                     R/CR.MA/11538/2016                                            ORDER



                  Direct Service is permitted.

                     High Court must consider whether it
                     would be unfair or contrary to the
                     interest of justice to continue with
                     the     criminal       proceeding      or
                     continuation      of     the     criminal
                     proceeding would tantamount to abuse
                     of process of law despite settlementPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                        Page 3 of 4      Created On Wed Sep 21 03:22:31 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/23908/2016                                                  ORDER



                             and compromise between the victim and
                             wrongdoer and whether to secure the
                             ends of justice, it is appropriate
                             that criminal case is put to an end
                             and if the answer to the above
                             question(s) is in affirmative, the
                             High Court shall be well within its
                             jurisdiction to quash the criminal
                             proceeding."5.           Since, the parties                        have settled their
         disputes, though, some of the offences are not
         compoundable,                the    request            for         quashment                  is
         acceded to.6.           Resultantly,              this         petition            is       ALLOWED
         and the impugned complaint is QUASHED with all
         consequential                proceedings.            Direct            service                is

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

                         AMAR BABULAL PATEL & 2....Applicant(s)

         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         DARSHAN M VARANDANI, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 3
         MR RONAK RAVAL, ADDL. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s)
         No. 1
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                      Date : 21/06/2016


                                       ORAL ORDER1.   Applicants   have   approached   this   Court   for 

         quashment of the First Information Report ("the FIR"for   short)   being   C.R.No.II­3048   of   2010   registered 

         with   Ghatlodia   police   station   for   the   offences 

         punishable under sections 427, 294­A, 506(2) and 114 

         of theIndian Penal Code.2.   Parties   have   chosen   to   settle   their     disputes. 

         Respondent No.2 has filed his affidavit confirming itsPage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                 Page 1 of 5        Created On Tue Jun 28 00:40:47 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/12915/2016                                                ORDER



         contents   and   stating   therein   that   they   have   settled 

         the disputes which are purely personal in nature.4.   The   learned   counsel   Mr.Prajapati   appearing   for 

         the respondent No.2 confirms the aspect of settlement 

         by and between the parties.5.   He   urges   that   he   may   be   permitted   to   file   his 

         Vakalatnama   on   behalf   of   the   respondent   No.2   during 

         the   course   of   the   day.   Permission   as   prayed   for   is 

         granted.6.   Having considered the submissions made on behalf 

         of both the sides and the fact that it is a private 

         dispute   and   the   parties   have   arrived   at   an   amicable 

         settlement, especially when respondent No.2 has chosen 

         to put an end to the matter, no cause survives and, 

         therefore,   it   would   be   desirable   to   quash   the  first 

         information report in view of the decision of the Apex 

         Court in the case ofGian   Singh   v.  State   of   Punjab  

         and   another,   reported   in   AIR   2012   SC   (Supp.)   838, 

         whereby it is held that it is the duty of the Courts 

         to   encourage   genuine   settlements   andsection   482ofPage 2 of 5HC-NIC                                Page 2 of 5        Created On Tue Jun 28 00:40:47 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/12915/2016                                                ORDER



         theCode of Criminal Procedure, 1973, enables the High 

         Court to pass such orders.It would be beneficial to 

         reproduce   the   relevant   observations   and   findings   of 

         the   Apex   Court   in   the   case   ofGian   Singh(supra), 

         which read as under :"53.   Quashing   of   offence   or   criminal  
              proceedings on the ground of settlement between 
              an offender and victim is not the same thing as 
              compounding of offence. They are different and 
              not   interchangeable.   Strictly   speaking,   the 
              power   of   compounding   of   offences   given   to   a 
              court underSection 320is materially different 
              from   the   quashing   of   criminal   proceedings   by  
              the   High   Court   in   exercise   of   its   inherent  
              jurisdiction. In compounding of offences, power 
              of   a   criminal   court   is   circumscribed   by   the 
              provisions   contained   inSection   320and   the 
              court   is   guided   solely   and   squarely   thereby 
              while,   on   the   other   hand,   the   formation   of  
              opinion   by   the   High   Court   for   quashing   a  
              criminal   offence   or   criminal   proceeding   or  
              criminal complaint is guided by the material on 
              record as to whether the ends of justice would 
              justify   such   exercise   of   power   although   the 
              ultimate   consequence   may   be   acquittal   or  
              dismissal of indictment.54.  Where   High   Court   quashes   a   criminal 
              proceeding   having   regard   to   the   fact   that 
              dispute   between   the   offender   and   victim   has 
              been   settled   although   offences   are   not 
              compoundable,   it   does   so   as   in   its   opinion, 
              continuation of criminal proceedings will be an 
              exercise   in   futility   and   justice   in   the   case 
              demands that the dispute between the parties is 
              put to an end and peace is restored; securing 
              the ends of justice being the ultimate guiding 
              factor.   No   doubt,   crimes   are   acts   which   havePage 3 of 5HC-NIC                               Page 3 of 5        Created On Tue Jun 28 00:40:47 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/12915/2016                                                ORDER



              harmful   effect   on   the  public   and   consist   in 
              wrong   doing   that   seriously   endangers   and  
              threatens well­being of society and it is not 
              safe to leave the crimedoer only because he and  
              the victim have settled the dispute amicably or 
              that the victim has been paid compensation, yet 
              certain crimes have been made compoundable in 
              law, with or without permission of the Court. 
              In   respect   of   serious   offences   like   murder, 
              rape, dacoity, etc; or other offences of mental 
              depravity   underIPCor   offences   of   moral 
              turpitude   under   special   statutes,   likePrevention   of   Corruption   Actor   the   offences  
              committed by public servants while working in 
              that capacity, the settlement between offender  
              and victim can have no legal sanction at all. 
              However, certain offences which overwhelmingly 
              and   predominantly   bear   civil   flavour   having  
              arisen   out   of   civil,   mercantile,   commercial, 
              financial,   partnership   or   such   like 
              transactions   or   the   offences   arising   out   of 
              matrimony, particularly relating to dowry, etc. 
              or   the   family   dispute,   where   the   wrong   is 
              basically to victim and the offender and victim 
              have   settled   all   disputes   between   them 
              amicably,   irrespective   of   the   fact   that   such  
              offences have not been made compoundable, the 
              High   Court   may   within   the   framework   of   its  
              inherent   power,   quash   the   criminal   proceeding  
              or   criminal   complaint   or   F.I.R   if   it   is  
              satisfied   that   on   the   face   of   such 
              settlement,there   is   hardly   any   likelihood   of 
              offender   being   convicted   and   by   not   quashing  
              the   criminal   proceedings,   justice   shall   be 
              casualty and ends of justice shall be defeated. 
              The   above   list   is   illustrative   and   not 
              exhaustive.   Each   case   will   depend   on   its   own 
              facts   and   no   hard   and   fast   category   can   be 
              prescribed.7.   For   the   foregoing   reasons   and   in   view   of   thePage 4 of 5HC-NIC                               Page 4 of 5        Created On Tue Jun 28 00:40:47 IST 2016
                    R/CR.MA/12915/2016                                                ORDER



         decisions of the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra), the present application succeeds and the same 

         is,   accordingly,   allowed   in   view   of   an   amicable 

         settlement arrived at by and between the parties. The 

         first information report  being  C.R.No.II­3048 of 2010 

         registered with Ghatlodia police station  and all the 

         proceedings  emanating therefrom,  are quashed  and set 

         aside. Rule is made absolute accordingly.Direct Service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

              CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                                 FIR/ORDER) NO. 24049 of 2016
         ==========================================================
                    ALPESH JAYANTILAL GURU & 1....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                      STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         A S TIMBALIA, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 2
         MR RONAK RAVAL, PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         MR SS SAIYED, for the Respondent(s) No. 2
         ==========================================================
         CORAM:             HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
                                  Date : 20/09/2016
                                        ORAL ORDER1.           Both       the    petitioners             are       the        original
         accused, who are seeking the quashment of the
         complaint being I-C.R. No. 46 of 2016 registered
         with Bopal Police Station underSections 406,420and114of the Indian Penal Code.2.           It is a case of transfer of the landbeing      Block         No.    39,           admeasuring             about           730sq.mts.,         situated         at          Village:            Lapkaman                 by
         Petitioner No.1 to two persons and one of them is
         the original complainant-Respondent No.2, herein,
         and the second person is Petitioner No.2, herein.
         The second sale deed led to the filing of the
         impugned complaint and also a suit being Regular
         Civil Suit No. 160/2013 for cancellation of sale
         deed registered in favour of Petitioner No.2.Page 1 of 6HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 6      Created On Thu Sep 22 01:13:13 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/24049/2016                                                     ORDER3.           The parties have chosen to settle all
         their     disputes             amicable,               and        therefore,                the
         petitioners are before this Court.4.           This            Court         has         verified               from          the
         complainant-Respondent No.2, who is present with
         her    husband,          that        no       grievance              survives             now.
         According to the complainant-Respondent No.2, she
         and her family had always been in possession of
         the said property and as the sale deed registered
         in    favour       of        Petitioner            No.2        is      canceled,                 no
         grievance survives now.5.           Learned           Advocate               for     the         petitioners,
         Mr. Timbalia, urged that before the Civil Court
         concerned         also        a   joint            pursis            is      submitted,
         requesting the Court concerned to pass a decree
         pursuant        to       such         a       compromise                between             the
         parties. He has assured this Court to place on
         record      the       receipt             issued            by      the        concerned
         department in regard to the cancellation of the
         sale deed registered in favour of Petitioner No.2
         reflecting the cancellation as well as a copy of
         the decree passed by the Civil Court concerned in
         wake of the compromise between the parties.6.           Learned              APP                 has           assured,                     on
         instructions, that the petitioners neither havePage 2 of 6HC-NIC                                        Page 2 of 6       Created On Thu Sep 22 01:13:13 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/24049/2016                                                  ORDER



         criminal       antecedents            nor          are      there         any         other
         victims of the present crime.7.           As       the      parties             have         settled               their
         disputes amicably and before the Civil Court a
         decree is sought on the basis of the compromise
         between the parties and the subsequent sale deed
         registered in favour of Petitioner No.2, herein,
         is now cancelled, the request for quashment needs
         to be acceded to.8.In wake of the above, here, it would be
         profitable          to       refer     to      the         decision              of      the
         Hon'ble Apex Court in the case ofGIAN SINGH VS.
         STATE    OF     PUNJAB        AND     ANR.,         (2012)           10      SCC       303,
         wherein, at Paragraph-61, the Apex Court observed
         as under;""61. The position that emerges from
                             the    above     discussion    can    be
                             summarised thus: the power of the
                             High Court in quashing a criminal
                             proceeding or FIR or complaint in
                             exercise of its inherent jurisdiction
                             is distinct and different from the
                             power given to a criminal court for
                             compounding     the    offences    underSection 320of the Code. Inherent
                             power is of wide plenitude with no
                             statutory limitation but it has to be
                             exercised    in     accord   with    the
                             guideline engrafted in such power
                             viz.,(i)to secure the ends of justice
                             or (ii) to prevent abuse of the
                             process of any Court. In what casesPage 3 of 6HC-NIC                                    Page 3 of 6        Created On Thu Sep 22 01:13:13 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/24049/2016                                            ORDER



                     power     to     quash      the     criminal
                     proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may
                     be exercised where the offender and
                     victim have settled their dispute
                     would    depend     on    the    facts   and
                     circumstances of each case and no
                     category can be prescribed. However,
                     before exercise of such power, the
                     High Court must have due regard to
                     the nature and gravity of the crime.
                     Heinous    and    serious      offences   of
                     mental depravity or offences like
                     murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be
                     fittingly quashed even though the
                     victim or victim's family and the
                     offender have settled the dispute.
                     Such offences are not private in
                     nature and have serious impact on
                     society. Similarly, any compromise
                     between the victim and offender in
                     relation     to    the    offences     under
                     special statutes likePrevention of
                     Corruption      Actor    the    offences
                     committed by public servants while
                     working in that capacity etc; cannot
                     provide for any basis for quashing
                     criminal proceedings involving such
                     offences. But the criminal cases
                     having     overwhelmingly        and    pre-
                     dominatingly civil flavour stand on
                     different footing for the purposes of
                     quashing, particularly the offences
                     arising from commercial, financial,
                     mercantile, civil, partnership or
                     such    like     transactions       or   the
                     offences arising out of matrimony
                     relating to dowry, etc. or the family
                     disputes where the wrong is basically
                     private or personal in nature and the
                     parties have resolved their entire
                     dispute. In this category of cases,
                     High    Court     may     quash     criminal
                     proceedings if in its view, because
                     of    the    compromise       between    thePage 4 of 6HC-NIC                        Page 4 of 6      Created On Thu Sep 22 01:13:13 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/24049/2016                                                     ORDER



                               offender and victim, the possibility
                               of conviction is remote and bleak and
                               continuation of criminal case would
                               put accused to great oppression and
                               prejudice and extreme injustice would
                               be caused to him by not quashing the
                               criminal   case   despite   full   and
                               complete settlement and compromise
                               with the victim. In other words, the
                               High Court must consider whether it
                               would be unfair or contrary to the
                               interest of justice to continue with
                               the     criminal     proceeding     or
                               continuation     of    the    criminal
                               proceeding would tantamount to abuse
                               of process of law despite settlement
                               and compromise between the victim and
                               wrongdoer and whether to secure the
                               ends of justice, it is appropriate
                               that criminal case is put to an end
                               and if the answer to the above
                               question(s) is in affirmative, the
                               High Court shall be well within its
                               jurisdiction to quash the criminal
                               proceeding."9.          Resultantly, this petition is ALLOWED and
         the    impugned             complaint            is       QUASHED             with          all
         consequential               proceedings,                  SUBJECT               TO          the
         Petitioners           placing         on        record         a      copy         of      the
         receipt     issued          by    the       concerned               department                  in
         regard      to    the        cancellation                 of       the      sale         deed
         registered in favour of Petitioner No.2 and a
         copy   of       the    decree         passed           by      the       Civil          Court

         after this Court had passed an order                                          in Special

         He    has         urged         that     in      the          right         spirit,         the
         investigation needs to continue and/or there is a
         requirement              of     transfer         of      investigation to                        a
         superior officer to oversee the investigation.5.    This Court notices that the specimen writings of
         the petitioner have already been collected by the
         Investigating Officer. Those documents with the
         disputed writings and signature has been forwarded
         to the Forensic Science Laboratory (for short "FSL")
         and        therefore,           this     Court           had          directed              the
         Investigating Officer to get in writing the possible
         time the FSL is likely to take for delivering the
         report for            these documents which have already
         been sent for examination.6.    Learned APP Ms. Chetna Shah has brought to
         the notice of this Court that the communication
         received from the FSL is indicative of the fact that it
         may        take        minimum           two          months'              period               for
         preparing the report, considering the pendency ofPage 2 of 6HC-NIC                                      Page 2 of 6        Created On Fri Sep 23 01:39:29 IST 2016
                 R/SCR.A/5068/2016                                                ORDER



         other serious matters like murder , POSCO etc.7.   One of the grievances since is that the
         Investigating Officer insisted to give the specimen
         writings/signature as is found in the disputed
         documents, it is necessary for this Court to refer to
         the order passed by this Court in Special Criminal
         Application No. 19877 of 2015                            dated 26.4.2016
         wherein the Court had directed the Applicant to
         provide her specimen writings of the signatures as
         required by the Scientific Officer looking after the
         Handwriting and Photographic Bureau.8.   With regard to              the averment set out in the
         petition, it is clearly referred to in the petition memo
         that the respondent No.2 had made, the petitioner
         copy the signatures              and has refused to take the
         natural handwriting of the petitioner despite the
         petitioner making repeated requests to furnish his
         natural handwriting. It surely does not amount to
         making forged signature as averred if otherwise the
         Investigating Officer has followed the criminal
         manual in respect of collection of sample.The collection of specimen writings is
         directed to be             completed in the manual and the
         same is also to be sent to the FSL. Once collected,
         the report needs to be obtained at the earliest, butPage 3 of 6HC-NIC                                  Page 3 of 6      Created On Fri Sep 23 01:39:29 IST 2016
                 R/SCR.A/5068/2016                                                   ORDER



         in no case later than four weeks from the date of
         receipt of these documents from the Handwritings
         and Photographic Bureau, Directorate of Forensic
         Science, Gandhinagar.9.   The Investigating Officer if has not followed the
         directions which are referred to hereinabove, he
         shall revisit the issue . This Court is aware of the
         fact that the FSL has already been sent the disputed
         handwriting         with      the       natural            handwriting                  and
         specimen writing.             So as not to give rise to any
         dispute     in      future     that          the        collection               of      the
         writing/signature was not in accordance with law,
         at this stage,             directions given earlier in Special
         Criminal      Application           No.           19877           of      2015           are
         reiterated.10. The reiterating grievance which can be noticed
         from the petition is the non-arrest of the accused
         despite      rejection         of       the         application                 of       the
         anticipatory bail by the District Court which                                                is
         alleged to be the act of                shielding               the accused by
         the Investigating Agency.11. This Court has noticed the say of the petitioner
         that the amount was paid by the petitioner to the
         Company          towards       the                consideration                  of      the
         purchase of the share by the petitioner from onePage 4 of 6HC-NIC                                  Page 4 of 6         Created On Fri Sep 23 01:39:29 IST 2016
                R/SCR.A/5068/2016                                            ORDER



         Amit Singh who is co-accused in this case. It is also
         his case that the company has paid the interest at
         the rate of 12% per annum for the financial year
         2014-15, in April, 2015 and the cheque was duly
         signed by the proposed accused Mr.Amit Singh.
         After various rounds of meetings, the petitioner was
         lured into advancing a huge sum of Rs.1,62,50,000/-
         to the accused.12.        This Court needed to direct the police
         authority to lodge the complaint in wake of the
         allegations. It is to be noted that the purpose of the
         investigation is to reach the truth of the matter. The
         investigation is going on. This Court will not dilate
         any of the disputes involved but, at the same time
         the Investigating Officer is also directed to look into
         all the aspects averred in the complaint and carry
         out the investigation in accordance with law,
         instead of merely waiting for the outcome of the
         report of the FSL.13. Mr. N.G.Pahwa learned advocate appearing for
         the respondent No.2 has urged that the Company
         petition No. 348 of 2015 is filed by the present
         petitioner for winding up underSection 433(e),434(1)(a)and439(1)(b)of the Companies Act read
         with Rule 95 of the Company Court Rules wherein,Page 5 of 6HC-NIC                             Page 5 of 6      Created On Fri Sep 23 01:39:29 IST 2016
                   R/SCR.A/5068/2016                                            ORDER



         the detailed reply has been supplied by the present
         respondent by way of affidavit in reply. Bearing in
         mind these details, suffice to directed that                                        the
         investigation shall be completed as far as possible
         within a period of 10 weeks from the date of receipt

         endeavour to deliver the report of the disputed
         documents which have already been sent to it,
         within 10 weeks unless the Investigating Officer find
         it necessary to once again take the specimen
         handwriting of the petitioner as is directed in
         Special Criminal Application No. 19877 of 2015.14. None of the observations made by this Court

                                          ORAL ORDER[1]     The present application is filed underSection 439of the Code
         of Criminal Procedure by the applicant for regular bail in connection
         with an FIR being C.R.No.I-5 of 2016 registered with Aadesar
         Police Station, Gandhidham Kutch East for the offences underSections 302, 498A,201read withSection 114of the Indian Penal
         Code.[2]     Learned senior counsel Mr.Nirupam Nanavati for Nanavaty
         Advocates for the applicant submits that the FIR came to be filed on
         16.01.2016 whereas alleged incident took place three months prior to
         the date of the FIR. The role attributed to the present applicant who is
         father-in-law of the deceased lady is that he has buried the dead
         body meaning thereby allegations underSection 201is alleged
         against the applicant. It is submitted that applicant has not played
         any role in committing murder of the deceased. It is further submitted
         that the applicant who is senior citizen aged about 70 years is in
         judicial custody since 1.02.2016. Moreover, investigation is over and
         charge-sheet has been submitted and therefore, now there is no
         possibility of tampering with the evidence and he is ready and willingPage 1 of 3HC-NIC                                     Page 1 of 3      Created On Sat Aug 06 00:39:19 IST 2016
                      R/CR.MA/15234/2016                                            ORDER



         to abide by the terms and conditions that may be imposed by the
         Court under the circumstances, the applicant may be enlarged on
         regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.[3]   Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the
         respondent-State has opposed this application and submitted that
         looking to the charge-sheet papers there is a prima facie case against
         the present applicant for committing serious offence and looking to
         the nature and gravity of the offence, the applicant may not be
         enlarged on bail.[4]   I have heard learned advocates appearing on behalf of the
         respective parties. Learned advocates appearing on behalf of the
         respective parties do not invite reasoned order.[5]   Regard being had to the above submissions and considering
         the nature of allegations made against the present applicant in the
         FIR and other charge-sheet papers as also looking to the nature of
         accusation made against the applicant from the charge-sheet papers,
         the present applicant who is senior citizen aged about 70 years
         deserves to be enlarged on bail as the investigation is over and
         charge-sheet has been filed now having no possibility of tampering
         with the evidence by imposing following conditions.[6]   Hence, the present application is allowed and the applicant is
         ordered to be released on regular bail in connection with an offence
         being C.R.No.I-5 of 2016 registered with Aadesar Police
         Station, Gandhidham Kutch East on executing a personal bond of
         Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand Only) with one surety of the like
         amount to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court and subject to
         the conditions that the applicant shall;[a]       not take undue advantage of liberty or misuse liberty;
               [b]       not act in a manner injurious to the interest of the
                         prosecution;Page 2 of 3HC-NIC                                    Page 2 of 3      Created On Sat Aug 06 00:39:19 IST 2016
                      R/CR.MA/15234/2016                                             ORDER



               [c]       surrender passport, if any, to the lower court within a
                         week;
               [d]       not leave the State of Gujarat without prior permission of
                         the Sessions Judge concerned;
               [e]       mark presence before the Aadesar Police Station,Gandhidham Kutch East once in a month between
                         11:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. on Monday of every English
                         calendar month till the trial is not commenced;
               [f]       furnish latest and permanent address of residence to the
                         Investigating Officer and also to the Court at the time of
                         execution of the bond and shall not change the residence
                         without prior permission of this Court;[g]       the applicant shall not try to contact, approach or make
                         any      endevour to influence to witness Nandini or any
                         other witness of maternal side or those who are taking
                         care of minor Nandini.[7]    The Authorities will release the applicant only if he is not
         required in connection with any other offence for the time being. If
         breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions
         Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take appropriate
         action in the matter. Bail bond to be executed before the learned
         Lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case. It will be open for the
         concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above
         conditions, in accordance with law. At the trial, learned Trial Court
         shall not be influenced by the observations of preliminary nature, qua
         the evidence at this stage, made by this Court while enlarging the
         applicant on bail.[8]    Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent. Direct service is
         permitted.(P.P.BHATT, J.)
