                    IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD


         CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR REGULAR BAIL) NO. 12286 of 2012

                           In CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 1246 of 2012

         ==========================================================
                     RAMSINGBHAI SAMJIBHAI BHABHOR....Applicant(s)
                                      Versus
                          STATE OF GUJARAT....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR VIJAY PATEL, ADVOCATE for HL PATEL ADVOCATES, ADVOCATE for
         the Applicant(s) No. 1
         MS HANSA PUNANI ADDITIONAL PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the
         RESPONDENT(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

                  CORAM: HONOURABLE MS.JUSTICE HARSHA DEVANI
                         and
                         HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE G.R.UDHWANI

                                         Date : 28/01/2016


                                          ORAL ORDER(PER : HONOURABLE MS.JUSTICE HARSHA DEVANI)1.    By     this     application,         the         applicant-convict                 seeks
         suspension of the order of sentence dated 30.6.2012 passed
         by the learned Principal Sessions Judge, Dahod in Sessions
         Case No.16 of 2009.2.    Mr. Vijay Patel, learned advocate for the applicant
         submitted      that       the   prosecution              case        is     based         upon
         circumstantial        evidence.       It        was      submitted            that        three
         circumstances have been held to have been proved againstPage 1 of 6HC-NIC                                     Page 1 of 6         Created On Sat Jan 30 00:35:15 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/12286/2012                                                ORDER



         the applicant herein. The first circumstance is in the nature of
         a confessional statement of the applicant before the witnesses,
         secondly, the theory of last seen together and lastly, a
         demonstration panchnama whereby the accused had shown
         the scene of incident as well as the motorcycle. It was
         submitted that insofar as the confessional statement is
         concerned, it is an admitted position that the same was made
         at the time when the applicant was in the custody of police.
         Under the circumstances, the same is hit bysections 25and26of the Evidence Act and is not admissible in evidence. As
         regards the theory of last seen together, it was submitted that
         in terms of the evidence which has come on record, the
         applicant is stated to have dropped the deceased at the place
         of one Shakuntalaben, however, no evidence has been brought
         on record as regards what happened thereafter. It was
         submitted that insofar as the demonstration panchnama
         stated to have been drawn undersection 27of the Evidence
         Act is concerned, no incriminating material has been recovered
         and, therefore, the same is also not admissible in evidence. It
         was submitted that if the documentary and oral evidence of
         confession is taken out, the other evidence does not connect
         the applicant with the offence in question.2.1    Reliance was placed upon the decision of the Supreme
         Court in the case ofAghnoo Nagesia v. State of Bihar, AIR
         1966 SC 199 as well as on the decision of a Division Bench of
         this court in the case ofPatel Manabhai Mavjibhai v. State
         of Gujarat, 2013 (4) GLR 3215 for the proposition that the
         court cannot make extra-judicial confession as the basis and
         then search for corroboration. The correct approach for the
         court would be to first consider and marshal the evidencePage 2 of 6HC-NIC                              Page 2 of 6     Created On Sat Jan 30 00:35:15 IST 2016
               R/CR.MA/12286/2012                                                   ORDER



         against    the     accused   excluding        extra-judicial            confession
         altogether from consideration and only if on such consideration
         of evidence available, other than extra-judicial confession a
         conviction can be safely based, then only extra-judicial
         confession could be used to support their belief or conclusion.
         It was submitted that extra-judicial confession being a very
         weak type of evidence, requires consideration with great
         caution and in the absence of any corroborative evidence, the
         same cannot be relied upon. It was submitted that apart from
         the fact that the so-called extra-judicial confession is not
         admissible in evidence, even otherwise in the absence of any
         corroborative evidence, the same cannot be made the basis of
         conviction. Under the circumstances, the relief prayed for in
         the application deserves to be granted and the applicant is
         required to be enlarged on bail.3.    Opposing the application, Ms. Hansa Punani, learned
         Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that the prosecution
         through the testimony of the witnesses has duly proved the
         charge against the accused. It was submitted that the motive
         behind the incident has been duly proved by the prosecution,
         inasmuch as, the applicant had an illicit affair with the
         deceased and the DNA test has proved that the applicant was
         the father of the foetus. It was submitted that since deceased
         Urmila was insisting upon residing with the applicant, the
         applicant had done away with her.              It was further submitted
         that the prosecution witnesses, namely, Kabuben Harsingbhai
         Ninama and others have clearly stated that they had gone to
         the police station and that the applicant herein had confessed
         to them that he had committed murder of Urmila as she
         intended to reside with him as his wife but as his wife and sonPage 3 of 6HC-NIC                                Page 3 of 6     Created On Sat Jan 30 00:35:15 IST 2016
               R/CR.MA/12286/2012                                                 ORDER



         had refused to reside with her. It was submitted that apart
         from the confessional statement, the deceased was last seen
         with the applicant herein. Moreover, during the course of
         investigation the Investigating Officer had drawn a panchnama
         undersection 27of the Evidence Act whereby the motorcycle
         on which the applicant had taken the deceased has been
         recovered. It was submitted that in the light of the evidence
         which has come on record, no prima facie case has been made
         out so as to exercise discretion in favour of the applicant.4.    This court has considered the submissions advanced by
         the learned advocates for the respective parties and has
         perused the record and proceedings of the case as pointed out
         by the learned counsel for the respective parties.5.    On a perusal of the impugned judgment and order, it
         appears that the trial court has placed reliance mainly upon
         three circumstances, namely: the confessional statement of
         the accused to the witnesses; the theory of last seen together;
         and the discovery panchnama. On a perusal of the material
         which has come on record, insofar as the theory of last seen
         together is concerned, the prosecution case is that the
         applicant had dropped the deceased at the house of one
         Shakuntalaben, however, no evidence has been adduced as to
         where she went from the house of Shakuntalaben and with
         whom. No material has been brought on record to establish
         that the deceased had left the house of Shakuntalaben with
         the applicant. Prima facie, therefore, the theory of last seen
         together cannot be invoked in the present case.6.    As regards the extra-judicial confession made by thePage 4 of 6HC-NIC                              Page 4 of 6     Created On Sat Jan 30 00:35:15 IST 2016
               R/CR.MA/12286/2012                                                    ORDER



         application before the witnesses, it is an admitted position that
         such confession was made at the police station while the
         applicant was in the custody of the police. Prima facie,
         therefore, such confession would be hit bysections 25and26of the Evidence Act and would not be admissible in evidence.7.    While it is true that a panchnama undersection 27of the
         Evidence Act has been drawn by the Investigating Officer
         during the course of investigation, however, no incriminating
         material has been collected so as to connect the applicant with
         the offence in question.8.    In the aforesaid premises, the court is of the view that a
         prima facie case has been made out for exercise of discretion
         in favour of the applicant.9.    The application, therefore, succeeds and is, accordingly,
         allowed. The sentence imposed by the learned Principal
         Sessions Judge, Dahod vide judgment and order dated
         30.6.2012 in Sessions Case No.16 of 2009 is ordered to be
         suspended till the final hearing of the appeal. The applicant be
         released on regular bail on his executing a personal bond of
         Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one solvent
         surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the lower Court
         with following conditions;(a)    he shall not take undue advantage of his liberty or
                abuse his liberty;(b)    maintain law and order;Page 5 of 6HC-NIC                                 Page 5 of 6     Created On Sat Jan 30 00:35:15 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/12286/2012                                                       ORDER


                 (c)    surrender his passport, if any, to the lower court,within a week and if he does not possess any passport,
                 then he shall make a declaration to that effect before
                 the trial court;(d)     If during the pendency of the criminal appeal any
                 change       in    his   residential       address,          permanent              or
                 temporary, takes place, then the applicant shall intimate
                 the same to the trial court as well as the concerned
                 Police Station.10.     Bail before the trial court having jurisdiction.11.     However, it is made clear that any observations made
         while deciding this bail application will not affect merits of the
         case at the time of final arguments.12.    Rule is made absolute. Direct service is permitted.(HARSHA DEVANI, J.)

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

         SPECIAL CRIMINAL APPLICATION (DIRECTION - POLICE PROTECTION)
                                     NO. 1272 of 2016
         ==========================================================
               SANTOKBEN D/O. SHANKARBHAI NAYAK & 1....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                      STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR SANDIP M PATEL, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 2
         Mr.H.K.Patel, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================
          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                     Date : 02/03/2016



                                      ORAL ORDERLeave to amend is permitted. To implead the
         Dy.S.P as party respondent No. 3.Rule returnable today. Mr.H.K.Patel, learned
         APP waives service of notice for and on behalf of
         the respondents.The applicants herein are the husband and
         wife. Their         marriage has been registered on 15th
         January, 2016. They belong to the same community.
         However, it is their apprehension that a false
         complaint may be lodged against them and they
         apprehend           danger to their lives. Parents of the
         applicant No.1 are not in favour of this marriage.Page 1 of 7HC-NIC                                 Page 1 of 7      Created On Sun Mar 06 01:53:38 IST 2016
                  R/SCR.A/1272/2016                                                    ORDERThey have approached this Court underArticle 226of the Constitution of India seeking the following
         reliefs :-(A) Your Lordships may be pleased to admit and
                allow this application ;(B) This Honourable Court may be pleased to allow
                this Special Criminal Application by issuing an
                appropriate writ, order of direction, directing the
                respondent           authority            to       provide           the        police
                protection to the petitioners against the family of
                the      petitioner        No.1          and         further          direct        the
                respondents           to     not         to     register          any        offence
                regarding            the      petitioners                without             hearing
                considering the documents of the petitioners, in the
                interest of justice;(C) Your Lordships may be pleased to direct the
                concerned            authority           to      taken          concrete            and
                effective steps in the case of present petitioner in
                the interest of justice.(D) That this Honourable Court may be pleased to
                such other and further relief that may be deemed
                fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the
                case.Mr.S.M.Patel, learned advocate appearing for
         the applicants has urged that this is not a case of
         intercaste marriage but marriage within the same
         caste and community . However, as parents ofPage 2 of 7HC-NIC                                     Page 2 of 7         Created On Sun Mar 06 01:53:38 IST 2016
                  R/SCR.A/1272/2016                                             ORDER



         applicant No.1 have not accepted this marriage,
         there is a likelihood of some danger to both the
         applicants. They have also an apprehension                                               of
         violent acts          on behalf of            some members of the
         community           and therefore, they have approached
         this Court seeking police protection.Mr.H.K.Patel, learned APP has no objection if
         the Court gives an appropriate                         directions as the
         parties are reeling under the threat of so called
         honor of        the family or community.                         He has also
         pointed out the decision rendered in case ofLata
         Singh Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anotherreported in 2007(1) GLH 41
                Having thus heard both the sides. Petition
         deserves to be allowed, acceding to the request of
         the applicants to provide the protection as prayed
         for.It would be profitable to reproduce some of the
         observations made by the Apex Court in case ofLata Singh Vs. State of                        Uttar Pradesh and
         Another(Supra) :-"4. This case reveals a shocking state of
                     affairs. There is no dispute that the petitioner
                     is a major and was at all relevant times a major.Page 3 of 7HC-NIC                                Page 3 of 7       Created On Sun Mar 06 01:53:38 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/1272/2016                                              ORDERHence she is free to marry anyone she likes or
             live with anyone she likes. There is no bar to an
             inter-caste marriage under theHindu Marriage
             Actor any other law. Hence, we cannot see
             what offence was committed by the petitioner,
             her husband or her husband's relatives.5.       We are of the opinion that no offence was
             committed by any of the
             accused and the whole criminal case in question
             is an abuse of the process of the Court as well
             as of the administrative machinery at the
             instance of the petitioner's brothers who were
             only furious because the petitioner married
             outside her caste.               We are distressed to note
             that instead of taking action                            against the
             petitioner's brothers for their unlawful and high-
             handed acts (details of which have been set out
             above) the police has instead proceeded against
             the petitioner's husband and his relatives.6.       Since several such instances are coming to
             our knowledge of                  harassment, threats and
             violence against young men and women who
             marry outside their caste, we feel it necessary
             to make some general comments on the matter.The       nation   is      passing         through            a     crucial
             transitional period in our history, and this Court
             cannot remain silent in matters of great public
             concern, such as the present one.7.       The caste system is a curse on the nationPage 4 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 4 of 7      Created On Sun Mar 06 01:53:38 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/1272/2016                                                   ORDER




             and the sooner it is destroyed the better.                                         In
             fact, it is dividing the nation at a time when we
             have to be united to face the challenges before
             the       nation        unitedly.               Hence,           inter-caste
             marriages are in fact in the national interest as
             they will result in destroying the caste system.
             However, disturbing news are coming from
             several parts of the country that young men and
             women who undergo inter-caste marriage, are
             threatened with violence, or violence is actually
             committed on them. In our opinion, such acts of
             violence or threats or harassment are                                    wholly
             illegal and those who commit them must be
             severely             punished.            This       is     a      free       and
             democratic country, and once a person becomes
             a major he or she can marry whosoever he/she
             likes.      If the parents of the boy or girl do not
             approve of such inter-caste or inter-religious
             marriage the maximum they can do is that they
             can cut off social relations with the son or the
             daughter, but they cannot give threats or
             commit or instigate acts of violence and cannot
             harass the person who undergoes such inter-
             caste           or    inter-      religious         marriage.                 We,
             therefore, direct that the administration/police
             authorities throughout the country will see to it
             that if any boy or girl who is a major undergoes
             inter-caste or inter-religious marriage with a
             woman or man who is a major, the couple are
             not harassed                by any one nor subjected to
             threats or acts of violence, and any one whoPage 5 of 7HC-NIC                               Page 5 of 7      Created On Sun Mar 06 01:53:38 IST 2016
                R/SCR.A/1272/2016                                            ORDER




                   gives such threats or harasses or commits acts
                   of violence either himself or at his instigation, is
                   taken to task by instituting criminal proceedings
                   by the police against such persons and further
                   stern action is taken against such persons as
                   provided by law.8.       We sometimes hear of `honour' killings of
                   such persons who undergo inter-caste or inter-
                   religious marriage of their own free will. There
                   is    nothing honourable in such killings, and in
                   fact they are nothing but barbaric and shameful
                   acts of murder committed by brutal, feudal
                   minded persons who deserve harsh punishment.
                   Only in this way can we stamp out such acts of
                   barbarism."In the event of apprehension of honor killing at
         the hands of persons of the community, both the
         applicants deserve to be protected. The concerned
         Dy.S.P. shall direct the respondent No.2 to give
         necessary protection and do the needful in the
         matter and to ensure the         safety of both the
         applicants .With the above observations, this application
         stands disposed of. Rule is made absolute to the
         aforesaid extent.Direct service is permitted.Page 6 of 7HC-NIC                              Page 6 of 7      Created On Sun Mar 06 01:53:38 IST 2016
                 R/SCR.A/1272/2016                                           ORDER

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

         CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR REGULAR BAIL) NO. 11535 of 2016

         ==========================================================
               HIMALAY MAHESHBHAI MATAWALA( MACCHI)....Applicant(s)
                                    Versus
                        STATE OF GUJARAT....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR PM THAKKAR, SENIOR COUNSEL ASSISTED BY MR HARDIK A DAVE,
         ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         MS. BHAVNA D ACHARYA, ADVOCATE for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         MR JK SHAH, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE P.P.BHATT

                                     Date : 22/06/2016


                                      ORAL ORDER1.          The present application is filed underSection 439of the Code of Criminal Procedure by the applicant for
         regular bail in connection with First Information Report
         being C.R.No.I-234 of 2015 registered with Khatodara
         Police Station, District-Surat for the offences punishable
         underSections 302,120-B,201and34of the IPC andSection
         135(1)of the Gujarat Police Act.2.          Heard learned counsel for the applicant and
         learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State.3.          Mr.P.M.Thakkar, learned Senior Counsel for the
         applicant submits that the FIR was lodged after three daysPage 1 of 6HC-NIC                                 Page 1 of 6      Created On Fri Jun 24 02:28:26 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/11535/2016                                               ORDER



         from the date of alleged incident against unknown person and
         the entire case is based on circumstantial evidence. It is
         submitted that the case of the prosecution is mainly based on
         demonstration panchnama and extra judicial confession.
         Therefore, evidentiary value of such evidence may also be
         taken    into     account     while     considering           the       regular            bail
         application which is preferred after submission of charge-
         sheet.3.1           Mr.Thakkar, learned Senior Counsel pointed out
         from the material available on record that as per the version
         given by one of the witness namely, Kayum, the alleged
         incident took place between 10.30 to 11.00 O' Clock in the
         night. whereas the statement of Jaiwant Ramchandran, ASP
         indicates about CCTV footages collected during the course of
         investigation which suggestive of the fact that the applicant
         and two other friends met with an accident by falling down
         from the Activa Scooter and sustained certain injuries around
         11.00 O' Clock on the same day in some other area which is
         about more than 7 k.m. from the alleged place of incident.
         Therefore, according to Mr.Thakkar, the alleged story is not
         probable one. It is also pointed out that though there was an
         ample opportunity, no test identification parade has been
         done by the investigating agency. Learned Senior Counsel
         Mr.Thakkar has also referred to and relied upon certain
         applications made by the mother of the applicant before the
         Magistrate wherein she has complained about certain ill-
         treatment meted out to the applicant-son so as to pressurize
         him to confess the alleged offence. The order passed by the
         learned Magistrate below production report dated 15.12.2015
         is also referred to and relied upon in support of hisPage 2 of 6HC-NIC                                   Page 2 of 6      Created On Fri Jun 24 02:28:26 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/11535/2016                                             ORDER



         submission.3.2         Mr.Thakkar, leraned Senior Counsel while his
         argument, submits that there is no eye witness to the incident,
         the entire case is based on circumstantial evidence and prima
         facie, chain of circumstances does not establish. Moreover,
         the applicant is a student of engineering faculty and resident
         of Surat and his presence can be secured at the time of trial
         by imposing appropriate conditions as may be deem fit and
         proper by this Court.3.3         It is also submitted that the applicant was released
         on temporary bail for the purpose of allowing him to appear in
         the examination. During the temporary bail period, no
         complaint has been received by the concerned Investigating
         Officer that the applicant has tried to misuse liberty granted
         to him and thereby made any attempt to hamper the
         investigation or tampered with the evidence. It is lastly
         submitted that the applicant is ready and willing to abide by
         all the conditions which may be imposed by this Court and,
         therefore, he may be enlarged on regular bail.4.          Learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr.J.K.Shah,
         appearing on behalf of the respondent-State has vehemently
         opposed grant of regular bail and submitted that from the
         charge-sheet papers, there is a strong prima facie case
         against the present applicant for committing the alleged
         offence. It is submitted that though the case is based on
         circumstantial evidence but the chain of circumstances are
         suggestive of the fact that there is involvement of the
         applicant in the commission of the alleged offence and,Page 3 of 6HC-NIC                               Page 3 of 6      Created On Fri Jun 24 02:28:26 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/11535/2016                                                  ORDER



         therefore, looking to the nature and gravity of the offence,
         this application may be dismissed.5.             Ms.Bhavna Acharya, learned advocate appearing
         for the original complainant has supported the argument
         advanced by the learned APP and has submitted that it is a
         pre-plan murder and, therefore, looking to the role attributed
         to the present applicant from the charge-sheet papers, he may
         not be enlarged on regular bail.6.             Regard being had to the above submission, it
         appears that the case is based on circumstantial evidence and
         considering the nature of accusation made against the
         applicant in the First Information Report and other charge-
         sheet    papers       and     also     considering           the       fact      that         the
         investigation is over and charge-sheet is filed, now there is no
         possibility to tampering the evidence, this Court is of the view
         that the applicant, who is student studying in engineering
         faculty and resident of Surat, his presence can be secured at
         the     time   of     trial   by     imposing         appropriate             conditions.
         Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that haivng regard to
         the facts and circumstances of the present case, discretion is
         required to be exercised to enlarge the applicant on regular
         bail.7.             Hence, the present application is allowed and the
         applicant is ordered to be released on regular bail in
         connection with an offence being C.R.No.I-234 of 2015
         registered with Khatodara Police Station, District-Surat,
         on his executing a personal bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees
         Ten Thousand Only) with one surety of the like amount toPage 4 of 6HC-NIC                                      Page 4 of 6      Created On Fri Jun 24 02:28:26 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/11535/2016                                             ORDER



         the satisfaction of the learned trial court, and subject to the
         following conditions, that the applicant shall;[a] not take undue advantage of liberty or misuse
                       liberty;[b] not act in a manner injurious to the interest of
                       the prosecution;[c] surrender passport, if any, to the lower court
                       within a week;[d] not leave the State of Gujarat without prior
                       permission of the Sessions Judge concerned;[e] not enter into District Surat for a period of one
                       month except for the purpose of attending the
                       trial Court and marking presence before the
                       concerned Police Station on every Monday of each
                       English calendar month. He shall also mark
                       presence before the concerned Police Station on
                       every Monday of each English calendar month for
                       a period of six months, between 11:00 a.m. and
                       2:00 p.m.;[f] furnish   latest and permanent                      address          of
                       residence and contact details to the Investigating
                       Officer, and also to the Court at the time of
                       execution of the bond, and shall not change the
                       residence without prior permission of this Court;Page 5 of 6HC-NIC                               Page 5 of 6      Created On Fri Jun 24 02:28:26 IST 2016
                        R/CR.MA/11535/2016                                                     ORDER8.                 The Authorities will release the applicant only if he
         is not required in connection with any other offence for the
         time being. If breach of any of the above conditions is
         committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue
         warrant or take appropriate action in the matter. Bail bond to
         be      executed          before        the      learned         Lower          Court         having
         jurisdiction to try the case. It will be open for the concerned
         Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above
         conditions, in accordance with law. At the trial, learned trial
         court        shall      not        be   influenced          by     the      observations              of
         preliminary nature, qua the evidence at this stage made by
         this Court while enlarging the applicant on bail.9.                 Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

         SPECIAL CRIMINAL APPLICATION (DIRECTION - POLICE PROTECTION)
                                       NO. 4938 of 2016

         ==========================================================
                 VANDANABEN W/O PIYUSHBHAI DAKSHINI....Applicant(s)
                                    Versus
                      STATE OF GUJARAT & 2....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR V B MALIK, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         MR RONAK RAVAL, ADDL. PP for Respondents.
         ==========================================================

         CORAM        HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
             :

                                       Date : 13/07/2016


                                        ORAL ORDER1. By   way   of   present   petition   preferred   underArticle   226of   the   Constitution   of   India,   the 

               petitioners   have   prayed   for   the   following 

               substantial reliefs :"13(B)            To   issue   a   writ   of   mandamus   or 
                     direction to the respondents No.1,2 and 3 to 
                     protect   the   present   petitioner   and   her  
                     husband Piyush's family from her father and 
                     his family members relatives in the interest 
                     of justice."Page 1 of 6HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 6      Created On Fri Jul 15 02:46:17 IST 2016
              R/SCR.A/4938/2016                                             ORDER2.The   petitioner   herein   and   one   Shri   Piyushbhai 

           Daxini   are   the   legally   wedded   couple,   whose 

           marriage has been solemnised and registered with 

           the office of the Registrar of Marriages on April 

           01,   2016.   The   petitioner   has   sought   for   police 

           protection. It is the case of the petitioner that 

           their   marriage   was   an   inter­caste.   A   marriage 

           certificate   is   also   brought   on   record   of   the 

           matter.3.It   is   the   say   of   the  learned   counsel   appearing 

           for the petitioner  Shri V.B. Malik that despite 

           the best of the efforts made by the petitioner to 

           convince   her   parents,   they   have   chosen   to 

           pressurise the petitioner to marry elsewhere with 

           a   boy   of   their   choice   and,   therefore,   the 

           petitioner is apprehensive of her life and life 

           of her husband as well as her in­laws and afraid 

           of   even   honour   killing.In   support   of   her 

           submissions,   the  learned   counsel   appearing   for 

           the   petitioner  has   relied   upon   the   decision   of 

           the   Apex   Court   in   the   case   ofLata   Singh   v.  

           State of Uttar Pradesh, reported in AIR 2006 SCPage 2 of 6HC-NIC                           Page 2 of 6      Created On Fri Jul 15 02:46:17 IST 2016
              R/SCR.A/4938/2016                                                ORDER



           2522.4.Heard Shri V.B. Malik,  learned counsel appearing 

           for the petitioner  and Shri Ronak Raval,  learned 

           Additional   Public   Prosecutor   for   the   respondent 

           No.1­State.5.Having   considered   the   contents   of   the   petition 

           and   the   material   on   record,   as   also   the 

           submissions made by both the sides as well as the 

           decision of the Apex Court in the case ofLata  

           Singh(supra), this Court is of the opinion that 

           the   petitioner   deserves   to   be   granted   police 

           protection. At this stage, it would be profitable 

           to   regurgitate   the   relevant   observations   and 

           findings   ofthe   said   decision,   which   read   as 

           under :"17.            The caste system is a curse on the  
                 nation   and   the   sooner   it   is   destroyed   the 
                 better. In  fact, it  is dividing  the nation 
                 at a time when we have to be united to face  
                 the   challenges   before   the   nation   unitedly. 
                 Hence, inter­caste marriages are in fact in 
                 the national interest as they will result in  
                 destroying   the   caste   system.   However,Page 3 of 6HC-NIC                              Page 3 of 6      Created On Fri Jul 15 02:46:17 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/4938/2016                                             ORDER



             disturbing   news   are   coming   from   several 
             parts   of   the   country   that   young   men   and 
             women who undergo inter­caste marriage, are 
             threatened   with   violence,   or   violence   is 
             actually committed on them. In our opinion, 
             such   acts   of   violence   or   threats   or 
             harassment are wholly illegal and those who 
             commit them must be severely punished. This 
             is a free and democratic country, and once a  
             person becomes a major he or she can marry 
             whosoever he/she likes.If the parents of the  
             boy   or   girl   do   not   approve   of   such   inter­
             caste   or   inter­religious   marriage   the 
             maximum they can do is that they can cut off 
             social   relations   with   the   son   or   the 
             daughter,   but   they   cannot   give   threats   or 
             commit   or   instigate   acts   of   violence   and 
             cannot harass the person who undergoes such 
             inter­caste or inter­religious marriage. We, 
             therefore,   direct   that   the   administration/ 
             police   authorities   throughout   the   country 
             will see to it that if any boy or girl who 
             is   a   major   undergoes   inter­caste   or   inter­
             religious marriage with a  woman or  man who 
             is a major, the couple are not harassed by 
             any one nor subjected to threats or acts of 
             violence, and any one who gives such threats  
             or   harasses   or   commits   acts   of   violence 
             either   himself   or   at   his   instigation,   is 
             taken   to   task   by   instituting   criminal  
             proceedings   by   the   police   against   suchPage 4 of 6HC-NIC                       Page 4 of 6      Created On Fri Jul 15 02:46:17 IST 2016
             R/SCR.A/4938/2016                                             ORDER



                persons   and   further   stern   action   is   taken 
                against such persons as provided by law.18.   We   sometimes   hear   of   'honour'   killings  
                of   such   persons   who   undergo   inter­caste   or  
                inter­religious   marriage   of   their   own   free 
                will.   There   is   nothing   honourable   in   such 
                killings, and  in fact they are nothing but 
                barbaric   and   shameful   acts   of   murder 
                committed   by   brutal,   feudal   minded   persons 
                who   deserve   harsh   punishment.   Only   in   this  
                way can we stamp out such acts of barbarism.19.In   the   circumstances,   the   writ   petition 
                is   allowed.   The   proceedings   in   Sessions 
                Trial No. 1201/2001 titledState of U.P. v. 
                Sangita   Gupta   and   Ors.arising   out   of   FIR 
                No.   336/2000   registered   at   Police   Station 
                Sarojini   Nagar,   Lucknow   and   pending   in   the  
                Fast Track Court V, Lucknow are quashed. The 
                warrants   against   the   accused   are   also  
                quashed.   The   police   at   all   the   concerned 
                places   should   ensure   that   neither   the  
                petitioner nor her husband nor any relatives  
                of the petitioner's husband are harassed or 
                threatened   nor   any   acts   of   violence   are 
                committed against them. If anybody is found 
                doing   so,   he   should   be   proceeded   against 
                sternly   in   accordance   with   law,   by   the 
                authorities concerned."6.In view of aforesaid facts and circumstances ofPage 5 of 6HC-NIC                          Page 5 of 6      Created On Fri Jul 15 02:46:17 IST 2016
                    R/SCR.A/4938/2016                                              ORDER



                 the   case   as   well   as   the   decision   of   the   Apex 

                 Court   in   the   case   ofLata   Singh(supra),   the 

                 present   petition   is   hereby   allowed.   Let   the 

                 respondent   No.2­Police   Inspector,   Radhanpur 

                 Police   Station,   District   Patan,   look   into   the 

                 matter and provide requisite police protection to 

                 the   petitioner   herein   without   further   loss   of 

                 time and shall ensure her safety. The duration of 

                 protection   shall   be   decided   by   the   respondent 

                 No.2 looking to the ground realities.With above observations and directions, 

                 the present petition stands disposed of.Direct service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

               CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                                 FIR/ORDER) NO. 17328 of 2016
         ==========================================================
                    SANJAYBHAI SHIVABHAI VASAVA....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                      STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR MM SAIYED, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         MR RONAK RAVAL, PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         MR MT SAIYED, ADVOCATE for the Respondent(s) No. 2
         ==========================================================
         CORAM:             HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
                                  Date : 30/08/2016
                                          ORAL ORDER1.           The petitioner is seeking quashment of
         the      complaint             being           I-C.R.             No.          134/2015
         registered with Ankleshwar Rural Police Station
         for the offence punishable underSections 363and366of the Indian Penal Code andSection 8of the
         Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
         2012.2.           Heard.           This      Court           notices             that          the
         complainant is the mother of the prosecutrix. The
         parties       have           settled       their          disputes               as       the
         prosecutrix has already married the petitioner,
         herein. Their marriage registration certificate
         is    also      brought          on      record,             which           is       dated
         31.03.2016.           The petitioner is about 23 years old
         and the prosecutrix is about 21 years old.Page 1 of 4HC-NIC                                    Page 1 of 4        Created On Fri Sep 02 01:36:41 IST 2016
               R/CR.MA/17328/2016                                             ORDER3.In above view of the matter, here, it
         would be profitable to refer to the observations
         made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case ofGIAN SINGH VS. STATE OF PUNJAB AND ANR., (2012) 10
         SCC 303, wherein, at Paragraph-61, the Apex Court
         observed as under;""61. The position that emerges from
                          the    above     discussion    can    be
                          summarised thus: the power of the
                          High Court in quashing a criminal
                          proceeding or FIR or complaint in
                          exercise of its inherent jurisdiction
                          is distinct and different from the
                          power given to a criminal court for
                          compounding     the    offences    under
                          Section 320 of the Code. Inherent
                          power is of wide plenitude with no
                          statutory limitation but it has to be
                          exercised    in     accord   with    the
                          guideline engrafted in such power
                          viz.,(i)to secure the ends of justice
                          or (ii) to prevent abuse of the
                          process of any Court. In what cases
                          power    to    quash     the    criminal
                          proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may
                          be exercised where the offender and
                          victim have settled their dispute
                          would   depend    on   the   facts   and
                          circumstances of each case and no
                          category can be prescribed. However,
                          before exercise of such power, the
                          High Court must have due regard to
                          the nature and gravity of the crime.
                          Heinous   and    serious   offences   of
                          mental depravity or offences like
                          murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be
                          fittingly quashed even though the
                          victim or victim's family and thePage 2 of 4HC-NIC                             Page 2 of 4      Created On Fri Sep 02 01:36:41 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/17328/2016                                             ORDER



                     offender have settled the dispute.
                     Such offences are not private in
                     nature and have serious impact on
                     society. Similarly, any compromise
                     between the victim and offender in
                     relation   to    the    offences    under
                     special statutes likePrevention of
                     Corruption    Actor   the    offences
                     committed by public servants while
                     working in that capacity etc; cannot
                     provide for any basis for quashing
                     criminal proceedings involving such
                     offences. But the criminal cases
                     having    overwhelmingly      and    pre-
                     dominatingly civil flavour stand on
                     different footing for the purposes of
                     quashing, particularly the offences
                     arising from commercial, financial,
                     mercantile, civil, partnership or
                     such   like    transactions      or   the
                     offences arising out of matrimony
                     relating to dowry, etc. or the family
                     disputes where the wrong is basically
                     private or personal in nature and the
                     parties have resolved their entire

                    IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

                  BHAVNABEN CHAMANBHARATI GOSWAMI....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus

         Appearance:

         PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                           Date : 13/06/2016


                                            ORAL ORDER1.     Petitioner is a Chief Officer of Jasdan Nagarpalika,

         District:Rajkot. He seeks quashment of First Information Report

         being    CR.No.II-3131 of 2016 registered with Jasdan police

         station, Rajkot for the offences punishable undersections 3(1)

         (2)(6)of    the     Scheduled          Castes        and       Scheduled            Tribes

         (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.2.     Learned advocate for the petitioner has urged that the

         parties have settled the dispute and the complainant is

         present.      According      to     the      complainant,            due       to    certain

         misunderstanding she had lodged this complaint. Things have

         been worked out amicably and no grievance survives.Page 1 of 4HC-NIC                                       Page 1 of 4      Created On Sun Jun 19 00:35:14 IST 2016
                  R/SCR.A/3779/2016                                             ORDER3.   On enquiring from the complainant, who is represented

         by   learned     advocate    Mr.Vimal          Purohit       and       also       being

         specifically enquired by learned Additional Public Prosecutor

         for respondent No.1 and confirmed once again by the Court, no

         cause, according to the petitioner, has been survived, as

         parties have amicably settled the dispute and in wake of the

         decision of the       Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh vs.

         State of Punjab and anotherreported in (2012) 10 SCC

         303 with all consequential proceedings.4.   Having considered the submissions made on behalf of

         both the sides and the fact that it is a private dispute and the

         parties have arrived at an amicable settlement, especially

         when the respondent No.2 has chosen to put an end to the

         matter, no cause survives and, therefore, it would be desirable

         to quash the first information report in view of the decision of

         the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra), whereby it

         is held that it is the duty of the Courts to encourage genuine

         settlements andsection 482of the Code of Criminal Procedure,

         1973, enables the High Court to pass such orders.It would be

         beneficial to reproduce the relevant observations and findings

         of the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra), which

         read as under :Page 2 of 4HC-NIC                                 Page 2 of 4      Created On Sun Jun 19 00:35:14 IST 2016
            R/SCR.A/3779/2016                                            ORDER



         "53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on the
         ground of settlement between an offender and victim is
         not the same thing as compounding of offence. They are
         different and not interchangeable. Strictly speaking, the
         power of compounding of offences given to a court under
         Section 320 is materially different from the quashing of
         criminal proceedings by the High Court in exercise of its
         inherent jurisdiction. In compounding of offences, power of
         a criminal court is circumscribed by the provisions
         contained in Section 320 and the court is guided solely and
         squarely thereby while, on the other hand, the formation of
         opinion by the High Court for quashing a criminal offence
         or criminal proceeding or criminal complaint is guided by
         the material on record as to whether the ends of justice
         would justify such exercise of power although the ultimate
         consequence may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.54. Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding
         having regard to the fact that dispute between the
         offender and victim has been settled although offences are
         not compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, continuation
         of criminal proceedings will be an exercise in futility and
         justice in the case demands that the dispute between the
         parties is put to an end and peace is restored; securing the
         ends of justice being the ultimate guiding factor. No doubt,
         crimes are acts which have harmful effect on the public
         and consist in wrong doing that seriously endangers and
         threatens well-being of society and it is not safe to leave
         the crimedoer only because he and the victim have settled
         the dispute amicably or that the victim has been paid
         compensation, yet certain crimes have been made
         compoundable in law, with or without permission of the
         Court. In respect of serious offences like murder, rape,
         dacoity, etc; or other offences of mental depravity underIPCor offences of moral turpitude under special statutes,
         likePrevention of Corruption Actor the offences committed
         by public servants while working in that capacity, the
         settlement between offender and victim can have no legal
         sanction at all. However, certain offences which
         overwhelmingly and predominantly bear civil flavour
         having arisen out of civil, mercantile, commercial,
         financial, partnership or such like transactions or the
         offences arising out of matrimony, particularly relating to
         dowry, etc. or the family dispute, where the wrong is
         basically to victim and the offender and victim have settled
         all disputes between them amicably, irrespective of the
         fact that such offences have not been made
         compoundable, the High Court may within the framework
         of its inherent power, quash the criminal proceeding orPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                          Page 3 of 4      Created On Sun Jun 19 00:35:14 IST 2016
                     R/SCR.A/3779/2016                                             ORDER



                  criminal complaint or F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the face
                  of such settlement,there is hardly any likelihood of
                  offender being convicted and by not quashing the criminal
                  proceedings, justice shall be casualty and ends of justice
                  shall be defeated. The above list is illustrative and not
                  exhaustive. Each case will depend on its own facts and no
                  hard and fast category can be prescribed.5.       For the foregoing reasons and in view of the decisions of

         the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra), the present

         application succeeds and the same is, accordingly, allowed in

         view of an amicable settlement arrived at by and between the

         parties. The first information report being CR.No.II-3131 of

         2016 registered with Jasdan police station, Rajkot and all the

         proceedings emanating therefrom, are quashed and set aside.

         Rule is made absolute accordingly.Direct Service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                        Date : 21/03/2016


                                   ORAL ORDERThe present petition is preferred underArticle 226of the
         Constitution of India seeking following reliefs :A)Your Lordship may be pleased to admit and

                      allow this application;B) Your Lordship may be pleased to quash and

                      set aside the FIR being C.R. No. I-51/2001 registered

                      with Jamkhambhalia Police station, District Jamnagar

                      and Criminal Case No. 777 of 2001 pending in the

                      Court of learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class,

                      Khambhalia,District Jamnagar, qua the applicants.C) Pending admission and/or final disposal of this

                      petition, your honour       may be pleased to stay further

                      proceedings of Criminal Case No. 777 of 2001 pending

                      in the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class,

                      Khambhalia, District Jamnagar.Page 1 of 6HC-NIC                                    Page 1 of 6         Created On Thu Mar 24 01:52:34 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/3852/2016                                                ORDER2.   Ashishkumar Ashwinkumar Kayasth one of the
         officer of Essar Oil Ltd on 3rd March 2001 filed a
         complaint and the same culminated into filing of the
         charge sheet dated 20th October 2001 which is
         presently pending as Criminal Case No. 777 of 2001
         before      the              Judicial      Magistrate,               First         Class,
         Khambhalia, District Jamnagar. During the pendency
         of the petition, both the parties have chosen to
         compromise.            The Compromise memo                            is placed on
         the record of the case. The compromise memo                                             has
         been signed by the parties wherein it has been
         confirmed that the petitioner do not have any claim
         over the said shares. All the disputes of the parties
         end with this.3.   The complainant has filed an affidavit interalia
         stating that the settlement deed/compromise was
         executed on 13th October 2010, and                                the settlement
         deed           arrived on 2nd February 2016. However,
         earlier the application for compounding the offence
         had been filed before the Judicial Magistrate(First
         Class) at Khambhalia which was rejected as the
         offences were not compoundable.4.   Learned Addl. Public Prosecutor                                        has also
         verified from the complainant that the settlement hasPage 2 of 6HC-NIC                                     Page 2 of 6      Created On Thu Mar 24 01:52:34 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/3852/2016                                                ORDER



         been arrived without any coercion and out of his own
         volition.5.   The ratio laid down in                    case ofGian Singh Vs.
         State   of     Punjab        and       Anotherreported in 2012
         (10)SCC 303 deserves reproduction at this stage which
         is as under:"57.    Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on
                      the ground of settlement between an offender and
                      victim is not the same thing as compounding of
                      offence. They are different and not interchangeable.
                      Strictly speaking, the power of compounding of
                      offences given to a court under Section 320 is
                      materially different from the quashing of criminal
                      proceedings by the High Court in exercise of its
                      inherent jurisdiction. In compounding of offences,
                      power of a criminal court is circumscribed by the
                      provisions contained in Section 320 and the court is
                      guided solely and squarely thereby while, on the other
                      hand, the formation of opinion by the High Court for
                      quashing a criminal offence or criminal proceeding or
                      criminal complaint is guided by the material on record
                      as to whether the ends of justice would justify such
                      exercise of power although the ultimate consequence
                      may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.58.. Where High Court quashes a criminal proceeding
                      having regard to the fact that dispute between the
                      offender and victim has been settled although offences
                      are not compoundable, it does so as in its
                      opinion,continuation of criminal proceedings will be an
                      exercise in futility and justice in the case demands that
                      the dispute between the parties is put to an end and
                      peace is restored; securing the ends of justice being
                      the ultimate guiding factor. No doubt, crimes are acts
                      which have harmful effect on the public and consist in
                      wrong doing that seriously endangers and threatens
                      well-being of society and it is not safe to leave the
                      crime-doer only because he and the victim have settled
                      the dispute amicably or that the victim has been paid
                      compensation, yet certain crimes have been made
                      compoundable in law, with or without permission of
                      the Court. In respect of serious offences like murder,
                      rape, dacoity, etc; or other offences of mental
                      depravity underIPCor offences of moral turpitude
                      under special statutes, likePrevention of Corruption
                      Actor the offences committed by public servants while
                      working in that capacity, the settlement between
                      offender and victim can have no legal sanction at all.
                      However,certain offences which overwhelmingly and
                      predominantly bear civil flavour having arisen out of
                      civil, mercantile, commercial, financial, partnership or
                      such like transactions or the offences arising out ofPage 3 of 6HC-NIC                                    Page 3 of 6      Created On Thu Mar 24 01:52:34 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/3852/2016                                               ORDER


             matrimony, particularly relating to dowry, etc. or the
             family dispute, where the wrong is basically to victim
             and the offender and victim have settled all disputes
             between them amicably, irrespective of the fact that
             such offences have not been made compoundable, the
             High Court may within the framework of its inherent
             power, quash the criminal proceeding or criminal
             complaint or F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the face of
             such settlement, there is hardly any likelihood of
             offender being convicted and by not quashing the
             criminal proceedings, justice shall be casualty and
             ends of justice shall be defeated. The above list is
             illustrative and not exhaustive. Each case will depend
             on its own facts and no hard and fast category can be
             prescribed.61. The position that emerges from the above
             discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the
             High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR
             or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is
             distinct and different from the power given to a
             criminal court for compounding the offences under
             Section 320 of the Code. Inherent power is of wide
             plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be
             exercised in accord with the guideline engrafted in
             such power viz; (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii)
             to prevent abuse of the process of any Court. In what
             cases power to quash the criminal proceeding or
             complaint or F.I.R may be exercised where the
             offender and victim have settled their dispute would
             depend on the facts and circumstances of each case
             and no category can be prescribed. However, before
             exercise of such power, the High Court must have due
             regard to the nature and gravity of the crime. Heinous
             and serious offences of mental depravity or offences
             like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly
             quashed even though the victim or victims family and
             the offender have settled the dispute. Such offences
             are not private in nature and have serious impact on
             society. Similarly, any compromise between the victim
             and offender in relation to the offences under special
             statutes likePrevention of Corruption Actor the
             offences committed by public servants while working
             in that capacity etc; cannot provide for any basis for
             quashing criminal proceedings involving such offences.
             But the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and
             predominatingly civil flavour stand on different footing
             for the purposes of quashing, particularly the offences
             arising from commercial, financial, mercantile, civil,
             partnership or such like transactions or the offences
             arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or the
             family disputes where the wrong is basically private or
             personal in nature and the parties have resolved their
             entire dispute. In this category of cases, High Court
             may quash criminal proceedings if in its view, because
             of the compromise between the offender and victim,
             the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and
             continuation of criminal case would put accused to
             great oppression and prejudice and extreme injusticePage 4 of 6HC-NIC                           Page 4 of 6      Created On Thu Mar 24 01:52:34 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/3852/2016                                               ORDER


                      would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal
                      case despite full and complete settlement and
                      compromise with the victim. In other words, the High
                      Court must consider whether it would be unfair or
                      contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the
                      criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal
                      proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of
                      law despite settlement and compromise between the
                      victim and wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends
                      of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to
                      an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in
                      affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its
                      jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."5.    Request         for    settlement           of    the       parties              and
         quashment of the complaint where nature of dispute is
         personal and          some of the offences are otherwise non-
         compoundable is permitted in exercise of powers of
         inherent jurisdiction assailed by the Apex Court.6.    Such   dispute,   even   if   not   compoundable,   can   be 

         compounded   undersection   482of   the   Code   of   Criminal 

         Procedure,   1973.   When   the   dispute   is   predominantly   of   a 

         private   character   and   the   complainant   having     decided 

         against supporting the prosecution case, no useful purpose 

         would     be   served   in   allowing   the   trial,   which   may   cause 

         wastage of public time, money and energy.7.    Resultantly this application is allowed. Criminal Case 

         being     Criminal  Case  No.  777  of  2001  pending   before  the 

         Court   of   learned   Judicial   Magistrate,   First   Class, 

         Khambhalia, District Jamnagar and the FIR being C.R. No. 

         I­51/2001  and the consequential proceedings  are quashedPage 5 of 6HC-NIC                                    Page 5 of 6      Created On Thu Mar 24 01:52:34 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/3852/2016                                           ORDER



         and set aside.8.     This Application stands disposed of.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

         has been called with the papers of the investigation. He also confirms 
         that the injury to the complainant was very minor and discharge from 
         the hospital was given to the complainant the very next date. Learned 
         advocate   Mr.   Chaudhary   has   submitted   that   had   there   been   any 
         criminal   antecedent   in   serious   nature   of   the   injuries,   it   would   have 
         different   aspect,   but   here   none   of   these   ingredients   exists.   The 
         investigation is still going on and this may result into lodging of the 
         complaint for very minor offence  and, therefore, he has urged that this 
         application   be   allowed   by   quashing   the   complaint.   The   complainant 
         who   is   present   confirms   the   contents   of   the   affidavit   and   has   no 
         objection to the application being allowed. Learned APP Mr. Raval had 
         ascertained   from   the   Investigating   Officer   also   the   status   that   the 
         applicants are neither high handed person nor they have any criminal 
         antecedent,4.     The dispute being personal in nature and keeping in mind that 
         no serious injury has resulted and the parties have chosen to end their 
         dispute amicably due to intervention of the family and the community, 
         in the opinion of this Court, no purpose is likely to be served as the 
         same is not to result into conviction.In view of the decision of the Apex 
         Court in the case ofGian Singh  v. State of Punjab and another, 
         reported in AIR 2012 SC (Supp.) 838, whereby it is held that it is the 
         duty of the Courts to encourage genuine settlements andsection 482of 
         the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, enables the High Court to pass 
         such   orders.It   would   be   beneficial   to   reproduce   the   relevant 
         observations and findings of the Apex Court in the case ofGian Singh(supra), which read as under:53.   Quashing   of   offence   or   criminal   proceedings   on   the  
                        ground of settlement between an offender and victim is notPage 2 of 4HC-NIC                                       Page 2 of 4      Created On Fri Jun 24 03:13:18 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/13797/2016                                                  ORDER



              the   same   thing   as   compounding   of   offence.   They   are  
              different   and   not   interchangeable.   Strictly   speaking,   the  
              power of compounding  of offences  given to a court  underSection   320is   materially   different   from   the   quashing   of  
              criminal  proceedings  by  the  High  Court  in  exercise  of  its  
              inherent jurisdiction. In compounding of offences, power of  
              a   criminal   court   is   circumscribed   by   the   provisions  
              contained inSection 320and the court is guided solely and  
              squarely thereby while, on the other hand, the formation of  
              opinion by the High Court for quashing a criminal offence  
              or criminal  proceeding  or criminal  complaint  is guided  by  
              the  material   on   record   as  to   whether   the   ends   of  justice  
              would justify such exercise of power although the ultimate  
              consequence may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.54.  Where   High   Court   quashes   a   criminal   proceeding  
              having regard to the fact that dispute between the offender  
              and   victim   has   been   settled   although   offences   are   not  
              compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, continuation of  
              criminal   proceedings   will   be   an   exercise   in   futility   and  
              justice in the case demands that the dispute between the  
              parties is put to an end and peace is restored; securing the  
              ends of justice being the ultimate guiding factor. No doubt,  
              crimes   are   acts   which   have   harmful   effect   on   the   public  
              and consist in wrong doing that seriously endangers and  
              threatens wellbeing of society and it is not safe to leave the  
              crime doer only because he and the victim have settled the  
              dispute   amicably   or   that   the   victim   has   been   paid  
              compensation,   yet   certain   crimes   have   been   made  
              compoundable   in   law,   with   or   without   permission   of   the  
              Court.   In   respect   of   serious   offences   like   murder,   rape,  
              dacoity,   etc;   or   other   offences   of   mental   depravity   underIPCor offences of moral turpitude  under special statutes,  
              likePrevention of Corruption Actor the offences committed  
              by   public   servants   while   working   in   that   capacity,   the  
              settlement between offender and victim can have no legal  
              sanction   at   all.   However,   certain   offences   which  
              overwhelmingly   and   predominantly   bear   civil   flavour  
              having arisen out of civil, mercantile, commercial, financial,  
              partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising  
              out of matrimony, particularly relating to dowry, etc. or thePage 3 of 4HC-NIC                             Page 3 of 4      Created On Fri Jun 24 03:13:18 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/13797/2016                                                   ORDER



                       family dispute, where the wrong is basically to victim and  
                       the offender and victim have settled all disputes between  
                       them amicably, irrespective of the fact  that such offences  
                       have  not  been  made  compoundable,  the  High  Court  may  
                       within   the   framework   of   its   inherent   power,   quash   the  
                       criminal   proceeding   or   criminal   complaint   or   F.I.R   if   it   is  
                       satisfied that on the face of such settlement,there is hardly  
                       any  likelihood   of   offender   being   convicted   and   by   not  
                       quashing   the   criminal   proceedings,   justice   shall   be  
                       casualty and ends of justice shall be defeated. The above  
                       list   is   illustrative   and   not   exhaustive.   Each   case   will  
                       depend on its own facts and no hard and fast category can  
                       be prescribed."5.     For the foregoing reasons and in view of the decision of the Apex 

         Court   in   the   case   ofGian   Singh(supra),  the   present   application 

         succeeds and the same is, accordingly, allowed in view of an amicable 

         settlement arrived at by and between the parties. The first information 

         report   being  I­C.R.   No.71   of   2016   registered   with   Chanasma   Police 

         Station and all the proceedings emanating therefrom, are quashed and 

         set aside. Rule is made absolute accordingly.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)
