                                          Date : 22/03/2016


                                           ORAL ORDER(PER : HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE M.R. SHAH)1.             Present application for Leave to Appeal has been

         preferred by the applicant-State to grant permission to prefer appeal

         against the impugned judgment and order of acquittal passed by

         learned (Ad-hoc) Additional Sessions Judge, Junagadh                            by which

         learned trial Court has acquitted the original accused for the offence

         undersection 304of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).2.             To satisfy ourselves, prima facie, whether there is any

         substance in the appeal, we have heard Ms.Moxa Thakkar, learned

         APP appearing for the State, at length. She has placed before the

         Court entire evidence of the case for perusal of the Court. We havePage 1 of 3HC-NIC                                     Page 1 of 3      Created On Tue Mar 29 00:03:17 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/4528/2016                                            ORDER



         re-appreciated the entire evidence on record.

         2.1          Original accused was charged for the offence undersection 304of the IPC. It was the case on behalf of the prosecution

         that, on 01.12.2011 there was a marriage ceremony/reception at Leo

         Resort, Junagadh. The contract for electrical decoration was given to

         the accused. That at 10.30 p.m., nephew of original complainant,

         aged 2 years, while playing in the party plot, fell down on the electric

         live wire   due to which he died. It was the case on behalf of the

         prosecution that the contract for electrical decoration was given to

         the accused and because of his sheer negligence                   by keeping live

         electric wire open, the deceased died. That on appreciation of the

         evidence, learned trial Court has acquitted the original accused.3.           On re-appreciation of the evidence on record, we are of

         the opinion that the prosecution has failed to make out any case for

         the offence undersection 304of the IPC. To convict a person for the

         offence undersection 304of the IPC, prosecution has to prove that

         the person has committed culpable homicide not amounting to

         murder. Culpable homicide is defined undersection 299of the IPC.

         As persection 299of the IPC, whoever causes death by doing an act

         with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing

         such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge

         that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of

         culpable homicide. In absence of any such evidence that the act of

         the accused was with the intention of causing death of the deceased,Page 2 of 3HC-NIC                                Page 2 of 3      Created On Tue Mar 29 00:03:17 IST 2016
                        R/CR.MA/4528/2016                                           ORDER



         learned trial Court has rightly acquitted the original accused for the

         offence undersection 304of the IPC.4.                Under the circumstances, appeal lacks merits. When the

         appeal lacks merits, application for leave to appeal deserves to be

         dismissed and accordingly dismissed.                    Consequently, the main

         criminal appeal also stands dismissed.(M.R.SHAH, J.)

                                            ORAL ORDER1      By this writ application underArticle 226of the Constitution of 
         India, the writ applicant ­ mother of the deceased has prayed for the 
         following reliefs:"14(a) This  petition  be  admitted  and  record  and  proceeding  of  I Crime

                Police Station be referred to C.B.I. for further and impartial investigation.(c)       Any other as may be deemed just and proper be passed."2      It appears from the materials on record that dead body of the son 
         of the writ applicant herein, namely,  Yogeshsinh Nandusinh Rathod  was 
         recovered   with   multiple   injuries.   A   First   Information   Report   in   this 
         regard came to be lodged at the Prantij Police Station. The same was 
         registered as the C.R. No.I­60 of 2014 for the offence punishable underPage 1 of 3HC-NIC                                       Page 1 of 3      Created On Sat Dec 17 00:21:30 IST 2016
                     R/SCR.A/242/2015                                                  ORDERSections 279,304(A)of the Indian Penal Code andSections 177and184of  the  Motor   Vehicle   Act.  It   also  appears  that   the  writ   applicant 
         herein filed a complaint in the Court of the learned Judicial Magistrate 
         First Class, Prantij for the offence of murder. It is the case of the writ 
         applicant, being the mother of the deceased, that her son was done to 
         death and the case is not one of accident.3      The   learned   Magistrate   passed   an   order   of   police   investigation 
         underSection 156(3)of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. It was 
         expected of the police officers of the concerned police station to abide by 
         the   order   passed   by   the   learned   J.M.F.C.   However,   it   appears   that   a 
         report came to be filed in the Court of the learned J.M.F.C., Prantij that 
         they are already investigating into the F.I.R., which was registered prior 
         in point of time and therefore, there was no question of undertaking any 
         fresh investigation underSection 156(3)of the Cr.P.C. Such report filed 
         by the Investigating Officer came to be rejected by the learned J.M.F.C., 
         Prantij condemning the approach and the understanding of the police. 
         The learned J.M.F.C., Prantij, vide order dated 6th April 2016 directed to 
         undertake the investigation under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C.4      The   police   officer,   who   is   present   in   the   Court,   states   that   the 
         investigation is in progress. Till this date, no further report has been filed 
         in the Court of the learned J.M.F.C., Prantij.5      The   writ   applicant,   being   the   mother   of   the   deceased,   has   lost 
         confidence in the Investigating Officer. In my view, there are reasons for 
         her to say so.6      In   such   circumstances,   the   Deputy   Superintendent   of   Police, 
         Sabarkantha is directed to take over the investigation of the matter from 
         the present Investigating Officer. The Deputy Superintendent of PolicePage 2 of 3HC-NIC                                        Page 2 of 3      Created On Sat Dec 17 00:21:30 IST 2016
                       R/SCR.A/242/2015                                             ORDER



         shall consider the order passed by the learned J.M.F.C., Prantij dated 6th 
         April 2016 in the Criminal Inquiry No.16 of 2014. Let the investigation 
         proceed further in accordance with law at the earliest and in the right 
         direction.7       With the above, this writ application is disposed of.   Direct service is

         in the FIR, being C.R.No.I­212/2004 for the offences 

         under Sections­307 and 397 of theIPCregistered with 

         Vijapur   Police   Station   qua   the   incident   which   took 

         place on 05.08.2004 around 7.30 in the evening while 

         the complainant was returning to his residence after 

         performing  pooja  and offering his prayers at Hanuman 

         Temple, nearby village Lodhra, the  respondent­accused

         head and other parts of body and ran away with a goldPage 2 of 9HC-NIC                               Page 2 of 9      Created On Tue Jul 19 05:16:22 IST 2016

         ring worth of Rs.4,000/­ and cash amount of Rs.110/­.

         for the offences as above and as the case was triable

         injured complainant­Purshottam Chhabilal Panthiji, at

         respondent. It is submitted that minor discrepancies

         for offences under Sections­307 and 397 deserves to be 

         allowed by quashing and setting aside the judgment and 

         order to the extent as above.4.   Shri   Shrikar   Bhatt,  learned   advocate  for   the 

         respondent  however   would   contend   that   in   complaint 

         what is stated by the complainant and testimonies of

         testimonies of Shantaben, wife of injured complainant

         respondent  is   falsely   implicated   of   committing

         accused   had   also   received   injuries   and   never   denied

                      with Criminal                      Misc.       Application                 No.

         2.        This            Court         has        heard           the         learned
         Advocate,       Mr.        Chaudhary,               appearing               for         thepetitioner and the learned Advocate, Mr. Savjani,
         appearing for the Respondent No.2.3.        Before adverting to the facts of this
         case, here, it would be beneficial to refer to
         the observations made by the coordiante Bench of
         this Court in Criminal Revision Application No.
         58 of 2016 and the allied matters, which has been

          R/CR.MA/19183/2016                                            ORDER



                 now directed to frame charge against
                 all 12 accused which include new
                 accused against whom additional charge-
                 sheet is filed. While framing fresh
                 charge,    the   Sessions    Court   shall
                 consider entire record available before
                 it from both the chargesheets and shall
                 not omit anything which was disclosed
                 in the previous charge either regarding
                 facts    related    to    commission    of
                 particular offence or conspiracy to
                 commit such offence, so also basic
                 details of offence with sections with
                 reference to the offence for which
                 charge is to be framed. Since charge is
                 to   be   re-framed    against   all   the
                 accused, it becomes now clear that the
                 prosecution is required to recall all
                 the witnesses, if at all necessary,
                 subject to their role against each
                 accused.7.     One more strange and surprising
                 position is revealed from the record
                 I.e. examination of Mahesh Ramanlal
                 Choudhary as a witness though initially
                 he was disclosed as an accused, but
                 could not be prosecuted for want of
                 sanction.8.     Now when the charge-sheet is

                 that he is not witness in the entire
                 case, but he is accused and in that
                 case, prosecution should not examine
                 him as a witness. It goes without
                 saying that certainly he would not
                 support prosecution when he is examined
                 as a witness. In any case, when charge-
                 sheet is filed against him and charge
                 is framed against him, his deposition
                 is to be discarded from the record,Page 3 of 8HC-NIC                        Page 3 of 8      Created On Wed Sep 21 06:06:09 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/19183/2016                                                   ORDER



                         though   it               will         remain            on        record
                         physically.9.     The Sessions Court is directed
                         to expedite the trial since one of the
                         accused is in custody. It goes without
                         saying that the Sessions Court shall
                         decide the Sessions cases purely on
                         merits and in accordance with law and
                         without being influenced by this order.In view of the above, the Revision
                         Application   and   Misc.    Criminal
                         Application   stand    disposed    of
                         accordingly."4.           Learned Advocate for the petitioner, Mr.
         Chaudhary, urged that one of the accused is in
         the jail for past nine years, and therefore, also
         there is need for this Court to interfere.5.           At      this          stage,          learned          Advocate              for
         Respondent           No.2,          Mr.           Savjani,           invited              the
         attention of this Court to an order passed by the
         co-ordinate          Bench         (Coram:           Hon'ble           Mr.       Justice
         S.R. Brahmbhatt) of this Court in Criminal Misc.
         Application          No.       10306         of      2016,         wherein,            this
         Court     has       taken          note       of     the        fact         that         the
         petitioner, herein, is in custody for about nine
         years. However, the Court has observed that the
         period      of      nine       years,             otherwise,             would         have
         weighed       with           the     Court           for       exercising                 the
         discretion, but, considering the peculiar factsPage 4 of 8HC-NIC                                       Page 4 of 8      Created On Wed Sep 21 06:06:09 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/19183/2016                                                  ORDER



         and circumstances narrated in the order, itself,
         when there were, at times, attempts of derailing
         the     proceedings            from          its       correct             path,              it
         indicates that the Court has endeavored to see,
         while     passing            the    order,           that        the        concerned
         persons are brought to book.                              The IO is of the
         rank of Dy.S.P., and therefore, there is no need
         to exercise discretion in favour of the present
         petitioner. At this stage, it would be profitable
         to refer to some of the observations made by this
         Court in Criminal Misc. Application No. 10306 of
         2016 in Paragraphs- 34 to 36, which reads thus:"34. The proposition of law qua delay
                        in trial being one of the factor for
                        considering the exercise of discretion
                        in favour of the applicant in a given
                        case cannot be disputed by anyone. But,
                        in the instant case, while dealing with
                        the      earlier      successive      bail
                        applications,    when   this   Court   has
                        categorically observed that delay alone
                        can never be pleaded as a ground for
                        exercising discretion in favour of the
                        accused, especially when the accused is
                        in   custody   in   respect   of   heinous
                        offence of murder and the methodology
                        of murder and the aftermath thereof
                        need to be examined in its proper
                        perspective.35.     The Court is called upon to
                        examine   this  application  when   the
                        Supreme Court has in fact dismissed the
                        regular bail application, as could be
                        seen from Supreme Court's order datedPage 5 of 8HC-NIC                                      Page 5 of 8      Created On Wed Sep 21 06:06:09 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/19183/2016                                            ORDER



                1st December 2014 in S.L.P. (Criminal)
                No.9228 of 2014, which is reproduced
                hereinabove in paragraph no.(xi). In
                that view of the matter, when the
                Supreme Court was rejecting the bail
                application by the order of dismissal
                of S.L.P.(Criminal) No.9228 of 2014,
                there was already ground of delay
                available    to    the   applicant,    which
                appears to have not been accepted by
                the Supreme Court. The period passed
                thereafter, is not merely a period
                which could be said to be a period
                without any events. The narration of
                the     factual      aspects    hereinabove
                conclusively       indicate     that     the
                complainant is all along endeavoring
                for   arresting      or   restricting    the
                plausibility of any laxity in the
                prosecution and in the said process if
                he is constrained to bring proceedings
                as permissible under the law, can those
                attempts    be    classified   to    be   an
                attempts to thwart the trial and can
                those attempts be classified to be
                attempts for prolonging the custody of
                the accused. The answer would be in
                emphatic 'No', as the attempts of the
                complainant     in    bringing   in    those
                applications,        taking     out      the
                proceedings are also part and parcel of
                the system in which now the right and
                grievances of the victim and his family
                members have been duly acknowledged and
                appreciated. In this scenario, when the
                complainant's attempts to vigilantly
                pursue the course of justice and create
                a   way    for   avoiding    any   possible
                infraction in the course and when the
                Court has also at times granted some
                orders, which would indicate that those
                proceedings and applications takenout
                by the complainant were not frivolous
                so as to brush them aside, this CourtPage 6 of 8HC-NIC                        Page 6 of 8      Created On Wed Sep 21 06:06:09 IST 2016
                R/CR.MA/19183/2016                                                ORDER



                      will have to hold that the complainant
                      or his attempts cannot be classified or
                      designed as for prolonging the custody
                      of the accused or prolonging the trial
                      so as to give a ground for bail to the
                      accused in the custody. The Court
                      reiterated at the cost of repetition
                      that ordinarily in a given case the
                      period of nine years would have surely
                      weighed with the Court in exercising
                      the   discretion  in   favour   of   the
                      applicant accused, but in theinstant
                      case, the peculiar facts, which have
                      narrated hereinabove betraysthat there
                      is somehow or the other, attempts at
                      some quarter to thwart and/or derail
                      the proceedings from its correct path
                      and   therefore,   the   orders    cited
                      hereinabove issued by this Court, would
                      indicate that the Court has endeavor in
                      passing the orders to see to it that
                      the concerned are brought to the book
                      namely the investigating officers of
                      the rank of even Dy.S.P.36.    In light of this background, the
                      delay alone, which is pleaded for
                      urging the Court to exercise discretion
                      is not so gross and deliberate as to
                      outway   the  other   consideration  or
                      reasonings indicated by this Court in
                      earlier orders and hence, the Court is

         (Criminal)       No.       9228   of        2014      arising           from         thePage 7 of 8HC-NIC                                 Page 7 of 8       Created On Wed Sep 21 06:06:09 IST 2016
                    R/CR.MA/19183/2016                                                    ORDER



         order of this Court dated 12.09.2014 passed in

         appears that while disposing of the said matter,

         Apex Court and the subsequent directions issued
         by this Court vide its order dated 06.09.2016
         passed in Criminal Revision Application No. 58 of

         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR BM MANGUKIYA, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 5
         MS BELA A PRAJAPATI, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 5
         MS MH BHATT, ADDL. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
              ==========================================================
         CORAM:             HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
                                  Date : 06/05/2016
                                        ORAL ORDER1.           The         petitioners,             herein,              seek           the
         quashment of the complaint being I-C.R. No. 127
         of 2007, registered with Kamlabaug Police Station
         and a consequential case being Criminal Case No.
         2270 of 2008, which is pending before the Court
         of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, First
         Class, Porbandar.2.           Respondent No.2-the original complainant
         has filed his affidavit stating, therein, that
         the dispute is in relation to a family property,
         which,      with        the   intervention                of       the       elders,
         friends and relatives of both the sides, has been
         resolved.Page 1 of 4HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 4      Created On Sun May 08 03:37:39 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/10426/2016                                               ORDER3.           The truthfulness of the contents of the
         affidavit has also been verified by the learned
         APP.4.           Bearing in mind the decision of the Apex
         Court    in      "GIAN       SINGH     VS.       STATE        OF      PUNJAB          AND
         ANR.", (2012) 10 SCC 303, wherein, at Paragraph-
         61, the Apex Court observed as under;"61.    The position that emerges from
                        the above discussion can be summarised
                        thus: the power of the High Court in
                        quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR
                        or   complaint   in    exercise   of   its
                        inherent jurisdiction is distinct and
                        different from the power given to a
                        criminal court for compounding the
                        offences under Section 320 of the Code.
                        Inherent power is of wide plenitude
                        with no statutory limitation but it has
                        to be exercised in accord with the
                        guideline engrafted in such power viz;
                        (I) to secure the ends of justice or(ii) to prevent abuse of the process of
                        any Court. In what cases power to quash
                        the criminal proceeding or complaint or
                        F.I.R   may  be    exercised   where   the
                        offender and victim have settled their
                        dispute would depend on the facts and
                        circumstances of each case and no
                        category can be prescribed. However,
                        before exercise of such power, the High
                        Court must have due regard to the
                        nature   and   gravity   of   the   crime.Heinous and serious offences of mental
                        depravity or offences like murder,
                        rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly
                        quashed even though the victim or
                        victim's family and the offender havePage 2 of 4HC-NIC                                   Page 2 of 4      Created On Sun May 08 03:37:39 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/10426/2016                                            ORDER



                settled the dispute. Such offences are
                not private in nature and have serious
                impact    on    society.    Similarly,    any
                compromise     between    the    victim   and
                offender in relation to the offences
                under special statutes likePrevention
                of Corruption Actor the offences
                committed by public servants while
                working in that capacity etc; cannot
                provide for any basis for quashing
                criminal    proceedings     involving    such
                offences. But the criminal cases having
                overwhelmingly      and    pre-dominatingly
                civil    flavour     stand    on    different
                footing for the purposes of quashing,
                particularly the offences arising from
                commercial,      financial,       mercantile,
                civil,     partnership     or     such   like
                transactions or the offences arising
                out of matrimony relating to dowry,
                etc. or the family disputes where the
                wrong is basically private or personal
                in nature and the parties have resolved
                their entire dispute. In this category
                of cases, High Court may quash criminal
                proceedings if in its view, because of
                the compromise between the offender and
                victim, the possibility of conviction
                is remote and bleak and continuation of
                criminal case would put accused to
                great oppression and prejudice and
                extreme injustice would be caused to
                him by not quashing the criminal case
                despite full and complete settlement
                and compromise with the victim. In
                other   words,     the   High    Court   must
                consider whether it would be unfair or
                contrary to the interest of justice to
                continue with the criminal proceeding
                or    continuation      of    the    criminal
                proceeding would tantamount to abuse of
                process of law despite settlement and
                compromise     between    the    victim   and
                wrongdoer and whether to secure thePage 3 of 4HC-NIC                        Page 3 of 4      Created On Sun May 08 03:37:39 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/10426/2016                                                 ORDER



                         ends of justice, it is appropriate that
                         criminal case is put to an end and if
                         the answer to the above question(s) is
                         in affirmative, the High Court shall be
                         well within its jurisdiction to quash
                         the criminal proceeding."5.            Bearing in mind the ratiolaid down bythe Hon'ble Apex Court inthe above decision, as
         the disputes are of purely private nature, i.e.
         the dispute being the family dispute in nature,
         where, the parties have chosen out of their own
         volition and free will to end the same and to buy
         the lasting peace, the Court needs to indulge and
         permit        the    quashing         of         the    complaint,              though,
         some of the provisions mentioned in the complaint
         are not compoundable.6.            Resultantly,             the        request         for       quashment
         is acceded to and the impugned complaint as well
         as      the     criminal          case           are    QUASHED             with         all
         consequential                 proceedings.             Direct          service                is
         permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                    IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

               HIRALBEN VISHNUBHAI JOSHI W/O VIPULKUMAR BHOJANI &

                                       Versus
                       STATE OF GUJARAT & 3....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR ANKIT Y BACHANI, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 2
         SATISHKUMAR M PRAJAPATI, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 2
         MR RONAK RAVAL APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                       Date : 06/09/2016

                                        ORAL ORDER1.     The petitioners are already married and their marriage
         has been registered under theGujarat Marriage Registration
         Acton 28.06.2016. The petitioners are apprehensive of some
         serious consequences on account of their marriage as the
         same has been performed without the blessings of parents of
         the petitioner no.1 - girl. They have urged to provide police
         protection as they are also apprehending honour killing.2.     Having heard both the sides and having considered the decision in the
         case of Lata Singh vs. State of UP and Anr. Reported at (2006) 5 SCC 475
         wherein the Apex Court has directed to provide police protection in a case
         whether either marriage is intercaste or inter-religious marriage. At this
         stage, it would be profitable to regurgitate the relevant
         observations and findings of the said decision, which read as
         under :"17.   The   caste   system   is   a   curse   on   the  
                        nation   and   the   sooner   it   is   destroyed   thePage 1 of 4HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 4      Created On Sat Sep 10 00:36:02 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/5988/2016                                             ORDER



              better. In  fact, it  is dividing  the nation 
              at a time when we have to be united to face  
              the   challenges   before   the   nation   unitedly. 
              Hence, inter­caste marriages are in fact in 
              the national interest as they will result in  
              destroying   the   caste   system.   However, 
              disturbing   news   are   coming   from   several 
              parts   of   the   country   that   young   men   and 
              women who undergo inter­caste marriage, are 
              threatened   with   violence,   or   violence   is 
              actually committed on them. In our opinion, 
              such   acts   of   violence   or   threats   or 
              harassment are wholly illegal and those who 
              commit them must be severely punished. This 
              is a free and democratic country, and once a  
              person becomes a major he or she can marry 
              whosoever he/she likes.If the parents of the  
              boy   or   girl   do   not   approve   of   such   inter­
              caste   or   inter­religious   marriage   the 
              maximum they can do is that they can cut off 
              social   relations   with   the   son   or   the 
              daughter,   but   they   cannot   give   threats   or 
              commit   or   instigate   acts   of   violence   and 
              cannot harass the person who undergoes such 
              inter­caste or inter­religious marriage. We, 
              therefore,   direct   that   the   administration/ 
              police   authorities   throughout   the   country 
              will see to it that if any boy or girl who 
              is   a   major   undergoes   inter­caste   or   inter­
              religious marriage  with  a woman or man  who 
              is a major, the couple are not harassed byPage 2 of 4HC-NIC                        Page 2 of 4      Created On Sat Sep 10 00:36:02 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/5988/2016                                            ORDER



              any one nor subjected to threats or acts of 
              violence, and any one who gives such threats  
              or   harasses   or   commits   acts   of   violence 
              either   himself   or   at   his   instigation,   is 
              taken   to   task   by   instituting   criminal  
              proceedings   by   the   police   against   such 
              persons   and   further   stern   action   is   taken 
              against such persons as provided by law.18.   We   sometimes   hear   of   'honour'   killings  
              of   such   persons   who   undergo   inter­caste   or  
              inter­religious   marriage   of   their   own   free 
              will.   There   is   nothing   honourable   in   such 
              killings, and  in fact they are nothing but 
              barbaric   and   shameful   acts   of   murder 
              committed   by   brutal,   feudal   minded   persons 
              who   deserve   harsh   punishment.   Only   in   this  
              way can we stamp out such acts of barbarism.19.In   the   circumstances,   the   writ   petition 
              is   allowed.   The   proceedings   in   Sessions 
              Trial No. 1201/2001 titledState of U.P. v. 
              Sangita   Gupta   and   Ors.arising   out   of   FIR 
              No.   336/2000   registered   at   Police   Station 
              Sarojini   Nagar,   Lucknow   and   pending   in   the  
              Fast Track Court V, Lucknow are quashed. The 
              warrants   against   the   accused   are   also  
              quashed.   The   police   at   all   the   concerned 
              places   should   ensure   that   neither   the  
              petitioner nor her husband nor any relatives  
              of the petitioner's husband are harassed or

                statutory   limitation   but   it   has   to   be

                the   ends   of   justice   or   (ii)   to   prevent

                cases   power   to   quash   the   criminal

                   IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

              SPECIAL CRIMINAL APPLICATION (QUASHING) NO. 3958 of 2016
         ==========================================================
                     DHARMIK SUDHIRKUMAR SONI....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                      STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR P P MAJMUDAR, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         MS BHAKTI THAKER, for the Respondent(s) No. 2
              ==========================================================
         CORAM:              HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
                                   Date : 20/06/2016
                                             ORAL ORDER1.           The original complainant is the mother
         of the prosecutrix. She is present before this
         Court     along         with    the          prosecutrix,                 so      as       the
         petitioner.            The families on both the sides have
         agreed       to      bless      their             relationship,                  as        the
         prosecutrix is short of about seven months from
         her    marriageable            age.         After        once,          she       attains
         that age, the families are likely to arrange the
         marriage of the petitioner with the prosecutrix.2.           The complainant has filed an affidavit
         to that effect and the learned Additional Public
         Prosecutor also has confirmed the veracity of the
         same.3.           Considering the subsequent developments
         and    the     happy         turn     the         things        have        taken,             noPage 1 of 4HC-NIC                                       Page 1 of 4      Created On Thu Jun 23 01:59:24 IST 2016
                R/SCR.A/3958/2016                                           ORDER



         purpose is likely to be served by continuing the
         impugned    complaint.      The         request        for       quashment,
         therefore, requires to be acceded to, keeping in
         mind the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in the
         case of "GIAN SINGH VS. STATE OF PUNJAB AND ANR.",
         (2012) 10 SCC 303, wherein, at Paragraph-61, the
         Apex Court observed as under;"61.    The position that emerges from
                      the above discussion can be summarised
                      thus: the power of the High Court in
                      quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR
                      or   complaint   in    exercise   of   its
                      inherent jurisdiction is distinct and
                      different from the power given to a
                      criminal court for compounding the
                      offences under Section 320 of the Code.
                      Inherent power is of wide plenitude
                      with no statutory limitation but it has
                      to be exercised in accord with the
                      guideline engrafted in such power viz;
                      (I) to secure the ends of justice or(ii) to prevent abuse of the process of
                      any Court. In what cases power to quash
                      the criminal proceeding or complaint or
                      F.I.R   may  be    exercised   where   the
                      offender and victim have settled their
                      dispute would depend on the facts and
                      circumstances of each case and no
                      category can be prescribed. However,
                      before exercise of such power, the High
                      Court must have due regard to the
                      nature   and   gravity   of   the   crime.Heinous and serious offences of mental
                      depravity or offences like murder,
                      rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly
                      quashed even though the victim or
                      victim's family and the offender have
                      settled the dispute. Such offences are
                      not private in nature and have seriousPage 2 of 4HC-NIC                             Page 2 of 4      Created On Thu Jun 23 01:59:24 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/3958/2016                                           ORDER



                impact    on    society.    Similarly,    any
                compromise     between    the    victim   and
                offender in relation to the offences
                under special statutes likePrevention
                of Corruption Actor the offences
                committed by public servants while
                working in that capacity etc; cannot
                provide for any basis for quashing
                criminal    proceedings     involving    such
                offences. But the criminal cases having
                overwhelmingly      and    pre-dominatingly
                civil    flavour     stand    on    different
                footing for the purposes of quashing,
                particularly the offences arising from
                commercial,      financial,       mercantile,
                civil,     partnership     or     such   like
                transactions or the offences arising
                out of matrimony relating to dowry,
                etc. or the family disputes where the
                wrong is basically private or personal
                in nature and the parties have resolved
                their entire dispute. In this category
                of cases, High Court may quash criminal
                proceedings if in its view, because of
                the compromise between the offender and
                victim, the possibility of conviction
                is remote and bleak and continuation of
                criminal case would put accused to
                great oppression and prejudice and
                extreme injustice would be caused to
                him by not quashing the criminal case
                despite full and complete settlement
                and compromise with the victim. In
                other   words,     the   High    Court   must
                consider whether it would be unfair or
                contrary to the interest of justice to
                continue with the criminal proceeding
                or    continuation      of    the    criminal
                proceeding would tantamount to abuse of
                process of law despite settlement and
                compromise     between    the    victim   and
                wrongdoer and whether to secure the
                ends of justice, it is appropriate that
                criminal case is put to an end and ifPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                       Page 3 of 4      Created On Thu Jun 23 01:59:24 IST 2016
                  R/SCR.A/3958/2016                                                    ORDER



                        the answer to the above question(s) is
                        in affirmative, the High Court shall be
                        well within its jurisdiction to quash
                        the criminal proceeding."4.          In the result, this petition is allowed.
         The     impugned            complaint            is       QUASHED             with          all
         consequential proceedings.5.          Ms. Bhakti Thaker is permitted to file
         his     appearance            on        behalf             of        the         original
         complainant. Direct service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                   IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

         SPECIAL CRIMINAL APPLICATION (DIRECTION - POLICE PROTECTION)
                                          NO. 4782 of 2016
         ==========================================================
              NITABEN W/O ASHWINKUMAR CHAUDHARY & 1....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                      STATE OF GUJARAT & 4....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR DIPAK R DAVE, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 2
         MR RONAK RAVAL, PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================
         CORAM:              HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
                                   Date : 11/07/2016
                                           ORAL ORDER1.           Leave to amend prayer clause. Amendment
         be carried out, forthwith.2.           The parties have approached this Court,
         seeking following reliefs;"12.         ...A.   be pleased to admit and allow the
                         present petition;B.    be pleased to issue a writ of
                         mandamus and / or a writ in the nature
                         of   mandamus  and   /  or   any   other
                         appropriate writ, order or direction:(i) directing the respondent Nos. 1 to
                         4 to immediately protect the lives and
                         liberty   of    the   petitioners    and
                         directing    the    concerned     police
                         authorities to immediately take action
                         against the respondent no.5 and allPage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                      Page 1 of 5      Created On Wed Jul 13 01:50:16 IST 2016
               R/SCR.A/4782/2016                                              ORDER



                     concerned persons and also to register
                     appropriate   criminal   complaint  for
                     their   barbaric   and   shameful  acts
                     against the petitioners;(ii) directing the respondent No.2 and
                     3, Director General of Police to take
                     appropriate    and    immediate    action
                     against   the    respondent   No.5    for
                     misusing their official position and
                     for harassing the petitioners and the
                     relatives of the petitioner No.2;(iii)  directing the respondent Nos. 1to   4   to   ensure  safety   of   the
                     petitioners as well as relatives of the
                     petitioner No.2;(iv)    directing the respondent Nos.2
                     and 3 to take immediate and stern
                     action   against   all   the    concerned,
                     including the respondent No.4 for his
                     illegal action     /   inaction    in  the
                     matter; and further be pleased to
                     direct the respondent No.3 to protect
                     the    lives   and    liberty     of   the
                     petitioners;(v)    pending admission, hearing and
                     final disposal of present petition, bepleased to direct the respondent Nos. 1to 4 to immediately protect the lives
                     and liberty of the petitioners and
                     directing    the     concerned    police
                     authorities to immediately take action
                     against the respondent no.5 and also to
                     file appropriate criminal complaint for
                     their   barbaric   and   shameful   acts
                     against the petitioners;C.      ..."

         3.       On      noticing      that          the     petitioners                havePage 2 of 5HC-NIC                               Page 2 of 5      Created On Wed Jul 13 01:50:16 IST 2016
                   R/SCR.A/4782/2016                                                      ORDERmarried with each other, without the blessings of
         the girl's parents, because of their likeness,
         they are apprehending that they may become victim
         of    honour       killing.               It           appears        that        both         the
         petitioners are neighbours and they belong to the
         same community. It is only the resistance on the
         part    of     the      parents           and           the     relatives              of      the
         girl, who are against such relation, which is
         formed       by     the           petitioners               out        of      their           own
         choice.4.           Heard both the sides. Bearing in mind
         the fact that both the petitioners have married
         and    they         are           apprehending                 threat            from          the
         community and the family of the girl due to such
         a    step    taken           by    them,           a    possibility               of      their
         being victim of honour killing also cannot be
         ruled out.In that view of the matter, here, it
         would be relevant to refer to the observations
         made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of
         "LATA SINGH VS. STATE OF U.P.", 2007 (1) GLH 41,
         in Paragraph-16 which reads as under;"16.   The caste system is a curse on
                         the nation and the sooner it is
                         destroyed the better. In fact, it is
                         dividing the nation at a time when we
                         have   to  be   united  to  face   the
                         challenges before the nation unitedly.
                         Hence, inter-caste marriages are in
                         fact in the national interest as they
                         will result in destroying the castePage 3 of 5HC-NIC                                        Page 3 of 5         Created On Wed Jul 13 01:50:16 IST 2016
          R/SCR.A/4782/2016                                           ORDER



                system. However, disturbing news are
                coming from several parts of the
                country that young men and women who
                undergo   inter-caste     marriage,    are
                threatened with violence, or violence
                is actually committed on them. In our
                opinion, such acts of violence or
                threats   or    harassment   are    wholly
                illegal and those who commit them must
                be severely punished. This is a free
                and democratic country, and once a
                person becomes a major he or she can
                marry whosoever he/she likes. If the
                parents of the boy or girl do not
                approve of such inter-caste or inter-
                religious marriage the maximum they can
                do is that they can cut off social
                relations with the son or the daughter,
                but they cannot give threats or commit
                or instigate acts of violence and
                cannot harass the person who undergoes
                such inter-caste or inter- religious
                marriage. We, therefore, direct that
                the administration/police authorities
                throughout the country will see to it
                that if any boy or girl who is a major
                undergoes     inter-caste    or     inter-
                religious marriage with a woman or man
                who is a major, the couple are not
                harassed by any one nor subjected to
                threats or acts of violence, and any
                one who gives such threats or harasses
                or commits acts of violence either
                himself or at his instigation, is taken
                to   task    by    instituting   criminal
                proceedings by the police against such
                persons and further stern action is
                taken against such persons as provided
                by law. We sometimes hear of `honour'
                killings of such persons who undergo
                inter-caste or inter-religious marriage
                of their own free will. There is
                nothing honourable in such killings,
                and in fact they are nothing butPage 4 of 5HC-NIC                       Page 4 of 5      Created On Wed Jul 13 01:50:16 IST 2016
                  R/SCR.A/4782/2016                                                 ORDER



                        barbaric and shameful acts of murder
                        committed by brutal, feudal minded
                        persons who deserve harsh punishment.
                        Only in this way can we stamp out such
                        acts of barbarism."5.          Under           the   circumstances,                 this         petition
         is PARTLY ALLOWED. Respondent No.4 is directed to
         PROVIDE      police          PROTECTION            to     the        petitioners,
         herein.      The      duration          of      the      police          protection
         shall be determined by Respondent No.4 with an
         intimation to Respondent No.3.                                In case of any
         difficulty, it shall be open to the petitioners
         to approach this Court. Disposed of, accordingly.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR YN OZA, SENIOR COUNSEL WITH MR APURVA R KAPADIA,

         MS SHRUTI PATHAK, ADDL.PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for Respondent No. 1
         ==========================================================

         CORAM HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
             :

                                      Date : 22/04/2016


                                        ORAL ORDER1. Let   a   notice   be   issued   to   the   respondents,  

              returnable   on   May   02,   2016.   The   Investigating 

              Officer   shall   follow   the   decision   of   the   Apex 

              Court in the case ofJoginder Kumar v. State of  

              Uttar  Pradesh  and  others,  reported   in  (1994)  4  

              SCC 260, which inter alia provides as under :"20. In India, Third Report of the National 
                     Police   Commission   at   p.   32   also   suggested:"An   arrest   during   the   investigation   of   a 
                     cognizable case may be considered justifiedPage 1 of 4HC-NIC                                  Page 1 of 4      Created On Wed Apr 27 01:10:40 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/9487/2016                                           ORDER



             in   one   or   other   of   the   following 
             circumstances :(i)      The case involves a grave offence like 
             murder, dacoity, robbery, rape etc., and it 
             is necessary to arrest the accused and bring 
             his   movements   under   restraint   to   infuse 
             confidence among the terrorstricken victims.(ii) The   accused   is   likely   to   abscond   and 
             evade the processes of law.(iii)   The   accused   is   given   to   violent 
             behaviour   and   is   likely   to   commit   further 
             offences   unless   his   movements   are   brought 
             under restraint.(iv) The accused is a habitual offender and 
             unless   kept   in   custody   he   is   likely   to  
             commit similar offences again.It   would   be   desirable   to   insist   through  
             departmental   instructions   that   a   police 
             officer making an arrest should also record 
             in the case diary the reasons for making the 
             arrest, thereby clarifying his conformity to 
             the specified guidelines......"The   above   guidelines   are   merely   the 
             incidents   of   personal   liberty   guaranteed 
             under   the   Constitution   of   India.   No   arrest  
             can   be   made   because   it   is   lawful   for   the 
             police   officer   to   do   so.   The   existence   ofPage 2 of 4HC-NIC                       Page 2 of 4      Created On Wed Apr 27 01:10:40 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/9487/2016                                                  ORDER



             the   power   to   arrest   is   one   thing.   The  
             justification   for   the   exercise   of   it   is  
             quite   another.   The   police   officer   must   be 
             able   to   justify   the   arrest   apart   from   his  
             power   to   do   so.   Arrest   and   detention   in  
             police   lock­up   of   a   person   can   cause 
             incalculable   harm   to   the   reputation   and 
             self­esteem   of   a   person.   No   arrest   can   be  
             made   in   a   routine   manner   on   a   mere 
             allegation of commission of an offence made 
             against a person. It would be prudent for a 
             police officer in the interest of protection  
             of   the   constitutional   rights   of   a   citizen 
             and   perhaps   in   his   own   interest   that   no  
             arrest   should   be   made   without   a   reasonable  
             satisfaction                   reached                 after               some 
             investigation as to the genuineness and bona  
             fides of a complaint and a reasonable belief 
             both as to the person's complicity and even 
             so as to the need to effect arrest. Denying 
             a person of his liberty is a serious matter. 
             The recommendations of the Police Commission 
             merely              reflect              the            constitutional 
             concomitants   of   the   fundamental   right   to 
             personal   liberty   and   freedom.   A  268   person 
             is   not   liable   to   arrest   merely   on   the  
             suspicion of complicity in an offence. There  
             must be some reasonable justification in the  
             opinion of the officer effecting the arrest 
             that such arrest is necessary and justified. 
             Except   in   heinous   offences,   an   arrest   mustPage 3 of 4HC-NIC                             Page 3 of 4       Created On Wed Apr 27 01:10:40 IST 2016
                      R/CR.MA/9487/2016                                             ORDER



                         be avoided if a police officer issues notice 
                         to   person   to   attend   the   Station   House   and  
                         not to leave the Station without permission 
                         would do."It   is   clarified   that   the   Investigating 

                 Officer shall not effect arrest of the applicant 

                 without   justifying   the   same   as   provided   inthe 

                 said decision.Direct   Service   is   permitted   qua   the 

                 respondent   No.2.   To   be   served   through   the 

                 concerned Police Station.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                                      Date : 13/06/2016
                                       ORAL ORDER1.            The      petitioners,            herein,          belong           to      same
         community and they have married with each other.
         Since,      the      petitioners          have        married           against               the
         will of father of petitioner No.1-Respondent No.4,
         herein, they are apprehensive of strong reaction
         from     the      parents       of     petitioner               No.1        and        other
         relatives.          They      have,       therefore,               preferred                  the
         present petition with a prayer to direct police to
         provide them            protection.2.            I    have       heard      learned           Advocate             for           the
         petitioners, Mr. Bachani, and learned APP for the
         Respondents.3.            Considering the material on record, more
         particularly,            an   application,               Dated:           11.05.2016,
         addressed by petitioner No.1 to PSI, Taluka Police
         Station, Tharad, it appears that the petitioners
         are     facing       apprehension           including             the        threat            ofPage 1 of 3HC-NIC                                    Page 1 of 3        Created On Fri Jun 17 01:18:40 IST 2016
                R/SCR.A/3347/2016                                             ORDER



         honour killing.In that view of the matter, here,
         it would be relevant to refer to the observations
         made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of "LATA
         SINGH VS. STATE OF U.P.", 2007 (1) GLH 41, which
         reads as under;"       The caste system is a curse on
                       the   nation    and   the   sooner    it   isdestroyed the better. In fact, it is
                       dividing the nation at a time when we
                       have to be united to face the challenges
                       before    the   nation    unitedly.    Hence,
                       inter-caste marriages are in fact in the
                       national interest as they will result in
                       destroying the caste system. However,
                       disturbing news are coming from several
                       parts of the country that young men and
                       women who undergo inter-caste marriage,
                       are    threatened    with     violence,    or
                       violence is actually committed on them.
                       In our opinion, such acts of violence or
                       threats or harassment are wholly illegal
                       and those who commit them must be
                       severely punished. This is a free and
                       democratic country, and once a person
                       becomes a major he or she can marry
                       whosoever he/she likes. If the parents
                       of the boy or girl do not approve of
                       such    inter-caste    or    inter-religious
                       marriage the maximum they can do is that
                       they can cut off social relations with
                       the son or the daughter, but they cannot
                       give threats or commit or instigate acts
                       of violence and cannot harass the person
                       who undergoes such inter-caste or inter-
                       religious     marriage.    We,    therefore,
                       direct that the administration/police
                       authorities throughout the country will
                       see to it that if any boy or girl who is
                       a major undergoes inter-caste or inter-
                       religious marriage with a woman or man
                       who is a major, the couple are notPage 2 of 3HC-NIC                             Page 2 of 3      Created On Fri Jun 17 01:18:40 IST 2016
                  R/SCR.A/3347/2016                                                ORDER



                         harassed by any one nor subjected to
                         threats or acts of violence, and any one
                         who gives such threats or harasses or
                         commits acts of violence either himself
                         or at his instigation, is taken to task
                         by instituting criminal proceedings by
                         the police against such persons and
                         further stern action is taken against
                         such persons as provided by law. We
                         sometimes hear of `honour' killings of
                         such persons who undergo inter-caste or
                         inter-religious marriage of their own
                         free will. There is nothing honourable
                         in such killings, and in fact they are
                         nothing but barbaric and shameful acts
                         of murder committed by brutal, feudal
                         minded   persons   who    deserve  harsh
                         punishment. Only in this way can we
                         stamp out such acts of barbarism."4.           In the case on hand, as stated above, as
         the petitioners, who have entered into marriage,
         are facing threat from the parents and relatives of
         the girl, i.e. petitioner No.1, herein, Respondent
         No.2-Police           Inspector,         Taluka           Police            Station,
         Tharad, is DIRECTED to look into the matter and to
         provide       police        PROTECTION          to      the         petitioners,
         herein, for the reasonable period of time, as it
         may be deemed fit in the facts of the present case.
         DISPOSED OF, accordingly.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

         CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR REGULAR BAIL) NO. 19408

              RAMESHBHAI DAHYABHAI DHUVA ( MAHESHWARI )....Applicant(s)
                                      Versus
                         STATE OF GUJARAT....Respondent(s)
         =============================================
         Appearance:
         MR UMESH A TRIVEDI, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         MR. MITESH AMIN, PUBLIC PROSECUTOR WITH MR. DHARMESH
         DEVNANI, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         =============================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE P.P.BHATT

                                       Date : 08/09/2016

                                         ORAL ORDER1.      The present application is filed underSection 439of the Code

         of Criminal Procedure by the applicant for regular bail in connection

         with First Information Report being C.R.No.I-64/2016 registered with

         Gandhidham "A" Division Police Station, District Kutch for the

         offences punishable underSection 302of the Indian Penal Code.2.      Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned Additional

         Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State.3.      Learned advocate for the               applicant submitted that the

         applicant implicated in an offence punishable underSection 302of

         the Indian Penal Code. The allegation against the present applicant is

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

            CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE 
                         FIR/ORDER) NO. 15625 of 2016
         ========================================================
                 JAYANTIBHAI SHIVABHAI PATEL  &  4....Applicant(s)
                                    Versus

         ========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR ASHISH M DAGLI, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 ­ 5
         PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ========================================================

             CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI
          
                                       Date : 01/07/2016
          ORAL ORDER1.     The   petitioners   have   approached   this   Hon'ble 

                Court seeking quashment of FIR being C.R. No.I­

                59/2016   registered   with   Vadi   Police   Station, 

                Vadodara.2.     The   complainant   resides   with   his   family   members 

                in Haribhakti Industrial Estate and enjoying 5000 

                sq. mtrs., area of Survey No.303. Complaint came 

                to   be   lodged   in   respect   of   very   land.   Now, 

                however, the dispute between the parties has been 

                amicably   settled   and   MOU   has   been   entered   into 

                between the parties. In view of the MOU entered 

                into between the parties, the amount of MOU was 

                agreed   to   be   paid   through   cheques   to   thePage 1 of 5HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 5      Created On Tue Jul 05 02:46:58 IST 2016
                    R/CR.MA/15625/2016                                              ORDER



                 complainant. Therefore, learned Advocate for the 

                 petitioners   has   produced   three   banker's   cheques 

                 of  Union  Bank  of  India  before  this  Court   to  be 

                 handed   over   to   the   complainant   and   his   family 

                 members. The details of the said banker's cheques 

                 are as under:Sr.      Date                  Name                  Amount                Cheque
         No                                                     Rs.                   No.
          .
             1   27.06.20 Prakashbhai N.                      7,50,000/-             409823
                    16    Naika
             2   27.06.20 Sanjaybhai Naika                    7,50,000/-             409824163   28.06.20 Naranbhai B. Naika                  5,00,000/-             409825163.      The parties out of their own volition and mutual 

                 understanding   the   dispute   is   resolved   amicable 

                 and peacefully between the parties.4.      The   complainant's   affidavit   is   also   on   the 

                 record, wherein he has confirmed that the dispute 

                 is   amicably   settled   without   undue   influence   or 

                 threat and are willing to enter into compromise 

                 as   stated   in   MOU.   He   has   no   objection   if   the 

                 impugned   FIR   and   all   proceedings   in   pursuancePage 2 of 5HC-NIC                                   Page 2 of 5      Created On Tue Jul 05 02:46:58 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/15625/2016                                             ORDER



              thereto are quashed by this Court.5.   Learned   APP   also   has   been   heard,   who   has   no 

              objection   if   the   complaint   is   quashed   by   this 

              Court.6.In  above  view  of  the  matter,   here,  it  would  be 

              profitable to refer to the  observations made by 

              the     Hon'ble   Apex   Court   in   the   case   of   "GIAN  

              SINGH  VS.  STATE  OF  PUNJAB  AND  ANR.", (2012) 10 

              SCC 303, wherein, at Paragraph­61, the Apex Court 

              observed as under;"61.      The position that emerges from the 
                       above   discussion   can   be   summarised   thus:the power of the High Court in quashing a 
                       criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in 
                       exercise   of   its   inherent   jurisdiction   is 
                       distinct and different from the power given 
                       to   a   criminal   court   for   compounding   the 
                       offences   under  Section   320  of   the   Code. 
                       Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no 
                       statutory   limitation   but   it   has   to   be 
                       exercised   in   accord   with   the   guideline 
                       engrafted in such power viz; (I) to secure 
                       the   ends   of   justice   or   (ii)   to   prevent 
                       abuse of the process of any Court. In what 
                       cases   power   to   quash   the   criminal 
                       proceeding   or   complaint   or   F.I.R   may   be 
                       exercised   where   the   offender   and   victim 
                       have settled their dispute would depend on 
                       the   facts   and   circumstances   of   each   case 
                       and no category can be prescribed. However, 
                       before   exercise   of   such   power,   the   High 
                       Court   must   have   due   regard   to   the   nature 
                       and   gravity   of   the   crime.   Heinous   and 
                       serious   offences   of   mental   depravity   orPage 3 of 5HC-NIC                               Page 3 of 5      Created On Tue Jul 05 02:46:58 IST 2016
          R/CR.MA/15625/2016                                             ORDER



                offences   like   murder,   rape,   dacoity,   etc. 
                cannot be fittingly quashed even though the 
                victim or victim's family and the offender 
                have settled the dispute. Such offences are 
                not   private   in   nature   and   have   serious 
                impact   on   society.   Similarly,   any 
                compromise between the victim and offender 
                in  relation  to  the offences under special 
                statutes likePrevention of Corruption Actor   the   offences   committed   by   public 
                servants   while   working   in   that   capacity 
                etc;   cannot   provide   for   any   basis   for 
                quashing   criminal   proceedings   involving 
                such   offences.   But   the   criminal   cases 
                having   overwhelmingly   and   pre­dominatingly 
                civil   flavour   stand   on   different   footing 
                for the purposes of quashing, particularly 
                the   offences   arising   from   commercial, 
                financial,   mercantile,   civil,   partnership 
                or  such  like transactions  or the  offences 
                arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, 
                etc. or the family disputes where the wrong 
                is basically private or personal in nature 
                and the parties have resolved their entire 
                dispute.   In   this   category   of   cases,   High 
                Court may quash criminal proceedings if in 
                its view, because of the compromise between 
                the offender and victim, the possibility of 
                conviction   is   remote   and   bleak   and 
                continuation   of   criminal   case   would   put 
                accused   to   great   oppression   and   prejudice 
                and   extreme   injustice   would   be   caused   to 
                him   by   not   quashing   the   criminal   case 
                despite   full   and   complete   settlement   and 
                compromise with the victim. In other words, 
                the   High   Court   must   consider   whether   it 
                would be unfair or contrary to the interest 
                of   justice   to   continue   with   the   criminal 
                proceeding or continuation of the criminal 
                proceeding   would   tantamount   to   abuse   of 
                process   of   law   despite   settlement   and 
                compromise between the victim and wrongdoer 
                and whether to secure the ends of justice, 
                it is appropriate that criminal case is put 
                to an end and if the answer to the above 
                question(s)   is   in   affirmative,   the   HighPage 4 of 5HC-NIC                        Page 4 of 5      Created On Tue Jul 05 02:46:58 IST 2016
                    R/CR.MA/15625/2016                                             ORDER



                          Court shall be well within its jurisdiction 
                          to quash the criminal proceeding."7.      Resultantly, the request for quashment is acceded 

                 to   and   the   impugned   complaint   being   C.R.   No.I­

                 59/2016   registered   with   Vadi   Police   Station, 

                 Vadodara   is  QUASHED  with   all   consequential 

                 proceedings.  DISPOSED   OF,   accordingly.   Direct 

                 service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

                was   abusing   on   phone.   When   the   complainant   asked   him,   he

                namely   Joslinbhai   @   Ladvo   Vinfredbhai   Thakor,   Jayantibhai 
                Manibhai Patel, Bhimsingbhai Ravjibhai Chauhan, Dinesh Lilaram 
                Marvadi, Atmaram Chhogaji Marvadi and Savitaben Laxmanbhai 
                Patel   and   in   their   presence,   the   deceased   was   attacked   by   thePage 2 of 4HC-NIC                                       Page 2 of 4      Created On Fri Apr 29 00:35:46 IST 2016

              present   applicant   with   a   big   stone   and   brutally   killed.   He,
