                                       ORAL ORDER1      Rule returnable forthwith. Ms.Nisha Thakore,
         learned APP waives service of notice of Rule for and
         on behalf of the respondent -State.2.     The       petitioner       before           this         Court            seeks
         quashment of the order dated 7th July 2016 passed
         by the learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class made
         in Search Warrant Application No. 101 of 2016. It
         appears that petitioner No.1 herein has chosen to
         marry out of her own volition and without wish of
         her parents.Page 1 of 7HC-NIC                                  Page 1 of 7      Created On Fri Aug 12 03:29:01 IST 2016
                R/SCR.A/5256/2016                                            ORDER3.   An Application underSection 97of the Code of
         Criminal Procedure, 1973, was preferred, being
         Search Warrant Application                     No. 101 of 2016,
         wherein the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate,
         First Class, Morva Hadaf, after issuance of notice,
         directed     the petitioner to be kept present before
         the Court.4.   The petitioner has approached this Court
         seeking quashment of the complaint on the ground
         that she has voluntarily married and such order
         would have no basis. She is 22 years old and her
         certificate of marriage dated 25th July, 2013 is also
         brought on the record.5.   This Court verified from the petitioner about
         her well being and she has confirmed that it is not
         out of any compulsion that she had left her parents
         and joined with her husband because her study was
         going on. She also reveals that it is only because at
         later point of time,      when talks of marriage were
         going on, she needed to join her husband.6.   Having heard learned advocates appearing on
         both the sides and having considered the materialPage 2 of 7HC-NIC                             Page 2 of 7      Created On Fri Aug 12 03:29:01 IST 2016
                R/SCR.A/5256/2016                                                ORDER



         available on record, this Court is of the opinion that
         the order of Search Warrant passed would not be
         required to be sustained.7.   It is to be noted that to ensure that the
         relationship of the parties in future i.e. parents of
         the petitioner and the petitioner, continues to be
         smooth     and        cordial,     the         petitioner             would              be
         permitted to meet with the parents in presence of
         the learned advocates which has resulted into
         break through in the relationship. However, it is
         expected that both the sides would work out some
         solution in maintaining the relationship in future.8.   Deputy Superintendent of Police, Dahod                                       shall
         ensure that there is no harm caused to the young
         couple or         his family members. These are the
         formative months, where the emotions are running
         high, there shall          not be any repetition of any
         event which may cause apprehension or lead to
         honor killing. There should be apt protection along
         the lines of decision of the Apex Court, rendered in
         case of Latasingh Vs. The State of UP & Ors.
         reported in 2006 (5) SCC 475, whereby the Apex
         Court had directed that "..since several instancesPage 3 of 7HC-NIC                               Page 3 of 7        Created On Fri Aug 12 03:29:01 IST 2016
                R/SCR.A/5256/2016                                               ORDER



         are coming to our knowledge of harassment,
         threats and violence against young men and
         women who marry outside their case, we feel it
         necessary to make some general comments on the
         matter. The nation is passing through a crucial
         transitional period in our history and this Court
         cannot remain silent in matters of great public
         concern."The relevant observations of the said decision

         needs to be reproduced at this stage, which reads

         as under:-"The caste system is a curse on the nation and the
             sooner it is destroyed the better. In fact, it is dividing
             the nation at a time when we have to be united to
             face the challenges before the nation unitedly.
             Hence, inter-caste marriages are in fact in the
             national interest as they will result in destroying the
             caste system. However, disturbing news are coming
             from several parts of the country that young men and
             women        who      undergo          inter-caste         marriage,                are
             threatened with violence, or violence is actually
             committed on them. In our opinion, such acts of
             violence or threats or harassment are wholly illegal
             and those who commit them must be severelyPage 4 of 7HC-NIC                                Page 4 of 7      Created On Fri Aug 12 03:29:01 IST 2016
            R/SCR.A/5256/2016                                             ORDER



         punished. This is a free and democratic country, and
         once a person becomes a major he or she can marry
         whosoever he/she likes. If the parents of the boy or
         girl do not approve of such inter-caste or inter-
         religious marriage the maximum they can do is that
         they can cut off social relations with the son or the
         daughter, but they cannot give threats or commit or
         instigate acts of violence and cannot harass the
         person who undergoes such inter-caste or inter-
         religious marriage. We, therefore, direct that the
         administration/police         authorities            throughout                   the
         country will see to it that if any boy or girl who is a
         major      undergoes       inter-caste            or       inter-religious
         marriage with a woman or man who is a major, the
         couple are not harassed by any one nor subjected to
         threats or acts of violence, and any one who gives
         such threats or harasses or commits acts of violence
         either himself or at his instigation, is taken to task by
         instituting criminal proceedings by the police against
         such persons and further stern action is taken against
         such persons as provided by                    law. We sometimes
         hear of 'honour' killings of such persons who undergo
         inter-caste or inter-religious marriage of their own
         free will. There is nothing honourable in such killings,
         and in fact they are nothing but barbaric and
         shameful acts of murder committed by brutal, feudal
         minded persons who deserve harsh punishment. Only
         in this way can we stamp out such acts of barbarism.Page 5 of 7HC-NIC                          Page 5 of 7      Created On Fri Aug 12 03:29:01 IST 2016
                    R/SCR.A/5256/2016                                                    ORDER

                        etc. or the family disputes where the

                        proceedings if in its view, because of

                        victim, the possibility of conviction

                        great oppression and prejudice and
                        extreme injustice would be caused to
                        him by not quashing the criminal case
                        despite full and complete settlement

                        other   words,   the   High    Court   must

               coercive steps that might affect personal liberty and life

               district of Mehsana, Gujarat.C.       Such other and further relief as Your Lordships may
               deem fit and proper in the interest of justice be granted."Mr. Jit P. Patel, learned advocate appearing for the
         petitioners has urged that both of them are married and
         they belong to the same community and their Gotra being
         the same. However, parent's approval is not with them.
         He has lamented that both the petitioners are in the
         hospital. They have been beaten, after taking them away
         from Ahmedabad.Learned APP Ms. Chetna Shah has no objection, if
         Court orders grant of police protection to the petitioners.Having heard both the sides and considering the fact
         that they both are adult and married on 6.2.2016. Their
         marriage is registered under theGujarat Registration of
         Marriages Act, 2006which is brought on record. Not only
         they have made out apprehension, but their apprehension
         appears to have been genuine, as per the version of
         learned advocate for the petitioners.Not below the rank of Dy. S.P                      shall look into the
         matter and provide police protection to the petitioners
         without further loss of time; as prayed for in this petition.
         The    time shall be decided by the concerned officer,
         bearing in mind all the facts and circumstances of the
         case and the ground reality of the case.While parting, it will be necessary for the concernedPage 2 of 5HC-NIC                                  Page 2 of 5      Created On Sat Aug 20 01:19:12 IST 2016
                 R/SCR.A/6014/2016                                               ORDER



         police officer to have a look at the dictum of the Apex
         Court rendered in case of Latasingh Vs. The State of UP &
         Ors. reported in 2006(5) SCC 475 had directed that "since
         several instances          are coming to our knowledge of
         harassment, threats and violence against young men and
         women who marry outside their case, we feel it necessary
         to make some general comments on the matter. The
         nation is passing through a crucial transitional period in
         our history and this Court cannot remain silent in matters
         of great public concern."The relevant observations of this decision needs to
         be reproduced at this stage:"The caste system is a curse on the nation and the
             sooner it is destroyed the better. In fact, it is dividing
             the nation at a time when we have to be united to
             face the challenges before the nation unitedly.
             Hence, inter-caste marriages are in fact in the
             national interest as they will result in destroying the
             caste system. However, disturbing news are coming
             from several parts of the country that young men and
             women         who      undergo          inter-caste        marriage,             are
             threatened with violence, or violence is actually
             committed on them. In our opinion, such acts of
             violence or threats or harassment are wholly illegal
             and those who commit them must be severely
             punished. This is a free and democratic country, and
             once a person becomes a major he or she can marry
             whosoever he/she likes. If the parents of the boy orPage 3 of 5HC-NIC                                 Page 3 of 5      Created On Sat Aug 20 01:19:12 IST 2016
                  R/SCR.A/6014/2016                                             ORDER



             girl do not approve of such inter-caste or inter-
             religious marriage the maximum they can do is that
             they can cut off social relations with the son or the
             daughter, but they cannot give threats or commit or
             instigate acts of violence and cannot harass the
             person who undergoes such inter-caste or inter-
             religious marriage. We, therefore, direct that the
             administration/police           authorities            throughout               the
             country will see to it that if any boy or girl who is a
             major        undergoes       inter-caste            or       inter-religious
             marriage with a woman or man who is a major, the
             couple are not harassed by any one nor subjected to
             threats or acts of violence, and any one who gives
             such threats or harasses or commits acts of violence
             either himself or at his instigation, is taken to task by
             instituting criminal proceedings by the police against
             such persons and further stern action is taken against
             such persons as provided by                     law. We sometimes
             hear of 'honour' killings of such persons who undergo
             inter-caste or inter-religious marriage of their own
             free will. There is nothing honourable in such killings,
             and in fact they are nothing but barbaric and
             shameful acts of murder committed by brutal, feudal
             minded persons who deserve harsh punishment. Only
             in this way can we stamp out such acts of barbarism.

         of UP & Ors. (Supra ), the request of the petitioners

         officer    has      clearly    stated     that     at    the      time       when        thePage 1 of 6HC-NIC                                     Page 1 of 6      Created On Tue Feb 02 01:58:34 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/16811/2015                                                  ORDER




         postmortem        of        the   body      of     deceased            Girishbhai            @
         Gordhanbhai Chitharbhai Bariaya came to be carried out, it
         was not possible to give any definite opinion as regards the
         cause of death and that it was after the FSL report was
         received, it appeared that the cause of death could be due to
         consumption of excessive ethyl alcohol. The learned advocate
         submitted that therefore, the cause of death of the deceased
         was due to consumption of excessive ethyl alcohol and not on
         account of strangulation or throttling of the deceased.
         Referring to the testimony of the first informant, PW-4,
         Minaben Girishbhai, it was pointed out that she has stated that
         the applicant herein had made an extra judicial confession
         before her stating that he had committed murder of the
         deceased by catching hold of his hand and putting his leg on
         his neck, however, the testimony of the medical officer and
         the post mortem report do not reveal any corresponding
         injuries. It was submitted that the trial court has based its
         conviction solely on the extra judicial confession of the
         applicant without there being any corroborative evidence in
         that regard.In support of his submissions, the learned counsel
         placed reliance upon the decision of the Supreme Court in the
         case ofAnanda Poojary v. State of Karnataka, (2015) 1
         SCC 235 for the proposition that when there is a possibility of
         two different causes of death, in the absence of a clear
         certainty about the cause, benefit of doubt should be given to
         the accused. It was submitted that in the facts of the present
         case, since the cause of death is not certain, the applicant is
         entitled to the benefit of doubt in that regard.2.1   It was urged that the applicant was on bail throughout
         the trial and that having regard to the circumstances whichPage 2 of 6HC-NIC                                     Page 2 of 6      Created On Tue Feb 02 01:58:34 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/16811/2015                                                ORDER




         have been brought on record by the prosecution, which do not
         establish the charge against the applicant, this court may
         kindly exercise discretion in favour of the applicant and
         suspend the order of sentence and enlarge him on bail.3.   Opposing the application, Mr. Hardik Soni, learned
         Additional Public Prosecutor invited the attention of the court
         to the postmortem report to point out that against column
         No.21 - Neck, the remark is "Brownish - blackish discoloured".
         It was pointed out that Dr. Chandramauli, in his testimony, has
         stated     that     there     appeared        to      be      brownish           blackish
         discolouration on the neck of the deceased which supports the
         prosecution case that the accused had caused the death of the
         deceased by pressing his foot on his neck. It was submitted
         that in the light of the medical evidence and testimony of
         Meenaben wife of the deceased whereby she has testified that
         the applicant had made a confessional statement before her to
         the effect that he had killed her husband, the trial court was
         wholly justified in holding that the prosecution had duly
         established the charge against the applicant-accused.4.   This court has considered the rival submissions advanced
         by the learned advocates for the respective parties and has
         perused the evidence on record as referred to by the learned
         advocates for the respective parties.5.   . It is by now well settled that a detailed examination of
         the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the
         case is to be avoided by the court while passing orders on bail
         applications. Therefore, it is not necessary to refer to the
         evidence on record in detail.Page 3 of 6HC-NIC                                   Page 3 of 6        Created On Tue Feb 02 01:58:34 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/16811/2015                                            ORDER6.    On a brief appraisal of the evidence which has come on
         record, it appears that Dr. Chandramauli, in his testimony, has
         clearly stated that at the relevant time when the autopsy of
         the body of the deceased was carried out, it was not possible
         to ascertain the cause of death and it was only subsequently
         when the FSL report was received, that it was opined that the
         possibility of death was due to excessive ethyl alcohol
         intoxication cannot be ruled out. A perusal of the postmortem
         report of the deceased shows that no injuries are indicated in
         column No.17 thereof. Moreover, the concerned Medical
         Officers have not opined that the deceased has died due to
         strangulation or throttling. A perusal of the column No.21 of
         the   postmortem report shows that whereas there                                  was
         brownish - blackish discolouration on the neck, column No.12
         thereof shows that the skin of the body was brownish -
         blackish discoloured. Therefore, prima facie, it appears that it
         was not only the neck which was discoloured, but the entire
         body was discoloured. The final opinion given by the
         concerned doctors is that the cause of death cannot be
         ascertained, however, the possibility of death due to excessive
         ethyl alcohol intoxication cannot be ruled out. From the
         testimony of the wife of the deceased it is apparent that the
         deceased used to consume a lot of liquor. As per the opinion of
         the medical officers no specific cause of death has been
         indicated, but on the basis of the FSL report it has been opined
         that possibility of excessive ethyl alcohol intoxication cannot
         be ruled out. The testimony of the medical officer and the
         postmortem report prima facie do not appear to support the
         prosecution case that the applicant had killed the deceased by
         pressing his foot on his neck. The trial court appears to havePage 4 of 6HC-NIC                               Page 4 of 6      Created On Tue Feb 02 01:58:34 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/16811/2015                                            ORDER




         based the conviction mainly on the confessional statement
         stated to have been made by the applicant before the wife of
         the deceased, without there being any corroborative evidence
         to show that the death of the deceased was a homicidal one.
         Therefore, a prima facie case has been made out for exercise
         of discretion in favour of the applicant.7.   For the foregoing reasons, the application succeeds and
         is, accordingly, allowed. The sentence imposed by the learned
         Second Additional Sessions Judge, Rajula vide judgment and
         order dated 29.11.2013 in Sessions Case No.14 of 2011 (Old
         Sessions Case No.74 of 2008) is hereby suspended till the final
         hearing of the appeal and the applicant is ordered to be
         released on regular bail on his executing a personal bond of
         Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one solvent
         surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the lower Court
         subject to the following conditions;(a) He shall not take undue advantage of his liberty or abuse
         his liberty;(b) He shall maintain law and order;(c) He shall surrender his passport, if any, to the lower court,
         within a week and if he does not possess any passport, then
         he shall make a declaration to that effect before the trial
         court;(d) If during the pendency of the criminal appeal any change in

         deciding this bail application will not affect merits of the case
         at the time of final arguments.10. Rule is made absolute accordingly.Direct service is permitted.(HARSHA DEVANI, J.)

         ==========================================================
                      BUTABHAI JOGABHAI BHARWAD....Applicant(s)
                                      Versus
                          STATE OF GUJARAT....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR IH SYED, ADVOCATE for MR CHIRAG B UPADHYAY, ADVOCATE for the
         Applicant(s) No. 1
         MR HK PATEL, APP for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

                CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE J.B.PARDIWALA

                                  Date : 04/03/2016


                                    ORAL ORDERBy this application, the applicant has prayed for bail. This
         is a successive regular bail application after charge-sheet. The
         charge against the applicant is that of a murder. Out of eight
         persons, he is the only one who is in jail. As it appears, he has
         been attributed with an overt act of inflicting fatal injury on the
         head of the deceased.Be that as it may, it appears that the condition of the
         applicant is bad. He is suffering from L4-L5 Prolapse Vertebral
         Disc Disease with Bilateral Nerve Root Compression. The
         doctors have certified that he needs conservative treatment in
         the form of analgesics physiotherapy and root block, and if
         necessary, may also have to undergo surgery.Page 1 of 2HC-NIC                              Page 1 of 2     Created On Sun Mar 06 03:02:27 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/23080/2015                                                ORDERI take notice of the fact that he has been ordered to be
         released on temporary bail on number of occasions. It would
         always be open for him to pray for temporary bail before the
         trial Court in case of acute necessary. However, since in the
         past regular bail application was not entertained, this being a
         successive regular bail application, I am finding it a little
         difficult to exercise discretion in favour of the applicant.I am told that the trial has commenced and about four to
         five witnesses have been examined so far. I also called for the
         report of the trial Court as regards the status of the trial and,
         according to the report, it appears that the trial might still take
         about four to six months before the same is completed.Having regard to the medical condition of the applicant,
         which I have described above, the trial Court is directed to see
         that top priority is given to this particular case even if there
         are old cases bending before it. The trial Court shall make all
         possible endeavours to ensure that the trial is completed
         within three months from today. If necessary, let the evidence
         be recorded on day-to-day basis.It will be open for the applicant to file a fresh application
         if the trial is not completed within three months as directed.With the above, this application is disposed of.(J.B.PARDIWALA, J.)

                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

         ==========================================================

                                     Versus
                      STATE OF GUJARAT & 1....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR ANVESH V VYAS, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1 - 2
         Mr. Rutvij Oza, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MS JUSTICE SONIA GOKANI

                                     Date : 04/05/2016


                                      ORAL ORDERRule       returnable        forthwith.              Mr.Rutvij              Oza,
         learned APP waives service of notice of rule for and
         on behalf of the respondent -State.The applicants are seeking police protection as
         both the applicants have married without the
         blessings of their parents.The Apex Court rendered in case of Latasingh
         Vs. The State of UP & Ors. reported in 2006(5)
         SCC 475 had directed that "since several instances
         are coming to our knowledge of harassment, threats
         and violence against young men and women who
         marry outside their case, we feel it necessary toPage 1 of 4HC-NIC                                 Page 1 of 4      Created On Thu May 05 03:19:48 IST 2016
                R/SCR.A/2917/2016                                              ORDER



         make some general comments on the matter. The
         nation is passing through a crucial transitional
         period in our history and this Court cannot remain
         silent in matters of great public concern."
             The relevant observations of this decision
         needs to be reproduced at this stage:"The caste system is a curse on the nation and the
             sooner it is destroyed the better. In fact, it is dividing
             the nation at a time when we have to be united to
             face the challenges before the nation unitedly.
             Hence, inter-caste marriages are in fact in the
             national interest as they will result in destroying the
             caste system. However, disturbing news are coming
             from several parts of the country that young men and
             women        who      undergo          inter-caste        marriage,            are
             threatened with violence, or violence is actually
             committed on them. In our opinion, such acts of
             violence or threats or harassment are wholly illegal
             and those who commit them must be severely
             punished. This is a free and democratic country, and
             once a person becomes a major he or she can marry
             whosoever he/she likes. If the parents of the boy or
             girl do not approve of such inter-caste or inter-
             religious marriage the maximum they can do is that
             they can cut off social relations with the son or the
             daughter, but they cannot give threats or commit or
             instigate acts of violence and cannot harass thePage 2 of 4HC-NIC                                Page 2 of 4      Created On Thu May 05 03:19:48 IST 2016
                  R/SCR.A/2917/2016                                             ORDER



             person who undergoes such inter-caste or inter-
             religious marriage. We, therefore, direct that the
             administration/police            authorities            throughout              the
             country will see to it that if any boy or girl who is a
             major        undergoes        inter-caste            or      inter-religious
             marriage with a woman or man who is a major, the
             couple are not harassed by any one nor subjected to
             threats or acts of violence, and any one who gives
             such threats or harasses or commits acts of violence
             either himself or at his instigation, is taken to task by
             instituting criminal proceedings by the police against
             such persons and further stern action is taken against
             such persons as provided by                      law. We sometimes
             hear of 'honour' killings of such persons who undergo
             inter-caste or inter-religious marriage of their own
             free will. There is nothing honourable in such killings,
             and in fact they are nothing but barbaric and
             shameful acts of murder committed by brutal, feudal
             minded persons who deserve harsh punishment. Only
             in this way can we stamp out such acts of barbarism.
             "Bearing in mind the directions and observations
         of the Apex Court rendered in case of Latasingh
         Vs. the State of UP & Ors. (Supra ), the request
         of the applicants requires to be acceded to,                                             to
         ensure their safety and protection.Respondent              No.2-           The       In-charge                PolicePage 3 of 4HC-NIC                                 Page 3 of 4      Created On Thu May 05 03:19:48 IST 2016
                   R/SCR.A/2917/2016                                               ORDER



         Inspector,         Jamnagar         B          Division       Police          Station,
         Jamnagar          shall look into the matter and providepolice protection to the applicants. The time shall
         be decided by the concerned officer, bearing in
         mind all the facts and circumstances of the case
         and ground reality of the case.With      this        observation          and         directions,              the
         present         Special         Criminal            Application                 stands
         disposed of. Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid
         extent.Direct service is permitted.(MS SONIA GOKANI, J.)

             couple are not harassed by any one nor subjected to
             threats or acts of violence, and any one who gives
             such threats or harasses or commits acts of violence
             either himself or at his instigation, is taken to task by
             instituting criminal proceedings by the police against
             such persons and further stern action is taken against
             such persons as provided by                      law. We sometimes
             hear of 'honour' killings of such persons who undergo
             inter-caste or inter-religious marriage of their own
             free will. There is nothing honourable in such killings,
             and in fact they are nothing but barbaric and
             shameful acts of murder committed by brutal, feudal
             minded persons who deserve harsh punishment. Only
             in this way can we stamp out such acts of barbarism.

                                         ORAL ORDERThe applicant has moved this application seeking temporary
         bail for a period of 30 days on the ground that the applicant's brother
         namely Imran Dal got injured in firing and for that purpose FIR is
         lodged but till date there is no news is received about his brother.
         Therefore, the applicant has prayed for grant of temporary bail to find
         out whereabouts his brother.Learned APP Mr.J.K.Shah for the State while opposing this
         application submits that if the applicant will be granted temporary
         bail on the ground as projected in the application, chances of his
         fleeing away as well as taking revenge of his brother and thereby

         applicant who is accused of triple murder case cannot be released on
         temporary bail. Accordingly the application seeking temporary bail
